review_text:
I am terribly disappointed. After waiting months for this to open, walking by every night and peering in the window I was extremely excited to finally eat here. I am a huge fan of Buvette and I Sodi so I was so upset when I was not impressed by anything served. Granted this was their soft opening but they have a lot of work to do service and food wise. 
The meal began with our waiter unable to give us recommendations or his thoughts on what he his favorites were on the menu. Then once we told him our order he made us point it out on the menu so he could copy it down because he admittedly could not pronounce anything on the menu. We were there for 2.5 hours... way too long for ordering primarily vegetable dishes. The tables are so close that you are constantly shoved by a waiter or guest walking by.
Once we did get our food it was all so oily. The charcuterie was the only thing we could finish and even that was served on a dish that must have just been washed because it was sitting in a puddle of water. 
The cauliflower dish tasted like fish and the sea bream (which is the only dish with potential) was topped with a beautiful potato crust but it was so oily we only had a bite each.
One of our dishes was missing so we pointed it out on the menu again and he brought us the wrong dish. 
We had also told our waiter it was our friends birthday and to please bring a slice of cake at the end. He asked us at the end of the meal if we wanted dessert, which is the opposite of what you do when you are told ahead of time to make it a surprise, and when my friend responded no thank you. He just brought us the check instead of a cake and some chestnuts that weren't even hot... At that point we didn't even care because we had been there for over 2.5 hours for a meal that should have taken an hour less.

The decor is lovely and great italian wine selection but I was not impressed with any of the dishes that came out. Rosemary's on Greenwich has a similar menu so if I was going to even go back for wine and charcuterie, I would probably just go there.

While it's early days, I was really impressed with how much Via Carota already gets right, and the food we had was terrific--continental comfort food with superb ingredients and refined preparation. 

I can't say whether it was an off night or if perhaps there were just growing pains that prompted one of the reviewers here to say that the food was "oily," but that certainly wasn't the case when we were there. We had the foie gras crostini and endive salad to start, with the svizzerina (the "burger without the bun," though that doesn't do it justice) and the fried rabbit for entrees.  The foie gras was quite nice, and the endive salad was nicely balanced with the right amount of dressing and a mix of gorgonzola, walnuts and pears with the greens.  The svizzerina was fantastic and the fried rabbit with garlic and rosemary was cooked to perfection--beautifully tender and flavorful with a minimum of grease, the best rabbit I've had in ages. 

Our service was great--non-intrusive but warm and informative.  And, surprisingly, the sidecar I had was one of the better ones I've had anywhere--I didn't even have to ask them to hold the sugar on the rim, and it was more nuanced than I expected.

The lighting may need a little calibration and there may be a rough edge or two, but, again, it's early days for this place.  We wouldn't expect everything to be absolutely perfect yet, even if it's *almost* there.  Our overall feeling is that we will be back, and often.

People love Buvette, so I knew this new spot from the same team just a few doors away would be packed a few days after opening.

We showed up for the early bird special at about 5:30, and were turned away with the info that they would be open in "a half hour or so". I didn't know because they don't answer their phone and there's no info on social media or their website yet, so we were stuck waiting around. No problem though, just go to Big Gay Ice Cream a few steps away and get some ice cream as a dinner appetizer.

We returned right around 6, and the place was already filling up. By the time our meal was done, the fairly large space was completely full, with the crowd of mostly miserable old people couples and very West Village-y younger couples all on top of each other in the closely packed tables. It fits in perfectly with a very West Village atmosphere.

The menu is pretty large, but we got a good sampling of most of the sections, with stuff ranging from just ok to amazing:

- Choice of 3 Salumi, Formaggi or Crostini for ($20)
For these, we chose the Fegatin' di Pollo ($7) from the Crostini section and the Mangalista Lardo ($8) and Cacciatorini di Cinghiale ($8) from the Salumi section. The best was definitely the Mangalista, which actually should have been in the Crostini section, as it consisted of honey and walnuts on the excellent crusty bread. We asked for some additional bread to go with the Salumi option, which wasn't nearly as good as the bread used for the crostini.

- Lasagna Povera ($16)
This was one of the more disappointing items, as it was surprisingly quite bland. It also looked like it could have been cooked more, as the cheese scattered on top was completely unmelted. Some meat probably would have helped things instead of the winter vegetables inside.

- Cavolo Nero ($10)
From the veggies section, this is of course the best course, as the description reads "black kale & pork sausage". The little chopped up pieces of kale are in practically the same proportion to the crumbled up, delicious pieces of sausage. If you want a good vegetable side dish, but one that is by no means healthy, this is a great choice.

- Via Carota Svizzerina ($17)
This one's getting some hype on the food blogs, being described as an amazingly good, bunless burger. In terms of the meat, it was indeed incredibly good. Cooked very rare, and seasoned very well, this sizable patty served pretty much alone on the plate except for some garlic on top, is as excellent as it is simple. Make sure you try this one.

- Coniglio Fritto ($17)
Even better than that chopped steak actually, this fried rabbit was one of the best entrees I've had all year. It consists of 3 sizable pieces of rabbit and a crusty piece of delicious bread. Unlike most rabbit dishes I've had, instead of small, boney pieces with little to no meat, these pieces were really meaty, juicy and satisfying. The skin had a salty seasoning that made it so addictive. Make sure you get this one too.

- Cioccolata ($8)
This was an excellent, though fairly standard slice of flourless chocolate cake, served with a little dollop of whipped cream. It was quite good, and a nice choice to end the meal.

- Semifreddo ($8)
This one was much better than the cake, and a better choice if you are going to pick just one dessert. Topped with hazelnuts, the cool hazelnut semifreddo was also presented impressively overflowing out of the glass it was served in, with a long spoon sticking out for digging to the bottom. Another rich dessert to go with the flourless chocolate cake, this was also very sweet and delicious.

Some of the dishes weren't the best, like the lasagna, and service deteriorated quickly as the high maintenance dining room filled up, but the chopped steak and the rabbit were so good I see no choice but to give a 5 star rating,

We follow new openings and talented chefs.  This place just opened and we worried about getting a spot but the staff is incredible, worked us right in and the food is outstanding.  We sampled quite a few things and loved everything.  Highly recommend.

As big fan of Buvette I was more than happy to see it coming back here too in the decor and the presentation of food.

Food was really tasty, great quality and authentic flavors. 
Service was even better: kind, attentive, acknowledged and entertaining. Molly was so sweet and even ran after us with the credit card I had forgot on the table.

Hot, new rustic Italian in the West Village by Jody Williams and Rita Sodi. If you are a fan of Buvette and/or I Sodi, you shall not miss out. 

Came here on a Tuesday night around 8pm without reservation. Bar was almost full while there were two tables for two available. Dim light, nice vibe. I opted for the bar. I was greeted warmly and handed the menu promptly. Wine list is short and sweet. Can't recall the name of the previous restaurant in this space- the layout was unchanged. 

Onto the food. Menu offers lots options, all are small-medium plates. Perfect for sharing. Between me and my friend, we had:

- Cavolo Nero: black kale & pork sausage. It was OK but the chopped sausage tasted  pretty dry :/ prob better with sliced sausage or crispy bacon?

- Baccala Fritto: fried salted cod and potato balls. Yumm! I usually don't like fried stuffs, but this is good. Topped with whipped garlic cheese~ 

- Polipo: grilled octopus and green olive pesto. You bet, this is my fav! The tentacle was perfectly charred. Great texture, not chewy at all; meaty and scrumptious. Will come back just for this one.

Over the dinner, we got couple drinks, from wine to whiskey sour to grappa and amaro (an Italian aperitif). All good. Not the best I have had nor there is anything to complain about. 

I will def come back and try more item on the menu. If you come in any day on/after wed with 2 or more, make your resy.

Came here with my gf after seeing a movie.  Couldn't make reservations as the restaurant is too new and still getting everything up and running.  That didn't matter as the waitstaff was welcoming and got us drinks and a seat within a few minutes.

We shared a few dishes.  The pumpkin ravioli was really fresh and the pumpkin was very sweet.  We had a fish dish with a nice light sauce that blended well along with the leek dish we had.  The dessert we had was a chocolate budding whose flavors were layered from light to heavier chocolate which was divine.

Overall, this new space from Rita Sodi and Jody Williams hits certain notes which are not currently available in the village and does so quite well.  The service was a little confusing at first (no host) but impeccable.  We were made to feel special and were given great suggestions on what dishes go well together.  This is a great new spot and a great place for a date night.

We love Buvette and I Sodi! So my husband and I were so excited when Via Carota recently opened. It has quickly become our go to place in our neighborhood. Great food, wide selection, wonderful wine and a good cocktail list. The staff is very friendly. Overall feel is very nice, but has a laid back casual vibe. 

Last Saturday night we decided to invite our friends to join us. The hostess sat us in the private dinning area. It was perfect, delicious food and even a visit from owner Jody Williams! 

Thank you for bringing us a great place to meet friends in the West Village!
Felt compelled, and still in the restaurant. Pleasant staff, and delicious food. The I sodi, buvette, carota group kills it.  Polenta and burger thing are out of control.  Coming back soon.

Amazing! Was really excited to go here for my boyfriend's birthday. I tried for a week to call to no avail, so we showed up around 6:30 on a Sunday night and were luckily seated right away (right near Mario Batali). The space is much larger than Buvette, so it's a little less intimate. Nice bar area, but we skipped the wine and went straight for the food. Mostly everything was so declicious! Our service got a little screwy in the beginning and the wrong things came out, but they corrected it. Unfortunately my bf had to eat his pasta first, but he said it was great and wasn't worried about it! 

Crostini with Stracciatella (I think!) and tomatoes--incredible. the cheese was so good and melted a bit. the tomatoes were a little oily, but i would eat it again and again!
Salt Cod Fritters - so great. obviously salty, but that's to be assumed. the mayo it comes with was a lot on the plate, but it was very tasty
Cabbage with Farro and Pecorino--Delicious, fresh and light
Cauliflower Gratin - Creamy deliciousness
Papperadelle with Wild Boar - My bf ate this and said it was really, really good
Gnocchi with Gorgonzola - I always order gnocchi if it's on the menu. This version was good, but I've had better in the city and prefer Malatesta's. I'd skip this next time and try more veggies!

No dessert menu, but our server listed a few and my boyfriend picked the chocolate pudding. I didn't have any, but he said it was great. They also give you a few cookies and I tasted the chocolate with hazelnuts which was very tasty!

All in all $88 before tax and tip--Not bad at all. Can't wait to come back.

I know... If you don't have something nice to say, then don't say anything. But this place can be so cute, so here are my 2 cents, hope it helps to improve the restaurant.

Service: everyone was nice enough, but the service is disorganized and there was some women wearing all black walking around staring at the tables but not helping. It was weird and annoying, especially if you're looking for help.

Food: Menu had potential but the actual food was extremely salty (I can't feel my tongue).

Basically, my friend and I ran out of there... I didn't even get to finish my wine.

Happy to try again, if the menu and service improves. Btw, huge fans of I Sodi and have been going there for years, which is why we had high hopes for Via Carota.

So so very tasty. the restaurant had been open for about a month when I went, so reviews will be adjusted on the next visit.

The Good:
When your friends who are chefs in San Francisco say GO to this restaurant, you GO.  Thank goodness I listened.  

I have a rule: when a restaurant has a well seasoned chef, always choose something that pushes your limits as far as you are willing to try.  Our dinner was no exception.

We had an amazing cabbage salad and roasted squash for appetizers.  Both were flavorful and lovely on a cold winter night.  The cabbage salad blew me away.  Something so simple and yet so tasty.

For dinner we had the wild boar ragu and fried rabbit.  Both were amazing.  The rabbit was perfectly fried, the number of pieces were generous and there was actually meat on the bone!  The boar was deep, earthy and balanced perfectly with the slightly spicy sauce.  

Desert was an amazing hazelnut chocolate mousse.

The space is lovely, not too loud and inviting.

The Bad:

Please pick up your phone.  On a cold night we dragged ourselves across town for dinner hoping that they would be open.  Indeed they were, but with no hours posted ANYWHERE online, it is a little odd not to pick up a phone.

Service is a little odd.  No maitre d./hostess Lots of people bustling about but I had to ask the gentlemen (who I assumed was the manager) that we were ready to order.  I did everything to sign that we ready.  Menu face down on the table, eye contact, but I had to flag them down.  I can't ding them on this a month in.  Once we were served our waitress was perfectly charming and professional.

One of our soda syrups would not blend.  It sat on the bottom of the glass and REFUSED to mix with the soda water which was hilarious.  I make soda syrups and I don't know what was causing this issue.  In any case the house bought us our soda.

The tables smelled freshly stained-- again not a complaint, just an observation.  It took me a minute or two to identify the smell when we can in.

Even with the rough spots (which is to be expected a month in) Via Carota is on the return list in a city that has as many amazing restaurants to try and explore as SF.  See you in a year.

This is the ultimate neighborhood spot - so good that it's worth a trip from another neighborhood. The rare meal where nearly everything I ate was absolutely delicious and noteworthy.

The menu is split into sections that serve as courses - start with a crostini, move onto vegetables, then pastas, finished off with main courses. 

The beet salad with feta was delicious and refreshing, a perfect start. The kale and sausage was arguably the only "forgettable" dish of the evening. The vegetables section of the menu featured over a dozen options of which I'll be back to sample.

The pasta we sampled was the wild boar pappardelle - delicious ragu, delicate, thin, delicious pasta. I can imagine the other pastas are of this quality.

For the mains, we had both the grilled fish + escarole, and the chopped steak. Both were top notch. The fish had just the right amount of lemon to be refreshing and paired great with the escarole, the chopped steak, somewhat of a bunless burger, was delicious - topped with roasted garlic, it was only briefly seared on each side, creating a hard crust with a center that had a steak tartare type consistency.

We ended with a chocolate hazelnut mousse type dessert that was just the icing on the cake of this delightful meal. Will definitely be back.

Came here with a friend on this past Friday night. Place was PACKED. We probably waited about 30-40 minutes for our table, which we expected (since they do not take reservations). It was run in a very similar fashion to Jody Williams' other resto Buvette, which I LOVE and frequent constantly. So while were waiting, we had a glass of the montepulciano (fantastic!) especially at 10 dollars/glass. Unfortunately, that was one of the only well-priced things on the menu. 

My friend and I ordered 5 dishes to share. Here's the good:

The stracchino and sun-dried cherry tomato crostini (small but delish)

Grilled octopus-- SO yummy. Really cooked to perfection, but again, quite a small portion

Pumpkin Ravioli-- 2 words: Butter and cheese. I am a lover of all things butter-- and this pasta was smothered in it, almost to the point of it being too much...Wait, what am I saying? There can NEVER be too much butter. Also, the pumpkin filling was super fresh .  However, it was an incredibly small portion for what you're paying. This seems to be a recurring theme here..


On to the Not so good:

The mista salad-- IMO, really hard to mess this up. And this one just really failed to impress in any way. Which is strange.. because its literally lettuce and dressing. The dressing tasted like salt and oil. It badly needed acid. A good splash of vinegar of any kind would've made saved this. 

The pricing: Now I am not one to complain about food prices when you're getting amazing food. This is New York City. I get it. But this place is just plain overpriced. No getting around it. 

Overall, had an enjoyable night with some pretty good food. But not worth it for the cost. I'll stick to Buvette.

My boyfriend and I have been to i Sodi several times and so we were excited to check Via Carota out. Upon arriving, there was complete chaos - the hostess was nowhere to be seen for several minutes, and when she did show up, she was so busy speaking with other couples or running around that it took a while to get our name on the wait list. I don't mind waiting for 30-45 minutes, but please don't seat other couples before us, especially when they've arrived 10-20 minutes after us - and definitely don't give us an attitude or be dismissive when we ask about our table. The restaurant really needs to get a second person to manage the crowds, and indiscriminately at that. 

The food was delicious, and the waitress was wonderful and attentive - but the experience with the hostess really soured the experience and gave a terrible first impression.

I cam here in early-mid December with 2 friends, one of whom is a pescetarian. Overall, I agree with Eater's description of this spot being "mainly Italian and mainly delicious". The wait to get in at 8pm was pretty long, but we got seated almost immediately at the long communal table, right by the kitchen. The wine list was pretty good and reasonably priced, so I tried a new Italian one at the recommendation of the server. We split 8 dishes between the 3 of us plus dessert (but no large format ones), which was just about the right amount. The crostini came out first, but then all of our dishes followd up in really quick succession and we had too many on the table at once. Not ideal for all of the hot ones to get cold as we struggle to try everything.

The finocchi was really unique and a good counterbalance to some of our richer dishes. The baccala frito (salt cod fritters) were amazing, especially with the sauce. We probably could have split another serving of these. The squash was my favorite, for sure. There was a bit of cheese on it, but nothing too heavy. I also really liked the octopus (both the charred end of the tentacle and the fleshier upper part).

The gnocchi with gorgonzola was almost too rich for me, and I tend to love heavy cheese and cream pasta dishes. Good thing were were splitting it. The risotto limone was also not that great, verging on a tad hard and undercooked.

The hazlenut semifreddo was a delight and I happily scraped the bottom of the glass. I'd definitely come back to try the much-heralded rabbit dish.

Understanding this restaurant is new, I wanted to provide a suggestion to help improve the experience for other patrons since our visit fell short of expectations.  I had wanted to try Via Carota after being very happy going to iSodi and was expecting a great experience.

On busy evenings it could improve the customer experience to have dedicated staff at the front of the restaurant to take down names and another member of the staff seating parties in an effort to better organize the wait for groups.  It was clear parties could be seated ahead of others with the same number in their group and it could be difficult to receive an accurate suggestion as to the expected wait time.

To start: Small dish of oil cured black olives with a hint of sweetness and lemon. Yum. Excellent martini and a small glass jug of wine (expensive, but a hefty pour). 

Appetizer: Grilled radicchio was sweet, crunchy, cheesy, and heavenly--could eat it as dessert. 

Main: Roasted pig shank over faro and cranberry beans. The most scrumptious and perfectly roasted piece of meat I've ever had. 

We were on a tight time schedule on a Friday night. Arrived at 5:20, only one other table was occupied by a couple and there were a few people at the bar. We were done by 6:00 without feeling rushed. Wish we could have stayed for dessert. 

Wait staff was knowledgeable, approachable, friendly, and welcoming. 

We live in the neighborhood and are big fans of Buvette and i Sodi. A very nice addition to the 'hood. Will definitely come back.

Update: Have come back twice since and each dish is better than the next. I really don't think they could do anything bad if they tried!

I am a huge fan of Buvette so was very excited to try Via Carota which is just down the street.  They don't take ressies, so be prepared to wait.  The black kale and sausage is a crowd fav for a reason, so be sure you order it.  Also try the octopus, so tender!  The space is charming, especially love the bar, its beautiful, I am told the french doors will open once the weather gets nicer, for some wonderful al fresco dining options!

Pretty much the perfect experience. 

My friend and I ended up here because Buvette was too crowded (at 5:30 pm!) and were so glad we did. A truly wonderful experience. 

We had a lovely bottle of wine and shared 5 things from the menu. Absolute perfection. Especially that chopped steak--amazing.

Had dinner at the bar.  Was tight quarters but not uncomfortable.  Very nice bar marble bar and pleasant atmosphere.   Wait was not too bad on a Friday at prime time walking in 3ppl.   Wine prices were fair with some interesting selections as well.  
The food was nice, just not my tastes maybe.  The risotto and calamari were decent but not amazing.  The fried rabbit was texturally a failure I thought with the breading coming off, and the flavor of rabbit meat is not delicious I thought.   Was my first time eating rabbit however.   I'd probably like to come back and try a few other small plates at the bar rather than a full dinner.  It is a very pleasant atmosphere.

Huge disappointment. 
I am basically a regular at Buvette, one of my favorite eateries in the city. They have it down perfectly, from food to service, and atmosphere. Which is why I had such high hopes and expectations for Via Carota.
When it first opened, it was often empty when I walked by. Finally, one Friday night I decided to try it.
I was with a group of 5. We arrived and asked how long the wait would be, and the host gruffly responded, "ummm probably 45, I don't know- you have a drink at the bar, I'll put your name down." He then writes our name on a column with a piece of chalk. There are several other names, some half written, some half wiped away, a few crossed off. 

We then order drinks at the bar which take forever to come out. The cocktails arrived and then the wine came 15 minutes later. We wait and wait and people are being seated that have arrived after us. We then notice our name has been removed from the column. When we bring this to the hosts attention, and ask if we are still on the list,  he rudely says, "yes, I know you are here, don't tell me how to do my job"....
NOT how to treat a customer who has been patiently waiting in the cramped waiting area, being bumped and asked to move aside for over an hour.

Let's just say we ended up waiting for 2 hours, with no apologies. The food was mediocre, and overpriced. The atmosphere is very chaotic. The lights are too bright and it's very noisy.

Unfortunately, I will not be going back. They have A LOT of work to do if they want to meet the standards of Buvette.

We just spent a few days in New York, and our first food stop was Via Carota.  We showed up at about 6:30pm and put our names on the list to return 25 minutes later, and we were seated at the bar by 7.    

We split the Il Guado Poggio alla Querce 2011 wine, and it was the perfect complement to our dinner.

We shared the broccoletti, chopped steak, indivia, and wild boar ragu.  The indivia was excellent, the wild boar ragu was absolutely divine and made me very happy, and the chopped steak was also very good.  The broccoletti was nothing spectacular, but still good.  The kitchen accidentally made an additional plate of gnocci and gave it to us with compliments, which was also very good.

This is a great location and restaurant, and the food and service well worth another visit.  What a great way to start off our New York weekend.

Will not return for two reason, lack of hospitality (contrary to what the owner and staff claim) and overall salt-overload, painfully average food (especially consider it's west village).

Service: I dealt with two hostesses while during our 3 HOUR wait, neither was the least bit apologetic and one is straight-up unprofessionally rude. we had a 7-person party, put our name down around 7pm and ordered a couple of drinks while waiting. We checked in with the hostess a few times but can't get an estimated wait time from her. Advice #1 - if you don't take reservation be prepared to give guests an estimate. 

1.5 hours into the wait everyone was starving and tired of standing, the hostess kept telling us "the party in the back room got the check and they are leaving soon". That party stayed for at least 1 hour after she first told us. I asked the hostess if she could tell the group that they may only have the table for certain timeframe - a standard restaurant practice in NYC - she said no and snobbishly suggested that if I want I can go tell the group such myself. She then went on about how much they are proud of their hospitality and she's doing her best to accommodate us. Advice #2 - if you leave your guests wait for 2.5 hours without even offering a bread basket, hold off on the "perfect hospitality" speech. And oh, don't ask me to do your job for you.

When we finally sit down around 10pm...after a 3 HOUR wait, the owner came out and she pointed out to us that her staff were upset about our situation...and that SHE NEEDS TO TAKE CARE OF HER STAFF. AGAIN, NO APOLOGIES OFFERED TO MY PARTY. I asked her why her staff were upset and she mumbled about them being tired after a long day.  

It was at point that I stopped wondering why this place lacks mannerism to guests.

Food: overall WAY TOO SALTY. From the cheese plate to my pork belly, which also didn't have the fat properly cooked down so it tasted excessively fatty. Salad was okay, octopus wasn't bad, but it wasn't on par with many other restaurants in west village.

Classic case of high expectation under-deliver.

FYI: be aware of the "communal table" situation in the back room. As soon as we sit down, after 3 hours of waiting, the first thing waiter offered to us wasn't apology, or bread, but a warning that there may be another 3-person party to take the remaining 3 seat at the table.

3 hours and starvation may just lead to elbow-rubbing with strangers. Yay to the 0.0001% chance of new-found friendship.

Final word: drop writing your guest waitlist with CHALK on the poles where guests stand next (unavoidable given the space). Getting chalk on a nice winter coat isn't exactly what we signed up for.

Food and bar are delicious but holy crap your logistics are atrocious for this neighborhood. Operations staff should understand that on a Saturday night you will not only be busy but to expect a variety of party sizes. Because we brought six WHOLE people for dinner at 7, were told that we'd wait for an hour and a half, and weren't seated until 930. Granted, it's a great revenue grab for your bar but we were told, by a hostess, that we "were welcome to leave". No shit? Work on your process and maybe you'll stay in business without needing a bailout from the other restaurants you run.

KenScale: 8.5/10

Via Carota is a new restaurant formed from partnership of chef Jody Williams (from Buvette) and Rita Sodi (from I Sodi), who also happen to be domestic partners as well. I haven't had a chance to visit Buvette yet, but have been to I Sodi a couple of times and generally liked the food there, so I was looking forward to what the kitchen at this restaurant has to offer. Overall, I was very impressed with the soulful dining experience this restaurant offers. Nothing coming from the kitchen will wow you, but all the dishes were prepared with thoughtfulness that would make for a satisfying meal.

Via Carota's food is primarily Italian, which means you should always start your meal with delicious proscuitto di parma. There is a variety of vegetable dishes being offered, and you should definitely go for outstanding salsify with brown butter and thyme. Grilled octopus and green olive pesto was aromatic and tasted quite nice, and fried rabbit with rosemary and garlic was also tender. The chopped steak, which is sort of like meat in a burger without buns and has quickly become the signature dish of the restaurant, was also well-cooked and had the rustic touch I was a fan of. Both pasta dishes at Via Carota also turned out to be winners. I'm generally not a gnocchi person but the one at Via Carota was silky smooth with nice balance of flavor and texture. Pappardelle with wild boar ragu wouldn't surprise you with anything out of the blues, but it was also another very well-prepared dish that you would want somewhere in the Italian countryside. Panna cotta, which was smooth without being overly sweet, marked the end of a great meal.

The restaurant doesn't take reservations, so be prepared to wait or show up really early. I showed up at 7 p.m. on Saturday, and ended up waiting more than an hour. I really loved the West Village vibe of the dining room and the ambiance and crowd would make you believe this is an ideal restaurant to visit if you were vistiing West Village and had to choose only one place to dine at . The restaurant has a full bar, but my suggestion is to go with Italian wine menu, which is huge and has some solid selections. Via Carota is the type of restaurant I would visit over and over again. Hopefully they would start taking reservations soon.

Maybe I've been a little too generous with the 5-star rating lately, but I don't care.

Came here with another couple for a double date on a Friday night. They don't take reservations unless you're Sofia Coppola HINT: if you look UP at the wall to the right after entering the restaurant you'll see a chalkboard list of names. These are their reservations for the night, it's fun to play guess who, they're pretty cryptic though like ICE, Sofia, etc. 

We arrived around 6:30 to put our name in and have a glass of wine at the bar while we waited. I realize this is pretty much the time for the Early Bird Special in New York, but if you want to have a better experience I'd go earlier. By the time we left the place was swarming with the Buvette brunch crowd (if you don't know what that means you are part of of the Buvette brunch crowd)

We were seated at a small community table in the  back of the restaurant, maybe they brought us here because we were loud and I was in Hunter boots....but either way we ended up having an amazing time. The area was intimate, which allowed us to talk, enjoy the meal, and converse with our waiter. Who by the way was AMAZING. Some delightful man from the French countryside. Shout out to the french waiter we love you! We let him do a lot of the ordering. If every server there is as good as him I highly recommend following suit. If not, the whole menu is pretty divine so you really can't go wrong.


If it's good enough for Sofia Coppola,Mario Batali, AND @thefoodbabyny... it's good enough for me.
I really love this place!!! The food is great and the space is beautiful.  I was really looking forward to try this place after being a regular at Buvette and it didn't disappoint!

This restaurant is simply fantastic. About the most authentic Italian food I have eaten in New York. Beautifully prepared.  Jody Williams (Buvette) and Rita Sodi (I Sodi) strike gold again with this perfect mix of fun, energy and flavor!

I came here with a friend for dinner last night and was quite pleased.  

Upon arriving we were told there was about a 30 minute wait for 2, which actually turned out to be closer to an hour.  It was a bit frustrating but I was able to pass the time with a good friend so not the end of the world...

Once we were seated (at the bar) the bar tender fixed a good drink, and was quite attentive and friendly.  

Between my friend and I we split:
(1) the Octopus
(2) Chopped Steak
(3) Tortelli 
(4) Scorzonera  

all of which were highly dynamic and pleasing dishes, close to perfectly seasoned with complex depth of flavor and texture. My favorite of the four entrees was the scorzonera, which was something totally new and unexpected for me.  It was phenomenal... I've never tasted anything quite like it!

I will definitely go back as i'm eager to explore more of the menu, especially the vegetables.  Lovers of excellent food will really enjoy this restaurant.

Tables are too close together and it's too loud. Some of the food was excellent (beets and ravioli), other things like the pork belly were boring and bland. Odd mix of stylish/reserved patrons and loud/obnoxious yuppies.

So I had to do it! i came here late on a Wednesday night at 10pm. no wait or anything, i came right in and they sat me and my guest. I love the look of this place and design. four stars on the layout. the menu is great and broken up into sections and all priced accordingly. It reads inexpensive and it is but the portions are a touch small. Maybe thats the fat pig that is inside me. I had lardo crostini, citrus salad, smoked ricotta ravioli and braised sweet breads with tomato and polenta. They were all top notch. My wine was a glass of vermentino which was a bit on the warm side and it was very small for 14$ i think. kinda taken back on it when they poured it. (maybe I'm a lush) The negroni my guest ordered was nice. the plates and glasses are super cute and look elegant and rustic if that makes sense. Overall I will be coming here after work and they are still new on the block so maybe they are still tweaking. I will try more of the vegetable dishes too. oh the waiter I had was nice. but the girl explaining the specials to me was kind of shy and uncomfortable. thats it.

Great Easter Dinner. We came on the early side to ensure we'd get a table. Great decor - all restored wood floors and tables. Friendly service and wonderful food. First round we did Sardines, Artichoke - then had Sea Breeze + Tagliatelle. Only complaint would be a little heavy on the garlic oil.

What a treat, unbelievable food, I had the mixed salad which was nice, the artichoke hearts which were absolutely out of this world, and the flat chicken which may have been one of the best of my life...go here now

It's been a while since I've had a meal I thought of for days after, let alone one where the flavors were so simple and spoke, for the most part, for themselves. 

Let's start with the banga caudo: the most sublime radishes with an anchovy dipping oil. I could have stopped there, gone home and not eaten anything else just to preserve the splendid taste in my mouth. 

Next, the jumbo white asparagus and smoked prosciutto - OMG. But wait: the citrus risotto came next and it was sublime. So simple. Pure. Delicious. 

The grilled octopus I'd recommend - perhaps with a vegetable side. And the chopped steak - my mouth waters as I recall the dish. Basically that, grilled with salt and pepper, with roasted rosemary and whole cloves of garlic as garnish. The word that comes to mind is fresh. I could mainly taste the beauty of the beef! 

We shared the panna cotta after, finished with rough sea salt and the most sublime olive oil. Our waitress had informed us it wasn't sweet which is why it was perfect. PERFECT. 

The place is full of neighborhood regulars. The service is casual, attentive, and effortless. I can't wait to go back.

I went on a Friday Night, they didn't take reservations so I had to wait for a while until I was seated. As soon as I got in, the hostess offered drinks, I tried the Old Fashioned, which was good but a bit strong on the orange bitters. At least it kept me distracted for the almost-1-hour-wait-despite-the-fact-that-i-was-told-the-wait-was-only-10-minutes...

I tried the beef carpaccio, very generous portion but poor on flavor. The octopus was overcooked and a bit hard to bite, to be honest I enjoyed more the pesto that came with it, but it was loaded with salt. The highlight (in my opinion) was the Pappardelle with ragu, nicely cooked, tender and flavorful. I finalized with the 'Via Carota Svizzerina' - chopped steak. I ordered it medium-rare but it came overcooked, dry and too salty (I guess the chef loves Sodium), very disappointing. For dessert I had the olive oil pannacotta which was nice, but nothing spectacular. 

In general, service was just ok - I had to waive my hand more than a couple of times to get someone's attention, when I sat my table wasn't clean and there was no silverware or cups/glasses, which discouraged me to order wine.

1 star less for the overpriced and underachieved food, I'm not sure If I would go back.

So many places opening up in the West Village recently that it's gotten me actually out and about. I love the vegetable-heavy menu here because it's so hard to get a salad these days that actually tastes different and flavorful. Just wish they would do more eggs (their sister restaurant Buvette ahs an amazing brunch!)

Why would anyone wait 3 hours for a table in a neighborhood where there are a bazillion terrific restaurants within a 5 minute walk?!    That's just insane.  True, Via Carota does not take reservations, and it was filled to capacity when we walked in, but we (two of us) were graciously offered seats at the bar, where we had awesome food and an awesome time watching the bartender make awesome drinks.

Roast chicken, gnocchi and the risotto! Come with food friends and try to enjoy it all. Everything was good and the ambience was very good and the waiter was attentive but not hovering.  Worth checking out, get there a lil early and enjoy this restaurant and its wonderful food!

Very mixed. On the plus side the decor of the place is terrific and some of the first course plates (asparagus for example) were excellent. On the other hand there are a lot of missteps. One of our party of six got inedible meat, loaded with fat and gristle.   Also, as many of the reviews have said the service is not good - we had to search for our waitress several times.  But the real clunker came after the main course.  Desserts are lackluster.  The only tea is a choice of either the typical chamomile or mint, served in teabags and when we said we'd just have decaf coffee the snotty waitress informaed us that they would not serve decaf because the place is "purist" (I'm not sure what is purist about teabags of generic tea).  In fact the waitress was fairly snotty throughout the meal. A pretentious place trying to seem homey.

Terrible service for mediocre food. Hostess will tell you it is 30 minute wait when it takes two hours to seat you. Reason is that kitchen is incredibly slow. And the food is mediocre at best. Avoid at all costs. Lots of other good places in the area.

I had a lovely meal of delicious appetizers and good rose wine. Unfortunately I was over-charged and they have never contacted me regarding this issue. I will not return and will spread the word to my friends.

This place definitely gets 5 stars. They don't take reservations which should give them 4 stars but the food...shut the fuck up! It's incredible. I've been there twice and need to go back. The gnocchi is the most delicious gnocchi I've ever had. It seriously melts in your mouth. Maybe it's loaded with butter but I don't care. It's deliciousness wrapped in a little ball. The lemon risotto was was slightly undercooked, says my boyfriend, but it thought it was perfect. Very good. Go here! The staff speaks French and German and these are two languages that melt my heart. Beautiful place. Beautiful food. Beautiful and nice people. That's all you need.

I should add, they don't take reservations. You arrive and they write your name on some pole and you have to wait to be seated which isn't very long. But I thought I'd mention it because the place gets pretty busy.

I may have a new favorite restaurant in NYC, and I think this may be it. I love Buvette, so it's easy for me to like this place. Jody's restaurants always have a magnificent charm that make me want to make her places a regular stop for me. This feels like a neighborhood restaurant with a local flavor, and the rustic comfortable space certainly inspires it. 

The pastas all looked so fabulous, but I was craving the restaurant's famous chopped steak patty (think: fancy hamburger). It arrived at the table medium rare with juices combining with the olive oil that made each bite memorable. I chose to accompany the patty with the side dish of grilled asparagus, sautéed onion and prosciutto over a risotto like base -- I'm still thinking about it. 

The Manhattan was wonderful.

So many more things to try here, but I'll be back. This place is special and feels like home.

Sorry, Rita (I Sodi) does it better than Rita+Jody (Buvette). The vibe is cute and inviting but the food is very hit or miss. So many veggie side dishes but no veggie hits. A very sad, poor tasting grilled chicken. At least there was the pasta: papardelle with wild boar ragu was the star of the evening. Sigh. You can find me at I Sodi instead.

I tried a toast with ricotta and asparagus, broccoli rabe, and a polenta and prosciutto dish. All three were quite good and not too heavy. The service was uneven - the people indoors were extremely attentive and asked if I needed anything while I waited for my friend. The same cannot be said for our waiter outdoors who kept admitting that he had forgotten about us. This definitely slowed things down - especially when waiting to place our order and waiting for the check. I would come back, though.

Bloomberg Business recommended this restaurant and what a mistake.  Seating us was a bit confusing as we ask for a larger table, they said no and then 15 min later said ok, but we were already comfortable and said no thanks.  Not good. Second, waitress told us white salmon was the special of the day.  White salmon?  Could it be a new species of salmon or perhaps it was actually steelhead or even rainbow trout?  Third, the portions were extremely small and I was still hungry.  I had the sea bream, was maybe a 6oz fillet and was only one fillet on a bed of mixed greens!  And at $19 - wow what a bargain. When I mentioned this to our waiter he said "that's our normal portion" What, for a child maybe?? Bottom line, we are never returning. Thank goodness Big Gay Ice Cream was down the block!!

The place is exactly what we are looking for in a restaurant. The place is new clean and great interior. The service was great and food exactly what we wanted. Small dishes to share. We did 1 vegetable 1 pasta and 1 fish. Everything was really good. We ended it all with a bowl of berries with cream, you should defiantly try it!! 
The one negative is that it is extremely loud, I felt I was screaming to my friend which is fine for a while but after 2hours it's too much. 
But I will defiantly go back.

The food, the space, the people are all gorgeous. 

They don't take reservations. We were a two-top on a Friday 930pm, waited 30min at a crowded bar with a bottle of wine. Perhaps the wait was shortened due to our commitment to an entire bottle. 
 
Again, the room is decorated so beautifully that it would take the most perfect of weather to get me on the dark sidewalk. I want to see the food I'm eating, along with the people I'm dining beside. 

The lardo crostini, drizzled in honey, was perhaps the best bite of the night.

Well, then the polipo came, and that was pretty unbelievable, too. Of course anything drizzled in EVOO is delicious, but the tenderness of the octopus was extraordinary. 

Carrots are worth every penny ($17). Yogurt and pistachios are a dope touch. 

Prosciutto and melon are BFFLs and for good reason. 

The twice cooked lamb had both a softness to it that only braising can bring, but a smokiness straight from the grill.  

Then came the chopped steak which was basically--and I mean this as a supreme compliment--a  super fancy, carb-less burger. Whatever you call it, it was bloody perfection. No seriously, cooked medium rare, the plate is left in a puddle of blood, fat, and oil that only a carnivore can love. 

The service was excellent. Will certainly come back to try the other items we wanted.
Great meal and great service. Minus one star because the outdoor tables are tiny and set at an incline so you spend your entire meal catching your plates, utensils and drinks. Just sit inside.

Love the food here. Very straightforward and delicious Italian food with quality ingredients. At times it can be too salty or too oily, but it is mostly great. The vegetable appetizers and salads are among my favorite--like the scamorza and fungi--DELICIOUS! The lemon risotto was also quite good. I always go for the pappardelle with wild boar ragu, which can be salty, but yummy. The service is usually wonderful, except for my last visit, where we had a young waitress who sighed and rolled her eyes each time she came over. I mean, we were spending about $200 on the meal, she could at least keep her boredom to herself.

I've always thought of the West Village as a culinary wasteland for overpriced and underwhelming fare, where authenticity is butchered in favor of superfluous presentation. Too many places in this neighborhood leave you feeling unsatisfied and your wallet in a state of shock. I've had more than my fair share of such experiences in the West Village to justify that opinion.

But Via Carota was different...

It was such a perfectly balanced, yet exceptional experience from the moment we stepped inside, from the service to the quality of the food.

Here are the highlights from my experience:

SERVICE: 10/10

- Friendly, attentive staff (While waiting for our table, I asked for Dewar's on the rocks, which they didn't have, so I ordered a McCallan instead, even though I hadn't anticipated on spending that much. She returned with a comparable whiskey to Dewar's, one that was a lot cheaper than the McCallan. It was like she read my mind...)

- Only waited about 25 mins for our table (on a Friday night around 9pm)

- Efficient, yet extremely hospitable service.


AMBIANCE: 7/10

- A little noisy, but overall ambiance was intimate, chic, and homey all at the same time.


FOOD: 10/10

It was amazing...never been to Italy, but I imagine this is how Italian grandmas would cook...if Italian grandmas were hipster perfectionists.

Ordered the zucchini flowers (stuffed with ricotta and basil, then fried) and prosciutto for appetizers, the wild boar ragu for pasta, the polipo (octopus) and svizzerina (chopped steak) for entree, and the chocolate mousse for dessert. Note: Everything is meant to share.

My favorite was the chopped steak. It was cooked perfectly. A carnivore's wet-dream for sure.

HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

More like 3.5. 

Overall, this was a perfectly lovely experience, and I would definitely return. Great service.

The only negative, we found some of the food to be excessively oily, and salty. Some dishes were big hits - the Octopus, The Conglio Frito. Others not so much. The grilled artichokes were swimming in oil yet oddly paired with an aoli. The mushrooms with scamorza were salty. The garlic scamps with prosciutto and polenta was a little weird. The three elements didn't work so well together. The wine list is good, if not a bit overpriced. If this was a little cheaper overall, it would feel really, really good. It's not expensive, but it's getting there. We were seated right away which was also awesome.

I really like this spot. Very relaxed vibes, no reservations, no need to order your appetizers and entrees in order. Get them how you like them. 

I felt like I was in Europe the moment our waiter came to our table. Which was in way very refreshing.

The food was market fresh ingredients prepared in with complex flavor profiles. It seems simple but there are nuance and subtle flavors. 

Overall, I liked this place, I'd be wiling to go back. I'd give it five stars but it's not a five star spot.

Very attentive service and delicious food. Extremely highly recommended.

The hostess offered us a table when we arrived, but we decided it was too early to eat at 6:00. She said she would gladly seat us whenever we were ready. At 7:00, she gently reminded us that a table would be available in about a half hour, which was perfect for us. Sure enough, at 7:30 she had a small table near the window ready for us.

I appreciated the bartender's excellent service. We were drinking sparkling water rather than alcoholic beverages. He cheerfully refilled our glasses for 1 1/2 hours. He offered to take my oversized shopping bags & store them safely in the back for me until we were ready to leave.

The food was genuinely Italian, like the food in Italy, not typical cheese-y American-Italian. Cannellini heirloom Tuscan beans with green garlic, freshly grilled sardines and grilled chicken in lemon vinaigrette were scrumptious. The star of the evening was the dessert, not because I have a sweet tooth or because the dessert is nearly always better than the rest of the meal, but because of its uniqueness: Grilled peaches with Amaretto di Saronno sauce, sans mascarpone. Best of all, our efficient, professional server reassured us that everything we ordered was prepared with olive oil rather than dairy.

Prices within reason. Easy walk to two different subway stations.

Its good that finally they open for lunch (heard its impossible to get a sit eve time)
Fantastic crostini with figs and ricotta as well as the shrimp special dish .
Excellent -correctly done- pastas , mostly the tortelli .
The dishes are fair sized (and priced) that can be (and recommended ) shared. 
We had the Sardinian wine in carafe and it was surprisingly delicious .
One of the most beautiful spaces in NYC .

SPECTACULAR food. Divine ingredients, magical combinations, beautiful and knowledgeable staff. Only nightmare is the waiting for a table, no rezzies taken. Hope they expand asap or open more locations.

Amazing Italian food. Started with an incredibly friendly waitress and got better from there. Small portions that we shared amongst us similar to tapas. Really tasty food that had us wanting more. The grilled peaches due dessert were simply amazing

My friends and I came for dinner. We were quickly seated after the whole party was here but we ended up going to a long communal table that they sat other people with us later on during our dinner. Those people were extremely loud and elbow-y if you know what I mean. You would think they would have planned better for us but whatever. That really is the only complaint I have of the entire dining experience.

The food was delicious and perfectly executed.

We ordered several items to share: Burrata di puglia, ricotta di pecora, ramps with pancetta and polenta, grilled octopus and green olive pesto, and sea bream with grilled escarole.

I really enjoyed the appetizers and they were perfect to share. The burrata was perfect (then again, how could it not be!) I also really enjoyed the flavor of ramps. I would order those two dishes again, no question.

I found my grilled octopus a little more tough than I am accustomed and the pesto too salty.

Overall, I would return but ask not to share a table. 

Service was attentive in the beginning and near the end.

Tried this place for a casual date night with the misses on a Friday at 6pm.

Decor: upon entering the restaurant, I immediately liked the decor. A bit of an open rustic feel with cool little details. The open windows on a nice day gave a relaxing breeze into the restaurant.

Service: maybe it was because we came a little early but the service was subpar. Our greeter was not "confident" in greeting us and was a bit off. The waiter didn't inform us that the menus were discreetly placed behind our chairs - we were waiting for the waiter to bring our menus which took more than 10-15 minutes. Not a huge deal but still something.

Food: Chicken liver, Octopus, Fried Rabbit, and of course the Chopped steak. 

Chicken liver - highly recommend. Not as gamy and it was almost refreshing with the sauce it came with. 
Octopus - very good. It wasn't overly chewy and the texture was great. It was actually my favorite dish.
Fried Rabbit - it's definitely fried but I wasn't sure if it was rabbit I was eating or chicken. Tasted bland once you chewed past the fried part. 
Chopped steak - big disappointment. I didn't have high expectations but was more curious about this dish as everyone loved it. When it came, it was overly oily. While eating it, I had a hard time tasting anything else but the oil and had to wipe my mouth constantly after every bite. After about 3-4 small bites, I stopped eating it. I can understand the juices from the steak coming out because well, that's where the real flavors are but, this was neither flavorful nor tasty. Avoid.

Presentation: In terms of presentation of the dishes, I think the octopus was the best. I guess it's a little "easier" to present a single piece of say octopus leg, vs. let's say a salad but it was visually pleasing. On the other hand, chopped steak looked like a beef patty in oil soup. 

Overall: I would say it's worth a visit if you're in the neighborhood but not worth it to venture there specifically. I think as you can see based on some of the other reviews it's a comfortable local joint for either a casual date night, or dinner with friends.

My third visit to Via Carota tonight, and sad to say it was a mixed bag.  My first two visits (once for an early dinner and once for a weekend brunch) were sublime, and VC was fast becoming a new favorite.

The host was rude and officious.  We did not have a long wait (we were there at 6:30 on a weeknight) unlike many reviewers.  This no-taking-reservations stuff is for the birds.

We were a party of three and got seated at a TINY round table that honestly would've been tight for a party of two; for three it was comical.  Two chairs had backs and one was a stool - ridiculous but frankly I'm not sure a third chair would have fit!  The place was busy throughout our visit but they have jammed it so full of tables that no one, not guests, not staff, has enough room.  Very reminiscent of Buvette in this respect, as was the noise level (deafening).

We had the app specials -- squash blossoms and calamari.  The squash blossoms were good but incredibly salty.  The calamari was terrific (nice breading, not overly oily) but wasn't served with a sauce of any kind, which was odd.  We had the lemon chicken (fine but unremarkable) and the tortelli pasta (overly oily and just plain mushy).  Our server should have flagged that two apps, a pasta and an entree would not be enough for three people but did not, mostly because I think he was completely overwhelmed.  (Odd, because the place is small and full of staff.)  So we ended up having to call him back over and ordered a crostini (fine) and the melanzane (completely tasteless).

Across my visits it's felt like the desserts have gotten short shrift: often only two or three choices each night, and they sometimes run out which is silly given that we were there on the early side.  That said, we ordered both options tonight (the semifreddo and the warm peaches) -- and both were excellent.

While I have affection for the place based on my earlier visits, I can't say I'll be running back, which is a shame.  It feels like they've gotten careless and sloppy, with little attention to the actual dining experience.  

Definitely would not recommend for a date - this place has become scene-y, at least if tonight is any indication.

I'm doing it, I'm giving this restaurant 5 stars. I've been here twice now, both times equally delicious. Last week I went close to 8pm and had 4 people - we really lucked out because all of the groups waiting were parties of 2 so we snagged a table right away. This restaurant doesn't take reservations so I recommend coming on the earlier side to get a table - or just having luck :). One of the best things about this restaurant is the seasonal menu. I saw 2 completely different menus by going in April and then in July. They base their menu on the produce and ingredients available in that month. They also have half of the menu dedicated to vegetables. Some of the recent dishes we got were the grilled artichokes, burrata, wild boar ragu papardelle, a special of lobster spaghetti and the grilled octopus. The plates are small but easily shareable amongst a group. One dish that I think is always on their menu is the fried rabbit - we got this last time and it was delicious. The only negative about this place is service can be spotty. However, I'm over looking this as the food is delicious and the restaurant has such a great vibe to it. I thought of this restaurant as sort of a hidden gem as I hadn't read too much about it before going a few months ago, however now I just saw an Eater article on an am worried the secret is out! If you are looking for Italian in the West Village I highly recommend Via Carota. Another item to note is that they only seat full parties, and while this annoys me at places with reservations I understand it here as presumably your table would be waiting to order until everyone arrives.

Quite disappointed with Via Carota, would recommend you avoid this restaurant.

After an okay first experience, decided to check the restaurant out again since its close by.  Appetizers were okay, but main courses across the board were really lacking.  Not one dish out of the lamb, risotto, eggplant, or pappardelle stood out.  

The service was also really unwelcoming.  Surprised a staff / manager would act so poorly to patrons at their restaurant.

I went for my first -- and probably last -- meal here yesterday night.  I thought the food was good (had the spaghetti, grilled artichokes, and eggplant) but just not good enough to justify the price and portion size.  That's fine...Via Carota would get a 3-star review if that were my only issue.

In my book, the only thing that gets a restaurant - or any service provider - down to a 1-star review is poor customer service.  In this case, the staff was rude to me and my three friends.  When we brought this to the attention of the manager/chef, she appeared more interested in being right than by doing right (by the customer).  It was an odd interaction overall and left me with a bad taste in my mouth.  

I'd like to give the staff the benefit of the doubt (maybe they were having an off day?), but there are too many high quality restaurants in NY for me to consider going back to Via Carota.

I really enjoyed everything about this place. I came here, first time, and was not disappointed. I came in hating cabbage on all levels and walked out looking forward to the next time. I come here as often as I can! Their daily dinner specials are a great selection, from seafood to red meat.

Definitely order the pulpe and chicken. And for dessert don't forget to ask for the semi freddo (my spelling might be off?)

Great food. Fresh ingredients with creative twists in each dish. Then why two stars? - the food we didn't finish we asked to have them to go. Two completely different dishes - tomato mozzarella and chicken liver. One hot and one cold dish - were packed TOGETHER IN ONE TO GO TINY BOX. WHO DOES THAT??? Completely ruined the dish and the experience. I hope the manager would see this and either fire the waiter who packed our dishes ( also handed to us in the middle of the meal) or train him again.
Absolutely loved our lunch at here. Every dish that came out was amazing, including the charred peaches that closed the meal. Our waitress was great as well. Great place!

Upgrading my rating of Via Carota after giving them a second chance. This time around, everything we ordered was really delicious:
-grilled artchikes
-fried zucchini
-mixed seafood (was a special that night)
-salame & pecorino
-polipo (oustanding)

The staff was SO RUDE. I went for lunch on a Friday, it was not particularly busy. Maybe 4 tables were full. I arrived with 8% battery on my phone and my charger in hand. I approached the bar to ask the bartender for a plug and she just said "we don't have any" to which I responded by asking if it would be ok for me to plug on the wall. No smile, no help at all, just a perennial snobby attitude. She just said, sure, if you can find one. So I started looking around for a plug and was approached by a waitress who instead of asking, "Can I help you?" asked, "What are you doing?" so I explained that I was looking for a plug and she said... "Oh... we don't do phone charging here" to which I shockingly said, "what?" and she responded by saying, "Yeah, we don't charge phones. Period. You can't use our plugs." 

Shocked, I went back to my table and ate quite annoyed by the strange policy. The food was fine, nothing spectacular. I had the capresse special which was great and the carciofi with orange and parmesan which had WAY TOO MUCH parmesan. We shared the mushrooms with smoked cheese and she had the octopus. By the end of the meal my friend and I left and had to go buy a diet coke because the aftertaste of the food was pure oil. We felt so heavy and garlicky and particularly oily... That I don't expect we'll be returning. Oh and the bill was $100, no drinks.

Expensive, small servings. The cooking was overwrought. I had the gnocchi which was overcooked, too soft and too rich. The anchovy and dandelion salad was too salty. I appreciate the effort but perhaps they are trying too hard.

I was a little disappointed with my meal here, though think I may just have been a little unlucky with what I ordered.  The place itself was cute, and both the red and white wine I tried, were good, as was the artichoke appetiser.  But I wasn't impressed with the two larger plates we split: the grilled octopus had an unusual consistency, reminding me more of chicken or a white fish than the usual squeaky cephalopod (things with tentacles!) meat I am used to. Not sure if this to do with the particular animal or the way they prepared it, but I wasn't a fan.  Now my girlfriend reckoned it was because it was so fresh, in which case I prefer my octopus on the stale side. That said, while I thought the meat lacked flavour, the olive pesto dip it came with was excellent.  

We finished with fried rabbit, which came highly recommended but wasn't what I was expecting. I had imagined it would be pan fried, but was served deep fried and battered, a la bunny McNugget. Not my kind of food.  Though the little piece of egg fried breaded it was served on top of was a delight.   An excellent espresso to end.

I don't suppose I will go back, but if I did then some of the smaller plates sounded good and might be more to my taste.

Two friends and I went early to Via Carota in hopes of securing a table with less than a two- hour wait.  The first of us arrived at 6:15 and put our name in for a table.  Within 20 minutes, all of us had arrived.  Fortunately, we were able to secure seats at the bar.  15 minutes later, or so, the hostess told us it would take another 20 minutes for us to get a table.  She offered us the opportunity to eat at the bar, or to continue to drink there with the understanding that if someone wanted to have dinner at the bar we would have to relinquish our seats.  The no- reservation policy is behind such rudeness, but blackmailing the customer over a bar seat is really going too far.  Some restaurants are set up to have diners at the bar; that is, they have real seats with backs.  Via Carota's bar seats are stools meant for drinkers.

Feeling as if we had little choice, we settled for eating at the bar.  It meant, of course, that the growing hordes waiting for tables were continually reaching over us to order drinks, to ask for the wine list, or simply to talk to a waiter or bartender at the bar. 

Towards the end of the meal, I got up to go to the rest room.  My two companions, deep in conversation, paid little attention.  I was gone no more than five minutes, but when I returned I found that my bar seat had been given away.  Needless to say, we caused something of a scene.  The "manager" came over to sort things out, but she was unable to do anything more than to refer to the four points of dealing with angry customers she had been taught in her manager-training session.  A deeply felt, sincere apology for the bad treatment was all we needed, but Via Carota's management could not muster such a response.  

No-reservation policies assure restaurants that they will never have an empty table, but they come at the expense of the customers.  Giving away my seat because I dared to get up to go to the rest room is the logical extension of such policies.

Yes, the food is good, but it is not worth the bad treatment from the restaurant staff.  There are plenty of Village places that serve comparable food and still know how to be polite to the people paying the check.

Via Carota.  It's been almost a year since it first joined our little neighborhood. And yet, it seems like it's been here always. Dining at the bar offers a different experience than at a table. Alone and making new friends, or sitting with old ones, it is a relaxed experience.  The tables, whether in the middle of the room or along the windows, remarkably allow for a more intimate experience in public.

The wines and cocktails are expertly tended. The food is as marvelous as the staff describes. The svizzerina -- don't call it a burger -- is the way chopped meat should be: unadorned, the focus on the meat and not on anything else. Try the chilled vittello, with tuna sauce in the summer or with apples and parmigiano now. The entirety of the menu follows one rule: simple, good food.  The chefs treat vegetable as meals themselves, making you wonder why children don't eat more of them. 

A root vegetable, a carrot's beauty may seem to be hidden from immediate sight. So too it might appear that way at Via Carota (carrot street) if you read Peter B's review. But the beauty of Via Carota is readily discernible. What a shame a cranky disrespectful patron failed to see it. You would have to have been there, as I and others were, to see how poorly he treated the staff and manager in order to truly put his review in its proper perspective. 

But no matter. Go see for yourself. The menu changes seasonally, so try the lentils, beets or maybe the namesake carrots. Have a grilled lemon chicken that all chickens aspire to become. And don't forget the svizzerina. Mangia.

Sister restaurant to Buvette.  No reservations accepted, wait was about 15 minutes for 4 on a Monday night. 

What we ordered: 

Stracchino E Promodorini Crostini - fresh cheese was delicious.  Great appetizer choice before the main meal.  

Funghi Verdure - Also great appetizer choice.  The mushrooms had a nice crisp, and ever so tasty with the cheese at the bottom.  Get this if you like mushrooms. 

Coniglio Fritto (fried rabbit, rosemary and garlic) - too salty for my taste.  This is one of the dishes Via Carota is known for.  I actually liked the bread and the crushed garlic it came with more than the rabbit itself. 

Via Carota Sivzzerina (chopped steak) -  another dish that has been written about and what Via Carota is known for.  Again, a bit rare for my taste - and our friends felt that it was almost under-seasoned and lacked flavor.  

Wild Boar Ragu Papardelle - The unanimous favorite out of all the meat dishes we ordered.  Pasta tasted fresh and ragu cooked to perfection.  The sauce was also very good.  

Semifreddo - memorable dessert, perfect amount for 4 people to share.  

Overall, I think this place is great for vegetarians since there are many options and the vegetarian dishes stood out to me more than the meat dishes.  I would also do tapas style if I were to come back.
Food is good but the service is one of the worst in the city. Rude waitresses and hostesses with huge attitude totally ruined this place.

My wife and I brought some friends here a few weeks ago and loved it. I got the gnocchi and my wife had the pumpkin ravioli and we had a bruchetta as an appetizer. The food, while in small portions, was incredible.  Our server, a tall gentleman with dark hair, who kind of resembled Gérard Butler, was really amazing. He told us about specials and deserts and was very kind about putting up with my chatty friends who kept interrupting.  I will be back again- no doubt about it.

Food is delicious, but you should really order family style. If you don't, you will spend an arm and a leg. 

Would be really nice if they could have high chairs for (well-behaved) small children.

excellent food. I love the fact that this is a small plates menu format. it allows you to try all the delicious things that come out of the kitchen. I've come here a few times and one of my favorite desserts is the chocolate semifreddo. the last time I came here it tasted more like a mouse and wasn't rich enough. other than that this place is consistently great.

Food was decent but service was terrible. No hostess. Never refilled our drinks even though we tried to order several rounds of drinks. The food was decent - the plates were small but the flavor was good. It's a good neighborhood spot for a casual dinner.

This was my first time in New York and my friends and I were originally planning on going elsewhere, but luckily ended up here. The atmosphere was cozy and the staff was very friendly. Today I had the special, potato ravioli with Bolognese. It was probably the best Bolognese I have ever had! It was delicious!! I would highly recommend on stopping by and trying this place out! I plead with the restaurant to add this item to their menu, it was that amazing! My friends also enjoyed their items. We ended with their chocolate and hazelnut mousse which was also delicious! Thank you for the great service and an amazing first stop for my first time in the city !!

Really cute space in the village. Perfect to come for morning coffee and a bite or a long dinner and wine with friends or on a date. The owner is also the chef so you see her in often. Very nice Italian woman. Just went in this weekend and really enjoyed their new Barbera wine. My server told me sometimes on busy nights they will open one of the giant bottles of wine behind the counter (4 or 5 liters) and have them as the house wine or a special pour for the evening. I hope to catch that one of these nights. 

Didn't have time to eat but what was coming out of the kitchen looked good. New specials each day based on what the owner finds at the market too.

For drinks, if you aren't into wine they have a pretty impressive bourbon and whiskey collection. Impressive not just for an Italian restaurant but also for a restaurant in general. All around a solid spot to make yourself a regular at or come to special. Can't wait to come back.

We ate here in October, so review is delayed. Food poisoning. Lukewarm bolognese sauce was the culprit. Although it was after 1pm on a busy Saturday, we seemed to be the first ones to order lunch/ The restaurant, overall, was not very appealing... menus were stained, space looked pretty tired and not very clean, bathrooms were very dirty. Several tables of super casually dressed clientele (sweats, PJs?) lingering over coffee and newspapers,  Drinks were sub-par. Very disappointing, to say the least.

Amazing lite Italian fare. Walked in for lunch on a Sat at 2:30 and got seated within 10 minutes. Noticed Mario Batali casually eating lunch in the corner and realized this was probably a good culinary choice. Proceeded to order tea and the black kale, cannelli beans with sausage, grilled artichokes, and mushrooms and were blown away by everything (shared 4 dishes with a friend). The waiter was attentive but not on top of us. Will be back for sure!!

This could be a really good restaurant . It isn't.  From the moment you walk in you realize this is not going to be fun. They don't take reservations , which is fine , but the attitude at the door is ridiculous and there is no real seating system in place.
They seated three of us at what was obviously a table for two, but they  put a stool at the table to make it a three top.
Yes, I did not get a chair , but a tiny wooden stool like the kind Gepetto sat on as he carved Pinocchio .
The table was also so small that when one of our party ordered a certain entree the  waiter said the plate it came on was probably too large to fit on the table. The food itself was fine, nothing spectacular and they tried to get you through your meal as quickly as possible . Taking away food before you were finished and giving you the bill before you asked for or wanted it.
This was not a fun dining experience , you were pissed by the time you left.
If they cut the number of tables by a third and treated people well it could be nice.
Maybe sit at the bar, but then you'd miss the magic of stool sitting.

We walked in late afternoon in the middle of the week. A late lunch. No wAit, and pleasant server. Fantastic  FOOD! We ate family style and tried several items. The shaved artichoke salad with orange zest was spectacular . The carpaccio excellent, grilled artichoke delicious, veg. Soup fresh, meatballs yummy!!! Zabaglione over berries for desert... Can't wait to go back! I'll avoid the busiest hrs to not wait . Although it's worth the wait!

Every course was delicious! Service was friendly and also prompt. Atmosphere was cozy. We has the tomato and cheese crostini, polpito, carrots with pistachio and yogurt, lemon risotto, and the poached pear. Everything was delicious and fantastic. My dining partner felt that there should have been more polpito than there was, but that was the only complaint. I would definitely go back.
I love this place for casual, reliable Italian food and wine. It's a fun atmosphere although it tends to get very crowded. They make a good negroni.

Lovely restaurant. The food was delicious, the atmosphere was lively and the decor rustic and classy. Took off a star bc I felt it was really overpriced, but for a splurge it was worth it. The serve mostly small plates so obviously we wanted to try a lot of options, all were quite tasty. The mushroom veggies dish, the crostini and pumpkin ravioli were my faves, couldn't get enough. The chicken dish was too salty (and I do like salt!) and the bean veggie dish was just ok. The desserts were very good as well, but w the Big Gay ice cream shop next door would rather of had that. The wait was really really long, about 60 -90min for a Friday night table for 3. Would go back for a special occasion for sure!

I'm definitely a fan!!! A friend and I have been wanting to try this place for a while but weren't not the no-rese, long wait kinda people.  So what did we do you ask? Walked in at 5:30 on a rainy Wednesday night, that's what! I literally was the 3rd person there so I grabbed a stool at the bar. I absolutely LOVE the atmosphere and decor...very West Village meets adorable trattoria in Rome. The bartender was completely awesome, I was deciding between a Negroni and a Manhattan and I told him to chose, turns out that was a smart decision because he handed me a perfect Manhattan. I waited for my friend to join as I was a bit early and by 6:30 the place was packed with people waiting behind our bar stools for a table. We decided to eat at the bar which was the right decision, the tables for 2 are quite small. We were presented with a few thick slices of bread drizzled with excellent olive oil to start. From there,we had a hard time deciding because everything on the menu looked GREAT. Apparently we were over ordering and I appreciated the fact that the bartendress mentioned that. We ordered the olive all' ascolana, fried green olives with pork sausage which were amazing. We then ordered the salume e pecorino which was also very good but this was the only dish that was a bit on the small size. We then ordered the pappardelle with wild boar ragu which was out of this world, super fresh pasta with just the right amount of saucey funk. We had to order the svizzerina because everyone talks about it. There was one problem with this, I like my meat rare and he likes it on the well done side. They really only cook this one way and that's crunchy on the outside and pretty rare in the middle. I think I was let down a touch after all the hype but I did have the remainder the next day and it was very tasty. We just went with a glass of wine each, the Chianti Classico for me and the Nero'D'Avola for him. I walked out of there completely full with a substantial doggie bag! The QPR at this place is right on..I highly recommend a visit.
This place is great!  Excellent food and service.  Great pasta, appetizers and entrees.  Also the atmosphere is terrific!

UPDATE 04/21/2017 Fri - Just as good as our previous visit. Me and the GF spent 140, with the Orata alla Griglia (20) as the star of the meal, with a generous orata filet over a bed of escarole with flecks of dried pepper and olive oil from the saute. We enjoyed the Vignarola (13), which was a springtime-on-a-plate mix of peas, fava beans, and artichoke. I enjoyed my Americano cocktail (13). My previous reviews remain accurate.

TIP: Expect waits unless you time your visit for early first seating or after second seating.
