SHOUT OUT - To the thoughtful hostess

UPDATE 06/03/2016 Fri - We were more comfortable this second visit. The food and drink were more delightful than the first visit. I tried a Boulevardier (14), which was dry and crisp, with balanced flavors, a triumph in light of Campari as a primary ingredient. The Nebbiolo by the glass and a small carafe (15, 23) was pleasant. The prices seemed down to earth for the quality, quantity, and creativity (especially compared to Hillstone on Park Ave So, ouch!). The crowds were loud. We were always able to hear each other at the bar. We also found our advice to ourselves to order four items instead of five. That was a full meal for us. Here's the deets:

Boulevardier, 14 - excellent
Sbagliato, 12 (listed as Bicicletta on the menu) - nice, but could seem sweet to some
Asparagi blanco, 16
Insalata fava, 17
Tagliatelle Prosciutto, 20 
Swordfish, 19
Nebbiolo, glass, 15
Nebbiolo, small carafe (250 cl), 23
TOTAL 136

BONUS - vegetable forward
SHOUT OUT - Taylor at the bar who served us, and the charming hostess, who remains nameless and memorable here

A charming space, very good service, and very good, creative food rise to 4 stars, even in light of medium-high prices and tight spaces for waiting and dining. There are delights to be had at Via Carota.

Deets (01/16/2016):
Prosecco, glass, 12
Americano, cocktail, 12
Salame e Pecorino, 10 - nice prosciutto and cheese; the salami is more of an individual taste IMHO
acciughe (anchovies), 10 - very good
Cavolo nero (black kale) salad, 13 - excellent
Carote (roasted carrots), 16 - worth it for amazing varietal carrots with an uncommon topping of lemon, pistachio, lemon, and yogurt
Orata alla Griglia (grilled orata), 19 - excellent
Coniglio fritto (fried rabbit), 20 - delicious and perfectly fried with a feather-weight crust
Frappato Planeta (red wine), bottle, 42 - good value
TOTAL, 154
We over-ordered for two. Three or four items should be good, instead of five.

TIP - I wouldn't go out of my way to go back because of the crowding unless I was going early or at an off-time
TIP - no reservations

Came for lunch on a Saturday afternoon.  Love the vibe here.  Similar vibe as their sister restaurant Buvette...  Portions are decent.  had the Kale with lardo to start.  I had veal carpaccio for my main and my husband had the chicken with lemon.  Both were delicious.  Great wine selection, great grappa selection.  I would definitely go back.

I was very excited to try Via Carota...it's my friend's favorite place and she has been raving about it for a year. What can I say, I trust her taste in food and wine but I'm just not as impressed as she is.

Love the look and vibe of the place...beautiful, expensive glassware, rustic wooden tables, warm lighting, lots of vintage touches...every detail is eclectic and thoughtful. They do not take reservations and do get exceptionally crowded, so make sure you factor in a long wait time.

Is the food worth the hassle of waiting for a table? Not really. Some of the food is mediocre, and some of it is quite good, but I certainly did not find it transcending.

The branzino was perfect...simply grilled with lemon...a highlight. It came with no side dishes and needed some, so keep in mind that's quite a bit of extra $. The crostinis...well, the bread was kind of burnt, not in a good way, and the toppings were a bit boring (egg salad, chopped liver?) Hated the funghi with scamorza...the cheese was overly smoked and rubbery and ridiculously salty.

Via Carota is a good choice for vegetarians, with lots of salad and veggie options. I liked the carrots, but it was not popular at our table...no one finished it. The Insalata Mista was simple and slightly boring but very fresh.

The pasta is made in-house and it is excellent, but the preparations don't always work. The pappardelle with wild boar ragu was delicious...everyone's favorite (though it was overly sauced.) The gnocchi was disappointing...the gnocchi itself was light and fluffy, but it was drowning in a gorgonzola sauce (more like soup) that was mostly heavy cream. The pasta carbonara was good but not as good as the one I make at home, and again, the chef had a too-heavy hand with the pancetta.

I would not go out of my way to go back, but if a friend wanted to go, I wouldn't resist. It's a nice room to hang out in and there are enough good dishes on the menu...you just have to know what to order.
This place deserves 5 stars - the food, ambiance and staff are amazing. This is a place I go to when I want a nice long dinner with great food to share.
The food here was very good. I ordered one of the specials (a pasta) and the rabbit. Both dishes were superb and service was great. I recommend anyone in the West Village to come and eat here.
Great meal in this cute west village spot. Valentines dinner without reservation and we were accommodated with a table within 30 minutes or less. Food was great. Def go back.

Via Carota shares a certain aesthetic with its french sister, Buvette. But where Buvette was overly crowded and pompous, Via Carota's open space and Italian fare make for a more pleasant dining experience.

I don't think I've ever been so let down by a restaurant before. People talk about this place as if it's heaven -- however the food is salty, not done properly and mediocre at best.

Every part of the meal tonight, from the octopus to the fried olives to the bacon wrapped hen was not good. The meal was dry and salty and timing of appetizers to entrees was off. Do not waste your time or money here, sadly you'll be let down (as we were) tonight.

This restaurant is incorrectly rated on Google and represented by it's reviews. Every dish we tried (kale, raviolis, steak, ribbon pasta) was sadly small, overpriced, over salted and over buttered.

If I had know this was an expensive Italian place serving  "tapas" sized portions ranging from $17 to $27 a plate, not entrees, I'd have been less disappointed. Expect to pay around $60 for a mixed and matched meal.

Ambiance: bright.

I just went for drinks with a friend. Wine was good and staff was really friendly and knowledgeable. They give you a wine taste even for a 'wine by the glass' order.
It became insanely busy around 8PM (we went for happy hour) and people could barely move. For a Thursday evening, with a chilling NY weather I was surprised. By the look of it, this restaurant is filled by locals, 45+ year olds. Will definitely come back for dinner!

Although the venue is two years in, Via Carota's space still feels like it was just built. One thing you come to expect from Jody Williams is her warm and inviting spaces with that lived in feeling of a familys' laughs, tears, and special moments permeating throughout its walls. You definitely can breathe it in at Buvette- just not quite yet here at Via Carota. I love the aquarium like windows- people watching is fun on Grove Street (an homage to Cafe Angelique). 

The wine list is beautiful- juicy, emotive, Italian. It is a great complement to the food. Try something new- you'll be happy you did.

The warm lentils with smoked trout is perfection. I'm still dreaming of this dish, and it has been a week since I have tasted it.

The funghi is magnificent- nutty, plump, succulent with a piercing sauce. The cheese is gorgeous underneath.

The wild boar tagliatelle was just ok. It's not the gaminess that got me, it just wasn't complete.

I can't wait to come back and try dessert and sit and watch these poor servers put orders in a computer that's hidden within a basket. When I saw that on our way out, I couldn't stop laughing at how absurd restaurants will go to try to hide the technology in their overall narrative. 

All in all, beautiful memories again made by Jody Williams' touch.

We will be back and ready for more!
Definitely one of my favorite go to restaurants. Food is always delectable and service is spot on. Especially Loved the prosecco cocktail drinks, ribolitta!! This place is always Good vibes....

A very cute Italian place I have been meaning to try - perhaps the trick to getting a table with no wait is coming on Easter Sunday at 5pm (when it was still quite full, mind you!). I love the design and decor of the place - it would be an equally good spot for a first date, a bite by yourself while you read, a catch-up with friends, or a big family dinner.

As far as food goes, I think I liked the vegetables better than the pasta, which is not usually the case! Boar ragu and homemade pasta was good, but a little dry. My mushroom ravioli was the best, but I could have used a few more! Definitely try all the vegetables - the grilled artichokes were sublime, the tuscan beans revelatory with sausage, and the broccolini delicious. I could have made a meal just out of the vegetables and skipped the pasta. Will also want to try dessert next time!

As a village resident for over 20 years,  I'm thrilled to have another superb addition to the neighborhood from two of my favorite chefs. Everything here is excellent,  especially the veggies. Brava, ladies,  brava!

The star goes to our excellent waiter but the food is mediocre at best , the steak is a hamburger with a lot of grease . The Burrata a mini acidity mix was laughable at $17 and the main dish came in a cereal bowl for $24
Check out the full review from Caleb Tripp and me: http://wp.me/p6Xylz-5v

It lives up to its hype being the sister restaurant of Buvette.  We ordered the Grilled Artichokes, Lemon Zest Risotto and Sautéed Branzino Special of the Day.  You can go wrong with anything on the menu. I'd come back to try more dishes!

go-to for cute delicious food and drinks. we keep coming back. try the campari spritz. ask for advice on the amaros after dinner. There are always tons of specials and everything is so good.
it can bit a little bit of a wait and the service can be a bit table-turning focused, but these are minor observations compared to how cute and tasty this place is.

Awesome brunch! Scrambled eggs, chicken livers and crispy pancetta... Never had that combo before but now I dream about it every night. The pasta was also delicious. I've been here a few times and never disappointed.

Way overpriced and tiny portions! As an Italian I can say that Italian food is not fancy and pasta should not cost more than $14 max. A disappointment for NYC. You are much better off at places like Otto!
Fantastic modern Italian! Consistently great, get the mushrooms and cheese and the fried rabbits. Great beer and cocktails while you wait for a table!

Just had maybe my 7th or more meal at Via Carota and every meal is as delicious and memorable as the last.  Jody Williams and Rita Sodi simply just knock it out of the park.  Love the format of the menu as it's all small plates which encourages sharing.  Start the meal of with one of the delicious crostini, my personal fav is the stracchino as it encompasses everything about this place.  The simplest dishes are highlighted to out-of-this world delicacies.  Just bread, cheese, sundries tomatoes and capers but so yummy.  Then move on to one of the salads and veggie options.  All great and rotated seasonally.  After, split a pasta - you literally cannot go wrong with any of them and finally end the meal with the branzino.  A friend of mine who isn't a fish lover, went back for thirds.  I really think that sums it up.  The berries and zabaglione is the perfect way to end the meal.  Again, the most simplest dished elevated to perfection.

Blunt bordering on rude from front staff. Long wait to be noticed and offered a drink while waiting. Water glass never filled despite neighboring table asking for and receiving water - you'd think they wd look over to see that the next table cd use a refill! Was never told the specials when seated. Had to ask a follow up question on why food order was so late. Was not offered dessert. Really slap-dash service.
Food was very good and will return to try a few more items. Grilled artichokes were lovely, strong char and lemony. Paired very well with the lemon risotto (which was a long wait coming). Go for the food, if you must.

My amazing GF lives in the west village, and we eat out a lot. I am a NY foodie who is consistently amazed by the wealth of quality restaurants in this neighborhood. And here is another. Via Carota is terrific, and it is not just about the tender, sliced double cut pork chop smothered in sauteed kale and lardo.The service and energy of the place stood out. It was a busy Saturday night, and we were greeted by Antoine. He was running the front of the house. He turned out to be our maitre d, our bartender and our server. He was efficient, knowledgeable and relaxed, and it made for a great experience. We noticed this same good energy seemed to permeate the entire restaurant, from the staff to the regulars. Happy we discovered another W. Village gem.

We came here on a Sat night with a couple of friends and the meal and service def met our expectations.  We only waited for about 15-20 minutes which was much quicker than expected, especially around 7:30-8pm on a Saturday night.  

From the menu, we especially loved the wild boar pasta, fried olives, but would highly recommend everything on the menu!  Definitely will come back!

This place has fantastic food if you know what is good on the menu. The ambience is pleasant and the portions are healthy for the price. However, it should be noted that the clientele seems like a combo of dressed-up bridge-and-tunnel and dull corporate types. The table next to us was an obnoxious group of wanna-be real housewives of New Jersey who were talking so loudly that it was difficult for my friend and me to have a conversation. Our waitress was very helpful and attentive, even though it was difficult to hear her given the deafening roar of the surrounding patrons
Via Carota is one of my neighborhood favorites. Amazing cocktails (particularly their Manhattans and Negronis), good food and an upbeat atmosphere.

Seating is very uncomfortable...
Service is horrible, servers are unorganized and clueless...
Food portions are unacceptable, a $17 pasta was presented in a small bowl (about 1 cup)
Had to inquire about food, server can't be bothered to give an update as to why food is taking so long, while people around us are being served when they were seated after us... Crazy.
Don't waste your time or $$$

Whats not to love here...staff amazing and always friendly...the freshest Burrata in town, and a killer Chicken livers, not to mention grilled Artichokes, fresh and buttery, with a little splash of their very own olive oil......i drink way too much wine here but thats probably because i love it so much !!!!.....Those 2 gals  are rocking the little triangle in the West Village- Buvette and I Sodi.....and now this ......can i eat anywhere else now please  ?

Arrived on a Friday night around 6 pm expecting to wait for a table but was pleasantly surprised. I was the first of our party to arrive so chilled out in the bar area with a delicious Negroni. Once our party arrived we were seated promptly. Service was friendly and efficient. Ambiance was nice and not terribly loud. 
We shared several items from the menu and standouts were the Wild Boar Pappardelle (absolutely delicious) chopped  steak, Crostini, Grilled Octopus and Burrata. Portions were ample. Several cocktails and a few bottles later and we were full and happy. Nice spot to enjoy a lovely dinner. Would definitely visit again.

Restaurants in Manhattan do not get better than this. Every dish on the menu is absolutely delicious. The staff are lovely, helpful and professional. The decor is stylish and simple. And the food, oh man the food !!! It's really amazing !!!So so fresh and tasty. No pretension. You genuinely feel spoiled at this restaurant. It attracts a great crowd. So excellent people watching. The wine menu rocks. And honestly the prices are fair. Large portions made for sharing. It's hands down my favorite NY restaurant. Run.

This might be one of my favorite restaurants in the city. I love the vibe. I love the food. I came here for the first time last summer and have probably been ten times since! They have incredible seasonal specials but one thing that they always have that I absolutely love is the svizzerina! I went a couple of weeks ago and had the carrots and they were heavenly.. Especially the purple ones!

8 of us had a fantastic birthday meal in the Wine Room 7.19.16, with Truly Exceptional Service!

Food was great as always, deserts were outstanding. 

Only complaint: when you are drinking $$$$ bottles of wine, please provide DECENT STEMWARE! Come on. I get what you are going for, but it hurts. You aren't serving martinis up in rocks glasses, so why do we have to drink Quinterelli in trattoria glasses ? 

Otherwise would have been 5 stars!

Just amazing, every single second. Kevin was our waiter and I think I'm in love with him now. I had the wild boar pasta, fried olives with sausage (HEAVEN), fava bean salad, Octopus, pickled figs with speck, and two desserts. Everything was perfection and I can't wait to go back.
Average to adequate for the price. Found my meal underwhelming, wouldn't return.

Great brunch spot with a diverse menu of Italian small plates and great wine selection.

I hope a can remember all the things we ate: tuna with olives, oil, chilis, and capers; green olives stuffed with sausage and fried; broccoli rabe with oil and garlic, salad with prosciutto, pasta with oil and clams, a bruschetta with sheep's cheese and cured ham, and white wine (roero aneis).

Very trendy atmosphere. Great service.

Would go back any time.
Horrible. They don't have anything. My pasta had old tomato sauce and they don't have non fat milk for coffee - who does that?!
Best date night spot. Wonderful, fresh food, ice cold martinis, lovely service. Sit at the marble bar with your loved one and forget about everything else.

Ate in the wine room last night. Food was even better than I had anticipated. Service was amazing both at bar and at table. Everyone knew what they were doing and talking about. Wine list needs a some tweaking. Some great stuff to drink but looking at it as a whole just needs a bit more care and though to curate something that matches up to this menus diversity

I had a really nice experience when I went to Via Carota-- I popped in around 7:00pm last Friday evening with two friends and we were seated at the bar right away. (The restaurant quickly filled up once we were seated, so we got there at the right time.) The bartender/waiter behind the bar was wonderful. He helped us navigate the food menu and pair our meal with drinks the entire time.

We started off with the olive all 'ascolana (fried green olives filled with sausage), the Burrata di Puglia (small), zucchini fritti (surprisingly light), and carciofi alla griglia (grilled artichokes with aoili). All of the starters were good-- particularly the grilled artichokes-- I don't even think they needed the aoli. 

For the entrees, we split a pasta special (which was excellent) and the chopped steak-- also extremely tasty. Chopped steak is never my first choice when getting steak-- it is essentially a glorified hamburger patty-- but the chopped steak here is 100% worth getting. It has a really nice, salty crust on the outside and a medium rare, delicious center.

For dessert we got the panna cotta (with olive oil) and a chocolate mousse dessert-- both were great. Overall, I had a great meal/experience at Via Carota and would go back for another meal.

The food here is wonderful. Shared several dishes with friends and all of them were delicious - fried zucchini, prosciutto and Parmesan, truffles and beef carpaccio, several pastas, pork, and branzino. Yum!! It is noisy so if you can get the small, semi private room go for it.

I finally actually had dinner here, which was mostly a good experience.  I had the Branzino special entree.  At $52 it was pricey but it was one of the best prepared Branzino's that I have ever had.  It was flavorful and moist as well as well filleted.  It's always annoying when you have to spend an inordinate of time picking around bones which was not the case this time around.

The wines were good, as always.

The damper on the experience was that the waiter made a big point of saying that the fish did not come with a side and suggested that we order an appetizer salad, so we did and it was underwhelming.

Low and behold, when the fish came it did have a side of kale and the server gave a coy apology for having been wrong, which I did not really buy.

Love this place, always great food. We had the soe k cabbage salad with Parmesan- such unique flavors and great taste, the papardelle with wild boar which is consistently excellent,  and the white. Wants, tomatoes and sausage which was satisfyingly filling. Great service too

Love the atmosphere, it was cool and chill. Food was expensive but I loved the taste. Small portions, quite expensive, typical NYC. Waiters were nice. They are definitely tourist friendly, they have a luggage rack in case you were travelling like I was...

Had dinner here last night and it exceeded my expectations! Roasted carrots with pistachios and yoghurt, grilled artichokes, pasta with proscuitto and peas and roasted branzino. Felt like i was back in firenze!

4.5 stars, but i rounded up to 5 because we had a great dining experience overall and the service was fantastic.  

Came here with a group of 5 on a Sunday night (They don't take reservations) and they gave us the communal table in the back (smart on their part because some in our party had been drinking for a few hours), which was private and fantastic.  A party of 3 joined us eventually and they were a pleasure to sit with. The service was spectacular and we very much enjoyed the food.  

We got a mix of cocktails and 2 bottles of wine and shared the following:
Fried olives.  I've never had them before, and thought they were fantastic.  The crispiness of the batter combined with the olive saltiness was a fabulous combination.
Burrata. Who doesn't like Burrata. It was creamy and served with some vegetables on the side (cucumbers, peppers, etc.). I wish it had come with regular tomatoes, but can't really complain since it tasted great.
Carciofi Crudi.  I've never had raw artichoke before and was very intrigued by the dish.  The flavors were great (very citrusy) and there was a nice crunch from the rawness of the artichoke. Could definitely taste the pecorino.
Polipo. Grilled Octopus was perfectly grilled and extremely flavorful. The green olive pesto was on point.
Cacio Pepe.  This was deliciously creamy and had fantastic pepper flavor. Must order.
Leeks.  These were cheesy and truly fantastic.  Another must order.
Risotto.  This was very fluffy and had also cheesy (you can tell we like cheese).
Meatballs.  I didn't actually get to try these but they looked delicious.
Ribeye steak special.  Cooked to a perfect medium rare, buttery and very well seasoned.
Carciofi Alla Griglia. We ordered the grilled artichoke as a side to the steak. It was cooked very well (charred ever so slightly).
Broccoletti.  Again a side to the steak.  I don't really like broccoli rabe, i find it to be quite bitter, but this was drenched in garlic, so that was good.
Chocolate mousse.  Came in a sundae cup and was pretty tasty 

My boyfriend could eat everything except the pasta, the fried olives and the meatballs, so they are definitely gluten free friendly!

It ended up being about $100 per person with tip, which for the amount of food and alcohol we got was pricey but reasonable.

This was a night with some interesting synchronisity. In the four-star film "No Reservations" (*not* the Anthony Bourdain show) starring Aaron Eckhart and Catherine Zeta-Jones--a film that I have an oddly clear memory of--there's a scene in which the luxury of truffles are discussed. As a young foodie, I took note. Fast forward maybe a decade and there I was at Via Carota--a restaurant that indeed does not take reservations--during truffle season. Fitting, no? In any case, though it took quite a while for us to get seated (to be expected at 8:30pm on a Friday night), our night here was lovely. Everything was solid at the very least, and the vibe was delightful.

As stated, we came at peak time. We decided that if that wait was under an hour, we'd wait it out. I'd say it was about 45 minutes. Though we were pretty starving by the time we were seated, our time waiting turned out to be quite pleasant. Nestled in one corner of the space are three small tables perfect for imbibing while you wait, and we managed to snag one. Otherwise we would've had to stand (thankfully there's enough space for that here). Because the service here is top-notch, we were checked on quite frequently, despite how busy the restaurant was at the time. 

Drink-wise, your best bet is probably wine. Wine pairs beautifully with Italian food (spoiler alert, I know) and they've got an impressive selection here. We decided to go with cocktails, though, because we late-night plans that demanded a certain level of alertness. As delicious as wine is, it's kind of a sedative. Though the cocktail menu here isn't particularly interesting, they do the classics very well. I had a Boulevardier and a dry martini and both were high-quality and delicious. Clearly made with great spirits. 

Once we did get seated, we were right in the thick of things. Central table amidst the bustle of the very well-ran operation that is Via Carota. Though this is an Italian place through and through, the menu here is a lot more varied than a lot of the Italian spots I've visited up to this point. Namely, there's a massive section dedicated solely to vegetables (grouped by price). In addition to their normal menu, Via Carota also has a number of specials, some of which are proteins meant to be split between two. Our eats, below: 

Brussels sprouts salad: A
This dish currently isn't on the online menu so unfortunately I can't give you too many details. Important note: we thought this was going to be a cooked Brussels spouts preparation, but it turned out to be a good-sized salad. Thankfully, it was still super yummy. It was paired with a soft cheese, walnuts, either apple/pear, and a few other things. Fresh and flavorful.

Polipo (grilled octopus & green olive pesto): B+
Looks can be deceiving. Okay, maybe that's too harsh, but octopus happens to be one of my favorite foods, and my standards are high. This dish wasn't bad, but I'd still say somewhat discouraging. The pesto was yummy (don't expect it to taste like normal pesto, though) but the octopus itself felt kind of boring. 

Funghi (mushrooms & smoked scamorza): A
Mushrooms happen to be another one of my favorite foods, though I'm far less particular with them than I am with octopus. These were stellar. Savory and flavorful. Whatever that cheese was underneath, I bow down to you. A total splurge, but who cares?

Pappardelle w/ wild boar ragu: A-/A
I hardly ever eat pasta, so this was a special treat. Very simple preparation but the boar meat was rich and totally delicious. The pasta preparations here are on the smaller side (which I think is typical for traditional Italian places), so consider that when making your entree/app choices. 

Special Beef Carpaccio/White Truffle dish: A-
Because white truffles are the most decadent of all truffles, this dish--appetizer-sized--was a healthy $32. I'm not sure it was quite worth *that* much, but it was still incredibly delicious. Served with some delicious shaved cheese as well (parmesan maybe?). A very well-rounded bite.

We just went there for my 65th birthday with a group of 11 people.If I could give them 10 stars i would!The ambiance is charming old world Italy and the staff is welcoming and friendly.Our waiter was beyond helpful in suggestions and explanations about the food choices.I think we probably ordered almost every salad and appetizer on the menu.Every plate was greeted with a chorus of ooohs and aahhs as we tasted each delicious selection. The plates  of lentils,artichokes,meat and cheese selections and vegetables were each more delicious than the last. We thought we were full until the entrees arrived.Dover sole ,perfectly cooked steak and the culinary masterpiece ,the white truffle pasta! If you try nothing else in this wonderful restaurant you must order this dish. . We were bursting and still ordered another plate of the truffle pasta our taste buds craved.A perfect meal. This will be our  new destination restaurant for family celebrations.Thank you Via Carota!
Absolutely beautiful flavors and excellent service. Let the waiter recommend you the specialites of the day.

dinner for 3 of us last night. the rating is driven by the excellent tasty food (especially the cacio e pepe) and the water/bus service (not the waiter). the overall rating is pushed down by:
- awful 1st seats offered--early dinner at apprx 545pm, were at a long empty table that holds apprx 8. however, the waiter sought to 'optimize' for 10 and thus offered us 2 seats plus a chair at the table end--where waitstaff passed all evening. had to negotiate--again, early, restrnt 1/3 empty, to get 3 real seats at this empty long table.
- waiter asked us to leave after tipping $41 on $167 (apprx 25%)!!!
(3 drinks, 2 apps, 3 pastas, 2 desserts), Having affirmed we were done eating (we were chatting after dessert), the Waiter Asked Us to LEAVE!!! "sorry, but we have people waiting....otherwise would love to have you stay longer...." This has never happened to us in eating out many years--high end, low end, etc. Yes, our meal passed 2 hours--but partly b/c the waiter covered several tables with a natural delay between sightings, and with only water glasses, it should be obvious we're not going to chat all night....
- at nearly $70 per person, this is not a cheap place, and such rudeness means we can't recommend this place to others...

My second visit and brought an old friend along. Had a wonderful meal of shared plates: our first plate was a daily special of noodles with carpaccio & olives, followed by shaved fennel with pecorino (a little too heavy on the cheese) and the most perfectly cooked octopus I've ever tasted. And for dessert we had fresh persimmon and a unusual custard with bitter orange & olive oil. Both were superb. The staff was wonderfully attentive and the drinks well presented. So glad that all lived up to my recollection of dinner here a year ago.

Ate her last week  and the food is all excellent, really fresh and the service was perfect, attentive to the right degree.  Great wine list, we had the Cannonau, which is hard to find outside Sardinia, and was perfect with the food.

Diana, one of the hostesses, is truly amazing. Tonight, on a really busy Friday night, she took the time to  find a chair for my elderly mother to sit down for a few minutes, as she has gotten quite winded as we were walking to Hudson St and went inside to warm up for a few minutes. Diana was so sweet, brought my mom a glass of water, even though we were not even dining there tonight. Such kindness. We will pay it forward.

Ok I know this is crazy but the green salad is amazing I don't know what they do but it's so fresh and crisp and distinctive .. also if you don't drink alcohol the bartenders brew their own Ginger Ale that's so good ! No reservations get there early to avoid a wait

After all I read and heard about this place, I wound up being very disappointed. I feel that a big part of the problem was communication with our waiter. The food descriptions and portions were not adequately described, in order to help us make a proper meal. Instead we cobbled together a few things that didn't really add up. I won't bother coming back. I've been to many better Italian restaurants.

Very Good and at this point in time, probably one of the best Italian Eats in Greenwich Village .. My date and I started with Insalata Frutta di Mare (Seafood Salad), then moved on to the Cacio Pepe (Pasta with Pecorino Cheese & Pepper Sauce), then Scampi e Polenta, then dessert of Panna cotta. Everything was excellent including quite fine service . Nice atomosphere and reasonable moderate prices.
My favorite restaurant from now on. Every single dish we've tried (and we got A LOT) was spectacular. Rich, full of flavor, and simply prepared plates. Amazing!

This place is super good. We tried to find something in the city but then we decided to go south because we got a car and parking in the city is like super expensive so now we are super happy with this place and chewing our blood orange salads that is tasty enough!!

Some friends were in town visiting and one had found Via Carota on Instagram. We were walking the High Line pretty early so we got to the restaurant probably around 5:30-6pm, still pretty early for dinner in Manhattan. We didn't have a reservation, but the wait was ~30minutes for a group of four and we got a bottle of wine while we waited for the table. The ambiance is nice, and we also got lucky being at a larger table. There are some areas that looked a little cramped, but that can be seen in most restaurants around the city.

It is a sharing-style menu, which is great if you're with a group that likes to try different things. We tried a good amount of items on the menu.

To start - burrata, prosciutto, brussels sprouts, grilled artichokes, and the cod.
The burrata wasn't the best I've ever had, but was still delicious. Brussels sprouts came out looking like a salad, which we didn't expect but still enjoyed. The best was the cod - with the chickpeas and tomatoes it was extremely good!

Second round, we got 4 of the 5 pastas. I would rank them 1. Tortelli (MUST GET), 2. Tonnarelli, 3. Gnocchi, 4. Risotto. Beware with the risotto: it is EXTREMELY lemony. It would be better if you go that to share with either a meat or a fish and had it on the side. The tortelli was extremely good, and the table agreed that it was the best thing we ordered.

Definitely would recommend this place! If you go big and also get wine, it will be pricey. Still comparable to the restaurants in the area though. 

They also had rooms it looked like for larger parties.

Excellent! Had a religious experience drinking their real fresh squeezed orange juice and eating a bowl of cacio e pepe. Most places serve you "fresh squeezed" orange juice out of a jug or use tasteless oranges for juicing. These oranges were perfectly ripe. This place has a strong attention to detail. That is the most admirable quality a restaurant can have.

I come straight from Italy and ..The food is absolutely delicious. I did have some issues with condiments especially when it cam to the meats, but the tonnarelli, and the black truffle pasta was really good. They cooked it right enough without making it soggy as pasta is usually made here, and I really appreciated. The number one thing to try in my opinion is the scamorza with mushrooms, I'd go back and have that again no question. 

Had no wine that night, didn't feel like ti but they seemed to have a decent number of picks.

Did not like the tiramisu. Even one extra drop of liquor in it takes away the flavor of the whole dessert.
I order the octopus as appetizer and their special pasta for main course. Octopus was just perfect, high quality and very tender. The pasta was just ok, nothing else. A good place though.

So this restaurant came recommended to me by Mario Batali himself (well - truth be told - it came via a Tweet his posted to someone else about his favorite non-Mario restaurants in NYC). Thank you Mr. Batali. It came in handy after my son and I watched a play in Times Square. We were seated right away, and promptly given water and menus.

We asked our server for his favorites on the menu and his advice was spot on. He even allowed me to taste my wine before settling on my glass. We loved the two pasta dishes we had, the parpadelle with wild boar ragu and tonnarelli with cacio and pepe. Both so delicious. I wanted to lick the pasta bowl. I also had the grilled sea bream with escarole. Perfectly cooked fish. So tender and well-done. Escarole was a nice addition. Lovely flavor.

Tiramisu was nothing to write home about, but very nicely done dessert. Generous portion.

Incredible Italian dining in the West Village! I was heading to the Comedy Cellar and this was our dinner stop before hand, so we were definitely on the earlier side of the dinner crowd. At 5:30p on a Saturday we were seated right away, but not in the main dining room- there was a back room with a long table that we ended up sitting half and half with another family. A little funny, but the room was definitely more quiet and relaxing.
For apps we started with the Fried olives, Fried Atichoke, and the Insalate Verde. I was semi against ordering a plain salad at a place with as many great app options as this, but it ended up being the right choice. A delicious pile of Bibb lettuce, covered in a really clean dressing kicked off the meal well.
Entrees we ordered the Duck Ragu Parpadelle, the Cuttlefish, and the Octopus-all of which we walk out highly recommending. You can't go wrong, at least with what we ordered!
My favorite Italian in NYC at the moment. Had another great meal there last week with my brother. I've eaten there many times in the last year and it continues to impress.

4 on a Friday, 8ish, late winter, long wait
3 on a weekday, 730ish, late winter, moderate wait
4 on a Saturday, 6ish, late winter, beat rush by a nose, 20 minute wait

Delicious food in a pleasant setting, worth a little wait.

Food
Dense, punchy flavors from well crafted but not overwrought dishes.  Confident food that doesn't rely on gimmicks.  Most things hint at familiarity but aren't boring copies.  The heavy lifting is done by consistent execution and sturdy composition.  On subsequent meals, our choices were driven by wanting to taste something else on the menu rather than avoiding something we didn't like from the time before.  The size and range of options allow for flexible, accessible dining for eaters from picky to voracious, all seated together.

Atmosphere
Great light, nice decor.  Bustling but not frantic.  There's a pleasant energy and hum when you're seated.  Waiting is uncomfortable longing, even if you manage to get one of the tiny, cramped cocktail tables.

Service
Very nice and thorough, but there is a hint of table turning brusqueness and the food can come out fairly quickly.  I understand it but it's unfortunate.  The wait can be punishing and the door area loads up quickly.  Luckily, there's plenty of bars in the area.

Their no reservations policy and reasonable size make the experience feel fair.

If I could give half stars this would be a 4.5.  It is an incredible place. The waiter was really good, took his time going over the menu and answered all our questions with detailed explanations.

As an appetizer we had the carpaccio which was really good (and I don't like carpaccio at all).  As the main plate I had the beuschettas with skirt steak which were off the charts, it included french fries which were some of the best I've ever had.  I also tried the bolognesa gnocchis, and again, were very good.  For dessert had thw affogato which was amazing.

An extremely good restaurant and even Mario Batali was eating there that day.

I've lived in the neighborhood for over a year now, but hadn't heard about this spot until a friend suggested it and I am SO happy she did. We went with a group of 6 and were so impressed with the menu we decided to split multiple dishes and appetizers and actually wound up ordering a second round because we loved everything so much. Here's a quick breakdown of some of what we ordered.

The burrata is great, but isn't it always. Nothing too special compared the other Italian places in the neighborhood.

The insalada verde was recommended by our waiter as simple, yet delicious and he so so right. I believe it was a sherry shallot dressing and it was amazing, we wound up ordering a second.

The grilled artichoke was another waiter recommendation that was sweet, delicious and unique.

We had a branzino special that was not fishy at all and melt-on-your-fork good. So you can trust they know how to cook their fish here.

And now the pasta... the amazing, incredible pasta! We ordered the lemon risotto, ricotta tortelli and wild boar papardelle. All were delicious, but the tortelli was by far our favorite and possibly the best pasta I've ever had in the city. You MUST get this pasta.

Beyond the food, the setting is also great. Unique, yet rustic decor fits the food and the neighborhood. It's also a larger space than most Italian spots in the neighborhood with a sizable dining area, at least 2 private rooms, a bar and even communal seating. Also, not sure if this is a typical celebrity hotspot or I just came on the right now, but both Marisa Tomei and John Slattery were both dining here separately while I was there.

All in all, love this place, can't wait to go and would recommend to everyone.

Great atmosphere, good vibe and great foods. Just send one person first to get a table!! I went there 5:30 to wait for my colleague to come. Just after my colleague  arrives, there was so many crowds.
Very nice restaurant with fresh and good tasting Italian food. Service is also good. All in all nice but a little high priced for the village.

Sort of give this spot a 3.5, but going to give it a 4.  Sat at the bar and had some decent food. We had a nice seasonal salad with peas, which was pretty good. Had the fish, which was ok, enjoyable, but was a tad salty for my liking.  Had the home-made pecorino with parmesan cheese which was the highlight.

Service was great.

Honestly, I had high expectations from this place. A friend of mine (who has great taste in restaurants) told me that the Cacio e Pepe was as good as it is in Italy.

That said, while I did think the Cacio was great - as was the Tortelli and the Chicken, I felt like the veggies (asparagus verdi, roasted carrots, grilled artichokes) we ordered had way too much oil, and the insalata verde, while quite fresh, was overdressed, in my opinion. We also obviously got the burrata, which was very tasty!

Thankfully we got here at 5:45 on a Tuesday night - it got PACKED right after we arrived and got seated. Did I mention how loud it gets too? The sound definitely does not get absorbed.

All in all, I loved the space and the pasta dishes (wish they had more), but don't think I would rush back. Would rate 3.5 if I could.

I heard SUCH good things about this place & was so excited to go. The food is amazing (prices are high, but the food is truly great). However, our waitress was so unpleasant and made me feel so uncomfortable. We were rushed & shoved into a table the size of a side-table with 2 chairs & a tiny stool. 

She mocked me & was rude when I was asking for potatoes ("those aren't on our menu" and proceeded to point to the menu) as well as describing their vegetables. She was appalled I asked for crispy vegetables - "we have some grilled vegetables - those are the vegetables that say grilled next to it." 

There are plenty of places in this city with GREAT food. No need to be treated this way. I'd recommend Gemma or Galli if you want an all-around great experience.
An amazing place with great food, great atmosphere and amazing pasta.  Service is also top notch.  I will return.

Quoted "a little over an hour" for a wait. It has now been 2 hours. When we asked about their wait system (names on a chalkboard, where ours wiped off probably because someone leaned up against it) we were told, "well it works for us," by the waitress.
Love it. Best food ever. They have outdoor seats which is the best. Good drinks good food what else I can ask. Highly recommend

The service is abysmal. They told us we would wait 5 minutes and we were the next table. An hour and half later we are still waiting........ no table in site....Incredibly frustrating and we will not be back.

Best service I've had in a long time. The hostess was so friendly and greeted us in such a warm way after we came back (45 minute wait at 7:30 pm on a friday night). Our server for the outside seating area was so energetic and welcoming and explained everything well and checked in on us often even though she was super busy. The food was some of the best italian I've ever had in my life. The cacio e pepe is their signature pasta for a reason. It's so simple, yet incredibly rich and flavorful. This dish is good for sharing because it's HEAVY and I could not finish it all by myself. M ordered pappardelle w/ wild boar ragu which was also heavy on the sauce side, which I loved. The pasta was all cooked just right. Everything was a tad on the salty side since I was drinking a LOT of water after I got home. We didn't get to sample from their extensive wine list since we already drank at a different spot while waiting for a table here, but we will definitely be back!

Amazing dinner and experience. Everything was delicious, specially the artichoke. Great place for vegetarians too. Why a 4 then? Although great, I just found it a bit too pricey, same thing it will put me off from coming back again.

After a nice concert, my wife and I stumbled into this well decorated place. At first the attention was great, the appetizers were delicious but the waiter became less helpful and friendly. We order a pasta and a main course that it wasn't to our liking. The waiter (French guy) never came by to ask if the food was great, never offered if we wanted coffee or dessert but I guess it was late and he probably wanted to go home. The prices were high for the amount of food that they served. I wouldn't go back to this place.

I had walked past Via Carota multiple times before trying it for the first time last weekend. I was a little biased, assuming it would be a generic Italian eatery (mostly because of how oddly large the space is amidst tinier, more intimate restaurants in the neighborhood), but am happy to say I was wrong.

It was justifiably busy on a Friday night, but nothing felt rowdy or uncomfortable. If anything, I felt like I was joining a large dinner party hosted by a friend of a friend. The staff is friendly without being overbearing and you feel you're in the company of the warmest New Yorkers you possibly could be.

If that's not enough to persuade you to try Via Carota, the food most certainly should be. The grilled sea bream is the best fish dish I've had in New York. It's the simplest way you can enjoy fish--olive oil, lemon, and salt--and therefore the most respectful of the ingredient; it brought me back home.

There's something very special about restaurants that can make you feel things and Via Carota is one of them. Its beauty lies in its simplicity and effortlessness, both exhuding poignancy.

Best new Italian in the neighborhood - surprisingly accommodating to locals who show up with no reservation. Outstanding homemade pastas. Great for vegetarians- quite a selection of seasonal veggie dishes. The restaurant has a festive vibe, great for celebrating.

Can't figure this place out... have been there probably 10 times now and the food is always incredible. The cacio pepe is my go to. However, the service is consistently lackluster. One particular experience involved a manager giving away our table of 6 to friends of hers that came in after we waited for nearly two hours and drank by the bar. Last night's dinner consisted of unfriendly service from a waitress and quite frankly, an I don't give a $hit about you attitude. We kept having to wave her down for drinks, bread, etc. Our meals came on top of our appetizers which really bums me out at a place like that. No one came to clear our appetizer serving plates or offer to bring new plates. 
The whole night was just a mess with the exception of our friendly water boy and the man who brought us our drinks from the bar. 
So conflicted about this place!

What i love the most is that this classy upscale great quality italian restaurant is open until midnight or so. My friend and I walked in around 10:30. It was still packed at this time and we had to wait about 20 minutes which was fine! 

Absolutely delicious!!!! The only thing that I didn't quite enjoy was this anchovy salad cold dish. It was just way too many vegetables and extra food on the plate. The anchovy dip or dressing was really salty but quite good as it contrasted against the raw carrots and radishes.

The service was unbelievable as well - the waiter suggested a great wine to pair with our pasta.

A lovely restaurant and by that I mean you almost forget NYC and think "I am eating somewhere in southern Italy." This is a no reservations spot and it can be loud in there, I wish they'd put in some dampening effects but the food is so good, in a restaurant run by the chefs at Buvette and I Sodi who work ensemble here. This is casual Italian with focus on green market and it's inventive in a quiet and homey fashion. The food is modest, very fresh and packs a lot of surprises for what sometimes feels like comfort food with a twist. We have been a few times, and the corn succotash, served with fresh snap sugar peas and a few heirloom tomatoes is one of the finest appetizers/mini vegetable starters I've had. We tried the watermelon with sheep curd and it was unusual, fresh and outstanding. We started with a pork fritter, the pork wrapped with rice and deep fried. I don't know if this is Italian but it's a surprise and delicious. We tried two pastas --the cacio e pepe and the wild boar ragu--and have not eaten the mains yet as we like the vegetable list and the appetizers so much that we usually just order those. We had very good service. The ragu was the only dish I didn't like that much as the sauce was too dry and it was June,perhaps the wrong month. The first night we got into a discussion of the whites, an Arneis vs a Verdicchio and the waitress, Italian, brought us glasses of each along with another white. And then she poured us each a whole glass and said she'd be back to fill our carafe! Absolutely lovely place. If only it were a bit more muffled. We sat next to two couples who thought they were at a football game and they seemed to be cheering each other on to shout more loudly than they already were. The restaurant is open till 12 weeknights and till 1 on Saturday so this is the perfect place after a movie to just come and eat a little and drink and pretend it's Rome.

Quite frankly one of the most overrated Italian restaurants in New York. Essentially the reason you are paying $17 for a plate of four artichoke hearts is to say that you have been to a sceney West Village restaurant. The pasta is FINE, but not worth waiting an hour for - the cacio e pepe is smothered is grease and not given the generous amount of pepper that it deserves. The papparadelle is fine, but the portion size is laughable.

Heard this was related to Buvette and so we went. It was okay. More touristy. Bigger, some items displayed on a cart. The pasta was fine but not stand out. And the bread was soaked in olive oil. It's pretty pricey for what you get. The stand out menu item was the carrots and peaches and cream for dessert. That's only thing I would come back here for.

I really wanted to like this place, but the food was lackluster at best.  The fried olive and sausage appetizer was unique, but had an odd smell that took away from the dish.  The grilled artichokes were the best part of the meal.

The cacio e pepe had way too much pepper for my taste, and I didn't really get a good sense of the cheese flavor.  

My wife had the pappardelle, but there was too much wild boar in the sauce.  

You could tell the pasta was homemade, but the sauces don't do them any justice.

The friendly service helped make the meal, but overall it was over-priced for what was offered.

So freakin' solid. You know how in sitcoms or movies everyone has their go to place? This should be that place for everyone. It's so right and always on point. The carrots with yogurt, honey and pistachios are just heavenly and their salad with peas and prosciutto... omg don't even get me started! So crunchy, so ample, so fresh, so delish, and so not sharing! Their tagliatelle was everyone's favorite with again, ample amounts of meat to make a smaller, but hearty dish. 

Also, such a great place to people watch. They have outdoor seating and also large glass windows for you to look out into the streets and souls of nyc. Everything across the board, from people to food, was so good and I can't wait to try everything on the menu.

We started off with the Proscuiotto di Parma and for the main dish had the pappardelle with wild boar. DELICIOSO. The ingredients were so fresh! The service on the other hand wasn't the greatest. Our server was a little out of it, took her 10 mins to come greet us, then another 10 to come back and tell us the specials, and another 10 to take our orders.

Read so many good things about this place that I really wanted to try it out. Had been once before, for lunch and had an ok time. I was -not- greeted by someone that looked like a very lost manager and the server -whatever she was- was very rude and I had the impression that she just wanted to walk me out. I asked her for how long was the wait but instead she turned her back on me, when I asked again, she said probably about 45 minutes for the bar -which by the way was half empty- hmmm... very disappointing! Especially knowing how important the service it in New York! 
See you never?

Like flying coach but with good food. Via Carota's vegetable plates were delicious with fresh ingredients even though they were a bit heavy on the olive oil for my taste. The entrees were less uniformly successful. But the restaurant was cramped and inhospitable and it brought out the worse in my fellow New Yorkers.

Ate brunch there on Sunday.  The service was terrible, I had to ask for milk for my coffee twice and both times the staff were indifferent.  I had the steak and eggs.  It came on a very small plate and the steak was small pieces of meat over soggy tomatoes.  I live in neighborhood.  Will never step foot back in that place.

Well, this was certainly the highlight of our NYC dining experience this go around!  Service was 5 stars-super friendly and helpful!  The food - Mamma Mia my grandmother would be proud!  We enjoyed the Burrata $17- A-MAZ-ING!!!  The Piselli was to die for and so different$17.  Wine selection truly an experience with selections I've never seen at other establishments.  The cocktails were a mixologist's work of art.  We were full, but the server had our mouth watering over the Panna Cotta, which I'd recommend, so save some room!  The best part about our experience is that we felt like a native dining here- it's a local gem and very low key with something for everyone.  I wouldn't recommend bringing kids, unless you dine early, because this is an adult only crowd.
Wait wasn't too bad but the service and food was garbage. Just another basic Italian spot in the west village.

I am a big rustic italian fan and was excited to try this new entrant into the category.  Had dinner here recently.  Many very good aspects of this new place.   The prosciutto melon was wonderful - fresh and balanced.  The pea salad was crisp and tasty but had a bit too much dressing for me - would order it with dressing on the side in the future.  There were many tempting pastas but we decided on the ragu - while the housemade pasta was right on the ragu was overcooked and tough - i would recommend against this dish because of that - a bit suprising for a place aspiring to top status.   The grilled orata was grilled very well and tasty but again a bit too much olive oil on top.

Would like to try again.  But if it wants to enter true top shelf status - i would hope it corrects some of the oversaucing/dressing and the ragu issue.
The Baccala was amazing with chickpea and tomato. I would eat that every day if I could. It was a standout dish. Highly recommended.

Long wait, but worth it. Came here with two friends on a Friday night around 6:30p. Communal table (which looked a bit cramped) was available immediately, but we chose to wait for our own table. The wait was about an hour and a half, but we ran across the street to Amelie to catch their amazing happy hour in the meantime. 

The ambiance is classy and somewhat rustic. Portion sizes are somewhat small, but the food is delicious. 

Apps: We started with the burrata which comes with fresh tomatoes (but no bread) and our only gripe was that it was so good, we wish we had more. 

Entrees: Cacio e pepe is a must order! It was simple but perfect and reminded us of authentic dishes served in Italy. Basil pesto pasta was flavorful, and the Sicilian meatballs were soft and filling. Everything we ordered tasted very fresh and homemade.  

Would go back!

Service was spot on and so was the fish. But at $60 for a full Branzino fish, I don't expect any different. The server was delightful and took utmost care.

I loved the experience here and would go again for sure. 

The one thing they could fix is maybe make some more space in their outdoor seating. We sta outside since there was no place inside. The tables are too tiny to hold 2 people's food even.

We were denied entry due to alcohol intolerance. I would advise people to not visit this establishment if they have consumed any level of alcohol prior to visiting. As they are not tolerant of casual conversation or lively behavior. 

I have had other kind experiences at said establishment but given current circumstances I do not feel this is a good place to visit for larger groups. To be respectful of everyone, I'd suggest not coming here as a group. Perhaps attend solo or as part of an Alcoholics Anonymous group!

Great! We had a great meal, very sophisticated food but simple and rustic at the same time. We had a fava bean green salad, pasta with crab meat (my fave of our dishes), a fantastic Dover sole, and a fennel salad. Everything was prepared well and we enjoyed the vibe also. Great service!

We arrived just prior to 6pm and easily got a table but it got packed as we ate. I'd arrive early.

Side note - The village I grew up going to my whole life is no longer recognizable, that aspect I'd give one star.
Abosultely excellent food. Nice vibe. The menu is fresh and the food we ordered I cannot fault.
Deafening noise, uncomfortably crowded, rickety tables, food good but quite expensive for simple preparations and small portions.

Sometimes one wants a plate of pasta and a glass of wine, alone, before returning home. And if one is lucky, a certain "Kevin M" will seat him in a secluded corner and give him just the hospitality that he needs. One returns home grateful for excellent food and a perfect welcome.
Amazing food and drinks. Their cappuccino is the best we have had in NYC, will definitely be coming back!

AVOID. Hostess told us one hour. After 2 hours of waiting we finally gave up. And whenever we requested updates from the hostess during that period, she'd say sarcastically "if you don't want to wait feel free to leave". Absurd. Half of the people who were also waiting ultimately gave up as well. The most poorly managed restaurant in NYC right now.

Via Carota has always been among my favorite restaurants in the city. I live in the neighborhood and would take my friends and family here whenever they visited. However, after my most recent experience I will NOT be returning. This restaurant doesn't take reservations, despite being incredibly popular. Tonight, my party of 3 was told 1 hour. We waited for 1 hour and 50 minutes at which point when we asked about when we would be seated, we were told that we were free to leave the restaurant. The staff was incredibly RUDE with no regard for those waiting well over the time they were told. After waiting two hours, we left -- despite waiting for what I knew to be delicious food -- due to the extreme rudeness of the staff. While I understand that Via Carota cannot rush people through their meals, it is abundantly clear that their system has failed - and not only should they consider taking reservations on weekend nights, but the staff needs to check their attitude.
Wonderful place. The Negroni drinks are delish and seriously, they have the most beautiful ice cubes I've ever seen. The zucchini fries are wonderful to munch on. Everything we had was just great!

Via Carota is fast becoming a favorite for an informal meal by myself, with my wife, or with friends...

On the basis of five visits, Via Carota does justice to all parts of its not too limited menu.  The meats are generally good.  Here I must make special mention of the rabbit.  Fried to perfection, tender, and the taste and texture of the rabbit shines through.

On the seafood and fish corner, the sea bream would hold its own against some of NY's best in seafood.

Via Carota's biggest strength however is the greens section of the menu.  The tuscan beans, grilled mushrooms or artichokes are all cooked simply and taste as the respective dishes should.  The standout in the greens however is the Insalata Verde, which consists of layer after layer of leafy greens in vinaigrette sauce.  Too big to handle for one person - this in on my must order list if I'm with company.

Food aside, the vibe here is relatively calm.  Given the no reservation policy, it's best to come here in off-hours, or be prepared to wait for a long time.

Pricewise, it's not cheap, but then again it is much cheaper than I Sodi, and to me at least, the food is at least as good, and the setting more comfortable.

Great place on a nice day. The storefront has large windows which allow for the whole place to open up to the street. We had about an hour wait for 2 people when we got there around 6:30. They do not take reservation so it is one of those places you put your name down and go get drinks. (And we finished eating around 10 and there were still people waiting. Go early if you can)

It is a trendy spot with expected west village crowd. It was really nice day and the place was filled with great crowd. I enjoyed everything I ate. Did I think it was the absolute best Italian ever? It was good but not extraordinary. Overall, I would definitely go back if I am in the neighborhood and crave Italian

My friends had eaten here before (as well as at the two other restaurants with the same ownership) and that's why we chose this place for entertaining out-of-towners. The "no reservation" policy caused a lot of anxiety since we showed up on a sunny, mild Friday evening at 6:30 pm. Since we were a party of FIVE, we were seated quickly. We scored the large table to the left of the entrance, facing the windows. 

Noise level: Since there were no tables near us (entrance behind us shielded us as well as the windows directly in front), our table would logically be one of the quietest, right? Yet conversation was so difficult, I often had to stand up, walk to my friend, and repeat my remark. Any louder, and you'd have to file an environmental impact statement.

We ordered from the "specials," so I'm not sure of the prices -- and my friends were treating me. We ordered 2 appetizers for the table, 4 pasta courses, 5 entrees, two desserts, bottles of wine, and cappuccino for me  -- so we got to sample as we each consumed our own selections.

An appetizer with raw veggies and an anchovy puree was OK but completely unexceptional. And who puts those throw-away celery tops into the dish? We also received TWO (2) olives, which I thought was kind of skimpy for a party of 5. 

The pasta side orders were tasty. The gnocchi, served in an Alfredo sauce, were quite tiny but firm and, for me, a bit salty.

My friends enjoyed their pork medallions, which had a nice presentation.
My grilled tuna was delicious, served medium rare, and it a good size portion. However, it was served over highly salted baked beans. In the opinion of 5 individuals, these were the SALTIEST, eye-scrunchy baked beans ever. One former G.I. at the table said that C rations are more palatable.  Were the beans marinated in salt?  Holy moly!

The 2 desserts were very small but tasty -- with a nice presentation.
I didn't try the wine but my friends were happy with the 3 bottles of red they selected.

We were there from 6:30pm - 8:45pm. When we arrived and when we left, there was a never-ending stream of customers and a line outside.  We weren't planning to linger - - we were mindful of other patrons waiting to eat - - but it was a jolt when the bill was plopped on our table (unasked for) when the desserts and coffee came.  

This final gesture felt like the "bum's rush" and after we had just spent a few hundred dollars, it seemed like an ungracious.kick out the door.  Ouch.

Loud restaurants like this, where you have to pass hand-written notes to carry on a conversation -- or wish you had learned sign language --  are not my favorite environment when I'm trying to chat with friends I haven't seen for awhile.

The food, prices, presentation, ambiance and service at this restaurant are a winning combination. Our server was Nina. She was knowledgeable about wines, knew the menu well, attentive but not overbearing, absolutely great. Our food and wine was great, and Via Carota is an unbelievable value. This is one of my favorite restaurants in New York after our first visit, and I cannot wait to go back.
The standout dishes to us were the roasted carrots (no, really) and the pheasant and pancetta risotto.

Went here last week for dinner with two of my other gfs on a Friday night. We got there around 9pm and were told it was about 1.5 hours for a table. We were fine with that and put out names down and came back in an hour. While waiting for a table they asked if we wanted to sit outside and we declined since we wanted an inside table. We noticed a lot of other small tables opening up and some of them had three people sitting at them. We had to go ask the hostess if it was possible if we could sit at those tables since we didn't mind. She told us that one of us had to sit on a stool which we also didn't mind. If we didn't ask who knows how long we would have had to wait since it was already past 10:30pm by then. 

For food, it was okay. I don't remember exactly what we ordered but it was the octopus, which I do recommend, a pasta dish that wasn't that special and a dessert. When we were finishing up the dessert we had a friend come by that was going to join us after we were done with dinner, but since she wanted to sit they said they had to move us to a different table, again that was fine with us but where they moved us to was to a table by the entrance where we couldn't even face each other and had to sit in a straight line. We asked if we could get stools or chairs for the other side and they said it was against policy for that area. 

For the money and wait time, it wasn't worth it. The food was okay and I would have expected more in the service for a highly rated restaurant. I would only suggest this place for couples since they are very limited in seats. And to come very early if you're a large group since there's only 2-3 tables that can accommodate.

Food was pretty good. Nice outdoor seating. Probably good place for dates, albeit a little noisy.
recommended: grill artichokes, pappardelle ragu.
skip: brussel sprouts

I could eat myself into a coma here.... everything they make is decadent. Small pasta dishes with a punch! Flavorful and filling. Their dessert menu is out of control! Get at least 2 and try them all! 

However. If you're in a rush don't expect to make a reservation. But it's ok. They move quick.

Names written down at 6:30 for a party of 3. Told the host that the 3rd person would be arriving at 7pm, but we were not allowed to get drinks at the bar while we wait. Bar seating is for dinner only, so they said we could get a drink in the waiting area. We decided to go grab drinks somewhere else and come back. When we came back, and after a long wait the host asked if we wanted the bar which was open or a table. She pointed to a table inside that was on dessert, so we decided to wait. Finally got seated at 9pm, but we were brought OUTSIDE! No mention of what happened to the table inside, and the host did not even ask if this was okay. We sat outside just for me to smell smoke. I can't stand smoke, we just waited 2.5 hours for this! So we complained and got seated inside. Drinks were very pricy, food was alright, but salty and small portions. Decent food if you don't mind salt, but NOT worth the wait or price in my opinion. They don't need reservations because they are always packed, but I believe reservations would help with customer service. Other reviewers claimed they waited 3 hours, just isn't right and doesn't make sense, this place isn't amazing... Other places are just as good, cheaper, with less wait time and friendly service!

What a great place! We scored two seats at the bar around 8pm, which surprised us given the popularity of this restaurant. If you're showing up with more than 2 people then be prepared to wait given their no reservation policy. 

We started off our dinner with the grilled artichokes and Tuscan beans. The grilled artichokes were some of the best I've had, similar to the Maialino artichokes. The Tuscan bean is a hearty dish, served warm with sausage - good Fall dish. For our mains, we ordered the wild boar pappardele and the truffle pasta and shared a side of mushrooms. If I were to return, I would definitely order the mushrooms and grilled artichokes.

One area of improvement: they need to diversify their wines by the glass as the menu is rather limited.

We came here for a quick brunch on a rainy Sunday morning, and perhaps because of the weather, it was easy enough to get a seat by the window for two. Although there is a decent amount of space, the restaurant still has the feel of a cozy West Village restaurant. The design of the chairs are interesting to note, as the menus were rolled up and stored in the lower back support across the chair...not the usual place one would expect to find a menu. Service was a bit indifferent - plates put down and recited as though it were rote, and I didn't get a lot of sense of personality or interest from the waiters. The drink menu at brunch is pretty limited; while the wine selection is decent, neither the cocktail or beer selection are that inspiring.

The food was generally solid, but I wasn't really as impressed by it as I have been at other Italian spots, and overall the food came off on the heavier side. We shared the beans and sausage to start, and while I really enjoyed the rich tomato flavor of the sauce, the sausage was very generic in flavor while being chopped indiscriminately into smaller pieces, while the white beans were okay - but it made the dish very heavy for a starter. My wife went with the clam soup, which was prepared in a nice, light clam broth with white wine and garlic. However, the bread was toasted a bit too much, giving some parts of the broth a charred taste...not a good one for a clear, light broth like this. My tonnarelli, served as cacio e pepe, was quite delicious overall. The pasta was quite springy, and I enjoyed the texture quite a bit. It was a bit lighter on the pepper than I would have liked, though, with the generous amount of cheese sprinkled on top dominating the dish (and coagulating at the bottom of the bowl under all the pasta.

The food here isn't really much of a brunch at all - it's definitely geared towards a regular Italian-style meal - but it's generally solid with a nice ambiance, but it did not stick out as much given the plethora of options to sample from when it comes to Italian food in NYC. I might come back for a dinner meal to see if the experience sticks with me more than brunch did.

Just had a late lunch here today.  We sat at the bar and were waited on by a wonderful bartender/barista/server.  She was very friendly and her suggestions were spot-on!  We shared the amazing insalta verde and the delicious barrata di Puglia antipasti.  The Tonnarelli pasta was recommended so I went for that - it was fantastic!  My partner had the Rigatina (pork belly with cipollini onions) and he said it was great.  The Bloody Mary our server made for him was AWESOME!  With so many disappointing Bloody Marys to be had in this world, this one was top notch!  FANTASTIC LUNCH!!

Via Carota is large, extremely crowded Italian restaurant in the West Village. The service, wine and truffle dishes were excellent! The rest of the food was good to excellent. Wait time for 3 people was 1.5 hours. Parties of 2 are more easily and quickly seated. 

We went with friends for a truffle themed dinner. Via Carota has truffle themed-dishes during white truffle season (Sept- Nov). I was so excited to have delicious fragrant truffles in New York. The last time that I had truffles was 4 years ago. 

The night was very very cold. Most of us were underdressed and thankful for the waiting area by the bar (and away from the door). K got there first, then me and my friend. We got seated at a communal table in the back. The seats were perfect for a party of 3. My friend and I were so excited to try the dishes! 

We ordered: Black truffles with beef Carpaccio and cheese, sottobosco (sliced porcini, parmesan, and dried blueberries), stracci pasta with white truffles, wild boar pappardelle, fried rabbit, and funghi. We had a bottle of Sangiovese Bianco La Selva. 

The wine was crisp fruity and went well with most of the dishes. The black truffles were nutty, subtle and went well with the salty hard cheese and savory thinly-pounded-beef. 

The most amazing dish was the buttered thick stracci with the savory fragrant rich nutty white truffle. This was amazing and just as I remembered how delicious truffles tasted like. It was so decadent! And it blew all our taste buds away! My friend wanted two of these dishes! So did I! (But price is a limiting factor). 

The wild board papperdelle was moist and beautiful stewed chunks of meaty wild boar. The pasta was great. But after eating the white truffle dish, this dish could not compare. 

The sottobosco was a great break from the richness of the other dishes. I liked the sweetened blueberries but the dried porcini was raw. It was just sliced thin and topped with macerated olives, parmesan and blueberries. 

The fried rabbit was tender, juicy and served with fried fresh rosemary. It was such a unique way to eat rabbit! I really enjoyed this dish. 

The funghi was amazingly umami flavors of buttered seared chanterelles, hen of the woods, enoki, shitake and other mushrooms. This was so delicious with the seared cheese! 

The meal was so amazing and I really enjoyed the truffle dishes! I can't wait to return!

Great restaurant, food was divine. Long wait but food was worth it. Try one of the specials, can't be bad! Might even run into a few celebs like we did. Also, cute area, great decor, staff was really attentive , even as we waited we were constantly being attended to.

Castelvetrano olives are placed in the center of your table and neighboring New Yorkers sit, sipping on bubbly Aperol Spritz or Negroni's and twirling long strands of pasta on their forks... Even though its 1:30pm on a weekday. Why not? After all this is the sort of restaurant that makes you feel like your on vacation. 

Probably my new favorite restaurant in NYC. It checks all the boxes in terms of fabulous food, great atmosphere and lovely service. 

 A friend recommended it for lunch and I arrived on a cool fall day and there was hardly a wait. They do not take reservations and I hear that the wait can be very long for brunch and dinner. 

The menu is perfectly seasonal. The Verza salad reminds you of the cooler temperatures outside with zucca, speck, toasted farro and cabbage. Probably the best salad I've had this fall. I'll be trying to recreate this dish at home. 

Insalata verde was bright, huge and fresh with the most beautiful leafy greens in a light sherry vinaigrette. We were trying to keep it light so ordered the grilled octopus for a main. It was so tender with a green olive pesto. 

I was going to skip dessert but then thought, what the hell, and ordered the hazelnut semifreddo. Holy moly, this was out of this world! 

I cannot wait to return to this charming restaurant. This is the sort of restaurant that makes me wish I lived in NYC... if even for a a few weeks out of the year.
Great Service and Amazing Food. Food was very good. Roast carrots with yogurt and pistachios were excellent. Other dishes were excellent too. Amazing service, ambience, food...everything.

My friend and I went for dinner last night and it was a lovely experience! I got there around 6 to put our name in for a table and it was already packed. We were eventually seated at the bar which was fine because our bartender was really kind and attentive (and made us great cocktails too!). 

We ordered the fried olives, sardine special, wild boar pappardelle and the branzino special. Everything was really fantastic but the stand outs for us were the fried olives and the branzino. The olives were very unique, unlike anything I've had before and the branzino was impossibly delicate and fresh. But the absolute best part of the meal was the olive oil panna cotta with orange marmalade. Just stunning.
Try the artichoke dish, truffle pasta and generally speaking all pasta dishes are superb. They also have good chocolate flourless cake and the menus are actually all rolled up in your chair...

Whoa. Hands down best Italian food I have ever had in my life. My mom and I went in for some Italian food at about 10:15 p.m. following a show because a friend recommended it. My god. Everything was so delicious I wanted to cry. 

We started with the salad (insalata verde) and grilled artichoke (carciofi alla griglia). I don't even like artichokes but, dang it, I would eat 6 every single day of my life if this restaurant prepared them. The lettuce on the salad was so fresh it was unreal. The sherry vinaigrette is subtle but so so tasty! 

For our entree, we ordered the chicken and one of the specials they were offering: a DIVINE risotto topped with black truffles. You should know I have never used the word "divine" in a Yelp review before and it sounds kinda ridiculous but it's true. It had so much flavor. The chicken was so moist and delicious (dry chicken makes me crazy). 

If you're looking for a cozy, intimate Italian restaurant with the most amazing food you will ever eat, visit this place.

Just go. Go and enjoy the fried olives with sausage, the house made pasta pillows with beautiful, smoky ricotta with perfect caramelised shallots in an incredibly decadent brown butter sauce, along with a glass of red wine. Go. Do not hesitate, do not question. This place is sublime.

Came here with my boyfriend for dinner on a Thursday night and we were surprised at how busy it was. We showed up around 7pm and were told it'd be a 45 minutes wait, but they don't text you so you have to stand around and wait. After about 10-15 minutes the hostess came up and told us if we wanted to sit at the bar and eat they'd sit us now. Neither of us are picky so we decided that was fine. 

I ordered the tagliatelle and he ordered the pappardelle. You can tell by the menu that the food was authentic Italian, and it was no secret when the food came out. The pasta was cooked al dente which was perfect and the sauce was delicious. I could not finish the whole thing, and it was just as good the next morning for breakfast. 

The bartenders were very knowledgeable with the menu and were generous to offer suggestions.
