It's unfortunate that you can not make reservations, when they get very busy and they will not text when your table is ready since it's risky to show up. If we can come back with a short wait I definitely would.

Everything is totally overpriced. The food isn't that good. My pasta (with prosciutto and cream sauce) was very bland and I didn't even finish it. It also gave me a stomach ache for the next two hours. The Ragu was just ok. The waiter were very nice. I will not return to Via Carota.

Went here with my parents and a friend after a night out at the theater. The restaurant was packed when we arrived, but we were seated shortly thereafter. 

We were pretty hungry so we decided to split a few dishes:

Pappardelle (4 stars): This dish was very tasty and the pasta was cooked perfectly.

Tonnarelli (4 stars): I may have enjoyed this dish even more than the pappardelle--great flavor and pasta was also cooked perfectly.

Carote (4.5 stars): These may have been the most delicious carrots I've ever had. They were so tender and the accompanying yogurt sauce was a highlight.

Ribeye steak (4 stars): This was the special of the night and came at a cost of $60, but was well worth it as it was super flavorful and a huge portion as well.

Overall, this place was perfect for us to grab a late night bite in the Village. The food was tasty and reasonably priced and the service was top notch. Definitely a great Italian option in the area.
Came here for lunch on New Years Day. Very nice ambience and simple, rustic decoration. Great service and a healthy Italian menu. Prices are reasonable. Will definitely be back.

Came here on a Monday night at 7 and wait was about 20 min though they kept saying they would seat us "shortly" and that didn't happen. The service was very good and attentive. The food was mixed which is why I gave three stars. The bread was already covered in olive oil (though tasty) and the burrata appetizer and funghi with a cheese were very tasty. However, I found the pastas too greasy and not flavorful enough. As this is an Italian place, I was expecting pastas to be the highlight so took off two stars. The Cacio Pepe was cooked well and a big portion but the pepper flavor wasn't very strong and it definitely felt too greasy. The black truffle special was the same. Their semifreddo was good.

Ok, ok, I was stingy with my 4 star review of Via Carota the last time, so wanted to make it right......they must have canned that miserable server who made us feel so uncomfortable on that first visit.

We have been back at least 5 more times (always on a Sunday) and I have to say Via Carota has the best Italian food in the city.

Always fresh, seasonal and plentiful.
The servers have been consistently knowledgable and kind and we would go weekly if the wait wasn't so long!

I hope they will forgive me for giving them 4 stars.

;)

I was around the corner and thought to go to Via Carota for a warm, welcoming lunch on this snowy, wet day and that is just what I had. A wonderful Ribollita that was perfect and really hit the spot. They had a special of grilled sardines which were good, served on a bed of sauteed greens which were full of flavor and with a touch of spice. I look forward to going back for dinner!

Before I die, make sure my last meal is here. Definitely one of my favorite places in the city. Feels so authentic and I love how often the menu changes. I've never had something here that I did not LOVE. I think about the cacio e pepe often.

Trippa alla fiorentina: tripe, not my thing but my boyfriend loved it.

Tagliatelle: prosciutto was sooo good. Maybe I was just really hungry but this pasta was amazing!!

Funghi: grilled mushrooms and smoked scamorza literally the most amazing mushroom dish ever. 

This place is always packed and everything was amazing so it makes sense why. Service is impeccable, everyone was smiles even though it was busy and packed. I'd be here a lot more frequently if it wasn't so hard to get a table. Def come out of your way to dine here it's worth it.

Best Negroni. But i was very turned off by the burata.  How dare they call themselves Italian. The burata was ice cold. Burata needs to be room temperature.  My Italian grandfather from Tuscany is Rolling in his grave.  What a waste of money to eat cold burata.
Funghi, wild boar ragu and the chopped steak. Everything was good. The outside of the Chopped steak reminded me of Galouti Kebab if you have ever had some.

Best Italian in the city, one of my favorite restaurants. Always best to go early and leave your name for a table. Can't go wrong here. Great energy and amazing food and service. Cacio pepe, stuffed olives, pappardelle, calamari and fig bruschetta are stand outs

Celebrated my Brother's birthday here and everything was delicious. We shared the Pasta with Boar ragu, the Pork belly and the chopped steak which were all just incredible. The service was excellent and I loved the decor and their location.

Found this place by chance while walking around the neighborhood and it was fabulous!! Some of the most authentic Italian food I have ever had. Each dish was better than the lasts, and the service from the whole staff was excellent. We will definitely be back the next time we are in NYC.

Yummmmm. This place gets packed and doesn't take reservations - be prepared to come early or come by yourself or wait. The problem with the middle choice is that you don't get to try very many of the delicious-looking things on the menu. On the other hand, I got a seat at the bar at 7:30pm with no wait.

Based on previous reviews, I opted for the wild boar ragu papardelle. It was delicious (although I will admit I wanted a smidge more cheese). Pure comfort food, perfectly done. The guy next to me got the fried rabbit, which looked and smelled AMAZING. Definitely going to opt for the rabbit next time I go.

It was late afternoon and i was looking for a place to eat after an appointment in the area-I overheard two women talking and they said they just had had lunch at this great Italian place on Grove Street near Marie's Crisis. Finally, I stopped and asked them what the name of the place was and after they told me, I headed there for lunch. It is a large space with a bar in the center and tables radiating outward from there. The place was empty when I arrived and I was told to sit wherever I liked. I took a seat and looked at the menu. I got a glass of water and Italian bread arrived drizzled with EVOO. I decided on the cacio e pepe since I had not had it in a while and I really like it. It was excellent. The plate was filling but not overwhelming. The Italian bread, as always, was a wonderful complement. It was an excellent meal and Via Carota is a find in this neighborhood just off 7th Avenue on Grove. i would recommend and return.

The apps were among the best I have ever had. anything with funghi and polenta has my heart. Not being a meat eater the menu was a little difficult for me, but I expected it. I did have the fish bowl or something like that and it was fine but so small which was weird because friends that had pasta had heaping plates. Nice atmosphere. Expensive wine list. service was okay, not wonderful.

Finally made it here after passing by so many times! This is an adorable spot for dinner, and I had a really lovely time here this past weekend. 

My friend and I ordered the negroni and aperol spritz while we waited, and both drinks were tasty. For food, we had the branzino (OMG so good), the pappardelle with wild boar ragu, and the grilled artichoke with aioli. Everything was delicious, although the portions were definitely on the smaller side. I've heard really good things about the octopus so I would try that next time.

The service was on point - our server was super friendly and attentive. My only complaint is that they don't have a reservation system since there was a 1.5 hour wait on Saturday evening. However, Via Carota is well worth the wait! 

Overall, Via Carota has a lovely atmosphere, great drinks + food, and friendly service. I look forward to coming back very soon.
Wait situation is a mess and poorly organized. Good food but not worth it for the hassle.

The food is worth every penny. Thought out dishes with fresh and varietal ingredients, such as mushrooms and blueberries in one dish. 

Our waiter was great with explaining the dishes and was able to take our order without writing it down which was nice.

Downside is that you have to wait at leasthalf an hour to get a seat at night because they don't take reservations.
Great place, great staff, great music. Best Italian food in New York 'says an Italian'

One word, excellent!

Be sure to arrive here early. I think it gets very busy soon after 6 ( or even before). We were lucky we're party of 3 and was able to get seated right away once everyone was there. For party of 2, the wait was 1 hr 30 mins on a Thursday night around 6:30 PM.

The wait is well worth it, though. After indecisively hugging the menu for awhile, we decided to get 2 appetizers to share - Insalad and the grilled octopus. The salad really impressed me because I don't usualy like to order salad at a great restaurant. But here, it is done just perfectly with great simplicity. It was the perfect dish to start.

The grilled octopus was fantastic, very tender and well seasoned accompanied with the pesto.

The fried rabbit.. tasted like a more tender version of chicken. I personally may not order this because I kept picturing cute little bunnies but you do you!

The pappardelle with wild boar ragu was carb-y, meaty, and very satisfying.

The branzino special - very simple way of preparing the fish, with salt pepper, definitely some lemon to gice that acidic kick. 

Overall I think the food here is done very simple yet elegant and almost to perfection. You could probably order anything on the menu and not be disappointed. I will definitely come back to try their 19 ounce rib eye next time ( I could not stop staring at the table next to us who were feasting on the steak)!!

This is a no reservation, walk-in only restaurant so be prepared. Wait time is on average about 1.5-2 hours unless you come after 9pm or before 5pm. This isn't your typical spaghetti & meatballs/eggplant parm/ Brooklyn Italian kind of place. This is a LEGIT restaurant as if you're eating in Tuscany. If you want your pizza, huge, red sauce pasta plates and expecting free bread and butter as a starter, then get outtaaaa heaaaaa! Lol

Seriously though. This place is the real deal. Started with the Trippa alla Florentina (braised tripe). It was amazing. The best dish of the night for me. It's crazy soft and melts in your mouth. The tomato sauce is savory and somewhat tart and it's what makes the dish. We had the funghi mushrooms as well which was seasoned and cooked to perfection. My wife had the Pappardelle which was not gamey. Although the boar is lean, it's packed with flavor. Not much sauce though if you're a saucy person. I had the Tagliatelle which wasn't too rich. The prosciutto gives it that savory ness to the dish. Pasta dishes are big enough to share with another person. We ended with the Tiramisu which was pretty good. The cocoa was a little too rich and could've been more moist. The coffee bottom layer is really strong so it may keep you up at night. Not the best I've had but it was average.

One of my favorite meals to date with very little exception. A friend told us about this restaurant and was raving about it

We are there last night. They give you 2 hours for your meal. We ordered: Manhattan cocktail, tagliatelle and quinoa salad (excellent, bright and fresh!), steak tartare on toast (the best bite of the night for me), and the branzino (I did not like this fish very much)

The food was all good and definitely different from your average cuisine. They were really trying to be innovative. I enjoyed the bright flavors of the mushroom quinoa salad a lot and the steak tartare was so good I wanted to keep eating it. It was delicious. 

Their plates vary in size from micro tiny to "way too big in my opinion" branzino. The branzino was one dish I didn't enjoy much. I should have listened to the server when she told me it was a simple preparation and you really just taste the fish. I trusted Yelp over the server. The server was right. It was bland. The accompanying veggies were great and I filled up in them. The fish dish just wasn't my thing. 

I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone who wants to try something different.

Excellent; 
Atmosphere is great modern look , great place to meet up with friends for drinks and a bite 
Sorry no pictures ; food was too good to pick up the phone 
 Family style seating in certain sections - 
  It's like a typical loud Italian dinning room so don't expect to whisper . 

Cocktail Drinks; are awesome perfect they are strong yet balanced 

Servers : they are all attentive and work as a team  so the table are never left unattended.

Food : my favorite was everything 
   Grilled octopus was cooked perfect  
   Wild boar with pasta is a must , the amount given will fill you up  . 
Fried Spicy rice balls were delicious - they are made fresh - you can from the first bite

Love everything about this place. Super veg forward, light and delicate but filling portions. The salad is the perfect starter. Manages to be perfect for a date or a group dinner. Excited to come back for drinks and snack, and sit outside! (It's a big place but there's usually a wait on weekends)

This is a neighborhood gem. The food is consistently delicious and fresh. There are many options for people with all different dietary restrictions. The atmosphere is vibrant and also cozy. The staff is welcoming and warm. Can't recommend it enough!

Incredible food... if you can get in. Apparently my friend waltzed in at noon on a Saturday and was seated immediately. However, on a rainy Wednesday at 6pm, I waited 90 min. Granted there was some mix-up with a large graduation party, but still! Was it worth it? I'd say so, with the help of a few comped negronis (thanks to the same french-speaking friend). 

Once seated, the magic began. A beautiful plate of shaved white asparagus and parmesan (5/5), laced with sweet syrupy balsamic vinegar, rustic and simple and perfect. Then our 'nudja arancini (5/5) the size of kiwis arrived, perfectly fried, and gooey savory/funky in the center. You MUST order pasta - both the cacio e pepe (5/5) and the pappardelle (5/5) were the best that they could be. They appear in deceptively smallish-looking dishes, but they are deep bowls and that is a very good thing. They're some of the best bowls of pasta I've had. We ordered Orata alla griglia (4/5) as a lighter option. It was not as flaky as it could be, but fit the bill. A side of vignarola with fresh spring fava, peas, and artichokes (4/5) was a hearty seasonal vegetable dish, but I wish it had more brightness, perhaps more herbs/lemon? 

We finished with a traditional tiramisu (5/5), just boozy enough and nicely balanced so you don't leave feeling like you just split 7 things between 3 people. The negronis probably helped too (there are so many varieties, I loved the one with prosecco).

Service is efficient and quick, while managing to pace your meal nicely and never rushing. At Via Carota, you will be taken care of. 

Next time, I will be sure to order calamari with my first drink at the bar, it looked amazing. With a little luck maybe I'll even be able to get seated within 30 min. Even so, I quickly forgot any annoyances after the amazing food and warm service.

Excellent service with friendly warm servers. Ordered fritto misto for an appetizer which was perfectly fried and served with lemon aoli sauce. The cacio e pepe pasta was perfectly proportioned and the noodles al dente. I wish there was room for dessert !

Exquisite food, incredible ambiance!
My Opinion? WORTH A VISIT! 

Via Carota offers a fresh, colorful, and wide-ranging menu in a modern take on a street-side Italian cafe. I very strongly recommend the dish "Carote," cooked carrots in spiced yogurt and pistachios. The grilled octopus dish is also delicious, and is a great to share as an appetizer. Via Carote's dishes' ooze creativity and nuance. The restaurant's bar selection is very solid as well, with a variety of house cocktails and interesting brews on tap. 

In attesting to Via Carote's incredible dishes and fresh design, take a look at the pictures I attached to the review. 

A few side notes:
- No reservations, so arrive early and grab a drink before dinner
- Seating curbside is recommended, but is limited. Each table only fits two 
-A private farmhouse-styled room inside is great for large groups, but can't be reserved in advance. Arrive early to claim it!

Stopped in the restaurant to purchase a gift card for a Birthday. It has been some time since I dined here and almost forgot how cute it is. First of all, I love anything W Village, and this spot epitomizes exactly why. The space is romantic, yet relaxed and full of character. 
The staff is extremely friendly, offering me water as I wait for my gift card and providing a full dining experience..This is a spot I'd recommend to grab a wine with a friend, dine with a date, or share with our-of-towners. Especially in the warmer months, they have a great outdoor dining space as well. 
The food is flavorful and delicious. 
The bar is plentiful. 
Overall a great selection.
Great find, sat at the bar, great ambiance. Split the favs salad and cachi and pepi which was great....as good as I've had in Roma

What a great meal - weeks later and I'm still thinking about my dinner. I don't like escarole but when you're in the capable hands of Via Carota, that doesn't matter. The Escarole and Fava Bean Salad was highly recommended by my waiter and he was oh so right. Then on to the Bucatini Cacio e Pepe. A tap on my shoulder from my neighbor asking, "oooooh, what's that?" And I was practically bouncing in my chair when I answered. Wow!

One of the best/authentic Italian food restaurant in nyc. Usually very busy and sometimes had to wait in line for 1 - 2 hours. But this time we went, we got lucky - no waiting time. 

Our orders: 
1. Trippa alla Fiorentina - braised tripes with tomatoes and pecorino: this dish is AWESOME! If you don't mind trying Tripes, this is sth you must try. This is exactly what I had in Italy! Very good and authentic! The tripes is chewy and pairs well with the tomato paste. I usually like tripes in Chinese dishes, and never though Italian has such an amazing tripes dish.  It also has onions and cheese in it. Highly recommend. 
2. Vignarola - veggies: peas, fava, artichokes, pancetta, mint and basil. If you are tired of eating salad but still want some veggies, try this one. Mint and basil definitely made the dish shine and fresh. 
3. Pappardelle - ragu. Cheesy but not heavy! It's incredible pappardelle cooked perfectly and seasoned perfectly. It also has some small chopped meatballs. Highly recommend. 
4. Via Carota Svizzerina - hand chopped grass fed steak. To be honest, it's a little bit salty on the seasoning side. However, it cooked perfectly as medium rare. And it's what we asked for. The steak is so soft and juicy. I cannot ask for more! 

Drinks - Manhattan on the rock and Negroni classic
As a girl, I think Negroni tasted better. 

This is a restaurant (pretty much) only New York locals would know about. But it's still sometimes get crowded. If you don't wanna wait in line, better to make a reservation or come for a dinner before 6ish.

I had the pleasure of dining here right after Memorial Day, and luckily was able to splurge on many of the menu items here! Before I kick it off with the food, let me note that they do not take reservations (ugh) and their waiting here is quite cramped and busy, at least at the time we arrived (12:30ish on a Thursday). I highly suggest to order a few dishes and share with the table, much more fun!

APPETIZERS

burrata di puglia, wilted greens & fettunta
Delicious! The burrata was very soft and fresh. 

'nduja arancini, rice & spicy pork fritters
Great texture but almost NO pork to be found. I would skip this

I also had a calamari dish and an asparagus dish, both very good. The calamari had such a light batter, nice crunch and flavor.

MAIN

risotto, meyer lemons & olive oil
Super lemon-y yet fresh. I would get this to share. It is a bit plain, so if you want something more flavorful and fun, I would skip. 

pappardelle, wild boar ragu 
Good, but nothing to write home about. 

We also had a pasta dish with prosciutto that was EXCELLENT.

DRINKS

Negroni
Fresh and well made. Highly recommend.

DESSERT

There is no menu online, so I apologize I have to go off my memory. I had a delightful hazelnut and ice cream dish that tasted like ferrero rocher but way better. It has very chocolatey and may be too much for some people. Share!

OVERALL

This place is cute for lunch or dinner. The service is lovely and the food is good, BUT note that not all dishes are created equal. Try new and more exciting dishes. Save the usual orders for somewhere else. Overall 3.75/5.

Woman coming to eat lunch alone not welcome. 
Table free inside and outside, and I was offered the bar to eat my lunch. Why? Politely said no, because it made me uncomfortable. Three people sitting at the end of the bar seemed to be drinking only. So why should I eat at the bar when there are tables free?! Tables. Plural. I didn't say it, but it was obvious what was happening. The woman just walked off. A waiter wiped down the table between the bar and door and gave me a crumpled sheet of paper. That was the menu. I looked around and felt like I was at the unwelcome guest table. When there were two other tables and they don't do reservations - those two weren't blocked off. It was just humiliating.
Basically, you're not welcome as a young, lone woman at this restaurant. I was dressed as well or better than many of the other patrons and I was very polite. They just don't want you here, ladies. It doesn't matter about your education, your grooming, your manners, etc. You may have intended to spend more than the patrons at the bar. And maybe your bill would have come to more than the group or pair who got seated ALTOGETHER. It doesn't matter, because you are not welcome here. Don't degrade yourself by giving them your custom when you're met with this behaviour. Just don't go at all.

This place is almost always busy... but they don't take reservation, first come first serve.
Get the pastas - every one is great.
Tried also the octopus and meatball, and they're ok (ps the meatball goes well with plain pasta!!)
But the pastas are what you will remember

Came in for a late lunch on a Monday with two others.  I see a lot of these posts mention how crowded it was... I can say that Monday at 4pm is a safe bet!  Plenty of tables at an off-peak time!  Service was very friendly and attentive.  Our group went with Meyer Lemon risotto (yummy), Wild Boar ragu pappardelle (yummy), and Stracci with pesto (VERY yummy).  But the star of my lunch was the side of succotash.  It was so farm fresh and had a touch of red pepper flake heat.  I would go back just for another taste of it!  Server told us that this had just been added to the menu recently and I hope it sticks around for a while!  There is a super cute private dining room adjacent to the main dining room too that would serve excellently for a private party.  Cocktails are very Negroni-centric, if you are into gin!  Very clean, comfortable restrooms.  Great restaurant, looking forward to our next visit.

Excellent food , I wish the carrots were warm though ... still , the salads are amazing! The service was on point ! We were greeted promptly and served a drink while we waited.... having easy access to the bottles for your hostess.... genius!

Terrible, terrible, terrible. I had high expectations, and when the greeter was rude, I thought,  "oh well...i can deal with it."  Then, the table service was bad.  And to top it off, the food was way too salty.  Yuck all around.

Hands down best restaurant in the West Village. Honestly, GOOD LUCK getting a table (LOL) the wait is LONG but worth it. 

Pro tip: put your name down and whatever the # of minutes they tell you the wait will be, expect it to be about 3/4 of that time. Often people will walk away and go somewhere else and since there is no text/email notification system it works out if you stay close by. 

The cacio e pepe is the best in NYC in my opinion and the ravioli melts in your mouth. Grilled artichoke is a good dish but way too pricey for what it actually is (small portion of simple grilled artichoke). Stick with the veggies and pasta and you will not be disappointed!!
Love this restaurant!!  New to the area, already have taken friends and family, approx 8 Times, and they're all hooked!!

We had a nice casual lunch. Place was pretty packed for a Friday.

Nice space. "Cozy". Very good service.

We had one cocktail ($15) and glass of wine ($15). Appetizers were burrata (swell) and salame plate (a bit on the small side).

Entrees were pappardelle and risotto. Both quite tasty. Looked like small servings but quite filling.

Remember to ask for bread.


Damages for 2 with tip was $140.

Amazing restaurant, wonderful vegetarian options!  The octopus, tripe and carrots are all standouts. Lovely service as well, but need to make sure to arrive early and put down name as early as possible as the restaurant is really popular but doesn't take reservations.

Came in on a Saturday night and seeing as they do not take reservations, we had to wait a while and ended up grabbing two seats at the bar. The food was delicious. My friend and I split the pea and prosciutto salad (heavenly, perfectly tossed salad, exceeded expectations) and the pappardelle with boar ragu. The food and atmosphere were wonderful.

My friend and I came for dinner at 6:30 on a Friday and waited around 15 minutes for a table. The food is comforting and delicious - I loved almost every dish of this meal and would definitely come back! I'm not a huge olive fan, but we were given three olives in a little dish as a free starter, and they were so wonderfully salty and oily that I actually loved and ate them all. For our meal, my friend and I split a bunch of small plates and each ordered a pasta. The 'nduja arancini were HUGE, cheesy, funky and delicious. I could've eaten the whole plate. We had a special flatbread with fresh mozzarella and tomatoes (which I thought sounded basic, but my friend wanted) that was so good that I was glad we ordered it, as it was definitely elevated for such a simple meal. The octopus was tender and well seasoned; and the olive pesto it's served with was good, but I wish the dish had been served with some other sauce. The paparadelle with wild boar ragu was also great, meaty and with lots of cheese topping the fresh pasta. The one thing I was a little underwhelmed by was the svizzerina - the chopped steak. It was rare (not my style), but still delicious, salty, and a little buttery. I think if it were cooked medium, I would've enjoyed it more; it's' definitely just like a bunless high end burger but we had to try it. Regardless, can't wait to return and try more of the menu!

Agree with the other reviews with regards to the food but the service level was horrific. We were told one hour but ended up waiting 2 1/2 hours for a seat. I totally understand it's just an estimate but that is an absurd difference. To add insult to injury the hostess clearly sat regulars who had not put their name in ahead of us. Just disappointing to receive such treatment that ruined the night before we could even eat.

Literally one of the best Italian restaurants I have ever been to.  It's hard to get a seat and you will likely have to wait but it is well worth the wait.  Also there are places around the restaurant where you can pop in and have a drink if the wait is long.  As for food, the tortelli and cacio e pepe were out of this world and an absolute must try.  The salad had a simple dressing that was unreal.  It also boasts a lengthy wine list for whatever you feel like drinking so we went full Italian and ordered a bottle of Chianti to have with our pasta. The quality and detail in the food were unbeatable so you really cant go wrong with anything off this menu.

Stopped by for dinner on a Sunday night and was sat at a communal table where we ended up sitting right next to another party. Overall, the environment inside the restaurant is a little rustic and cozy, I did like the decor. 

Between the three of us, we had their old fashioned, pilsner, and a glass of their red wine. We also shared the burrata to start, which was very good and fresh.

I had the meyer lemon risotto and found midway through that I was getting a bit tired of the strong lemon flavor. Did not finish my plate. My friends also got the cacio e pepe, which we found to be a bit too salty and pepper-y. The tortelli with the smoked ricotta was the best out of our dishes, had a good depth of flavor, but the portion was a bit small (to be expected for a tortelli dish).

The bill came out to almost $150 between three of us, which seemed a bit high for having one drink each, 1 shared starter, and a small pasta dish each - considering it was not a phenomenal pasta dish. Not sure if I would rush to come back here, but I'm sure there are a lot of other options that could have been better.

This is my second review for this restaurant as I cannot rave about it enough. I almost don't want to because the spot is already too busy to begin with! Rita Sodi is a culinary genius the way she has crafted this restaurant from the menu prices, to the simplicity yet elegant plates of food to the authenticity of the overall establishment. There is nowhere else I will wait an hour (no reservations) in the city for a meal. 

The food is exactly what you would get straight out of Tuscany and Florence. Simple pleasures of high quality olive oil and ingredients truly elevate the dishes here. I always skip over meats and cheese bc you really can get those anywhere in the city at great quality so don't waste your plates there. The grilled artichokes and arancini are a must to start followed by any plate of pasta. Do get there early to put your name down and have a great drink at the bar!

"Prosciutto its a kind of tomato right? I'll get that 24 dollar aged tomato on a cantaloupe so good!"
SpiderWoman, saving the world !

I love Via Carota and been numerous times over the past couple of years.  I especially love the wild boar papardelle however the last two times I've been I don't think it was as mind blowing as the first time.  This last time a couple days ago, it lacked salt..... which is a big deal as salt is what brings the flavor altogether.  Had to drown it in parmesan to make up for it.  The flavors were there and the texture but the lack of slat made it bland.  Please fix this as its the stand out dish.  What made up for it was the mazing peach dessert.  I think its poached and then grilled and served with maybe a mascarpone cream?? Best peaches of my life, so amazing we ordered a second plate straight after.

Overrated. I had high hopes for this place. Service was very good but not particularly warm. Fried zucchini blossoms were tasty but oily. Liver pate was s bit heavy handed but good(not great). Tripe and its sauce were tasty but it was s bit mushy. Should be a bit firmer without being rubbery. Pastas were made well. Pretty thin and light but not the best I've ever had. Clearly hand made though. The pesto was good but the pasta was swimming in sauce. Not necessary. The wild boar ragu was average, not stellar. The panna cotta was above average but had a ton of very grassy olive oil and salt on top of the apricot compote that was on top of the dessert. I'm a fan of some sweet/savory mixtures but it was not good. It was better when i took 80% of the oil off. Not subtle or refined at all. I'm of Italian descent and lived in Italy for a decade. I'm not a food snob but I tend to know when things are authentic. Via Carota unfortunately gets as many things wrong as it does right. So much potential but ultimately a thumbs down. Would not return or recommend.
Been here a few times! I love the food here. There is always a wait, but it is worth it. I really like the ambience, and the service here.

Wow.  Everything was better than expected.  Don't miss the roasted multi colored carrots with yogurt sauce and pistachio, pesto green beans and mixed salad Verde with the flattened half chicken, buttery and perfectly tender.  Go to this place.

Pleasantly surprised with the food quality and service.   Seemingly simple dishes such as burrata with tomatoes, polipo, and grill artichokes, but the flavor was excellent.   The peach desssert was also very nice.

Honestly incredibly disappointed. I'm a regular at many Italian restaurants in the city and came back here to give it a second shot after a initial disappointing visit. After being turned away from I Sodi (amazing) for bringing our child (too small for a high chair), we were early enough to get a seat here (no reservations). 

We felt like being rushed out the door from the start of dinner. Wine was exorbitantly over priced and horribly mediocre. Pappardelle was over cooked and wild boar dry, the heaping mound of broccolinni was generous with zero flavor, and calamari "special" was tastier at the boardwalk at seaside heights. Given the wealth of beautiful Italian meals available downtown, I left wanting so much more for $80ish per person. I know Rita Sodi is capable of so much more, what a tremendously expensive and flavorless let down.
All the food was great, real highlight was the service though. Lily, our server, was especially fantastic.

This is hands down one of my favorite places to get food! The service is amazing and the food is even better. I think people should beware of the wait time for a table, which may be up to an hour or two on certain nights. My favorite dishes include: grilled artichokes,  truffle appetizer if they have it, and of course the cacio e pepe.
omg. those meatballs. with the shaved parmesan. full on erection while i ate them. and the tomato salad. omg!!!!!!!!!!

The hostess was horrible at estimated time for dinning. First we agreed to wait 1 hour and 15 minutes. Cake back, exactly when we were told. And were told to wait another 30-40 minutes. Very frustrating. They need a better system. I am nurse and need to work the next morning very early.
This is the best restaurant in nyc. Anything you get on the menu will be very authentic and amazing. The steak special is always f**king amazing and any pasta will bring you to the brink of an orgasm
Delicious casual Italian food! We had a great server at the bar! Very crowded during dinner.

Small cozy Italian place in West Village. You need to wait a little bit to be seated, but it's worth it. We had grilled sardines, bucatini and papardelle pastas - everything was delicious! Despite they are busy, service was excellent, the waiter was informative, he gave to taste wine but I even didn't ask, food was delivered quick, our table was kept clean all the time. The chocolate mousse dessert in the end was amazing! Want to be back and try fried zucchini!

Amazing Italian place! Been twice and have great pasta both times. Recently I got a special of sheets of pasta with shaved truffle on top - surprisingly light. Burrata was solid as well. Ambiance is great. No reservations so plan to put your name in and grab a drink somewhere.
Good Italian spot. I enjoyed the food there and we got a variety of small plates to share. My favorites were the chopped steak and Olive Oil Panna Cotta.

This was one of the best meals I've had in nyc or anywhere for that matter. It hit the spot. If you can get over the long ass wait times, you're good. We probably waited 2 hours on a random Tuesday. Made for some hangry people in our crew...myself included. But, once we sat the waiter was so nice and kept us in check. The wine carafes were good and kept us at bay. The food is fantastic. Highly recommend the octopus. It was the highlight for me. Otherwise, order all the things and crush it.

Hostess sat our party of 5 on a Saturday night in 20 minutes. You have to know how to weerrrkk it. Food was divine. The cacio e pepe was insanely delicious. I just wish the portion was much larger. Can't wait to dive back in to that dish!

I generally go to this place once every 3 months and usually it's a relatively enjoyable experience. However, this past Wednesday, I experienced something quite troubling. I went in for lunch and the place was more crowded than usual. An employee there asked if they could help me and I asked for a seat for 1 person. At this time, there was a still one seat at the bar. But he told me that I would have to check with someone named Ash about the wait. I remained next to the host counter, waiting for the host. Eventually, someone stops by the host counter (I'm not sure if this was Ash or not), and proceeds to ignore me even though it's obvious I'm trying to ask for a seat. Several seconds later, a white male in a suit walks in and the host immediately asks them how they can help. The man asks for a seat for one. The host immediately walks over to the empty stool at the bar and requests its neighbors to make more room for the new patron. He seats the male. He then returns and eventually asks me what I need. I ask for a seat and he proceeds to look around the bar. He tells me that there is a stool all the way at the corner of the bar with limited counter space (because there is a tall, wired, fruit rack on the counter in front of the seat). He says I can either choose this seat or I would have to wait a long while for a seat. I chose to leave. Needless to say, I won't be returning to this place anymore.

Checked out this place with a friend for an early dinner/ late lunch and was impressed! The restaurant gave off cozy, rustic vibes definitely a good spot to catch up with a few friends or bring a date, not so great for big parties. The wait wasn't too bad since we came in the middle of the day and started off with some cocktails. The one I ordered had a sweet yet minty taste to it and was certainly strong enough that I don't remember the name. We were immediately seated shortly after and ordered a bunch of dishes to share, some of my favorites include the carciofi crudi (raw artichokes), the grilled artichokes and the finocchi! We had two other pasta dishes as well, don't recall the name but the food was on point! We were so full by the end but the moment the waiter described the dessert menu, we were sold on the chocolate-hazelnut mousse. Overall, would definitely recommend! The restaurant had a vast selection of dishes even for a vegetarian like myself and provided great service.

Via Carota has recently received a lot of hype, but I came trying to keep my expectations modest. I was very pleased and enjoyed every part of my meal. Although perhaps not perfect, everything I had was scrumptious. The dishes were unique while still coming across as familiar, unpretentious, and far from over-worked.

Stand-out: cacio e pepe. One of the best iterations I've ever had. The noodles are delightfully irregular with almost ramen-like kinks. It is aggressively peppery, salty, oily, cheesy... in a perfect way. I also loved the charred leeks which were silky like a roasted eggplant and tangy like balsamic, cut by salty nibbles of cheese. The fried rabbit was good but a bit tougher than I'd hoped, but the garlic bread along with it was astounding. This was all accompanied by one of the better wines I've had in a while.

The atmosphere is cozy, convivial. Service was nothing exceptional, but we lingered and never felt rushed. And although more pricy than some places, it's not absurd. The wines are relatively moderately priced, and the vegetable dishes are more robust than you may expect from a small plate.

Overall: go! It won't be flawless, but it will be a very memorable, very delicious meal. One note: if you opt for an early dinner, you can avoid the wait. By 6pm, there was already a line.

This is now one of my favorite restaurants in NYC! A friend told me about Via Carota and it was the best recommendation. Definitely worth the wait, which can be anywhere from 30 min to 3 hours from what we were hearing the hostess say when we visited on a Sunday night. I would definitely recommend putting your name in then walking around the neighborhood or grabbing a drink nearby while you wait.

It's very bustling and cozy inside, and the food is amazing! We had the tonnarelli cacio pepe and tortelli smoked ricotta - both were some of the best pasta I have ever had!

Easily the best meal that we had over the Thanksgiving holiday weekend in NYC. We started with the insalata verde and the radicchio treviso. For our entrees, we shared the tagliatelle and the svizzerina. Dessert and coffee were delicious. Service was spot on. The food was out of this world. And lovely ambience. A wonderfully courteous and accommodating host. This is a place that I want to visit every day.
It's my favorite restaurant in nyc for an all around non pretentious great meal with great service

I don't understand the hype. The food is definitely good but they treat people as if they're just a number. The hostess was so rude, I've never been treated like that anywhere. We waited for 2 hours and it was not worth it.
Via Carota is the standard against which other New York restaurants should be measured.

Superb. Truly. And I hate to say so..... because this absolute gem will only be overrun by all you other YELPers!

Drinks are fabulous. Food is outstanding. (The fried olives!!!) Service is also always attentive and warm.

Obviously it's annoying that they don't take reservations and the place is a total zoo. But c'est la  vie.
Friendly service and great olives, but the rest of the food was just ok. Nothing was especially memorable.

Lets the pictures tell you how good the food were. My first time here and I already love them since I walked in, and we were told an hour to wait for a table. We didn't hesitant to wait and they offered to get some drink before table ready. We ordered 2 Martinezes and I love how they served while we were standing and waiting for the table.
Probably the best piniocacota in town. The service was great! Such a pleasant experience.

Yesterday, we came at 5pm (after the worthwhile Any Warhol show at the Whitney), expecting to be seated immediately.  I guess I didn't factor in the amount of tourists in town, and the number of locals who were off from work.  We could have had two bar seats ( no support for the back), and decided to wait for a table.  At 5:20, they combined two tables that were for two people, and we were offered seating at the communal table, not in the main room.  I kind of felt like being seated at the kids table.  Please note that I'm giving this 4 stars, and would give it 4.5 stars for the food- if I could.  The verde menu is really fantastic- reminds me of Lupa, but better.  We shared the fish for two,baked in salt to keep in moist, filleted.  it was wonderful.  So people need to decide if they can tolerate the wait.  I think we would return, at 5pm or so, not during a holiday period.  But maybe, I should just book a reservation at I Sodi.  I'm a foodie, so I will probably come back again.

Highly overpriced.
Food was tasty, but portions were small for the price and in some cases laking a good presentation. For example, the risotto, even though it was delicious, was served on a medium flat plate, seemed like overflowing and just not pretty.
BUT, my main complaint is for the "steak" (chopped they call it?) is just a big burger!! Good quality meat but really? Charging that much for burger and two garlic cloves on top should be criminal...
Not to mention we waited more than two hour for a table... DON'T believe the hype

Everything was perfect. Great service! Our waitress was amazing. She was very patient with us and explained the dishes perfectly. The food excellent. Portion sizes were just right and the desserts rocked. The ambiance of the restaurant is very nice as well.
Amazing food. This is my go to italian from now on. The tribe was delicious but showstopper is the caccio pepe. Amazing pasta

Loved it here. Worth the wait- put your name in two hours early and go for a drink somewhere close. We loved our server.

We all shared everything- cacio e pepe (SO GOOD), truffle pasta special (my fave), wild boar ragout (yup, yup, so good).

Went there last week and had to wait over an hour. I don't mind waiting for a good restaurant. The staff was very snobby. First of all they act like they are doing you a favor by putting you on the wait list. No place to stand while waiting and they won't let you go to their bar. They use bar as part as seating in restaurant. We finally sit down to eat and the waiter mumbles the specials. We asked them for some guidance with the menu. He responded everything is good in a snooty way. The food cones and there is hair in the meatballs and the meatballs were average at best. We tell the waiter about the hair and he claims it not a hair and takes the meatballs off the bill. Needles to say I won't go back. So overrated!

Via Carota is a great place to grab drinks on a date, maybe grab some snacks. Definitely a higher price point but well worth it if you enjoy really good wine/cocktails and food. We put our name down and waited about an hour or so to be seated, some people were being told that there was a 2 hour wait so I'm glad we got there when we did. 

I found it best to just put our name in and walk around the corner to Toby's for coffee and chill out. 

We sat at the bar, staff was pleasant, my bartender definitely forgot to put our food order in because people who sat after us were getting their food before us but it's all good we weren't in a rush. I'll be back.

Got seated very quickly for a 5-party table by sheer luck. Otherwise was told that we had to wait over 2hrs. 

Appetizers are very good and filling, but little pricey. 

Everyone ordered some form of pasta. While they were decent, didn't think that great. Little too creamy or cheesy for my liking 

Good spot for a date

One of my favorite Italians in the city.
Additionally, the chef deserves an honorable mention for their self respect: no "Truffle" oil in the menu.

The saying "if you got it, flaunt it" doesn't even begin to cover this restaurant. Via Carota is one of my absolute top favorites in the city for unlimited reasons. I love every little thing about this place from the no-straw policy in their delicious house-made ginger soda to the small horse-head coat racks in their restrooms. 

My foodie-boyfriend and I came here after a roommate showed me a instavid posted by a blogger of VC's pasta. We have tried to venture here at least once a week since then. Social media is tricky because people often confuse what's trendy with what actually makes a great restaurant, but VC is able to combine both. I have always been thoroughly impressed not only with the food but with the demand of the armies they have waiting at the door most, if not all, nights.

Speaking of the wait, they don't take reservations, and they don't need to, which makes me want them even more -- however that does make it harder to celebrate special occasions with larger parties of people. Those that do agree to wait have their names written in chalk on the wall podiums, which is the only thing I find questionable about this entire place (so daring! so edgy!). Still, every time I've waited they've been near perfect with estimations. Either go late at night or be prepared to wait several hours between roughly 5-11pm. Go get drinks somewhere else in the meanwhile. 

I won't go into specific dishes because their menu changes often (a very good sign of a fresh-eyed chef) but some that I get each time are the Cacio e Pepe (best in the city), the burrata, truffle bruschetta when they have it - and the smoked ricotta. My boyfriend and I literally close our eyes and stfu every time from the first bites to the check. The vegetable plates in the middle of their menu are also delicious and so super filling, as well as their fish dishes for their mains. 

Though this review is lengthy I think Via Carota deserves ALL the praise- phenomenal ambiance and staff. They may have a lot of tourists, but this is one of the most (and best) New York restaurants in the city.
The food is some of the best Italian in the city. The cacio e pepe is my favorite. Except for the lack of reservations and the consistent wait I love it here

I have been wanting to try this restaurant for a while 
Last night (Saturday January 11) I went at about 4;00.
It was busy as usual 
The very cordial host quickly (at my request )sat me at the bar as I was a party of 1.
Upon sitting at the bus the bartender quickly took my order 
So far so good
I ordered barratta/a pasta entree 
I was 1/2 way through my appetizer and my pasta arrived 
This is annoying when ur paying a premium price 
As I was eating my app/entree at the same time the staff changed.
New people sat next to me
The new bartender did told them about the specials of the evening (something never told to me) and they were offered additional bread (which I was also never offered)
As a person who works in the hospitality industry I must say I was disappointed.

A must try!!
I've been there twice : the first time for drinks and they have grate mixology and a good selection of Italians liquor , digestive ( not that easy to find) ; the second time was for brunch /lunch , we got appetizers ( big green salad with vinaigrette  and burrata with spinach and toasted bread) they were both good  & as main course We got Potatoes tortelli with ragù ( close to my grandma style ) and caccio e Pepe pasta ( delicious ) , Chianti wine and espresso . 
I definitely enjoyed the pasta, go for it! The service was attentive .
P.s. I am Italian .

Amazing food, but low rating due wait staff. Ouch! I felt like I was bothering them. That said, the food and drink was fantastic. They don't take reservations so show up early. We had a few pastas, salads, dessert, cocktails and the sodas. We were very satisfied. If they could get their service people on the same page, this would be an extraordinary place!

Overall it was a fantastic Italian meal! Great service, ambience and food quality! 

We had:
- broccolini (simply sautéed with garlic, soft and savory)! 
- octopus. Great chewy texture and roasted taste. 
- cacio pepe (pasta). Super rich and great umami! 
- meatballs! The secret ingredients (raisins and pine nuts) are the culprits for giving it such a divine taste! 
- adffogato for dessert since we are pretty full from the above!  

Love it and would come back anytime!

Via Carota is a cool but cozy Italian restaurant with tons of personality. I never like going to restaurants that have crazy long waits but this one is well worth it. I'd say that pretty much everything we tried was delicious in a soulful Italian sort of way. Homemade pastas, fresh bread, it was a party in my mouth. I only wish the service could have delivered on the level that everything else did. It would have been spectacular. I have to knock off a star for that.

I had one of the worst experiences here that I have ever had in NYC. In this city if you are not good to your customers word will get out so you need to hire a good team who knows how to treat guests. We went for dinner, knowing that the restaurant does not take reservations. But the attitude and nastiness of the hostess and the male server with the short sandy blonde hair were really disgusting. They rudely shuffled people out of the way while waiting for a table, and the server told us to move out of the way so someone could sit at the bar for dinner. He could have at least said it with a smile and an "excuse me but...". Really disappointing. Will never go back and will also make sure to warn all business associates not to go there.

Just another rave review of Via Carota here...

Since they don't take reservations the wait was over two hours for a group of 5 however we knew this going in so we checked in then went around the corner to a bar for some pre dinner drinks and chats and came back around the time they told us to and were welcomed back with warm respect. They're method of keeping track of tables is a DIY chalk written pole and wall and somehow they keep track of it all. 

The food was to DIE for. I have severe peanut and treenut allergies and they made me feel safe and were happy to accommodate and I had a delicious tomato and garlic pasta. I can't forget to mention how good the bread is -it's warm and delicious and comes with olive oil splattered across and I asked for a second serving...whoops! 

All in all 5 stars and I will be back without a doubt.

I don't get the hype - it seems like everyone in the food critic and restaurant world loves this restaurant but after eating here, I'm not quite sure why. I could see this being a lovely neighborhood restaurant, but when a restaurant has a 1 hour wait on a Sunday evening at 5pm and does not take reservations, I no longer consider it a cozy neighborhood restaurant. Plus the prices are quite high, expect to spend at least $40+ per person without alcohol. 

My chief complaint is that the food was too oily. The insalata verde was beautiful and stacked high with lots of greens, but had too much dressing / oil for my taste. The grilled artichokes were also sitting in a pool of olive oil, and I didn't find them to be anything special (even with the added aioli) - they still tasted just like any old artichoke and unfortunately I dislike the taste of artichoke. The funghi (mushrooms) was definitely the standout dish, mushrooms were delicious and meaty and the smoked cheese reminded me of halloumi and was quite yummy - but again the dish was too oily and I couldn't take more than a bite. The supposed pièce de résistance - the cacio e pepe - was fine but I guess I'm the wrong audience for it as I'm just not a fan of the cheesy / creamy flavor and it didn't seem all that special to me (and generally found it too rich / heavy). 

Honestly my favorite thing this meal was probably the complimentary olives at the beginning. Even the bread came drizzled with a bunch of oil on top.
Best Italian in NYC! Bold statement I know! You must try this place ASAP!  Everything is outstanding only thing I didn't love was the long wait :)
Holy cow!  The veggies, the veggies the veggies.  The other stuff is great too but the veggies rule.  Amazing to vegetarians and non-v's alike

I came here not only because this place was featured in The New Yorker, but I also heard amazing reviews about it from others. I heard the wait usually is quite long but when I got there around 10-11PM on a rainy night, there was only a five-minute wait. I ordered the Polpette (Sicilian meatballs with pine nuts and raisins), Caccio e Pepe (pasta), and the Risotto. I loved the meatballs and the pasta was cooked very well. However, I did not like the risotto because it was just too dense for me. I love the atmosphere of the place, and I believe this is a great Italian place for a date. Everyone who worked there was super helpful and knowledgable.

This place is ridiculously good. Been here a few times and it's always a 5 star experience. The green salad is the best salad in New York IMO, as well as some of the best pasta. A mark of a truly exceptional restaurant is when I trust that anything I order on the menu will be tasty and this place delivers just that. The menu and wine list changes regularly and keeps me coming back for more.

Apparently they don't take reservations.  My 7+ month pregnant wife showed up at 5:15 to secure a table for my 35th birthday.  My wife claims that there were plenty of open tables at the time.  They denied her and claimed that the tables are already spoken for.  What happened to "NO RESERVATIONS??"  The hostess proceeded to be rude to my wife and did not even look her in the eyes when answering her questions.  I showed up about 10 mins later and the restaurant still had some open seating...  I will never give a place like this my business... they have no humility and that hostess should be fired.

You miss dining in Tuscany? 
After a few visits to this place, I can safely recommend to visiting friends. I would warn them about what not to order (but since they change their menus, maybe my advice would be outdated by their visit)

Pro:
Friendly, informative, knowledgeable and patient staff
Simple, elegant, rustic and cozy decor
Mostly well prepared dishes  (ie. Excellent boar ragu, tiramisu and olive oil panna cotta)
Excellent wine selection


Con:
-Long wait
-No reservation 
-Some bland dishes and their unjustifiable price (vegetable bagna cauda +pork belly...Perhaps it's simply a matter of preference, but it's not something i would order again)
-I wish they were generous with their wine by glass portion....

This place is interesting, but slipping.  The decor is very nice and the food is above average, albeit a bit on the expensive side too.  The problem is the arrogant, bad attitude from the waitstaff.  They almost roll their eyes when you walk in and barely offer any warmth whatsoever.  This has been the treatment we have received each of the last three times we have been here (we live very close so it's convenient).  If someone would just swap out the majority of the front of house staff, this place would be a gem...but the culture of service there is cold and arrogant.  Too bad.

Not sure if I agree with the circle jerk around it being the best Italian place in Manhattan, but it was a pretty decent dining experience with above average food.

What people consider "character" about this restaurant just feels a bit worn down to me. The ghetto menu with creases and stains, the uncomfortable chair, and the unnecessarily dark ambiance wasn't what I would consider charming.

The food itself was actually well cooked, but nothing that stood out so much as revolutionary enough to call it the best in the city. Meatballs were flavorful and aromatic, and tonnarelli cacio e pepe was wonderfully creamy and delicious. The last dish we order was so unmemorable that I can't even recall what I ate.

Service is pretty good too. I'd probably come back in the future, but no way would I wait an hour or two in the future for this place or go out of my way.

If you go during lunch hours, often there's no wait at all! - Via Carota doesn't take reservations as others have noted. It's a lovely West Village restaurant with a relaxed, slightly rustic but elegant, ambiance, attentive staff, and just a wonderful menu selection with something for all taste preferences. My go-tos are the wild boar ragu or sea bream, and the carrots on the side (or ramps if they're in season!) I definitely suggest Via Carota to anyone that loves good Italian food.

I'd love to share a review of the food at Via Carota but after waiting for over 90 minutes, we left.  I wouldn't have minded the long wait if the staff could have shared an estimate of how long the wait might be. They have a weird system of writing on the walls with chalk to keep track. I kid you not. If you're an odd numbered party be forewarned Via Carota is not your friend. They are aggressive about the bar service while you wait.

Ohhhh myyyyyy, what can I say about Via Carota? There's a lot... but I'll keep it brief since I don't want to give away all of its magic ;)

I went here on a work outing and it was probably one of my favorite meals ever. First of all - the heavily vegetable based meal was perfect for me, since I've been trying to eat more plant-based in 2019. If they're serving the cardoons as an appetizer, GET THEM. Their crispy fried goodness was absolutely amazing and I could've eaten them all night long. 

While all of the entrees we ate were good, you MUST get an order of the cacio e pepe. If you don't, you're just not doing Via Carota right. Some of the best cacio e pepe you'll find in NYC. 

Finally, when you're ordering dessert, just order the first thing that strikes you're fancy you won't go wrong. Their chocolate hazelnut cake was divine and so was the olive oil panna cotta. 

Overall such a fresh yet filling meal. Also, Lindsey was the man, he helped us select our entire meal and all of his selections were on point!

Terribly rude hostess (curly haired blonde). We only wanted a drink, and the hostess seemed upset that we were only drinking. Asked us to stand near the bar, but not bother the bartender, and then continued to shuffle us around saying we were in the way.

Worth the hype.

Get there early - they have a nice little seating area and bar inside for those waiting. The cacio e Pepe was incredible - be sure to get the semifreddo for dessert.

You may also see a celebrity (by the initials of JG) like we did

They have amazing food. But they don't take reservations. On a rainy Sunday night it was a 2 hour wait and you couldn't  even get the bartender to get you a drink. But we were saved by Patrick! He came forward and welcomed us. Took our drink order and found a small corner bar table for us to wait at. So glad he came to the rescue. The food was delicious.

Very hot new restaurant, no reservations and 2 hour wait on rainy night.  Limited space for cocktails while you wait (matre d sends you away to wait somewhere else?). We were about to leave when one of their waiters offered is a menu and took our order for wine.  Worth the wait, everything we had was wonderful and Patrick is worth his weight in gold.  The food was really great, and Patrick made the experience great.  Restaurant come and go.  Those that are hot should be more like Patrick.  He understands how to treat customers.  Owners should be proud of this guy.

Well this place is good but it's not amazing like its reputation (for pasta) that precedes it. 

The atmosphere is cool though. I liked it, the lighting was nice. 

The best thing we had was an appetizer which was a seafood salad (insalata di mare). It was very light and bright and tasted fresh and great.

We ordered 3 pastas as our main meal. The pappardelle (wild boar ragu) was the best one we had and I enjoyed that one very much so. The second pasta we ordered was the cacio e pepe (maybe called tonnareli on the menu) and it was your typical cacio. I am never a huge fan of it since it's always too peppery, but I was told to order it (house specialty) here and I was disappointed - was same old same old cacio. Would not recommend it unless you are the number 1 pepper lover in NYC. The third pasta we had was prosciutto & parmigiano (called the tagliatelle on the menu). This was decent. I enjoyed it enough.

All in all, this place is solid but I don't think it is really much better than other italian places I have tried. Nothing game changing in terms of their pastas. Maybe next time I will order a carne or pesce and see how those are!

Usually great! Today not. Service was inattentive and basic. My baccaloa was super bland and barely there. The host was not very friendly either. I have to say all other experiences here have been always top

Their seating system really frustrates me and they don't take reservations. I arrived at 7pm on Saturday and they told me to come back at 11pm which I did. I was shocked to find that it was still packed at 11pm. After midnight we were seated at the BAR for dinner.. By then I was starving. You would imagine what expectations I had. 

- Seafood salad: Super fresh and delicious. The seafood was nice and tender. 

- Funghi: Not my favorite despite being a mushroom lover. It was a bit too heavy with the scamorza cheese. I also found it to be seasoned unevenly... 

- Baccala Fish: Very interesting and quite nice. I've never had mashed salted cod before. It was tasty. The texture had a good balance between creamy fish and crispy polenta. 

- Coniglio fritto (Fried rabbit): WOW!! It was perfectly fried. Crispy on the outside and tender inside. The texture of the rabbit was very much like chicken but slightly more chewy. Get this. 

- Tiramisu and espresso: Great coffee. Not the best tiramisu. It had too much espresso making it runny..

Overall I thought dinner was delicious. Service needs improvement. Our bartender/waiter did poorly in refilling our wine glasses. I don't think I would return due to the ridiculous wait times. It simply wasn't worth it.

This place is very delicious, but extremely hard to get in to. I'll start with the food. We started with grilled artichokes which were delicious and grilled with yummy spices. For our pastas we got the Cacio e Pepe, which is a must and the Tortelli. The Cacio e Pepe was probably the best Cacio e Pepe I have ever had. Extremely creamy and the noodles are soft and twirl. The tortelli was a little dissapointing as it was very oniony, the ricotta inside was really good but overall, I would not order this again. The restaurant is cute and has very nice vibes. The ambiance is great. Tables are tight together, but nothing not normal for NYC. Now, the wait is a little ridiculous. We got there at 5pm on the dot on a Sunday. We were told we would be seated by 610. I think the matridee messed up because they sat someone that was after us before us, and we didn't sit until around 620/625. We were excited to finally sit, because we have heard many marvelous things about this place but overall I do think that it is slightly over hyped. I would 100% go back, but I am not down to wait a long time again. People that were walking in at 545 and after were told at least 3 hours.
Got there early on a Friday night and was seated instantly. Everything we ate was perfect and truly special. The service was also top notch. We'll remember our night at Via Carota forever.

I had the best meal I've had in years here. Cacio pepe was on par with (if not better) than the same dish I got in Italy. Pasta was perfectly done and the pepper really shone through. Everything I got was incredible down to the way the bread that came with the burrata was toasted and seasoned. Portion sizes were also perfect. Larger than most similar restaurants, but enough that you can still walk after your meal ;)

 Wait was long (2 hours) on a Friday night, but it was WORTH IT. Go get a drink, come back, and have a religious experience eating here.
Love this place although it's gotten way too popular. Waits can be up to 3 hours! But once you eat here you'll know why. Food is delicious and the atmosphere is rustic and comfortable.

My husband and I was really looking forward to this place, as recommended by a colleague, as well as mentioned by Andy Cohen. I went inside and tried to look for a host, and bumped into one of the servers. I ask where I sign up, and he obviously didn't pay attention to my inquiry. I was wearing a jacket and a hat, a casual attire, as we just came from seeing Dear Evan Hansen matinee. He told me to go to the alley entrance and knock on the door. I thought this was how you put your name on the list to dine. I realized afterwards that it was the SERVICE ENTRANCE GATE. The [white male] server apparently automatically assumed that I was help, without asking. Prejudice exist, people. Anywhere you go.

Incredible. Profound. Mindblowing. Via Carota is the real deal, and every bit worth the wait!

There are two tips to dining at Via Carota. One, come as early as you can. We put our names in at 5:00pm on a Friday and were seated in an hour. Twenty minutes later, the line was out the door, and people were being quoted times after 9:00pm. Two, have a gameplan for what will likely be a very, very long wait. Bring good company and scope out some of the great bars and restaurants in the area.

The food is straightforward: it's all really, really good. There wasn't a single thing we ordered that we weren't obsessed with. The artichokes (carciofi alla griglia) were delightfully rich. The octopus (polipo) was accompanied by a uniquely delicious olive pesto that even won over my fiancee, who's very much not a seafood person. The highlight is obviously the cacio pepe, a cheesy, flavor-dense dish that's fully worth the decade it'll cut off your life expectancy. Really, you can't dine here and not get the cacio pepe.

For dessert, we went with the semifreddo, which was fluffy and airy, but still packed a ton of flavor. Everything on the dessert menu sounds great, though.

Credits to the restaurant for what we found to be pretty generous portion sizes. They recommend two per person, but we were quite full on three between the two of us. If you're dining in a large party, each dish could probably optimally be split up to four ways.

If there's any room for improvement, it's the drink selection. My whiskey sour was nice, but not particularly memorable or worthwhile. In an otherwise standout experience, it's the one weak link. Still, that shouldn't keep you from checking out one of the city's best restaurants. It'll definitely be a night to remember!

I knew Via Carota was crazy busy from the other reviews here, but I had a perfect plan, especially after an afternoon lecture was canceled. I arrived at about 4:30 and snagged the last seat at the bar. The extra effort was worth it. I really enjoyed my meal. 

Upon arriving, some lightly spiced olives are delivered with a small dish for the pits. I can't remember another place that thought about the pit. That is somewhat endemic of the whole meal. Finocchio is a mound of shaved fennel with shaved pecorino silently interspersed. Hidden underneath are smashed olives. What appears to be a bland pile of white reveals sparks of flavor throughout. Who knew fried Rabbit could be so amazing. I love rabbit, but never thought about it fried. The meat remained tender and moist and the crunch was a plus. The rosemary flavor also added just the right amount of variety. I thought the Olive Oil Panna Cotta was perfect just rich and creamy enough to set off the afternoon. 

By the time I left, the restaurant's evening was getting full. People were already lining up and for good reason. This is a great place for food.

Good service, excellent food. Everything tasted great. We had a lamb pasta special and the tagliatelle and prosciutto. Ordered a Negroni and was great, along with the burrata. Finished with the panna cotta, and my goodness very good as well. Would definitely come back.

Pros:
- The cacio pepe was delicious: loved the texture of the noodles and the flavor was incredible (unpopular opinion: I think I have had better though, but this dish at Via Carota was still really really great incredible)
- The meal overall was very delicious
- The staff and service was really friendly and helpful, super patient and gave great suggestions, super apologetic about the extra 2 hour wait on top of our already 2 hour wait and was very polite and accommodating 

Cons:
- the restaurant does not take reservations and the wait time is ridiculous... my party of 3 arrived at 5:30, was told that our wait would be 2 hours and to return at 7:30... we never received a text so we arrived at 8:15 and was told we were next... waited until 9 and we followed up and was told our table was paying... was not seated until 9:30... waited a total of 4 hours
- I honestly wish I remembered the name of the raw beef dish and truffle but I was very disappointed with the truffle. There was no flavor at all. 

OVERALL:
I don't think I would come again. I really had a great time and excellent meal but definitely not worth a 4 hour wait. I think because I waited 4 hours and the fact that the place was so crowded, I really anticipated something exceptional but it was only great. It was honestly pretty anticlimactic and I think the wait time really killed my experience here because I was just expecting so much more. With that being said though, this place is worth visiting... but definitely try going during off peak hours.

First and foremost, Via Carota doesn't take reservations. Two friends and I stopped by around 5pm on a Friday and ultimately got seated around 8pm. The Via Carota wait is amongst the longest I've ever seen in New York. Be sure to make arrangements accordingly and don't expect to just walk into dinner. Via Carota was really good, and I think it generally lived up to the hype. I think there's so many Italian restaurants in NY that are wayyyy overhyped for what they are, but I'll spare you that rant.

We started our meal with some aperol spritz because as New Yorkers, the minute the temperature outside is over 55 degrees after a long winter, we jump on the opportunity. The chianti wine we later ordered was also quite good.

As far as the food goes, I think everything is very sharable, which is what we ultimately did. We ordered a variety of things from the menu, but the dishes I liked the most were the carrots (I have seriously never had carrots so good and generally don't even like steamed carrots), the insalata verde (VERY good despite it basically just being just romaine lettuce), and the pappardelle. My friend LOVED the cacio e pepe and said it was probably the best he's ever tried.

The service was to my liking - they didn't stop by enough to disrupt the flow of our conversation, but were attentive enough so that we didn't feel ignored. Also shoutout to the staff for moving so quickly when it decide to torrential downpour outside!

We had the burrata, cauliflower gratin, fried rabbit and tagliatelle. It was one of the best meals I have had in a very long time. The service was impeccable and everyone gave us excellent remcommendations. We did wait about 2 hours for a table, but they sat us within minutes of the time they told us to come back at. Will certainly be back soon

We went to Via Carota for a birthday dinner on a Friday night. We were able to be seated at 5 pm outside, but the wait for inside was 90+ minutes. The service was excellent. We had the brussel sprouts salad, cacio pepe, lemon risotto, and bruschetta with anchovies/butter/fried capers. The meal was delicious. Great ambience, wonderful service and delicious food.

I really want to love this place.

There's no question that the food is incredible. Vegetables are given their proper due here- the mushrooms with scamorza are a thing of wonder. Artichokes grilled to perfection with the most delicate of aiolis. Food is not an issue, here. It's truly wonderful and each dish perfectly executed.
 
However, the service is just bizarrely bot-like and impersonal. 
Perhaps it was a case of the Mondays, though it happened to be a sunny and gorgeous spring day. The country farmhouse style interior and the zippy Italian pop background music was discordant with the attitude of every single person donning an off-white or white (Captain?) waistcoat. There is a lofty coldness that doesn't lend itself well to a bustling restaurant that celebrates delicious food. As the place filled up with a lunch crowd, I watched the staff expecting they'd warm a bit. Sadly, as I left an hour after being seated, the chill was still perceptible. 

Is this what happens to places that get incredibly popular and busy? Is it the location? Whatever the reason, I would love to visit Via Carota again but will have trepidation because of that less than stellar atmosphere. Total shame, as it could be so perfect.

Get here early and put your name down. I think all the hype is worth it but the lack of reservations and wait can be a pain. Via Carota is cozy and delicious and inviting. We had the pancetta pasta, fried olives, and pork braised in milk and it was all delicious. We sat at the bar and thought service was fantastic. Dessert was great, especially the cake. My only complaint is that the tiramisu had too much mascarpone. I'd definitely come back again.

We came in around 1130am for a quick bite on a beautiful Friday.  The Scafata, the Polpette and the Pappardelle with wild boar ragu were all delicious.  And the space too, lives up to the hype.  But bringing it all down was the lack of warmth from the entire wait staff.  Our food was dropped off and we were never asked how our food was.    Dour is the best way to describe it.   It's unfortunate because you feel it in the room and it really takes away from the entire experience.

Hands down top restaurant in NYC. My boyfriend and I are regulars and we love to bring our family and friends here. Staff is amazing and food is superb. 3 Michelin stars!! The owners also have Buvette which is their French restaurant down the street. Amazing as well!
Great find! Loved the Cannelini E Spinachi, Mixed greens with sherry vinaigrette dressing and an amazing egg dish with artichokes and Parmesan. And topped it off with a nice glass of white wine.

Would be five stars except for the process of actually getting a table. Waited nearly 3 hours on a Thursday after arriving at 545 - though lesson learned, don't go in or believe the host/hostess that you might be able to sneak in earlier. Go with their anticipated wait time and add 30 min, then find a nice sport nearby to hangout in. 

Aside from the the food does live up to the hype. Get the Cacio, artichokes and/or whatever has been recommended for you. Just be prepared for a wait... and then soak up the experience afterwards.

Amazing food!!! What can i say!!! The pork belly was out of this world!! My bartenders super friendly and professional!! The pork belly made me hungrier and then I ordered the cacio e pepe for desert!!!! Yes i like pasta for my desert! Lol.. best food in west village.... I can go on and on, i highly recommend it.

We tried to get into Via Carota last fall with no luck.  Came back today and we are glad we did.  I don't write many reviews but the food was fantastic, much better than many places with bigger names.  We shared wonderful grilled artichoke, fungi, and burata, as well as 2 fabulous pastas.  The place has a real friendly NY buzz but it is not to loud and the waiters were very helpful.  Can't praise this place enough
Obsessed with this place. Had a few average meals lately but overall it has been so amazing and tasty

so overrated! Staff are miserable, they don't take reservations and they recently removed the additional seating inside to be replaced with a console with a a few deserts on display. WHY? Food is ok though the last time I went there was a long blond hair in my salad. Not very appetizing and TBH if this place was in Italy it would be so basic. Really. 
Noet to staff: try smiling once in a while and also to owner/ owners why dont you ever promote the nice men there that bus the tables?They work so hard!

Fritto Misto Calamari & Shrimp
Calamari excellent ~ get a side of sea salt you will need it.  Shrimp were overcooked, and tasted frozen.  Scafata was under seasoned basically bland. Not enough mint or anything to give it lift.  Reggiano or Pecorino a splash of lemon or some wilted or roasted tomato.  Great ingredients but no Flavor.  Could not eat it all.  Salad with Prosciutto and peas was excellent.  Fried Rabbit was Dry.
What a shame.

(This was months ago, forgot to post) 
Shaved artichoke salad was soaked in orange juice and really too sweet, hardly any artichoke, and too much pecorino. buried alive.

This place was recommended by an Italian colleague as their favorite and it definitely lived up to the expectations!! Great service and excellent menu. The wait is a little long but that was expected as it is a very popular restaurant and they don't take any reservations. The menu is seasonal and its vegetarian friendly as well!
