We got the cece e Pepe pasta  and the mushroom verde which was bursting with flavor! Also ordered the olive oil panna cota. A must try! Will definitely recommend this place to our friends!

Just love this restaurant.  All dishes are spectacular.  From the appetizers to entrees I have now visited twice when in NYC.  TIP:  If you are open to it sitting outside is easiest.  Waiting for a table can be hours.

Well congratulations to these two fab women for their James Beard award. Happy to see them (once again) recognized. Only problem is that it is has become very difficult to get a table! It has become increasingly busy in the last year as VC has been listed in more and more guide books. Now it is often an hour wait. Worth it? Yep....best place in the city in our book. Here's a small tip for older people like us who don't mind eating early - Go at about 4:30 on the weekend. There is a lull when the lunch crowd finishes and the evening crowd hasn't lined up. At 5, the shift changes and they will tell you whatever specials there might be. Also always be willing to sit at the bar. That goes for Buvette as well.....And while I am at it, at Buvette, always ask if the secret burger is on the menu!

This is a restaurant that is on cruise control enjoying the good review it got from Michelin. They have clearly stopped making any effort to actually deliver good food. It was grossly overpriced and the food was - well, disgusting. My stepmother is Italian and found this horrifying. 

The process for getting  table is difficult. We waited the three hours to get a table and have never been more disappointed for doing so (wish we had just gone for Mexican across the road). 

My husband ordered the anchovies appetizer - which consisted of 4 small pieces of bread, each with 1 anchovy and a huge piece of butter. He had to scrape all the butter off (combined as a blob on the plate, it looked like about 6 ounces of butter). It was disgusting. My appetizer consisted of a plate of overcooked pasta (that tasted worse than box pasta), which I could not see under the drowning of brown sauce which had a couple of walnuts swimming in it. Again - disgusting.

Our entrees were not any better. The wine list is mediocre quality and extremely high priced. The table was tiny, the chairs hard, small and uncomfortable, and the a/c wasn't on, so it was sweaty and humid indoors.  

The dessert (tiramisu) was good. It actually tasted like someone cared when they prepared it.

This used to be one of our regular go to places but ever since Eater put it on the radar things have gone downhill. Tonight we waited well over an hour when three guys stroll in off the street and get seated. Exasperated, we express to the manager our feelings and she insists they have to use a four top for three people even though they just walked in. She sort of understands our frustration and offers to buy us a drink (because we suggested that's what a good manager should do). Nice? Not really. It would have been and should have been but instead of letting us order a drink she pours us some rose bubbly and charges us for the glasses of wine we order. Total lack of empathy or care for their customers. Avoid. There is an abundance of great food in West Village without being treated poorly. To be clear, the bartender was a pleasure. Managment is the issue.
As good as advertised. The cacio e pepe is maybe the most delicious pasta dish I've ever had. Dishes are on the small side, but everything was excellent.

Okay. Full disclosure I came here after reading the insanely glowing review in the NYT about a salad. And that is all I ordered. So I can't speak to the pasta or anything else. That was a very fresh and very simple salad with solid dressing. If I hadn't been thinking about the review and had eaten it, I would've enjoyed it fine and never thought about it again. It's not a revelation. It's a fresh, satisfying and enormous salad. 

The staff was incredibly friendly and attentive. The wait was quite long and it's a bit chaotic (I seriously don't understand why every restaurant doesn't have some texting wait list -- it really is quite easy and makes everyone's lives a little easier. Maybe it breaks the spell of seeming like a restaurant out of another era? After standing around for 30 minutes for a table for one, I would've been perfectly fine with them using basic technology to make the process a bit less stressful.)

Overall a solid place, great staff, beautiful decor and a perfectly adequate salad!
a casual and very enjoyable spot for great italian plates. the cacio pepe and chopped steak were extraordinary. will eventually try everything...and hoping they offer the peach dessert again.

I attempted to eat there tonight at 6p and had a remarkably rude experience. After waiting for some time in the line to get on the list for a table, a woman walked up to the front of the line pretending to be merely asking a question about how long to wait for a single seat.  The host proceeded to seat her at the bar without even asking me - or any of the 10 people in line behind me - whether anyone who was waiting in the line was waiting for a single seat.  When he came back from seating her, I explained to him that this woman had not actually been next; rather, she had simply barged to the front to see how long the wait was, and he had responded by seating her as if she were the next solo person in line.  He responded TOTALLY snottily, asking me with sarcasm whether I was solo.  I was not -- I was actually in line for two seats, and we would've totally taken the bar.  The host then rolled his eyes at me (!?), and proceeded to put me on the chalkboard list, for a two-and-a-half-hour wait.  When I asked whether he would take my phone number (he was taking everyone else's phone number), he said, oh, just come back by at 8:30 or so.  Total.Jerk.  Seriously, it was like early-90s UES.  Have fun with that a-hole approach, Via Carota.  Yuck.

Nothing short of amazing! The food is very flavorful, presentation is perfect and service is always on point! My husband and I truly enjoy this special place. Every time we try something new on the menu we become more convinced that the chef is truly a genius. Our top favorites that we always stick to are the tiramisu, the Zablione I believe it's called and we always get the Roero Arneis a light and sweet white wine.

Via Carota: an Italian restaurant which seems to be popular recently.
------------------------------
What we order:
Tonnarelli cacio pepe
Tortelli smoked ricotta (recommend)
Funghi grilled mushrooms  
Egg with Artichokes(off the menu)

Recommended for lunch only, in order to avoid a horrendous wait and receive much (MUCH) better service. That said, with Jodi Williams at the helm (Buvette), she never disappoints. For a simple and ever satisfying lunch, order the Cacio e Pepe and Insalata Verde, paired with a glass of wine. Perfetto!

Via Carota likes to play hard to get. They don't let you reserve so you have to wait for two hours just to get a table. The true devotees will brave the line. I am not one for games. So, I usually give up if the wait is that long. The food is quite good but not a revelation. I like the tripe. Though, there are about 500 grandmothers across Southern Europe who can make the same dish but better for about a fifth of the price. If the prices were lower and the wait was shorter, I'd give it 5 stars for good neighborhood non red sauce Italian.
Awesome lunch! Great food! Will return! And great service too! Our server was super attentive and came to us with several reccomendations and tastes of the dessert wines.

So this should be a 4 star review but just couldn't get there. The place is very inviting, cool space and wonderful menu and great bar, not to mention excellent staff all around. However, given the reputation of the chefs and the prices, a couple flaws can't be ignored even for this first time, me only lunch experience.  

They offer fantastic authentic Italian style veggies, salad, pastas and entrees and appear to use top tier quality produce and provision. But the execution is off. 

Started with artichokes, peas and escarole scafata - lighted sautéed with garlic.  Truly good stuff except nearly no seasoning.  Only a couple pinches of coarse salt would have done the trick in otherwise excellent veggie choice.  The pasta I ordered is where the experience went off the rails - way off.  House made Tagliatelle with peas, prosciutto and parmigiana.  Sounded great. But what came was right off one of the tourist places on Mulberry street.  Sticky, thick and pasty pasta globbed with butter and a crazy large amount of nutmeg.  The prosciutto was world class brilliant albeit a bit salty, cut perfectly to put into a pat dish and not too thin.  The peas (like those in the scafata) perfect tiny fresh.  But that nutmeg was crazy - about a tablespoon. So much so it turned everything brown and you could see it as a major element in the dish.  Nutmeg is intense and a little goes a very long way and when done properly it adds a nice accent to pasta like this. But this was just terrible aside from the sticky pasty glob of a mess. A kitchen should be ashamed to serve it. 

Had a beautiful floral Rosato from Apulia. The wine selection in general is very nice.  For dessert a panna cotta - one of the best ever with some strawberries on top with a tiny drizzle of evoo and sea salt. Wow nice.  Except too much vanilla - added a brown cast to the wonderful dessert. 

$110 for this single dinner lunch / 2 glasses of wine and espresso.  Sorry at that pride level the flaws are unacceptable.  

Looking forward to trying again. And I'll repeat the pasta order because I'm not shy at sending things back.  Today I was trying desperately to find that pasta pleasing in some way and couldn't. 

Should be 4 stars. But today for me no.

The cacio e pepe was amazing, the famous green salad was delicious, the special pesto pasta was lovely, but the table system here is awful. They don't take reservations and waits can be 3 hours. They don't even text. I really wanted to try this place so we put our name down and explored west village for 3 hours. Would never do this again as it is never worth it. This food better be reaching levels of nirvana and rolling in three Michelin stars for that kinda wait. I'm a 'hangry' type person so I'm not sure why I put myself through this torture. You can find similar quality at places without the insane wait. Would not be back unless guaranteed a table in less than half an hour.
One of my favorite restaurants in New York. The wait can be pretty long, but it's well worth it. My favorite dishes are the carrots and the smoked ravioli, but I don't think I've had a bad dish yet.

The overall ambience and flavors were quite good. I'd give the cacio e Pepe 6 stars, the famous insalate verde 5 stars, the carrots 4 stars, and the branzino 3 stars. The wait was unreal, but luckily we had put our names down before 5pm so were able to eat at 7.

Uhhhh-ohhhh...guess who just jumped across the pond and visited the Big Apple?  THis DivLA (An LA Diva...get with it!)  And yes, I know that middle America isn't a pond, but guess what sweety...there's a pond somewhere in there, so there's you're technicality, ya lil technicality babeee. 

Anyyyyywayyyyy...a quick visit to NY and I had to hit this place up.  Why?  Queen #1, Elisabeth Moss said it was her fave, and a cursory glance of some of these photos revealed Queen #2 JANE FONDA goes here??!?!  Or, at the very least...Queen #3, a lady who looks like Jane Fonda.  OH GAWD, IF ONLY!!!!!

Now, look, I'm all about sass...LITERALLY sass is my life.  But our sweety lil hostess may have had the most sass I've experienced...and you know what?  I liked it.  Because, see...Via Carota EMBRACES IT SWEETY.  You go, put your name down, she gives you a lil bit of sass then does the ultimate sass-ccentuation (sassy accentuation)...writes your lil name on a...black pole?  Coulda been a wall...but Imma say it was a pole, because it's more fun.  

How many?  Oh, 2?  What's your name, because Imma write it on this damn pole and then forget about it.  Buhbye!!!

I'm onto you Via Carota.  And guess what?  I like it.  If I could communicate my disgust for people by just picking up a piece of chalk and writing down there name wherever I damn well please?  Well guess what?! I WOULD!  

So I get my drink on, come back at the guestimated pole time, and end up being seated...pretty immediately?!?!  See!  Sass poles work!

We're seated and have a lovely little waitress who is...just fine.  Nothing scary, nothing remarkable, and guess what?  Sometimes that's just the best.  She mentions her favorites and we roll with some of them.  

Also, can I just say, I'm a G-D adult and I still don't know what a negroni is...ANNNNDDDD....I'm still Dory-fish enough to NOT REMEMBER that they taste gross.  Nothing against you Via Carota, but what the HELL is a negroni and why does it taste like that.   
Tangent...over.  I'm sure I'll order another negroni in an hour.  

FOOD! 

We started with the anchovy bread.  Now look, our little sweety neutral waitress said it comes with a good deal of butter, but I did NOT realize "a good deal" = ALL DA BUTTER.  Like, ALLLLLL DA BUTTER.  Was it delicious?  Hell yes it was.  Did it have more butter on it than I've ate ever before?  Hell yes it did.  Did I feel like I was just biting into a stick of butter.  Yep.  Would I suggest it?  Yes.  Would I also suggest that if you don't feel like eating a block of butter, you probably shouldn't get this.  BE WARNED HUNNY!!  But also be warned that it's sasslicious butta style!!!!!!!!

Next up, Artichokes.  Now, Imma let you in on a not so DivLA fact about myself.  When I was a lil baby child, I would eat artichokes, and they would consist of being boiled and then dipping those lil leaves into mayo.  Is that potentially gross?  Probably, but then again, SO IS EATING A BLOCK OF BUTTER!  But this artichoke, was un...real.  The only choking I'm doing on this lil arti...is from choking up crying thinking I'm not going to be able to eat it again anytime soon.  I don't know what you did to it, but I'm grabbing that lil chalk on writing on the wall that it is A MUST!!!!!!

Then, we got the carrots.  Why?  I honestly think I just lost my mind from that weird ass negroni.  Sorry if I rock some of your lil rabbit boats here, but carrots are one of the least exciting foods out there.  Think about it.  You know when you're dining on that delish T-gives meal and you have a plate of turkey, mashed potatoes, stuffing, and then you're like...WHY THE HELL DID I EVEN WASTE SPACE ON MY PLATE FOR THESE?!?!  Useless.  Sorry to say it but the carrots were a low point.  And it's not Via Carota's fault...carrots have no sass...no time to write it on a pole.  

Wrapping up our meal...some pasta sweetyyyyyyy.  

Boar Ragu.  Look, if you've ever been eating a dish and thought, I JUST CAN'T GET ENOUGH BOAR...this is the dish for you.  It's got more boar than the tinder date at the table next to me...heyyoooohhhhunnyyyy!  Also, here is a secret dating tip for all of you...PUT YOUR PHONE DOWN AND TALK TO ONE ANOTHER...IT MAKES FOR BETTER DATES!  At the very least if you talk to one another, one of you will offend the other and it'll get exciting for the rest of the restaurant.   

Finally...the Cacio Pepe.  Just get it...I guess.  It's fresh, it's fun, there's not too much boar, not too much butter, it's just...good.  

Overall...I'm not entirely sure why my Queens like this place. I'm confused, and I blame my third  negroni of the day.  For what it's worth, there's no middle ground with this place.  It's either delish or...boring.   

I give this one "Book Club" and one "Handmaids Tale."  Aka, a boring, and a WRITE IT ON THE DAMN POLE SENSATIONAL!
My favorite place in NYC. The green salad, cacio pepe and branzino are my go-to's! Amazing.
I don't get the hype. My fried olive appetizer was delicious, but the chopped steak, pasta, and meatballs were all just okay. Service was nice, but quite slow.

Via Carota is my favorite Italian restaurant in ny. The food is consistently delicious and leaves me craving more. Yes they don't take reservations but I actually prefer that over needing to make reservations weeks prior to when I actually am going to eat. 
I don't think you can go wrong with anything on the menu, but I highly recommend starting with the insalata verde which is just the green salad with a copious amount of crisp lettuces like Boston lettuce, little gem, frisée, endive in the most delicious shallot and mustard vinaigrette. The piselli salad with robiola cheese is equally as amazing. Then, get the arancini with 'nduja and the fritto misto if they have! 
My favorite pastas are definitely the tagliatelle with prosciutto and the cacio e Pepe. The meatballs are also delicious and they're sort of Mediterranean inspired with raisins. 
Basically, order everything and then go to sleep in a happy food coma.

Its a nice place.  Very popular.  Been on my list to try.  Food is good, but you can get the same quality Italian at other restaurants where you dont need to wait an hour for a table.  Service could be better.  Also, watch out for the expensive deserts.  $17 for baked peaches!  Unlikely to go back until they start taking reservations.

Yes the food is great and the vibe is great but I really just want to leave a comment on the people that work there. I really enjoyed their company. They were thoughtful and respectful and it's obvious they really love what they do and that's what makes a place special.

I had heard so much about the green salad, that's the primary reason I wanted to go to Via Carota.  It may have been an "off day" but I was disappointed with the blandness of it.  The friend I was with told me that she had had it once before and it had been delicious.  Not this time, we agreed, unfortunately.  I ordered the tagliatelle with prosciutto, peas, and parmesan.  It was sumptuous but very, very rich. One friend ordered the chicken - (pollo alla griglia
grilled free range chicken in salmoriglio). Not bad, but not much different from a grocery store rotisserie chicken.  Another friend ordered the cache pepe and liked it.  Service was fine.  I do resent paying extra for bread when I'm spending so much for a meal, though.

This restaurant was a wonderful place to have a lunch date! We started with an appetizer of burrata over freshly cooked spinach - simply amazing! My boyfriend had the steak, and I had the pasta with peas and prosciutto. Cocktails were also wonderful. Great, friendly service. Cannot wait to come back for dinner!!

One of the worst meals I have ever had at an Italian restaurant, anywhere.  No one should serve a bad Vitello Tonnato.  Just leave it off the menu.  The veal here is tough, not tender.  Even worse, is the tonnato sauce.  It looks too reminiscent of a white squirt and tastes of nothing.  The pasta was an overcooked, over-cheesed lead bomb.  The owner or owners have giving up on this place and it shows in the cooking.  Death spiral to follow.

Stay away from this place.  They don't take reservations understood.  Put your name in and they text you but never tell you wait time.  We were told we were next 4 top table to be seated so we were hopeful.  1:15 minutes later we were texted that our table was ready.  Ended up waiting another 30 minutes and then we were sat at community table with 8 other people! I wanted to leave but had no solid options at such a late hour.  Food average at best, wine list below average.  They are packed so other diners must see something I don't see but basic problem is being lied to.  Don't we have enough of that going on in the world.
This place is entirely over hyped and over priced. Wild boar rage was completely dry and over salted and the waiters were unhelpful and terse

I went to this place over the weekend and the food was phenomenal. The service was great too. It was a cute little place and everything was so fresh. Definitely real Italian food. Overall this place was amazing.

I don't understand the hype of this place. I live in the West Village and have tried almost all the reputable restaurants nearby. This one is just ok-good, but definitely not worth the usually long wait and price. I think people go there for people watching. It's more of a scene than a good dining experience. I would recommend going to Babbo if you want solid Italian food in the neighborhood, with a similar price point. Mario Batali no longer manages or profits from Babbo so you can dine in good conscience.

A four hour wait for a table!  Better be good.... and it was.  No reservation system (well none taken by phone).  Stand in line and give your name and come back 4 hours later.  It was Saturday after all.  Everything was delicious.  We had the green salad.  Delicioso.  We had the pasta and the fish.  Delicious.  Bread was delicious too.  Very professional and friendly service.  Great atmosphere and location.  Put your name in and take a really long walk!  We come back every visit to NYC.

Via Carota falls into 2 categories of New York restaurants--its a place you will have to wait a LONG time for a table and its a place you have probably been wanting to try for a while. That being said, I was so excited when I was finally able to convince a group of friends to endure the wait with me. We went on a Thursday, we put our name in around 6:15 and were seated a prompt 3 hours later (as predicted). This is another one of those restaurants that requires patience, if you know what you are getting into you will have a great time. If you are expecting to sit down immediately, prepare to be upset. 

Once we were finally seated, the service was great. Our waitress was well informed with the menu and prompt with our orders. She helped us select a wine and had the patience to deal with our more than tipsy group (I blame the wait). 

The food: we ordered the burrata to start. My only complaint with this was that they gave us 2 tiny slices of bread with our cheese, we were a group of 5. I recommend ordering extra, but I think they should assess the number of people dining and customize orders accordingly. We then got the Funghi, this was absolutely delicious--a huge crowd pleaser. We followed with three pastas: the Tonnarelli, Pappardelle and the Tagliatelle. I love each of these pastas and truly cannot pick a favorite.

All in all I HIGHLY recommend this restaurants. My advice is to get there super early, put your name in and track down a bar (we went to the Village Tavern to watch the NBA draft). I also recommend this restaurant if you have visitors coming but forgot to make reservations. You can just lie and say this was the plan all along.

Only an hour wait for lunch on the summer solstice -- what augury of the meal to come! Of course the famous green salad was as good as everyone says -- but also about twice as big as expected, which was a pleasant surprise because I was sharing it with my date. In addition I ordered the tonnarelli cacio e pepe (sublime) and she the pasta special of the day, a very simple and elegant spaghetti with a vaguely 'maritime' sauce treatment, though it was vegetarian. We also split an artichoke and fava bean dish that was delightful, though somewhat small. In fact, the pasta dishes seemed remarkably small too, but proved so filling as to be impossible for us to finish the very last bite. Perhaps that was the salad's doing! I will also say that my negroni rosa was a tad sweet, though by no means bad, and the service at the bar was prompt and courteous. It's also not *that* expensive. Believe the hype!

I just got a rejection from the guy saying I could get a table with a waiting time of 3.5 hours with a rude and angry face with no explanation whereas he was accepting people around for a waiting time of 30 min. It was Wednesday 26 at 7.30pm. His attitude is rude and unacceptable . I know the restaurant is famous but it's not worth taking people's attitude while we are supposed to be here and enjoy the food. If you value your time more, then don't come here. The queue is messy and not well organised. We do not know who came there before us, nothing was clearly explained
too much queue and not well organized when you arrive. the timeline for waiting is not clear at all.

This restaurant that was lauded in the New Yorker as one of the best was a major disappointment.  The host was surly and unhelpful.  Since this restaurant does not take reservations, the wait was nigh on to more than two hours!  When the food finally arrived, it was greasy and over salted.  The dish represented as lamb ribs was nothing but over cooked fat with almost no meat.  Bread was charged at an additional $2 for three slices.
The Village has many fine restaurants - this is not one of them.

The interior is classic like a nice italian trattoria . I  was forwarned and went at 5:15 on a monday. But when they put our name on the list was warned if the rest of my party wasn't there before 5:30 it could still be a wait . And so true there was a line by 5:30 . But we were NOT warned that even though he showed up , we could only get a table outside or wait 45 minutes . We sat outside.  ( we will NOT go again in summer ) if ever again, since I dont normally eat that early and have a job.  lol 
My friend enjoyed his heirloom tomatoe salad but wasn't special to me. The Cacio Pepe lived up to hype . Delicious . He liked his chicken . While I like the fried rabbit ( oh the fried bread with it was TOO good ) I would choose something else because while it was crispy & perfectly fried no real extra flavor . Better to get a rabbit ragout or something.

Returned for weekend brunch and had a great meal. Got seated within 20 mins outside (and menu is the same as dinner). Had an amazing salad with prosciutto and peas, a beautifully cooked fish, and of course the cacio e pepe. I'll be back again and again.

I love this awesome Italian restaurant. I discovered it walking around on Pride day. My server Paul was excellent and really made our dining experience great!! He is so kind and great to look at. He has a sexy Italian accent and knew the menu inside out. A real class act!!

It's rustic and charming and even has a communal table, where we sat today.  Kind of a 'secret' brunch spot. The menu at noon on a Sunday is the same as any other time - but there are always (I'm told) two egg dishes available off-menu. It worked for us very well at both our Sunday brunch time visits. 

Picture a little dish of oil drizzled olives on a wooden table and Tuscan style bread to die for with that beautiful chewy crust and meltingly soft interior. It's $2 for the bread but so worth it and they'll bring all you want. Have a steaming Americano pressed just for you.

Food is exquisite. Look at the photos. Taste and quality are every bit as high quality as the presentation.

Service fell short of perfect but still very good. 

There's a good number of sidewalk tables as well as a private room. 

Recommended!

This place was very delicious. My friend took me to a late lunch--good thing I didn't eat before because we ordered various dishes, it was so delicious. I watched a waiter bring out the tallest salad to a couple. This reminded me of one place that brought me the smallest salad on earth for $12: about 10 leaves in a dinky spot.

Now for what I ate: leek, rabbit, cacio e pepe, cannoli.

The large leek was juicy and a good sharing appetizer. You pick up the flesh by swirling it around your fork and then enjoy such delicious flavors and textures from its inside. 

Rabbit: Normally am super hesitant about eating rabbit for fear of it being too gamey or chewy. I don't know how old this rabbit was, but it took me a very short time to chew and enjoy. It was fried to perfection, super juicy, had a good bite (not hard, not dry, not chewy, just perfect, no game-y taste/aroma.) You could really mistake this for some exotic chicken or the juiciest chicken-pork animal. It was that good.

Cacio e pepe: This should be shared or else you will fall asleep immediately. I liked it, but did find it a tad salty--not so crazy salty, but just enough when paired with its insanely rich and thick sauce, you do need to drink water. This is what you call comfort food. It was delicious, but if they could tweak the saltiness, I'd be happier and eat more of it despite carbs not being nice to my waistline, but my tongue would say, just dance with me.

Cannoli: almost a healthier tasting version of cannoli compared to a place a like Ferrara's. This isn't as sweet as theirs, it's a lot smaller with a perfect shell (I mean perfect!) and it's beautifully piped and topped. Obviously this is piped fresh--who wants a soggy shell? I do like my sweets and appreciated that they held back on adding more sugar, but maybe a touch more sugar would be more...divine?

Overall I cannot wait to come back. My friend raved about this place and now I know why.

I have a couple of friends who consider this their "favorite restaurant" and I don't get it. I have celiac and they are not the most gluten free friendly. And whatever I had which supposedly was gluten free tasted good but not amazing. It's a good option if you're not GF, if you are, there are many other places that accommodate and serve similar food.

This Italian restaurant has dropped its quality so much that I cannot believe!!! I came for brunch a couple of time and as Italian I was so happy to find some real Italian specialties. But every time I came after there was something less... tonight they served me the TONNARELLI CACIO E PEPE WITH BUTTER!!!! It's terrible!!!!
Cacio e pepe is a very simple and authentic recipe that cannot be substituted with BUTTER AND BLACK PEPPER!!!! Pasta was dripping of oil ( look pictures) and was disgusting! Also I got the fried zucchini and they tasted oily and absolutely heavy, like they didn't change the frying oil for a long time. I'm happy to pay for real food but this really disappointing!!! I ate at the bar and I also asked the bartender if some changes have happened in the kitchen to have such a poor quality ... so really bad!

Omg. So amazing! We got a table for lunch on a weekday with about a 15 minute wait. We had arancini to start which were so delicious. I then had the Cacio e Pepe which was the best one that I've ever had. It had just the right amount of cheese to pepper ratio and the right amount of creaminess. I finished the meal with the tiramisu, wow! I though I'd had great tiramisu in the past, but this one is to die for. The two hour commute from Connecticut was worth it for this restaurant. The service was excellent as well.

If I could eat Via Carota's glorious acciughe e burro every day until it killed me, I'd die happy. Pastas, chopped meat, and negronis are also excellent. Service is warm and knowledgeable. Atmosphere is effortlessly classic. Don't fear the wait -- put your name down early and enjoy an aperitif at Bar Pisellino across the street!

Amazing pasta! Authentic and fresh! The place looks a little rustic in its decoration, which looks for me. My only complain would be about the staff that talks to you as they are in a rush.
It will be a mandatory stop for me next time I get back to NYC.

I had to go here after Samin Nosrat said that the Insalata Verde was the best green salad in the world, and she was right! 

Food 5/5 
My bf and I came right off of a bus from DC to NY and we were HUNGRY. -The Burrata de puglia was creamy and fresh, and the spring greens complimented the rich cheese well. 
-The insalata verde was deliciously fresh, and the vinaigrette wasn't too overpoweringly acidic. You really could drink it with a spoon. 
-The Fritto misto was light and well seasoned. The batter was light and not greasy.
-The polipo (grilled octopus) was tender and went well with the briny olive pesto. 
-The tagliatelle was very rich, and the hint of nutmeg cut through the sauce well. It was just a tad salty. 
-For dessert, the Zabaone with moscato marinated berries were good, but I couldn't really taste the moscato. If I went back I would order something else. The custard was smooth and rich and strongly vanilla. 

Service: 5/5
We sat at the bar and our bartender was amazing! He helped us find a wine that went well with every dish we ate, and brought out our food in a way that made sense, so we weren't overwhelmed with dishes. 

Price point: $$$ ($31-$60)

Dress code: Dressy casual

Saw so many great reviews about this place and made it a must visit spot for dinner. I read there were long waits being there are no reservations but we figured we would take our chances. We got there at 7pm and was told it would be 3-4 hours!!! They took my phone number just in case, but we decided to eat elsewhere. I got a text at 11:15 pm that my table was finally ready. A couple days later I decided to try to go for lunch and got seated in 15 minutes. We were so excited to try their famous pasta and chopped steak. Everything about this resturant seemed overrated and over priced. The steak was more like a good hamburger and the pasta was only ok. Not worth waiting for this spot and better off elsewhere. Very disappointed.

I didn't like the food here too much.  Had the meatballs which were the best thing I ate.  Cacio pepe which I thought was too peppery.  Also tried the chopped steak which was too raw for me.  Also tried the liver and the prosciutto and peas salad.  Both were just ok

When a restaurant makes you wait 4.5 hours for a table, it shows its absolute lack of respect for its customers. At that point, it should take reservations. Instead, they have extremely arrogant and unkind people keeping a wait list without ever smiling or displaying any sympathy. And the food? After a wait like that, it should've been a meal to die for. It was simply OK. The fad will wear off, and one day the space will be occupied by a Baby Gap.

One of our favorite Italian restaurants in New York! After reading the New York Times review on Via Carota and a whole write up on their Insalata Verde (salad), we had to pay a visit to this critically acclaimed restaurant. 

Getting seated: We came for lunch at around 11:30am on a Friday and while it was packed, our party of two was able to be seated immediately. 

What we ordered: We ordered the insalata verde, the Vitello tonnato and their famous Cacio e Pepe. All were absolutely delectable!

The insalata verde came as a layers of lettuce, endives, frisbee and watercress that were dressed with a sherry vinaigrette. The New York Times said it was the best salad in the world and while that is a huge statement, we have to say that the salad was amazing. The dressing was light yet filled with so much flavor. It was tangy from the vinaigrette, sweet from the honey, and had an extra kick from the dijon mustard and the generous amounts of mustard seeds. The perfect way to start our meal!

Vitello Tonnato: This dish was absolutely incredible. My mouth still waters when thinking about it. Its not listed on the menu but is usually listed as a special, so make sure to specifically ask for it. The Vitello Tonnato is a dish that came with thin slices of chilled veal, toped with a creamy white sauce made out of tuna and capers. The tuna was so fresh that you could barely taste the fishy-ness in the sauce. I think the saltiness of the tuna actually enhanced the flavor and complimented the veal perfectly.

Cacio e Pepe Tonnnareli: We ended our meal with the Cacio e Pepe, and it was amazing. Cacio e Pepe is such a simple dish but when done right, it makes a world of a difference. The cheese they used was impeccable and they had the right balanced of creaminess, thickness, and amount of pepper. 

We loved our experience in Via Carota. It was one of our first Italian restaurants we visited in New York, and after visiting 5 other Italian restaurants, Via Carota would have to be one of our top!

Came for Saturday lunch, ordered burrata, the famous insalata verde, and cacio e pepe.

Bottomline - Amazing texture and flavor for everything we ordered. Much better than some of $$$$ restaurants in midtown.

[Burrata] Simple but solid. The cherry tomatoes were really sweet.

[Insalata verde] Every leaf glowed in their bouncy fresh perfection. The sherry dressing was absolutely delicious, yes, but it was the freshness of the salad leaves themselves that really impressed me. Flawless and crunchy.

[Cacio e pepe] Pasta was cooked to hit the sweet spot - chewy but not undercooked. It was on the peppery side, but just enough to balance out the cheesiness of the dish.

READ BEFORE GOING!!!

Lets start off with the hospitality...the front hostess was very rude and short and when walking in trying to communicate when a table would be available. I understand this place is a first come no reservation place, but when I arrived it was 3 and half hour wait with reservations already in place. So I was confused about that because it should be on their website in bold letters "First come make your reservations". So I wound up coming back 3 and half hour later for a 10:30 reservation. As you could imagine it was a subpar Italian restaurant with people who work there looking like they are mad at the world. I tried to take my girlfriend to a romantic place and our waitress was unaccommodating/rude. 
To the food:
Arancini- weird taste very unusual for a traditional rice ball
Seafood salad- fishy and distasteful
Prosciutto and melon- very good juicy melon

Risotto- so lemony it felt like it was taking the enamel off my teeth 
Cacio e pepe- I love pepper don't get me wrong but this was just way too much. 


Overall somebody recommended this place to me and from the start it was downhill. The hospitality put a bad taste in my mouth of them not caring if people waited or enjoyed their food. 

Not worth the wait and not worth trying. Plenty of other fantastic Italian restaurants in the city with no wait and pleasant staff.

Really good spot , just wish they took reservations !!! Small portion sizes but fills you up. Overall would recommend, just make sure your coming in 3 hours before you intend to eat because that's usually how long the wait is (even on weekdays).

Ok this is definitely a food experience to remember, and one of my favorite Italian dinner in New York City. Everyone was right (reviewers, food critics, etc.) with regards to waiting line and deliciousness.

I came here in a Thursday evening around 6. I was in line to put down my name, and at 6:30 pm I was told my table for 2 was available between 7:30-8 pm. They do not take phone number; they just add names on a column with chalk. It's an honor system and it works! The person who manage that list is my hero. I went get drinks around the corner and come back at 7:35. At 7:45 we were seated inside in a lovely two people table. 

The menu is tackle in your chair, and it's monthly. There are delicious options for appetizers, 5 types of pasta, 5 fish and 5 meats, plus plenty of veggie sides. The server also has some special for the day that we gladly jumped on. We shared a vitello tonnato, and get a pasta with tomatoes and blue crabs and a soup with seafood and shells (zuppa con le vongole.) The vitello tonnato was to die for. Perfect in its thin slices of smoked viel, and top sauce of tuna and capers. We were awed by it. My pasta with blue crabs was amazing, so reach of blue crabs and fresh tomatoes, and the zuppa was apparently really good as well. 

We finished dinner with roasted peaches with amaretto and mascarpone cream. Top notch. 

This gem restaurant will make you feel you are in Tuscany or Italy in general for a couple of hours for sure. I can't wait to find another excuse to go there, and it was not too expensive either (compared to crazy nyc fancy restaurant prices!)

I don't know where to start. We were at this place at 11 PM and the place was packed and had to wait for 30 min to get seated. Worth the wait! They made excellent drinks  from the bar. Ordered the old fashioned and it was well balanced.
Their salad Insalate verde was outstanding. We just wanted to order everything from the menu and settled on the lobster pasta, Vongole (clams) and the steak. The lobster pasta was so tasty and one of the best pasta I ever had in NY.  Their service was outstanding and had good choice of deserts. The cannoli was yummy! The only feedback is they do not take reservations so you have to wait.
Fabulous Italian restaurant!! Very authentic!! I like the small dishes and thus ability to try multiple items!! Service was fantastic! Great ambiance and cute area of the city!

Visiting Via Carota was a highlight of my recent stay in New York. I wasn't aware of the Samin Nosrat and New York Times endorsements, but a friend who's vegetarian said that they had an abundance of high quality and substantial non-meat options, and this was enough encouragement for me. 

We arrived for lunch at noon sharp, and this was a good move. We were seated relatively quickly, but the place got progressively more mobbed throughout our meal (they don't take reservations). The space has a cozy yet refined aesthetic, like entering the dining area of one of those plush townhouses that fill this upmarket West Village neighborhood.

The Insalata Mista was ample enough for 3 to share, and deliciously balanced with acidity and oil. The funghi option, including grilled mushrooms and smoked scamorza cheese was off the charts delicious (so much umami, so much luxurious richness from the cheese)! My photos don't do it justice--it's a homely looking dish, but unbelievably good. The tonnareli with cacio pepe (cheese, black pepper, housemade pasta) was also glorious, if a bit on the modest side when split 3 ways.

I would happily visit here again in a heart beat. Service was excellent and efficient, and they offer some nice mocktails, like a housemade ginger and lime soda.

If I could lick a bowl in a restaurant without any shame I'd do it for the Cacio e Pepe.  This dish was the best item we ordered here and we almost fought over it at the end.  Another favorite of mine were the grilled peaches with mascarpone cheese and honey. So simple but so satisfying! Can't wait to come back here to try the other dishes.

Came here on a Wed night in late June for a "dinner club" with two girlfriends.  We try to go to a different and exciting spot every month and there's obviously been a lot of buzz about this place.  Since we knew they don't take reservations and we expected a wait, my friend got there just before 6pm to put our name down - they estimated a 1.5 hour wait.  They do take your number and text you when your table's almost ready, so we got a drink at a bar nearby.  Think we got in in less than 1.5 hours, but the estimate was close.  We sat at a communal table in a small back room, but we weren't squeezed and there was enough separation for the two distinct parties at the table.

For the food - we shared everything: arancini, burrata, prosciutto and melon, grilled artichokes, octopus although I didn't eat it, and three pastas, the cacio e pepe, pappardelle with wild boar ragu, and the tortelli.  We expected to have to take some to go since we ordered quite a bit, but... we pretty much ate it all! Everything was pretty good, but hands down the cacio e pepe was an absolute standout for me.  It's to die for.  The noodles are a perfect chewy consistency with the right amount of bite. I still think about it. If you've never had cacio e pepe before or if you've never liked it - come here and just get it.  I'd come back for this dish alone. The tortelli was also another favorite, but note it's another creamier dish. We probably could've done without the prosciutto and melon (a bit boring I guess), and the pappardelle was not that memorable. I wish we got the green salad instead but I didn't know the hype at the time. For dessert we had a simple dish of grilled peaches and cream. It was delicious and perfect for summer. We actually saw the table next to us ordered a second one after they tried it!

Overall, 4 stars because I loved that cacio pepe so much and want everyone to try it.  Minus 1 star for the wait and no reservations, and the rest of the food being good but not necessarily as memorable.

Food was tasty and served fast. Service was nice and friendly but felt a bit inattentive and short of perfect. 

Perhaps it was because I was seated at the bar and talked to different bartenders on a busy weekday afternoon, but they didn't tell me their seasonal special menus which were explained to the customer arrived after me. It was not a big deal but would've been great if they told me when I asked them their recommendations.

Also, I was told they didn't have the Polipo (grilled octopus entree) which I wanted to try at the time, however, I saw that dish was served to another customer.
The Svizzerina (chopped steak) which I finalized with was a bit oily for my taste but still juicy and flavorful.

I hope it was just because I came at the wrong time. I would like to come back and try different dishes some other time.

Unfortunately there has been a real decline in the quality of food at Via Carota. One out of 3 dishes that we recently ordered was overcooked and essentially inedible. We also had a pasta dish (which we had enjoyed a few months ago) that now has clear notes of iron and acidity. Are the tomatoes in the sauce fresh? Probably not. Overall we were very disappointed and will not be returning.

Walked in here on a whim and wow was I glad we did. Firstly, such kind staff that made the experience so enjoyable. On top of that, the food was delicious. My favorite being this bruschetta with goat cheese, figs, pancetta, herbs and honey. AMAZING. We also got the Bolognese which was super flavorful. Definitely one of the best restaurants in the area.

After hearing about this place for the past 2 years, and everyone hyping this so called "best salad ever," I finally committed to trying this spot. My friend put our name down and we waited 4 hours. Yes, you read correctly, 4 hours. But we knew this coming in, which is what you quickly learn after the first, second, and third time of trying to get in. The appetizers were phenomenal, but it went a bit downhill from there. We tried the zucchini friti which were seriously so addicting that we finished them all. We had the grilled artichokes with aioli which were divine. And lastly, we had the salad that everyone and their mother has bowed down to. The salad was good, don't get me wrong. But this salad isn't the best one I've ever had by any means. It's just a green salad with several types of lettuce and a good garlicky dressing. Good, but not the kind of salad I'd cut off a limb for. 

However, the pastas were quite disappointing, which I didn't expect for how hyped this place is. I got the Cacio e Pepe, which was absolutely delicious UNTIL I noticed while I was on my last couple of noodles, the pool of oil underneath it. It's not like I'm an italian whose Nonna has made Cacio e Pepe since I was in the womb by any means, but I'm pretty sure Cacio e Pepe is supposed to be primarily cheese, pepper, and a shit ton of butter. So that was a bit sad, but I'd probably order it again if I could get past the pool of oil. My friend had the boar ragu which I really didn't like. The meat was so incredibly dry and the sauce didn't do anything for me. They should take this off the menu IMO. We also had the tortelli, which were good but not great. Overall, this meal was GOOD, not great. This is the kind of meal I'd wait an hour, hour an half for. But I don't think the food is 4 hour wait worthy. Next time I go I will go heavier on the appetizers and skip the pastas. I do recommend you try it for yourself and see.

My boyfriend and I came here for lunch after I saw Via Carota recommended by The Infatuation. Just wow. Service was top notch and attentive. The food, even better. My boyfriend ordered the fried rabbit and I had the cacio e pepe. Both were absolutely delicious! We both kept digging into each other's food. The cacio e pepe was just the right amount of cheesy-ness and peppery-ness. It was my first time tasting rabbit and Via Carota managed to make the fried rabbit taste like perfectly fried chicken. For dessert, we ordered tiramisu which was a solid 9/10 (I am a tiramisu fanatic). We can't wait to come back and try other dishes!

Hearty tasty satisfying and unpretentious. Every neighborhood in America deserves a Via Carota, seasonal ingredients, plenty of veggies, clean flavors, filling and home cooked in the best way imaginable. Everything from the chairs to the plates and the menu design makes feel all warm and fuzzy... like I want to be friends with whomever designed it so more of that goodness can rub off on me. So how was the food? Order everything on the special menu and you won't regret it.

Came here on a Saturday afternoon and waited about 15 min - I normally don't like waiting for a restaurant but with their no reservation policy, I'd gladly wait again for their cacio e pepe and tiramisu. 

Tonnarelli cacio e Pepe - closest I've had to the cacio e pepe at Padella. At $23, the price is a bit steep for a plate of pasta and cheese but it's well worth it - the emulsified cheese sauce clings perfectly onto the noodles. I would like a chewy and thicker noodle (like pici) but the tonnarellI will do. 

Tiramisu - wasn't on the menu but we asked our waitress for it. A lot of tiramisu have soggy and gritty ladyfingers but this one doesn't have that issue. The mascarpone layer was also one of the smoother one I've had. If you're looking for a treat, the tiramisu is well worth it.

First thing to know is that you cannot book a table here. It is so hype that they can't make this work. 
We tried to go to this place 3 or 4 times in the past year and it was always ultra packed with 1 or 2hours before getting a table. This time, we went at 5pm on a Monday and they had free spots. 

We ordered 2 appetizers (Burrata and Bruschetta), had a Ragu and Salad as our main dishes. And we ended with a Tiramisu and Semi Freddo chocolate mousse. 

Around $150 for 2 including tip. 

The food was tasty and well presented. Service was kind of slow but great. Probably why you have to wait a lot to get a table there. But it is a good thing when you are seated, they don't rush you. 

Overall, a great restaurant with above average food. Not sure why the hype about this place. Plenty of similar restaurants in NYC. Not worth 2h wait IMO. Come early for quick seating!

Via Carota is the spot. Consistent over the top service, food and people watching. The can't miss items: Insalata Verde, Cacio Pepe and the funghi. The menu changes somewhat seasonally but the mains never leave the one pager (thank god). If you're visiting in the winter, make sure you try red wine risotto - looks simple on paper but is loaded with flavor. If you're stopping by in the summer - the fava e scarloe is just wow. Always listen carefully to the specials but don't get caught up on the branzino- they literally always have it. If you're lucky to go more than once, other items to taste: the prosciutto (so under rated, order extra bread + olives) the meatballs, & the roast chicken. Honestly everything is good. 10/10 every single time.

I am a fan, but not a four star fan. 

Positive: DELICIOUS! Outside seating, full of charm
Negative: Long wait, you have to pay for vinegar, but its "all the way from Modena" ;) 

So charming, so West Village. Via Carota is one of three very similar spots within a 1 block radius. The staff here will let you know of a 2-3 hour wait without batting an eye lash.

The food is quite delicious, although portions are indeed small.One dish will not be enough. 

Bread is not included, but $2 with olive oil and another $1.50 for a splash of vinegar "all the way from Modena". I still don't see how a splash of vinegar costs $1.50, but whatever. 

I recommend their citrus salad and a cocktail. Their tea selection is limited and bagged tea, so you can skip that. 

Come here to sit outside and enjoy the sunny weather with a light dish.

Rude Service, 3 hour wait (even with empty tables) for mediocre food. In a city filled better restaurants  which are amazing, much more lively and have better tasting food... this restaurant will be a loser inside of two months. If i'm waiting three hours to sit in this restaurant I better be getting a massage and the cook better tap dance in front of me while cooking. Huge waste of time, huge let down.

One of the best meals I've had in recent memory.  I dined here in December with a few coworkers and virtually everything we ordered was excellent.  Here are some of the highlights...

Olive all 'Ascolana
Burrata di Puglia
Zucchini Fritti
Carciofi alla Griglia
Polipo
Carciofi alla Griglia

The only downside is that Via Carota doesn't take reservations, and has a huge buzz so you can expect to wait if you're planning on stopping in on a Friday or Saturday night.  We came by on a Thursday and were seated, but at a family style table with other parties (which actually made things terribly fun).

Incredibly disappointed and worst service I have ever experienced. I had sent an email earlier in the week notifying the restaurant that I was coming to celebrate an anniversary and whether they can hold a table for me. Although they don't take reservations, they assured me that the busy hours are 630 to 930 and if i came before or after then i would have no issue. I came to put my name down at 550 pm and they told me my table would be ready at 8:30! 2 and half hour wait. I went to a nearby bar until then only to return and find out that the table wouldn't be ready until 9. The host had an array of excuses blaming the wait on the weather and that a few tables weren't getting up. I'm sorry but every restaurant deals with table turnover and time management so this is nothing new. Especially if you don't take reservations you should construct an effective system to get customers in and out. When i further explained the situation to our waitress, she mentioned she'd be able to take some items off our bill which I thought was appropriate. However, in the end, she gave us an extra dessert that we didn't even ask for. Would have made much more sense to just comp the dessert we ordered! The food was very solid but I've been to a thousand Italian restaurants in that area and this is certainly not worth waiting 3 hours for, or even 1 hour for that matter. I'd go to L'Artusi, Frankies 570, Don Angie, or Barbuto before i come here if I want Italian.

So good! The Cacio e Pepe is one of their most popular dishes and I can see why! The zucchini fries are amazing without being too heavy either, perfectly salted. And their olives are the best I think I've ever had. Just be prepared for a 3 hour wait!

From the atmosphere to the food, this was an amazing dining experience. The pasta was incredible, the selection of wines and negronis was pretty good and the service was great. In addition to some of the pasta we got the broccoletti, a pork special that was shareable among three people and panna cotta, biscottis and tiramisu for dessert. None of us could name a part of the meal that we weren't happy with.

If I were reviewing Via Carota solely based on their food, I would give it more stars.  Unfortunately, the dining experience isn't limited to the food quality, but service is just as important - a lesson Via Carota needs to remember.  We came here for my mother's birthday and waited about 1.5 hours.  After we were finally seated, everything seemed pleasant and we started our meal with the arancini balls and their signature salad which was absolutely delicious.  When we went on to the main dish of salt-baked branzino and svizzerina (which I definitely recommend), my father and I decided to have a glass of red wine each. The waiter brought the wine, poured a bit into my father's glass to taste and upon approval poured his glass.  He poured the remainder of the bottle into my glass, but it wasn't enough so he returned with a new bottle.  Now, at a restaurant such as Via Carota where the prices reflect a certain standard and quality, you would think that if a new bottle of wine is opened it should be tasted first to make sure it's not corked. Instead, the waiter directly poured this new wine over my half-filled glass.  It was clear to me the waiter had no training or understanding as to how to serve wine - something waiters at a restaurant with Via Carota's prices and reputation should definitely have.  Despite this, we continued with our meal and ordered some dessert and coffee.  While we were having coffee, instead of offering us an after dinner drink (they're known for their great grappa list), the waiter comes and leaves the check on our table without asking us if we'd like anything else.  It was clear he couldn't wait to get us out so that his shift would be over, but again this kind of poor quality service is enough to ruin your entire dining experience.  As if this weren't bad enough, after I asked for the grappa menu and ordered 2 glasses, he poured two very uneven pours into our glasses.  When I was about to ask about it, before I could speak he looked to me and said "you know, these are really generous pours I shouldn't even be giving you that much" and walked away.  I was shocked at how defensive and nasty his attitude was - so much so that we couldn't wait to leave.  This was such a disappointing experience, since the food really is quite good and Via Carota could be such a lovely place if they trained their staff better. With its prices and reputation, you expect a certain standard of service but this was nonexistent and such a shame. Very disappointed.

It was very busy when I arrived which made me excited. The wait time during lunch was over an hour but luckily, I got seated within a few mins. 

Pomodoro mozzarella salad - fresh and light. Can't go wrong with tomatoes and mozzarella 

Cacio e Pepe - it was okay. One of my favorite pastas because it's so simple yet delicious, however, I was a bit disappointed in this dish. It was quite oily and I was missing the black pepper flavor. 

Spaghetti alle vongole - same issue. It was a little too oily for my liking and the white sauce was more watery than what I'm used to. 

It's a cute restaurant. Urban, hipster plant decor and they have outdoor seating. Probably won't come back unless someone else wanted to go.

The only bad to thing to say, is the wait. Otherwise - a home run every time !!! Love this place. Food, design, service, wine - they get right every time!!!
Love the burger and their salads are amazing.
Can't wait to go back...
So many delicious vegetarian options. If you don't eat animals, make a meal out of all the side dishes and you won't be disappointed.

This place doesn't honor its waitlist. We submitted our name at 6pm and were told a table should be ready at 7:30pm-8pm, and they would text us. We wandered back at 7:40pm and although the hostess recognized us, we were told that due to "some large parties" our table would not be ready until 9:30pm-10pm. This was the same time told to the people in front of us when we returned who were just putting their name in. Despite this change, nobody ever contacted us. We had canceled our back-up reservation at Bobo (which is just up the street) at 8pm because we trusted the hostess to be honest. Fortunately, we ended up getting into Bobo anyway, and had a good meal.

I would steer clear. First, they won't take reservations. So we put our name on the waitlist for a table for two. Then another couple walked in after us. Their name was put on the waitlist ahead of ours and then they were seated immediately. Totally unacceptable. 
It doesn't matter what the food tastes like when the staff is so rude. We won't be back!

Fantastic restaurant and great service! We came here for lunch, they were quite busy, but we managed to get a table. We ordered cacio e pepe, seafood salad and their daily special, egg and artichoke, plus zabaione for dessert. Everything was excellent! Would love to come back here.

The experience at Via Carota is exactly what Italian dining should be. With my first bite of the cacio e pepe, I was transported back to rhe streets of Italy. It's the perfect ratio of pepper and cheese with perfectly thick and chewy pasta. They're known for the cacio e pepe but the specials and other menu items sounded amazing as well. The ambiance is lovely with a rustic chic atmosphere and the service is great. If you can make it for lunch on a weekday, you can avoid the long wait. I grabbed a seat at the bar around 1pm and the bartenders were friendly and engaging. I saw them churning out just as many cappucinos as they were plates of pasta so I had to order an affogato even though I was stuffed. It was creamy, smooth, and the perfect end to my meal. P.S. mini biscotti come with the coffee drinks and affogato.

The mushroom dish is every mushroom lover's dream. It's super delicious. That's probably the one dish I'd highly recommend. It has scamorza cheese at the bottom. I also suggest ordering plenty of appetizers. They are more creative than the mains. 

I'm giving this place a 4 star instead of a 5 because:
- wait time is long and they don't take reservations 
- pasta was way too salty
- leafy green salad was good but not worth $18
- portion for entrees is very small

Via carota is an amazing place to eat Italian food with a fusion with the taste and the style of Nyc. I loved the location, the environment and the food ... there's also a nice counter for delicious cocktails. The only negative note I need to express, is that some waiters aren't very kind or friendly, and I found always a long queue to get inside... whatever I'll recommend that places for the freshness and the quality of their food, which was always really tasty

Stumbled in as I saw an open seat at the bar and needed a wine and the bathroom.... 100 bucks later I walked out wondering where I just was and why it was so good......

Upon research, it all started to make sense.....

The setting was like a warm, festive garden ballet, with one graceful worker playing off the other with barely a gesture or nod... The bartender was right on top of it and offered a wealth of perfect, unforced information..... A bubbly Trebbiano started the dance, and perfectly complimented the robustly seasoned insalata di mare...... As I started to put my slightly stoned pieces together, I recalled reading about the place but assumed it was a vegan joint...until I noticed the chopped steak offering lurking and looming in the bottom corner of the menu.... I could tell by the smile from the 'tender that I had ordered something good... He matched it up wonderfully with a Frescobaldi Super-Tuscan, and it was truly a moment upon the first bite..... OMG, that was a Proustian experience of flavor explosion like no other.... The sear on the meat, with the spread garlic/rosemary confit and that perfectly pink salty, bovine center was something I'll remember for a long time.......wow...... I'm speechless...

After a delicate delicious cannoli desert and a splash of an obscure Amaro, I literally skipped home loving life, NYC, and my spontaneous adventure down Carrot Street with my new best friend Svizzerina..... Bravo!

Via Carota is absolutely lovely, this sublime mix of simple, delicious food and a vibrant, intimate, open feel. The waitstaff is approachable and helpful. Like actually helpful. Vegetables really shine, multiple need to be on your table. 

Most of all, Via  Carota is a place for all occasions- late Sunday night supper, big blowout celebration, special date night. The menu flexes to your need, chicken livers and a light fennel salad, grilled radicchio with goat cheese, tagliatelle with prosciutto and parm. Truly delicious.

What a charming place. Delish but quite the wait. A friend arrived at 5:45pm and there was already a line out the door to put their name down for rezzies. We heard the average wait was 3hrs even for a party of 2! But we rolled with it. There's a tiny seating/waiting area where you can order drinks but it seemed like a lot of people just went elsewhere while they waited. I arrived around 6pm and we stayed put, ordering wine while we waited and chatting with other patrons (particularly one gentleman who had arrived solo at 5pm ahead of his first date, and was eventually seated at 8pm! His date came at 7:30pm sooo #perseverance). Anyway, my friend and I were lucky - 2 spots opened up at the bar at 7pm, and to be honest, we didn't mind at all. I would gladly do bar seating next time as well. 

Sadly, I'm celiac so I did not try the pasta (although the cacio + pepe looked great). But we ordered a few veggie appetizers to share and they were simple but so good! We ordered (and I double checked that everything was gluten free):
1) Insalata verde: leafy greens in sherry vinaigrette
2) Pomodori grigliati: heirloom tomatoes & Mozzarella di Puglia
3) Carciofi alla griglia: grilled artichokes with aioli

I intended to order a main but didn't end up needing to! Even with splitting the above, I was so full! Next time I would do the same - apps + wine. My friend ordered the wild boar ragu, which she said wasn't spectacular - but she still finished it. We ordered the panna cotta for dessert and I would pass on that next time. The bartender recommended it but panna cotta in the US just doesn't compare to Italia! Anyway, will def be back.

THIS PLACE!!! OMG worth the wait! Worth every single minute of the two hours that we waited!! I loved this place it so amazing and the pasta...wowzer!! I would suggest getting there as soon as you can and putting your name down, grab a drink around the area and just wait to enjoy one of the best meals of your life.

Overall, a solid West Village Italian spot. I came here to try the cacio e pepe and it was great, but not the best I've had. I also enjoyed the bread with olive oil (delicious bread!), insalata verde (fresh greens with a tasty sherry vinaigrette), and broccoletti (ok, but not great broccoli rabe). Prices were on the higher side ($16-$21 for these basic salads, pastas, and vegetables).

Note: The restaurant does not take reservations and is very popular. I have found the wait to be hours on weekend nights, and opted to go elsewhere (don't think it's worth the wait). When I came on a Sunday for brunch, my party of 2 was able to get accommodated right away.

No food is worth a 2 hour wait...this is New York City and I can go somewhere equal or better that will take a reservation. I won't be going back to Via Carota. We dined here last night, Tuesday, Sept 24, 2019 and when we checked in at 6:45 the host told our party of 3 this would be a 1 hour wait. We had a drink in AOC's garden and came back after an hour. Although there were two tables of 3 ahead of us there were magically two tables of 3 ahead of us that had been seated and there were still 2 more tables of 3 ahead of ours. We were ultimately seated at 8:40 and it just felt like we were lied to. Just give me an accurate time or get a reservation system. This food was fine but this place feels like a Saturday night live episode with all the creepy wannabe influencers eating their green salad. Again, no food is worth a 2 hour wait. This is New York and there are too many good options to deal with Via Carota's BS.

I'm no Italian food expert but this place was great in my humble opinion. Ordered the tomato, onion and cilantro salad that was excellent. I had some sort of pasta with butter and pepper with the meatballs. Both were excellent. I would definitely recommend this place. Very clean and quaint place.
my favorite place for pasta   Love the people who work here   very chill and delicious food  I have been back 3 time

I came here for dinner with my boyfriend. It gets very crowded and it's first come first serve, so no reservations. They write your name on a wall and cross off as they seat.
This restaurant has so much charm. The food here was amazing. Everything was served on small plates. I'd definitely order two-four dishes, depending on how hungry, and family style it with a date.

Okay....

Well it's prettyyy pretty good.

Very very flavorful food and I can see why it's so popular. The place itself looks great. Obviously there is the wait. But really the food is terrific.

The items that I found truly remarkable:
-Pappardelle with wild boar ragu: this is just ridiculous. Get it. Don't even think about it.
-Mushrooms: delicious. It soaks in fat with cheese, and believe me it is very very flavorful.
-Fried rabbit: perfectly fried. The rabbit is moist and delicious.

The green salad is very good with a really nice seasoning however it's not amazing like certain people are saying (and I love salads).
The cacio e pepe is very good but it's nowhere nearly as good as the pappardelle.

After all of the hype and talk about Via Carota, I was a bit underwhelmed.  I went around 4:45pm on a Sat evening looking to eat dinner with a group of 4 expecting to wait after reading reviews and was pleasantly surprised that we would be seated by 8pm. Pretty crazy there's over a 3 hr wait and wouldn't say it is worth the hassle of waiting around if you want to eat immediately.

My group split a bottle of chianti, which was good and reasonably priced. We ordered the brussel sprouts salad and arancini to start. Both of these were worth writing home about. The brussels were shaved with raisins and slices apples in an awesome vinagrette. The arancini had a slight kick to them with some chopped hot peppers inside. 

After seeing so many pictures of pasta on yelp and instagram, the part my group was a bit disappointed with were the pastas. They were clearly fresh but didn't think they were out of this world. There's just as good homeade pasta available in NYC so I wouldn't rush here for it. We tried the seasonal pesto, tagliatelle with prosciutto and cacio e pepe. All of the pastas were very rich and heavy. The tagliatelle was an interesting flavor profile with nutmeg, which was mentioned on the menu and it was a bit overpowering to not call out. Glad the waiter warned us!! One friend got the steamed clams in a white wine garlic sauce; she enjoyed them but wasn't blown away either. 

Kind of odd they charge $2 for bread, but whatever. 

Service was really great and the ambiance was spot on. 

Overall, it's a good Italian option in the west village, but by no means the best I've ever had or worth over a 3 hr wait.

Tuesday at 5:30pm - my friend and I snagged one of the last tables here. I had previously tried to visit on a Saturday at 5pm and was given a 5 hour wait time.

We ordered the salad, Cacio e Pepe and the boar ragu. The salad was fine but I had higher expectations due to the reviews. I feel I could have made a similar salad and probably would opt for a different variant of greens if I was to order next time. It took us nearly 25 minutes to get our pasta after the salad... we did not receive any explanation of when it would come and why it took so long.

When we finally got the pastas - I thought the Cacio e Pepe was good. I had the version at Fiaschetteria Pistoia down the street a few weeks back and I would say this one is lighter and easier to eat more of but I love the decadence of the Fiaschetteria Pistoia version and I think I prefer it slightly to the one I had a Via Carota. The ragu was nice but not to the level of the Cacio e Pepe. I would try another pasta next time.

All in all, solid pasta establishment but not worth a wait in my opinion. I can't understand why people would wait hours to dine here when you can walk into places like Fiaschetteria Pistoia which are similarly good. This is one of those places where I'd go back if someone else wanted to go but maybe not on my own and especially not if there was a wait.

Omg! The wait was so worth it! From the bean soup to the Vinaigrette salad to the pesto pasta and broccoli  and the grilled artichoke with lemon and Chili's were beyond delicious! Service was fantastic. I  wish my 2 seater table was bigger because all the plates didn't fit! Lol!

It feels really silly to get excited about an Italian restaurant. But writing this now I'm already reliving this meal thinking about when I can make an excuse to get someone to eat here with me again. So without hope or agenda, I say to you Via Carota: To me, you are perfect. And my wasted heart will love you until I can figure out how to make that salad dressing. 

I came here for lunch on a Friday a whim with a friend. We had 0 wait time and sat outside. Our waitress was attentive but not overbearing and had great recommendations from the menu. The lunch menu is the same as the dinner menu, a great alternative if you're looking to avoid the long dinner wait. We did try to stay away from some of the obviously popular dishes for things that we both thought sounded interesting (don't worry we got THE salad.) Honestly you can order anything here and I'm pretty sure it'd be fantastic. We ordered the pear crostone, insalata verde, lemon risotto, and tagliatelle. It was all fantastic. We honestly had to restrain ourselves from ordering more.

TLDR: go with friends and share so you can order more things (I'm serious), prepare to congratulate yourself for the great decision you made by eating at this restaurant.

This is everything you want for your senses!! The radicchio salad was my highlight as well as the aesthetics. My husband really enjoyed the rabbit and our dining neighbor raved about the greens salad and Barbera wine. Our bearded bartender was very tolerant of our questions. He was charming and helped us pair wine with our food. He heard us tell our neighbor we were on our anniversary trip and he inquired if it was that day. When we said yes, he added a candle to the tiramisu we ordered. I can see why this is voted one of the best restaurants in NYC

I'm not from NYC so I don't know if this is still a hot spot, but I had read such good things about it. I came for lunch to avoid any long lines at dinner. I had to sit at the bar which was a bummer, but not the worst thing. I got the papardelle and WOW the portion was generous and they gave a huge helping of ragu and parm! What's not to love?!?!

Stellar food & exceptional service. The carrots are roasted & served in a mouthwatering yogurt. The salad defines freshness. Shaved Brussels sprouts have the most delectable dressing. Fresh squeezed juices. Every bite is healthy and gives you energy and happiness.

Via Carota seating policy makes it too difficult to visit. I will not be back. Knowing their policy of no reservations and needing to arrive early to put your name down I arrived at 5:30 pm, hoping to get a table for 5 around 7. I was unable to put my name down because there was not a wait list for a party of 5.  So I waited and at 6:30 the hostess said there were two tables available that could sit 5, but even though 3 of my party was present we could not be seated until all 5 arrived.  At 6:40 the hostess sat a party of 3 at the last available table for 5--I was told the chef told the hostess to sit the party of 3.  Oh!. New Policy? Foolishly I had tipped the hostess earlier to better enable us to get a table.  Dumb me. 25 minutes later (7:10) a communal table became available and we asked to sit only to be told that we would have leave by 8:30 since a large group was coming in for the table.  We were seated at the communal table and then 15 minutes later we were escorted to another table--even though I requested to stay longer. This is the second visit where I have waited nearly 2 hours for a table and badly treated and misled by the hostess. On the prior occasion I waited nearly 2 hours and the hostess told me the people at the communal table (he pointed to it) was paying their check and soon as it was set up we could be seated. Just before we were to be seated the hostess sat another party and squeezed our party of 6 around another table that seated 5. The hostess said he was told to that----foolishly I had tipped the him before and was very upset by how he lied to me.  Each visit I followed the policy of the restaurant and each time I was patient only to be misled (if not lied toby the hostess). Both experiences left me with a very bad impression of the restaurant---all I wanted is to be treated like every other guest and Via Carota failed both times.

Great experience! The no reservations is a bit stressful but we lucked out on a table for 6 on a Tuesday. Waitress gave excellent reccomendations. Cacio e Peppe was my favorite but ricotta pasta and boar pappardelle were still excellent. Must get the salad with hazelnuts & honey - stand out dish. I didnt get why reviews raved about the verde salad, wasnt as good. Tiramisu was rich but tasty!

Phenomenal food and great service. We decided to visit for lunch because of the non reservation policy, we showed up at 11:45am and got a table right away. We had the Nduja arancini, grilled mushrooms with scamorza and a couple pasta dishes (tonnarelli and tortelli), all incredibly simple and perfectly executed with high quality ingredients.
Service was friendly and attentive.Best dining decision during our trip to NYC, definitely lives to the hype.

I inhaled the pappardelle with wild boar ragu for dinner last night. The ragu was delicious but I would have preferred the meat to have more gristle on it and was trying to figure out if wild boar meat was naturally leaner than pork, which would make sense since they probably get more exercise. Anyhow, I also had the affogato for dessert, which came with almond biscotti. A lovely presentation for both. Bar seating wait is significantly shorter than for a table. But be prepared to wait since they don't take reservations.

The star here is the pasta.  It is hard to go wrong with any of the pasta dishes.  They are filling and are entre size dishes.  Appetizers are good too.  We had the squash and parma ham which was just like one would have in Italy.  The restaurant is a bit noisy which would be my only complaint.  Service is very good particularly the sommelier who steered us to a good, appropriate wine.  The restaurant does not take reservations, so there will likely be a wait for a table if you arrive at prime time.

Can I give this place 10 stars?!?  Def one of the absolute best meals my husband and I have ever had in the world!  There is a funny story behind this, but I will get to the food.  

We ordered THE BEST LAMB WE HAVE EVER HAD IN OUR ENTIRE LIVES!  It was lamb ribs with a pesto sauce on it! How in the world did the chef season it so well, cook it absolutely perfect on the inside, but the outside was crispy?!  Omg!  I thought I made the best lamb, Bc it is always mediocre when we go out, but now I'm embarrassed to even make lamb.  We visited the restaurant in August and I literally have not made lamb for my husband and I since. 

Best cacio de pepe ever!  I thought the best was in Rome... nope!  Not even close!  I mean!  Amazing!

We also ordered the whole fish!  When I was done, it didn't even look like a fish existed.  I mean it was lemony, garlicky, crispy, but soft!  God!  So amazing!   We also ordered more sides that were perfect!  

The desserts!  Omg!!  This chef is one of the best chefs ever.  Food was perfect!  Can't wait to visit again! 

I will not tell the story here, but at the chef's other restaurant.  Lol

Party of 2 on a Friday afternoon (around 3pm) and the wait was about 1 hour! Wow. I was shook by how packed it was at that time (were people eating lunch? Dinner? What's going on), but figured that meant this restaurant lived up to its hype.
