We got yummy cocktails while we waited and once we were seated, our server took our order quickly. Everything we ordered was delicious. 
To start: acciughe e burro (yum!!! Give me all the butter)
THE SALAD: when our server said it was "world famous," we couldn't not get it. I don't know about it being the best salad ever, but I was a fan.
Entrees: Via carota svizzerina (HOLY MOLY THIS IS AMAZING. Wow) and the pappardelle (good but not a standout)

Overall, we enjoyed a wonderful meal here and I look forward to finding an excuse to come back to try everything else (although I'll have to prepare myself for a wait and $$$). Lovely rustic space and comfortable vibe.

I don't understand the long waits for Via Carota. The food is just okay. Insalata Verde is good but not amazing. The greens are very fresh and crispy and the dressing was tasty but does not warrant all the fame it receives. It's just a good simple salad. 

Cacio Pepe was extremely salty. It was also sitting in a pool of oil. I love salty food and butter but found this to be inedible. Wild boar ragu was okay. The sauce was too sweet for me. I ended up mixing the two pastas together to balance out the salty and the sweet. It wasn't tasty this way but at least it was edible. 

Clams in white wine was overcooked and rubbery. The sauce had no flavor and wasn't seasoned. It tasted like it was just boiled in white wine. I would not go back.

We sat at the bar and the server was excellent. I give the service A+.

I was really excited to come here for dinner but the staff there was so rude. I came on Friday night, they told me come back in an hour. I came back to check the status and I approached one of the staff to find out. That staff member went to the another and said "This girl is confused" and then the staff member who originally took my name came up to me was very snarky and very dismissive and then  just walked away from me. I've never seen anyone push away customers. I normally wouldn't ever review someone negatively like this, I'd just talk to someone but FYI if you call them they tell you to email them to get in touch and then guess what? They don't respond to your emails. I've been emailing them for weeks. I don't care how good their food is, if this is how they treat people that are  willing to spend time and money they don't deserve it.

The food is AMAZING!!!!!! 
The service is AMAZING!!!! 
I love this place!! Also, be sure to save room for the olive oil cake. It sounds weird, but tastes AMAZING!!!

I was never interested in going to Via Carota because I figured that it was over hyped and not worth it. I mean a 4 hour wait, that's excessive, even for me! 

I ended up going on a Friday because friends from out of town wanted to. We put our name down at 5:30pm and were told we'd be eating around 9:30pm. 

I lost track of time but eventually we were seated. We ordered the artichoke, prosciutto, and mushrooms to start. All were fantastic. Quality vegetables prepared perfectly. For entrees I split the cacio e pepe and ragu. I adored both, but the cacio e pepe perhaps more. 

If you are okay with putting your name down insanely early and eating insanely late then it's worth it.

Finally made my way to this little gem in the West Village. Showed up for lunch around 1:00pm and was quoted a 30 minute wait time. The place was packed with a long waiting list as they do not take reservations.  Everything we ordered was delicious and well executed.  Enjoyed everything we ordered- the fried olive appetizer, grilled artichokes,  cacio e pepe and fried rabbit. The meal was nicely complimented by a bottle of rose recommended by our waiter. Service was excellent! Must visit!

This is a Cozy and Inviting Tuscan restaurant. We were initially told the wait could be up to 3 hours but we were seated in less than 30 minutes. The menu is vast with plenty of options for everyone in your party. It makes your typical Monday night dinner feel like an event. We enjoyed all of our food. The menu changes monthly and be sure to listen for the daily specials. Make sure that you pick something from each category and share everything. I would definitely recommend, but get your pocketbook out because it is expensive. Personally, I don't mind paying for good food but be sure you are ok with it too.

Incredibly ridiculous wait but was well worth it. Probably one of my favorite Italian spots in the city. But I'll probably dine alone at the bar next time to skip the insane wait time. 

Favorite of the night: 
- Crostone con Pere (pear + Gorgonzola crostini)
- Fried Sardines (special of the night)
- Cavoletti (cold Brussel sprout salad)
- Tonnnarelli (Cacio e Pepe)

Delicious but could live without:
- Ndjua Arancini (rice + pork fritter)
- Carciofi alla Griglia (artichoke)
- Pappardelle (wild boar ragu)

For dessert, skip the tiramisu and order the Zabaione (whipped custard with berries)

Was looking for the best Cacio e pepe while in NYC... well we found it along with the insalata verde! Great ambiance and decor! Service is top notch, they're very attentive compared to other NYC spots! If you're out looking for good Italian with a modern,  head to Via Carota.

Excellent pasta dishes, great drinks, lovely service.  Truly a gem in New York City.  A lot of places get hype but this is a must try for a celebratory meal.  Cacio e Pepe (hi Katerina) was the best I have ever tasted.  Important to know that on weekends you can get the lunch menu--it is not dumbed down to an Americanized brunch.

Wasn't bad, I had the ragu pasta, octopus, "steak" port fritter arancini and the mushrooms. Good was average but definitely not worth the 2 hour wait ( we heard of the 4 hours wait when we were here). Food was oily and also portions were small. The steak was just burger patties, which wasn't great

Worth it. Went here for a friend's birthday on a Monday night around 6:30 and our party of five was seated within 15 minutes. We sat in the back room at a long table with another group of people which was a lot quieter and more secluded than the main dining room. While the food was superb, we were enamored with our server, Matt, who was so personable, intuitive, and extremely knowledgeable when it came to the menu. He also was able to make helpful suggestions per everyone's dietary restrictions/needs, which just made the entire experience that much better. We felt very well taken care of and would come here again in a heartbeat!

Amazing experience at Via Carota! We ordered the cacio de pepe and the chicken and both were out of this world. We loved the pasta so much we ordered a second round. 

Not sure if we just got VERY lucky but we were seated immediately upon arrival. It was around 9:30 PM on a Monday night so maybe going late during the week is the trick? Either way, I would probably wait next time because if was scrumptious. Highly recommend.

I have tried going to Via Carota before and have been faced with a 3-4 hour wait each time; I've never waited around long enough for my table to ready. So, I decided to get takeout from Via Carota so I could enjoy the food without the wait! I tried the chicken, artichokes, broccoli rabe, and mushrooms/cheese. I have to say the artichokes were the star of the show - absolutely delicious flavor, great texture, perfect vegetable dish. The chicken was also fantastic - juicy and lemony. The mushrooms were really good, very oily (a lot of the food was decadently oily), and the cheese at the bottom was of course amazing. The broccoli rabe was my least favorite, but I always find broccoli rabe to have a bitter taste (they tried to mask this with tons of garlic, which was semi successful). I do want to dine in at Via Carota because I think that the experience/ambiance is half the price - the takeout was pretty expensive for what it was. However, I'm glad I had a chance to taste it after hearing about the food for so long!
Long wait but SO worth it! Food, service and ambiance were excellent.  Nice strong drinks!

To be honest - I am confused as to why Via Carota has so many 5 star reviews. It was okay. The staff working the front definitely has an attitude of "exclusivity," which has been referenced in other reviews.

Honestly, the wait time is disproportionate to the quality of the food. The arancini was good, the salad was good, the pastas were fine. Our server was so so so sweet.

Really I just don't get the hype. From a girl who is born and raised into a Sicilian family, I just don't think it's worth the wait.

Overall experience was underwhelming. I feel as though this place is overrated. There are way better Italian spots around. Misi in Brooklyn to name one.
The wait time is ridiculous, I found the host to be a little rude. I came in and was waiting to put my name down and the host walks up to the front and walks right past me and take the name down of a couple behind me (who came in after me). Food was good but nothing spectacular.  If you are seated by the windows your food will be cold in less than 10 minutes and you'll want to keep your jacket on while you eat.  The bathroom was also very poorly kept.

When I walked in there was nobody in the cue. Eventually a group came in after me and the hostess went to talk with this group before me which is incredibly rude. Everyone else on the staff were gracious and kind. The atmosphere was nice as well as the food but I left with a poor impression of the place because of that hostess...

Went for lunch, The food  was great but 65$. for plate of pasta and 2 glasses of wine? No bread? And that's without tip.
Ny is so yuppified, the yuppies destroyed the village.

Came here for an early lunch. I got there at 11 and it was empty except for one table, yet they were hesitant to seat me because my friend had not yet arrived. Not sure what that was about.

Had the insalata verde, which was good. Also had the braised lentils and kale -- not as good. Too salty, no texture, and got bored of it after eating half. Would maybe come back to try some other dishes, but overall, overpriced and nothing special.

Via Carota has wonderful pasta, of course, but what I like about this Italian place is its large menu of vegetables.  There are more vegetable options (15) than pasta options (5)!  Radicchio is generally a pretty bitter vegetable, but I like how Via Carota prepares it so that it's not bitter at all.  Serving sizes are on the smaller side, so make sure you spend enough to feel like the menu is over-priced.

I have been wanting to try this restaurant for a while. After a few attempts to go during the busiest dining hours, my friend and I went early to put our name down for a table. To our surprise, we arrived and there were tables free, but our entire party was not there yet. We waited at the side of the restaurant, ordered a bottle of wine and waited. We were seated as soon as our full party had arrived. 
First of all, the specials sounded amazing. We ordered one of the starters from the special, the ensalata verde, nudja arancini which taste similar to croquettes. All 3 were very delicious. 
For the main course, we ordered the radicchio, polpette, tonnarelli and the papardelle. 
Everything was amazing. It was exactly the quality that I expected and the flavors were on point. 
Our server 

I would definitely return for another delicious meal. was very friendly, explained the specials after we had a few questions and was very attentive.

After breakfast at Buvette my friend insisted that I try Via Carota for dinner. It was packed, but I was able to grab a seat for one at the bar with no problem. 

I started with a delicious glass of Chianti and went with the Cacio e Pepe for my main course as it seemed to be all the rage on Yelp. I'm happy to say that it lived up to the hype! It was easily the best Cacio e Pepe I've ever had and it was a perfect portion. The pasta was cooked perfectly and it was creamy and flavorful. 

I would absolutely come back to try one of their other dishes!
5 stars for their cacio e pepe. Everything else was mostly average. Service was superb though. That's all.

Some of the best Italian food I have ever eaten. They have a great menu  and daily special. Each item they brought out was mouthwatering. A very large wine menu. After reading most of the reviews regarding the wait time. They make each dish to order. They don't rush you out. It's a small restaurant. They have a few seats in the back (first come first serve with no reservation) But yes the wait is long but it's worth it. About the review about the bathroom. The bathroom was spotless. They have great soaps and lotions. Maybe you just had some jerk who came in the bathroom before you and left a mess. Whatever the case maybe this is a top notch true authentic Italian restaurant. We will be back!

I arrived with great expectations after reading a dazzling review of Via Carota's insalata verde in the New York Times. Although the salad stuns in its height, I found it to be unremarkable -- very leafy (even more than I would want in a salad) and a tad bitter. 
We also ordered the pappardelle  with lamb ragu which was delicious but tiny, especially for the price! The decor is charming but overall I felt that the restaurant falls short of its hype.

There is a reason why we come come at least twice a month. Whether brunch or dinner, you will never be dissatisfied.  The most wonderful staff, coziest environment,  freshest ingredients & most delicious dishes. This is perhaps one of the best spot in the city. So do yourself a favor & treat yourself with a good meal. No reservations taken, and a wait is always guaranteed.  So show up early & you will not regret it.

Via Carota comes with a certain reputation. Long waits, fantastic food, worth it. Today was no exception. We checked in and was told it was gonna be an hour and a half wait, which when you're hungry is a lifetime, so aim for "off hours on off days" if you hate waiting as much as i do. HACK: If there's seats in the "waiting area" you can dine there as well (full menu) and skip the wait - winning! Which is what we did. We ordered the burrata, the funghi and the insalate verde to start. Burrata was creamy served over greens, not the best you've had but good. The salad is refreshing but a little overhyped - its a green salad, let's calm down. It is huge so keep it around for your mains as well - its a nice "palet cleanser" since the pastas are quite heavy. The funghi was delicious if you're into mushrooms. The cacio e pepe is a must. Creamy and filled with flavor. It is heavy and you're gonna wanna take a nap after but very yummy. I'd recommend going hard on the appetizers since they seem more exciting than the mains. The service was good - lots of different waitresses which confuses me, maybe bc we weren't seated in the real part of the restaurant? But they were all super nice. Ambience is wonderful there, probably my favorite part about this place, you can tell people are enjoying themselves here with a solid meal and a stiff negroni. It's pricey but worth it. Would definitely come back!

This place was like a piece of Italy right in NYC. We sat at the large shared table in the back room. The walls were lined with bottles of wine and olive oil. So cute and homey. We went for lunch and only had to wait a half hour to be seated (which seemed a lot easier than going for dinner when it is EXTREMELY crowded).

The service was wonderful! They hung all of our coats up for us and even brought my brother and I little stools to put our bags and backpack on so they weren't sitting on the floor. 

The food was absolutely incredible and reminded my whole family of the meals we ate while in Rome. Very authentic Italian food, and so delicious. We started by sharing the insalata verde which was extremely fresh with a house made dressing, and a nice generous serving that could easily be shared amongst my four family members. Cacio e Pepe was creamy and wonderful, the tagliatelle was also creamy and extra savory topped with prosciutto.  

Excellent overall experience that I would recommend to anyone in the area and I will definitely be back for more next time I'm in NYC!

Overall 3.5 

Bagna Cauda - heard it's a very authentic Italian dish, interesting  and the anchovy broth was not overpowering. 

Insalata Verde - refreshing pretty good but just leafs.. 

Radicchio Treviso - too greazy

Verzo (cabbage / farro / speck) - delicious refreshing salad, love the mixture. 

Olive Oil Cake - dry

I never write bad reviews. This is my first one. And my experience at this place last night was awful. Our waiter, Nicolas M. could not have been more rude. It was a late dinner with my girlfriend on her birthday and  we were given nasty looks and smart responses from the waiter for asking questions about the menu. I had asked for a complimentary bread which never came. And I was charged for it? Then after he brought out a dish that we didn't order he gave me some snide remark when I requested to have what we asked for. After I wound up saying to cancel the dish, the check was slammed on the table . Didn't say thank you, have a nice nice night,  not a word. Is that how you treat your customers? As if we were an inconvenience, while we politely asked questions and requested that were given the dishes we ordered. I'm truly disgusted, and I'll never come back to this place again. Dear ownership, I recommend that you teach your server to change his tone. This was the rudest dining experience I've had in New York BY FAR.

I was here last night late, walk in.  4th time, but not as impressed with food as earlier times.  
Disappointed in a $42 truffle pasta (small portion) homemade (I thought too "eggy") but I asked if there'd be lots of truffles, the Very nice waiter assured me there would be.  To be fair I was thinking it would be a pasta with freshly shaved  truffle.  What came out was like a dish from a steamer oven, no real flavor except the eggy pasta.  Lots of slices of black truffle, but No taste,  I would assume from a jar?   Or shaved earlier + allowed to cook out any flavor?
Anyway, friends who we were with Adore this place + live in the nabe.  So while I mentioned it, I didn't speak up to the waiter.  
Maybe an off evening, holiday time.  Via Carota you were my Brag restaurant.  Do a better truffle pasta, Please!

The perfect negroni! And the Cacio E Pepe is all it is cracked up to be! I agree with other reviewers who have said that the insalata is maybe overhyped...but not that pasta. This is a charming location for a romantic dinner...but also a good place for a business lunch when you want to impress the client in a low-key way. Highly recommend!

I would give this restaurant a 5 star for the food, but the service was terrible. 
The host was great, the bus service was excellent, but our server disappeared for our entire meal. We had to ask other staff for things forgotten. I would have loved to been asked for another glass. I finished my 1st glass after the appetizer and salad, and my glass sat empty during my entree. 
This restaurant was highly recommended and I felt so disappointed when I left.

Frustratingly disappointing. Came in at 9p to put my name in. Woman who came in behind me was very pretty. The guy at the door looked past me to her and took her name. I didn't make a fuss, simply asked to put my name in, and he told me they weren't taking anymore names, but I should come back at 10p to see if they have openings. Came back at 9:45 and there were 5 names ahead of me behind the pretty woman. Just appalling behavior. Go somewhere else and get great food and better service.

Food really is worth it! Cacio e Pepe was the best I've ever had. Wild boar paparadelle also great. The rabbit was interesting, but could skip it. People are crazy about the salad - great fresh greens.

I'm terms of the wait-  I showed up on a Friday at 5:10, they said a party of 4 could be seated shortly... so I came back at 5:40 and the wait was quoted at 2.5-3 hrs. They will take your number if you have a party of 3 or more and text you when your table is ready.

I would give this place a 3.5 if yelp allowed. While the food was enjoyable, I found it it be a bit overrated and overhyped. They do not take reservations and I was confused at their waitlist policy. We arrived on a Saturday at 4pm and while they were open, they said they were not putting people on the waitlist for dinner now and to come back at 4:30pm. A bunch of people were standing there waiting for 4:30pm to put their names down and they kept asking people to move and leave and didn't allow lines to form. It created a bit of chaos and discomfort. Surely, there must be a better system for their waitlist. We were pretty dedicated to eating here so waited for the 4:30pm list opportunity and were seated around 5pm at the bar. Our bartender/server was not very helpful with selections. We ultimately decided on the octopus, pappardelle and fried duck. The pappardelle was good but was missing the wow flavor. Could have used a spice or something and the meat was just okay. The fried duck was also good but tasted like a standard fried chicken that you would get with waffles. The octopus was the best part. It was very flavorful and cooked very well. It came at the end of our meal. I would have maybe liked to start with that. We may have enjoyed the experience more if we had lower expectations for it and if the waitlist system was better. It was a nice meal but nothing I would be eager to go back for.

I fully expected to be underwhelmed and disappointed by Via Carota because of all the hype around it and I was absolutely NOT. We came on a Thursday night and my boyfriend arrived at 5:15pm. We were told there would be a 45 min-1 hour wait. For parties of 2 you just have to wait in the area or come back around your allotted time (they won't text you). We ran some errands in the area and checked back in after around 45 minutes and were seated immediately! By 6p when we checked in they were telling parties of 2 that the would be seated around 9:30p--so definitely get here early! 

We ordered a bottle of wine and I was happy to see that while they had some high end bottles, they also had a lot of affordable bottles in the $50-$60 range. The overall price is on the higher end, but you get what you pay for because everything tasted so fresh and flavorful--definitely worth the price tag. We started with the Arancini and the Insalata Verde...do not skip either of these! The Arancini had such a unique flavor and a little spice and the salad balanced their richness out perfectly. For pasta we ordered the Tagliatelle w procuitto and the Wild Boar Ragu. I would definitely order both again. They are also well known for their Cacio e Pepe. For dessert we ordered the Olive Oil cake and the fresh berries and homemade whipped cream--although the whipped cream was delicious, I would skip dessert. If anything, order an additional pasta instead!! By the time dessert came around we were both stuffed--so 2 appetizers and 2 pastas is a reasonable amount for 2 people. 

I'm almost disappointed Via Carota was so worth the hype because of so hard it is so get into, but I can't wait to go back!!

Amazing service, cleanliness and quality food.  

Drinks are off the hook, location and bar pIsselino being right across the street make the huge difference as far as locale and convenience.

Recommend as a no reservations spot when eating in the west village on the fly

My boyfriend and I came here around 4:30 on Wednesday because we kept trying to go and there would be hours long waits. They do not answer the phone so you can't even call to ask how long it'll be, you just have to show up. No reservations of course. Anyway because we got there so early on a weekday we were able to be seated around 5

The highlight of the night was actually our first dish- the Cavoletti. I'm not crazy about Brussels sprouts so I wouldn't have ordered it, but my boyfriend wanted to try it and thank goodness he did! It wasn't like balled up Brussels sprouts, it was like a salad. It was so good and you HAVE to order it.

I got cacio e pepe because people reviewed it well but was a little disappointed in how oily it was. It was in a pool of oil...

The other highlight of the night was the Polpette meatballs... so good. There are pine nuts and raisins in it which I thought would be weird but it tasted awesome! Must-have.

We also had something that wasn't on the menu-- fried root vegetables. I would advise against it, I didn't realize it'd be so deep fried and greasy. We also got the arancini which was tasty and my boyfriend had the tagliatelle with prosciutto which he enjoyed.

We had chocolate mouse for dessert and it was sooo good. Highly recommend.

In all-- 4/5 stars because it's kinda crazy to even get a seat. But if you go, you must get the cavoletti, it was our favorite of the night
Sooooo worth it! Sit at the bar and get one of the wonderful bartenders to guide you! Oh and arrive at 4 pm. A wonderful bite of Europe and ambience to go with it!

Started with arancini which was OK. Then Brussel Sprouts which was more like a salad but good. Pasta was excellent. Fried rabbit a one time try but not great. Service was very good. With so many great Italian restaurants in the Village, not sure why people will wait hours for this place but for the hype. One other downside. It was cold outside and our table was right near the door and it was freezing the whole time as the people waiting kept opening the door and there was not adequate heat. Our food even got cold before we could eat it. They could do better.

Amazing place!!! I like it ... I love everything here!

Staff, atmosphere, interior... How delicious it is... not possible to put into words!  You need to eat it!

You are cool ... Via Carota

The food here was very good but my friend and I agreed that it wasn't worth the 1.5+ hour wait. Via Carota doesn't take reservations and even on a Tuesday evening the waitlist was packed out the door. The hosts were nice and stayed calm even through the rush. There are many fun bars around the restaurant so I'd definitely recommend you check one or more of them out while you wait, since the drinks at the restaurant are way overpriced and there's no standing room by the door.

FOOD:
Complimentary olives (5/5) - These olives were just exquisite. I don't even like olives that much but these blew me away.

Octopus (5/5) - I can't eat octopus but my friend did and said it was the best he's ever had. He really liked the charring on the leg and the tender meat. 

Insalata Verde (4/5) - Ah, the famous green salad. I'll agree with many of my fellow Yelpers that this salad is definitely not worth $18, since it really is just leaves. However, I will say I thoroughly enjoyed every bite of the salad. The butter lettuce leaves tasted almost buttery combined with the sherry vinaigrette and each bite was so refreshing. If you like salad, definitely give this one a try.

Fried Rabbit (4.5/5) - This was probably my favorite dish of the night. The rabbit meat was tender and the fried shell had a delicious seasoning on it. I wish there was more rabbit, since they just gave us 3 pieces and a piece of fried bread. I also wish there was a sauce of some sort, or just anything to pair with the fried meat and give it more moisture and flavor. 

Wild boar ragu (4/5) - The pasta was incredible and the sauce was perfectly seasoned. I just wish the boat was a little more tender. I also think there was actually too much sauce and not enough pasta.

My wife and I with our oldest daughter knew  there is  a no reservation policy at Via Carota. When we arrived tonight at 5:30PM the host told  us we would be seated  in about an hour and  a half at 7:00 PM.  We agreed and provided a cell phone number as requested.  We went down the street to a fashionable wine bar, L'Accolade,  302 Bleecker Street and spent  the time over drinks and snacks. Just before 7:00 PM we went back to Via Carota and the  host told us that wait   would be another hour and half without any explanation.  We have dined at some of the  best restaurants in New York City, the  U.S.and around the world and never have we  been treated so callously.  We left and went to Boucherie, a French restaurant just down the street and had wonderful dinner in lovely. atmosphere, Hope this  review is helpful if you are treated in the  same off handed manner at Via Carota.

Disappointing. The waitstaff clearly needs to have a team meeting about customer service, respect and kindness. If the managers care to read reviews they need to have a very serious talk with the blonde ish tall waitress. 
Although I was cool with waiting for 5 hours bc many many people were waiting. Giving each other looks like this was some cool kids lunch table. 

That was not the problem. The issue was the waitress. She belittled my friend bc there was a miscommunication with the order he gave her. He wanted the wild bore Ragu and she brought some other pasta dish. Instead of customer is always right mentality and holding herself with grace bc this is "via fucking Carota" she got SNIPPY! Made it extremely uncomfortable and blamed it on my friend.... she then made sarcastic comments to our table for the rest of the dinner. Case in point we we were mocked after waiting 5 hours for this so called best restaurant in the WV. Give me a break. 

All the rage is to wait for this mediocre restaurant just to say to your other hip friends you've been. Trust save your money go to buvette.

Believe the hype. Went here on a rainy Friday morning. They open at 10 am and we arrived at 10:15 and were the first ones in the restaurant. Very quaint thoughtfully designed interior. Every dish we had was spectacular. The mushrooms with scamorza were incredible! If, and when, I come back I will just order vegetable sides as the meat dishes and pasta were good, but not the star. Impressive wine and cocktail list. The cynar spritz was a perfect morning cocktail! Lol For dessert we had the semifreddo as well as the zabaglione...both were excellent but the zabaglione was simple yet divine! By the time we left around 11:30am, the place was packed. They don't take reservations so forget about trying for dinner.

I guess it's a good thing that there are no bookings, otherwise this place will be always has booked.
From starters to pastas, deserts and negronis, everything is superb.

I do not understand the hype around this place. Small portions, mediocre pasta, longest wait times in the city. There are far better authentic italian places in the city and with waits that are half the time. so confused why people wait so long to get in here. save your money and go elsewhere.

I was worried this would be another overhyped restaurant and that I'd later regret the fact that I waited 1.5 hours for pasta. My concerns were immediately put to rest as soon as the appetizer hit the table. First of all, the bagna cauda was unreal. I hadn't had bagna cauda since I visited my godmom in Italy and honestly she would kill me if I told her I found a comparable version in Manhattan about 350 feet away from a Five Guys. The cacio e pepe? I have no words. I read another review prior to coming to this restaurant that said if you don't order the cacio e pepe you should be prepared to live with the fact that you could have done better but didn't. I thought that was dramatic, but now I'm realizing it was perfectly accurate. We also got the fried rabbit and the pork sausage and olive appetizer, which were delicious, but just barely outshined by the bagna cauda and cacio e pepe. I'm prepared to keep coming back, and as a result, I'm sure I'll get to know the bars around the area pretty well -- my boyfriend and I put our names on the waitlist at 4:30 and we were seated around 6:15. Definitely get there early, because around 6 they stopped taking anymore names until 9 pm. But Via Carota made me believe in the saying that good things come to those who wait, and trust me, you won't regret it.

This place is worth the hype.

Came here on Monday (MLK day, so a holiday). Waited in line to put our name on the list at 4:35pm (list opens at 4:30pm). Were told it would be a 1.5-2hr wait (we were expecting this), so we left and went to bar hop around the area until it was time for our seating. Came back and were promptly seated at the bar.

Started off with complimentary olives (I usually hate plain olives but these were delicious). Split a bottle of Chianti with my friend (great price point ~$40). Ordered the insalata verde - wasn't expecting much but it was surprisingly delicious & refreshing. Ordered the skate dish (on the waiter's recommendation) and cacio e pepe. Was blown away by the skate - my favorite dish of the night. Cacio e pepe was probably my favorite I've had in NYC, it's what Via Carota is known for and it shows. 

For dessert we ordered berries & marscapone. It was good, nothing out of the ordinary - and ended the night with espresso martinis. Best espresso martinis I've ever had, hand down. 

If you're looking for a quintessential, cozy West Village establishment with food you'll be thinking about for days after you dine - this place is for you

I came here with a couple of friends in the early evening on a weekday.  We were able to be seated right away.  This restaurant does not take reservations and is first come first serve.  There are many bars in the area if you want to put your name down and then come back.  We had a couple of plates of pasta, the chicken, and the olive oil cake.  I thought it was just ok and very been much more impressed with pasta by other restaurants. I would come again if someone really wanted to go but it's not somewhere I would go out of my way for and I would not wait in a long line to sit down.

Arrived at 11:40AM on a Monday and was seated immediately. Pleasant lunch here with attentive staff. All the food was delicious delicious and rich - only constructive feedback to the restaurant would be to use less oil. Everything was a little heavy on the oil. Between my friend and I, the leeks were our favorite!

One of the best meals I've ever had in NYC. Only downside is the wait. Need to put your name down, grab drinks and come back. Only take walk ins. That said, it is so so so worth it. Ambiance is super charming, rustic italian vibe. Back to the food:

Artichoke: 10/10 perfectly grilled paired with grilled onion drizzled in lemon, olive oil and herbs. As good as a vegetable gets. 

Burrata: 10/10 paired with a sautéed kale and crisp grilled cracker. Burrata itself, so creamy. As good as burrata gets.

Svizzerina (steak): 9.5/10 amazing salted char on the outside, cooked RARE on the inside. This is almost like a tartare in the middle, perfectly charred outside. This is one of the more unique ways ive ever experienced steak. Special dish for those appreciative. 

Branzino (special): 8.5/10 full branzino, scaled and straight forward...letting the quality of the fish do the talking with lemon, herbs and their incredible olive oil. Flavor was great, just wish it had a bit of a char, similar to the artichoke. Was also a bit cold..to note, we'd eaten the steak first than moved on to the branzino. Id go for the skate or sea bream next time. $59 dish. 

Cacio pepe: for those that are fans of the traditional dish, 10/10 as good as cacio pepe can get. Cheese was so fresh, spiced with fresh black pepper and ofcourse..olive oil. That said, id try a different pasta next time. For me this was a 9/10. Cacio pepe typically wouldnt be a go-to for me but I hads to!

This was my first time here and certainly will not be my last! This is one of those special, neighborhood NYC/West Village restaurants that you'd dream to be a regular at. Its as good as it gets. This will sit towards the very top of my as far as recommendations when friends, clients, etc are in town. Thank you for the incredible experience!

RUN, DON'T WALK!

The food was good, but it did not knock my socks off in any way, there are equally/better restaurants in the city. Not worth such a long wait (3hs), and even worse, not worth being TREATED LIKE GARBAGE by the host.

So, we put our name down 7 pm on Thurs night, 2 ppl. The list of illegible names at the door looks like a system out of rural Italy, doesn't even say how many ppl in the party! After the 2 hs wait, I came back 9pm and host says to talk to him when my fiance gets there. 3 min later, both there, he says oh it's going to be 45 more min. Ok, STRIKE 1, they send us to their bar (Bar Pisellino), probably a strategy to sell more drinks there lol

We come back, wait a few more min and they sit us at a COMMUNAL table! Without even asking if we were ok, like they do in normal places. We were there for a celebration and I'm sitting next to a group of girls, which none of their fault, but seemed we were all part of the same conversation! Ok, STRIKE 2. Not so ok, because it was unbearable. 

We ask to be moved and host says they have 2 spots at the bar (much better than communal table!). Getting to the bar and 2 guy sit in the only two spots we were supposed to sit! STRIKE 3. What??!

Host: "Oh, we have a table that will open up, I'm putting you there"
Why didn't you tell us? It was going to be a bit of a wait bc they are paying. Eff that, we want to sit now, so he puts at two other spots at the bar that open up 5 min later. Back to square 1 :\

Such a rude host, he never ever even apologized for the "confusion" (his LOUSY COMMUNICATION SKILLS and ARROGANCE). That guy should never work in hospitality. Opposite of hospitable.

I'm fine waiting for a table, but being bounced table to table, like they are giving away food or something? We stayed only bc we didn't want to hassle finding another place. After all the wait I had to try it to write an honest review.

To the food: I was really hungry by the time we got food. Maybe that's why people find the food delicious. Of course, ANYTHING TASTES GREAT WHEN YOU ARE STARVING. Had green salad, carchiofi alla romana (surprisingly cold?), funghi (fave), baccala (ok), meatballs (ok) and sabaion (meh).

They didn't offer to comp anything, or send us an app/side/dessert on the house, IDK, something! I don't care about the monetary value, a sign that you care! Many places do that, and they apologize profusely.

Thanks to Taylor, our sever at the bar, for making it up. He was super nice and apologized when he didn't have to, it had nothing to do with him. Hope he gets promoted or something.

We arrived around 4:15 and were told to wait until 4:30pm until they started taking names for dinner.  We were offered several bar seats, but choose to wait for a table. It ended up being around 6:30pm. Everything was well executed but the star is clearly  was cacio de pepe. Everything else was good, but not great. Still a place that is worth a trip.

Don't get me wrong. Pasta was amazing. But the service was incredibly rude. Servers ended up making me and my friend box our food to leave even though we waited for our reservation. We felt incredibly dismissed and undermined. The pasta sadly couldn't overpower the distaste I now have for this restaurant.

A long wait but worth it! The Cacio e Pepe is one of the best I've ever had and I lived in Italy. The grilled artichokes, arancini, crostini with pear and gorgonzola and radicchio salad with hazelnut and robiola were all inspired and amazing. Definitely recommend! Service was great too!

Ordered the sea bream and cacio e Pepe. So so delicious!! We got put on the list at 9:45 on a Thursday and had to wait an hour, but that was well worth it for the delicious dinner we experienced. We sat at the bar and were so treated by friendly and helpful service. The atmosphere was lively but not too loud. Will definitely be back!

Best meal so far of 2020 for me.

Went for my birthday and this place has been in on my hit list for awhile.

Sat by the bar and had some delicious glasses of natural wine to start.
Then had the fried olive with sausage bite, which was amazing, along with the anchovy toast, which was even more amazing. 
Their green salad was definitely needed with all of the heavy dishes, not to mention that it was perfectly coated in the dressing.
Cacio e pepe was incredible and so was the tagliatelle with prosciutto and parm. If I had to choose between the two, I'd go with the latter.

The best bite of the night was the octopus. I thought I had amazing octopuses at other michelin joints, but this one steals the show by far. I'd come back, sit at the bar, have a glass with anchovy toast and the octopus and call it a night.

Definitely need to come back asap..

I have been waiting to come here for a while! My friend and I were out and about on a Friday and got here about 30 minutes after they opened and I'm so happy we did. We were sat outside right away. 

We ordered the big green salad, and I got some sort of pasta. I feel like you can't go wrong with any sort of carb item here. It was all truly excellent! I'll be back again for sure.

Enjoyable pasta dishes and many vegetables dishes are featured at Via Carota.

Via Carota is one of those cult favorite restaurants that people always recommend. As a lover of Rita Sodi's other restaurant, I Sodi, I had high hopes. While overall the food is definitely enjoyable, I wasn't wowed by any of the dishes. The pappardelle with wild boar ragu and the tonnarelli cacio e pepe were both good and would satisfy any pasta craving, but I prefer any of the pastas at I Sodi over both of these. The funghi was also tasty, but soaked in olive oil, making the dish feel less than healthy. The special ricotta bruschetta with truffle was not as exciting as it sounds- the ricotta was rich and flavorful but the bread was neither toasted nor warm and the truffle was almost tasteless. 

Stopped in around 10:30AM on Sunday in a party of four and was seated immediately- by 11:30 there was a wait so aim to come on the early side for brunch.

This is particularly a tough one, when reviewing a hard to get into place almost with a perfect rating. Nevertheless, here we go. 
The restaurant doesn't accept reservations. You need to physically arrive there, wait in line, and then  get on the list. We arrived at 4:50 pm on Sunday, and we were seated at 6:10, group of 4 (different lists for the groups of 2 and 3+). When we were signing up at 4:50, groups of 2 were getting assigned timing of about 2 hours wait. By the time we came back at 6, there was already about 3.5 hours wait for the groups of 2. Yeah, a popular place. 
My first little gripe is with the wine list - looking for the reds, the average price is pushing $90, and the selection is truly mediocre. 
Okay, food. Literally everything we tried was good, but lacking perfection one way or the other. There was practically not a single dish which made me say "oh my god, this is so good". Arancini were not bad, but I really didn't care for the red sauce in the middle. Burrata was presented in a very sloppy way, on a bed of some unknown sautéed greens. Fried mushrooms was probably a better dish, flavorful. White beans and sausage were lacking sausage and presented in some red sauce? 
Entree didn't fare much better. Our pork shank special was good (I had better versions, though), but my wife's pappardelle with lamb ragout was lacking flavor. 
Pannacotta was perfectly executed, but again, was lacking the flavor. 
Service was good, with some little flops, such as wine drips on my pants. 
To conclude: 
This might be an issue of Sunday - I had been to the restaurants where the Chef was off on a given day, and all the food was close, but no cigars. I don't know if I will be back. If you want to try what is considered one of the best Italian restaurants in New York, maybe skip the Sunday for your visit.

Such an amazing place. The only downside is that you have to wait forever for a table because they don't take reservations no matter the circumstance -_-

but the food.... sent from the heavens.... and the dessert... tastier than hell

Went at 4:30 because I heard of the long waits and sat at the bar so i didn't have to wait! Ordered a drink and then food a little later so it worked out perfectly. Definitely recommend doing that! The food however was more than worth the wait! Incredible!
Very good and authentic Italian food, the only real problem I have is it can get very uncomfortable to dine here , but for the price it's worth the visit for sure

This place is amazing! 

The salad was unreal and simple. 

Pastas are to die for. 


This is the real deal.

Nuff said.

Via Carota doesn't take reservations but we showed up 11am on Saturday and although the place was packed, we only waited 5 minutes before getting seated. However, heads up, when the place is packed they don't text or call you so you have to stay alert and linger around. 

This place has the best cacio e pepe in the city and this is the one non-optional item to get if you come here. Called "Tonarelli", it's their flagship product and is extremely cheesy and rich. The noodles are sprinkled with pepper and parmesan and the perfect amount of chewy. There's a reason most tables will have this ordered but the papardelle, nduja arancini, and acchuighe e burro are other great options if you're feeling like a rebel and don't want to stick to the greatest hit.

I read a former food critic review stating that Via Carota is the most perfect restaurant in New York. Obviously, my friends and I had to test it out... and they are right. (at least for the most part... it's the perfect West Village restaurant.) 

Here's what you need to know about Via Carota:
1. The food is done well with the highest quality ingredients. Everything is just so perfectly put together and balanced, no matter what you're getting. And yes, the cacio e pepe is one of the most perfect bites of pasta.
2. The bar is lovely and the coffee is exactly what you need to kick off a perfect evening.
3. The vibe takes you to a special place and time in NYC. It almost feels like you're in Europe with the balance of New York magic.
4. Aesop products in the bathroom. Yes, this is nerdy. Whatever, I have perfectly moisturized hands to hold my fork to twirl my pasta.
5. Great service.
6. Yes, the wait is long and they don't take reservations. I recommend strolling around the area or visiting their sister location to get a negroni before your meal.

Via Carota captures this old school NYC magic that makes it the perfect West Village restaurant. Everything about it signals a good time -- a wonderful vibe, delicious food, and the promise of good company.

we dined here with 3.5 million reasons to hate this place. after trying every day for a week to get seated, rain cancellations, an exhaustingly heavy dinner from the night before (from which we still haven't recovered), we had some pretty high standards. but in spite of everything, via carota managed to swiftly knock our socks all the way off. let's start with the fried zucchini. i said: bruh, i would eat these by the pound, ardently and remorselessly. even the salad captured a melodic complexity and managed to stand alone as a dish. the pastas cured me of my lactose intolerance and aromatically refreshed the evening. we finished with that thicccc tiramisu, but i won't write its poetry here.

We ordered two main dishes from Via Carota for take away. When we got home, we were dumbfounded by how small the portions were. My family is Italian so I am used to eating pasta as an appetizer before a main dish but the portion sizes we received were RIDICULOUS when you consider the price of each dish and that the main ingredients are water & flour!!!!
Cacio Pepe $23
Pappardelle al Cinghiale $24
Tasted good but definitely not worth it. Also, EVERY time I walk by to try to eat at the restaurant (they do not accept reservations) they have an attitude.
Meh, Meh, Meh.

Really poor service & pretentious staff. Food is fine. Go to Malatesta, Malaparte, L'Artusi or any of the other great Italian restaurants in the West Village for a superior experience. The bar they own across the street, Pisellino, had an equally pompous host. 0/10 would not recommend.
Worth the wait. Recommend grabbing a hit chocolate across the street if it's chilly out.

Headed to west village to try outdoor dining at a favorite restaurant. Fully booked we decided to try Via Carota. Although we arrived at 6:00 and they don't begin taking reservations until 5:00, they too, were fully booked. The host seemed genuinely disappointed to tell us this - and in the same caring, disappointed tone told at least 5 parties after us. The good news is they provide take out. We ordered the salad with green beans and prosciutto and then the octopus main dish. The salad was big enough for two and delicious. I barely had room to try to octopus. We will definitely be coming here again. Can't wait to try other dishes.

I came here earlier tonight to do something nice for my girl friends birthday. The host told me it could be as long as 2 hours. We waited over 2 hours and nothing. The host told me I had not been waiting 2 hours. I showed her the text I received over two hours before and she shrugged and told me "it's a long wait." They did absolutely nothing. Not even an apology. The host just told me I was wrong. I hate it when places with good food act pretentious like I'm lucky to be there. Maybe if I didn't come from work and I was in a suit like all the other yuppies it would have been quicker? Stop with all the belittling shit and be accountable.

I have been wanting to eat at this restaurant for years, but every time I have tried to get into this no-reservations hot spot, the wait has been well over two hours (or the restaurant has been booked for the night). When I heard they were offering take-out during this time, I was excited to make the trip downtown to try their food. We ordered the piseli salad with peas, prosciutto, and robiolo; and the grilled octopus with green pea pesto. The salad was absolutely delicious - the combination of flavors and high-quality ingredients were perfect. Each of the dishes was a hearty portion and felt like a home-cooked, high-end Italian cuisine treat. We definitely plan to go back to try many of their other dishes.

TL;DR version: Go now! The wait isn't too bad since the city isn't overrun with tourists. The food and service is excellent! 

----

Pre-global pandemic, my BF and I once arrived here around 9pm naively thinking we might be able to snag a late night table. When we checked with the host, she let us know it would be best if we came back around midnight to see about availability. Ha! I miss the old NYC!

The city is especially amazing for residents right now. Restaurant waits are rare so if you've been wanting to try Via Carota now is the time!

BF and I met a friend here for a summer Friday lunch where we could all enjoy a bottle of wine and not have to worry about returning to work. We arrived around 2:15 pm and our wait for a table was about 5 minutes.

It was an overcast day and our server informed us that they were expecting rain. If that happened, they offered to move the umbrella but that was about as much as they could do since no indoor dining right now. She also kindly reminded us that any time we needed to interact with the staff, that we please put on our face masks before doing so. I appreciated the respect for my safety as well as theirs!

We ordered burrata di puglia (cherry tomatoes were so sweet!), scafata (I love fava beans - they are very labor intensive to prepare), funghi (mushrooms reminded me of enoki), and tagliatelle (excellent noodle texture). I can't wait to return to try more dishes!
Great ambience, good social distancing, great service. Cacio e pepe was amazing - would go back!

Popped in for lunch yesterday (no wait at 12:30 on a Tuesday) and it was great! Covid measures are in place and we felt very safe with everyone wearing masks (don't forget to mask up when you want to speak to your server). The food was phenomenal, standouts were the mushroom and cheese appetizer and the fried rabbit. We can't wait to go back.

COVID Take-our order review.
Disclaimer, precovid I had been to the restaurant several times and really enjoyed my experience and the food. However, my take out order was not only disappointing but it was late and the bag was soaking wet / ripped. By far the most expensive takeout we have gotten to date but we wanted to support the restaurant during these tough times. My boyfriend and I got our favorite salad "Insalata Verde" and the wild boar ragu parpadelle. The salad was huge and delicious which was great because it's our favorite. We ordered extra dressing but one of them was completely broken open which soaked and ultimately broke our takeout bag. The pasta was... lack luster. First, the portion size was insanely small... the bowl was barely enough for one person. We were so hungry at this point that we actually laughed at how small the bowl was. The sauce was soooo salty, we honestly couldn't believe it because we live this restaurant so much.
Overall very disappointing. The salad and complimentary biscotti were great but overall not worth it. 

This was $47 for the food alone. After caviar (app) fees and tip for our delivery it was$64.52.

It's worth noting that the menu is also super limited right now.

Lovely to see a "popular" place pushing Cynar and Gran Classico. 

I hope they don't become a thing. Nothing like running into a fellow Cynarite and share a sophisticated nod while acknowledging all the new negroni drinkers. 

Food was ok. Overpriced.

The food is amazing but the service is snide and usually blatantly rude.  I used to frequent this restaurant and it got too hard to justify the experience.  Especially as a local it was shocking to never get credit or recognition for support.  Every time I come here I regret it as I'm reminded how negative and off putting the actual experience is. Once whole dining there a friend noticed it and vowed to never return.  While 40% of the time the servers or hosts are lovely it's that 60% that no matter how good the food may be still leaves a bad taste in my mouth.

Stopped by Via Carota randomly around 2:00pm and decided to grab a late lunch. Heard great things about them but boy... am I disappointed.

I wandered around waiting the street, waiting for someone to acknowledge me, and was told to stand by one of the doors and the hostess will seat me shortly. I waited for about 10 minutes and I was seated by some parked motorcycles. I asked if I can be seated in the area where they have barriers separating the tables and traffic and was told that table was reserved. Ummm... excuse me? You guys do not accept reservations... Needless to say, that table was empty the entire time I ate. Not a great start.

The food was disappointing. It felt like the kitchen lost their salt and didn't bother looking for it. Got the fried calamari, and it was extremely bland. Nice and light breading, but it tasted like oil and lemons because there's no other detectable flavor. My local pizzeria manages to do better than this.

Also tried the meatballs, and ohh boyyy. It seemed like it is made from 100% meat and was so dense - if I lobbed it at someone it would kill them. Breadcrumbs are not a filler in meatballs, it helps them achieve a nice and light texture and it was sorely lacking, especially if you are going to make it Sicilian style with pine-nuts and raisins. To be fair the ground meat does taste like it's high quality - imagine if Subways made their meatballs with Wholefood ingredients but forgot to add salt or any other seasoning, and is dense enough to have it's own gravitational force, you will have the Via Carota meatballs.

Rounded off the meal with their much lauded cacio e pepe and I nearly fell off my chair at the first bite, not in a good way. I was already expecting it to be bland and by then I was ready to rummage through my purse to see if there is a random salt pack in there or if I can sneak off to a nearby bodega to get some, but what shocked me the most was the texture of the pasta. Definitely not al dente, when you bite into the pasta it has a springy texture and consistency more like egg noodles than spaghetti. Between the weird texture and lack of salt, it's nice to see that they have black pepper in their kitchen.

Maybe Jody Williams should actually check on the food, she was sitting in the main dining room doing what looked like paperwork.

I ate about 3-5 bites of each dish and couldn't do it anymore. Waitstaff didn't even wonder what's wrong and just packed everything up. The final insult was when I was paying my check and was looking to add the tip - it turns out my waitress already added a 20% tip for herself. Umm what. Last I checked, there is no auto-gratuity for this restaurant. Honestly I would have tipped about 40% to make up for the fact that I was a solo diner during Covid-19 but that's not the point. The point is you never decide what a diner should tip for them.

Between the poor service by the hostess, bad food and impropriety by the waitress - I will not return. I spent about $120 having a random solo lunch in hopes that it will help the restaurant during Covid-19, now I'm thinking if they do shut down, it wouldn't be the worst thing in the world. Maybe it will allow for restaurants that have salt to open. My Negroni was epic though!

We waited 40 mins for a table with a reservation and another 40+ for food. We had dry calamari, served with no sauce, and very bland pasta. Nothing about this experience was positive. I paid for a bottle of wine and waited forever for my glass to be filled each time because the server was nowhere to be found. I paid $100 to wait over an hour for some of the most bland food I've had in a while. We waited 40 mins for a table because the party ahead of us "wouldn't leave," but the host had no problem harassing us to leave right after our food arrived around 10:30 because the staff wanted to go home. This was the worst dining experience I can remember and I would never recommend this place to anyone.

Maybe 4 stars is just a product of my sky high expectations.  Been a couple of times now. Everything was good, but didn't change my perception of italian food.  

They cacio y pepe was the highlight for sure. Rigatoni and pappardelle were good, but under sauced. Insalata verde is always a go to.  Desserts are always mouthwatering. 

Each time I've gone, the meal took. about 2.5 hours due to the deliberate service. Could be a pro or con depending on what youre looking for.

I've been wanting to try this place for a long time but the long wait times pre-Covid prevented me from doing so. Luckily, I only waited about 20 minutes for brunch a few weekends ago to be seated outdoors.

Neither the service nor the food lived up to the hype. The host appeared annoyed when I requested to be seated at a different table (that was already open and available). The waitress was very nice and helpful for most of the meal but that changed as soon as my card swiped.

As for food, the cacio e pepe was not al dente and the sauce was too heavy. We couldn't eat much of it. Their arancini and brussel sprout salad were excellent though.
Really love the food here especially the caico e Pepe, it really lives up to the hype! Sometimes difficult to get a table but worth the wait.
Food is good but you should hire people that at least act like they want to work there. Very poor attitude and customer service. There's better options to spend money

Worthy of the hype! They have very thoughtful COVID-19 procedures and an outdoor dining setup. We loved everything we ate including the arancini, Tuscan beans and sausage (favorite dish of the meal), famous green salad, carrots in yogurt, and buttery cacio e pepe. We couldn't resist dessert either - the affogato and raspberry crostata were the perfect finish.

An article by Samin Nosrat in the New York Times said the salad is the best in the world. I laugh & wonder how much Samin was paid to write that. First things first don't waste your money on the salad it's. Just. Greens. 

A true testament to the chef & integrity of a restaurant is how well they can cook a chicken. The chicken was prepared the same exact way my Dominican/Italian mother prepared hers. Succulent, fresh, and delicious. 

The Cacio e Pepe: absolutely delicious worth 25$ even though I could make it at home for 10 ;) it's delicious and excellent. 

My glass of wine was exceptionally small

I can't give Via Carota five stars because the ambience is lacking- there isn't any special that stood out from the local Italian places in each neighborhood.
An overall wonderful experience. I kept telling my friend that I want to come back every week. Simply have nothing but good things to say about the food and drink they offer. So enjoyable.

I've been twice. Extremely overpriced and portions are 1/2 size. Good food.  Service was okay.  When asked for the check waiter stated total price with offering a written listing of items.  Just stated the total.  Later asked if I wanted a receipt and of course 10% sir charge.  Additionally I wasn't to restaurant the day before inquiring about reservations.  The manager or owner was just inside restaurant with no mask on sitting at a table.

My boyfriend & I finally got to Via Carota after hearing such great things from a bunch of our friends. It's usually a longgggg wait, but when we arrived to put our name down, an outdoor table surprisingly canceled their reservation and we were lucky enough to fill it! We sat outdoors and all staff wore masks and distanced the tables. 

Since we heard this is one of the best Italian spots in Manhattan, we went all out and ordered the following: Cynar Spritzs, Prosciutto di Parma, Insalata Verde, Tonnarelli Cacio Pepe, Pappardelle Wild Boar Ragu, and Olive Oil Panna Cotta. The meal was out of this world; no disappointments whatsoever! The star dish of the night was the Pappardelle (was even better than the Cacio Pepe). The rest of the menu looks amazing, so we definitely plan to come back soon. 

All in all, the service, ambiance and food/drink are stellar, so I agree with the hype!

Via Carota has decided to impose the covid task. I am in full support of helping local restaurants and all I want is to see these places stay in business. Sadly, this tax is not necessarily distributed to the employees, it goes straight to the owners. I'd love for them to disclose how they are distributing the added tax. 25% was also the tip requested today. How can you say no to that? Then again, as a local resident of over 20 years it's hard to want to continue to eat out, as expenses grow higher for all of us. I hate to think this, but I wonder if some local, still very busy establishments, with long wait lines are taking advantage of the devoted NY'ers also struggling to pay their bills.

This is an easy 5 star, and I don't see how anyone can give it anything less.
Came here with a group of 4 and it was one of the better meals we have had. Most things were "special."
The truffle butter pasta, truffle bruschetta with mushrooms, the caccio a pepe were all incredible and must orders.
The cod was good but not a must.
The deserts were all very good except for the chocolate mouse which had hazelnuts inside which through me off. I myself am not a a tiramisu guy but the others lovedddd it.
This is a must go and order as much as you can :)

I had visited here few times before the pandemic and honestly the food quality hasn't been up to the level before. The arancini was over fried without much taste. Service wise, I understand it was hard to accommodate the situation but the waitress was rushing us ordering/eating/getting the check... wasn't a great experience for me this time and a bit disappointed.

In my opinion best Italian restaurant in NYC. Everything is fantastic you really cannot go wrong. My personal favorites are the cacio e pepe, roasted artichokes, insalata verde and many others! Very hard to get a table but absolutely worth the wait. Excellent set up for outdoor dining the service is always a 10/10!

The maitre d was incredibly rude. He could had easily just told us there was no availability, but instead opted to look at us like we were nothing for having the audacity to ask him a question. No food is worth that attitude.
Got takeout from here for a date night. Everything was fantastic!! The grilled artichokes were my favorite but you can't pass up the arancini, sausage/olive croquettes, the cacio e Pepe

The day after dining here, we found a tiny line below the menus on their website stating that a 10% NYC covid recovery charge will be added to the bill.  We wish this was disclosed to us before the waiter took our drink orders.  The waiter also did not give us a physical bill, only verbally confirmed our entire order before handing us the credit card reader.  

As your customers, we are already supporting your business by coming and paying for your food, paying tips to your waitstaff so you don't have to pay them a real salary, and as taxpayers we contributed to the relief package benefiting small businesses like yours.  If those aren't enough and you feel the need to charge the entire 10% surcharge passed by the city, at least be upfront about it and communicate this to your customers.  But if I had known I would not choose to support your business by dining here.

Was so happy to visit Via Carota for dinner the other evening. The food was delicious, unfortunately there was a lot about everything else that was left to be desired, covid nonwithstanding. 

Due to inclement weather, we were able to get a table very quickly. The team was nice from the get-go. 

Unfortunately, the wind started to blow very strongly, blowing leaves and dirt from the metal roof structure erected for their outdoor dining extension - directly onto our food and into our drinks & water. Water glasses coated in dirt. Stingy pours of wine, diluted by dirt.

Despite multiple attempts to ask politely if we could move tables due to the leaves & dirt, we were left to fend for ourselves. Every 5 minutes or so (max!), we had to build our own tent of coats and napkins, held up against whatever direction the wind happened to be blowing. No single person from the staff ever got back to us on moving the table or asked whether we were okay (we saw them moving others, seating new guests). Our water glasses were coated, inside and out, with dirt. Our food, each dish "garnished" with 5 leaves or more from the dirty rooftop.

All in all, the food was good (until the leaves and dirt descended). The service was friendly, but far from attentive. If you're charging 20% service, 10% covid fund fee, could you at least look after your guests?

Out of the many restaurants I've tried in New York over the past few months, this has stood out to me by far. 

The pasta is so fresh and delicious, and you definitely need to get the cacio pepe. Negroni and calamari were delicious as well. 

Beware that if you don't have a reservation, you will be waiting a very long time. We came on a Wednesday night and had to wait 3 hours for a table, but if you're not starving and have time to walk around, it's with it. 

Coming here on the weekends is even harder, I'm not sure I would even try that without a reservation.

2 stars because we didn't even get a chance to sit at a table. Not that it was busy as we were IN A LINE at 5pm to even be spoken to. The manager didn't acknowledge the people waiting at the front door only a server did as he was playing around with the iPad not even bothering to look up. Only be told by a server to wait on the side with a plethora of others. If you're busy say something. If you can't sit people at your first sitting, say something. It was freezing and we heard good things about the pasta but to see a completely empty restaurant with oblivious observations; we went to Lupa instead where we were acknowledged upon arrival and graciously seated. We want to support restaurants during this time but only those who value their guests. The front door is the first impression and this was certainly our last.

This place is simply amazing. The quality of their ingredients is top notch and the service is impecable. We started with grilled artichokes and mushrooms with scamorza. The veggies were cooked to perfection and the natural flavors shined through. For main dish, we shared ragu di cinghiale and Cacio Pepe. They were both amazing. The ragu was very rich, flavorful and tender. The Cacio Pepe waz executed perfectly, not too dry, not too saucy. For dessert, we tried a Zabaione. Omg! It's been years since I had Zabaione and this was to die for. Definitely a must.

I've been dying to try Via Carota for ages, ever since the NY Times published an article calling their green salad the best green salad in the world. Yes, I know that says something about my tastes and the things that bring me excitement and joy ... and yes, that includes green salads. 

However, you know when you build up something so much in your head that when you finally come across the real thing, you're a wee bit disappointed? (Much like that time I saw James Franco, back when he was doing his MFA at Columbia. Let's just say homeboy was looking a little rough.) 

The green salad came in this enormous pouf of butter lettuce, endive, watercress, smothered in this dressing. First bite was, well, underwhelming. Maybe the dressing needed a little more acidity or zing; I did see on the NYT article that they drizzle rather than dress the leaves. Agree with my friend that the salad got a lot better the more I ate it. 

The star of the meal was definitely the pappardelle with wild boar ragu. The pasta was the perfect level of al dente. Eat a bowl of this and you'll definitely feel nice and cozy under the heat lamps. Perfect fall/winter dish. 

Tbh, I don't really remember much of the desserts (except the crostata was just a tad dry, would've been great with classic vanilla ice cream), because I was trying hard to savor the taste of the pasta.

Overall, this spot seems to serve solid meals whatever you choose. It is on the pricier side for the portion size - the two of us got 4 dishes which was a very full lunch ($100+), but we were able to finish everything, but that's the main reason I knocked it down a star.

'nduja arancini: 3.5/5 The ideal crispy/chewy texture, but the spicy pork was a little off for me. It was a bit of a thick paste that was supposed to contrast with the richness, but wasn't tasty to me. 

Castelfranco: 3/5 We got this salad instead of the Insalata Verde, and the flavors were all put so well together. I was surprised by the thick mayo-like consistency of the dressing, and for my personal taste, I like my salad to be lightly dressed.

Coniglio fritto: 5/5 This fried rabbit tasted like the highest elevation of fried chicken. It was so tender and juicy, and the breading was nicely seasoned. It also came with fried bread with roasted garlic that nicely complemented the rabbit. This was the highlight of the meal for me.

Pappardelle: 3/5 Wild Boar Ragu's tomato sauce had a much darker flavor, perhaps due to the wild boar meat? It was good and the pasta had a nice consistency, but wouldn't get again.

The Italian food here hits the spot as standard West Village Italian fare but the food itself doesn't really stand out compared to the top tier like L'Artusi or Don Angies. Don't get me wrong the place is good, but West Village just has too much good Italian food.

Of the dishes, the cacio pepe was definitely the highlight, being pretty well made and tasty. The boar ragu on the other hand was a bit salty and mediocre. 

The salad was a good start, but was still just a salad at the end of the day.

Via Carota was everything I heard it would be. We walked up and got in for outdoor dining on election night - I couldn't believe we got a table. I want to go back to try the entire menu. The fried olives were insane... they are the size of golf balls! Service was professional and wonderful.

After discovering what cacio e pepe from my trip in Roma, I needed to find the RIGHT place nearest to me & my search led me to here! And that's what I got! The portion looks larger in the pics, but don't be fooled this buttery, creamy, cheesy, starchy, peppery chewy fresh exquisitely simple yet intricate pasta dish that is a belly-full! It also is served with a hefty topping of shredded cheese...

I enjoyed every bite. Of course as you munch down into the bowl, the noodles get slathered into the pooling of peppery butter. Wowies, a star dish. Couldn't fit any apps or dessert honestly.

Ordered a hot toddy, not knowing what it was but "HOT" since I was freezing cold after long distance walking without offering socially-distanced indoor dining huhuu... but it was strong! Lemony! And hot! I had to unconventionally ask for more honey (don't judge me! I shoulda got a latte instead hehe) Anyways, this didn't affect my rating at all, just not my preference of drink..

Also side note... they have 2 types of seating areas: one underneath the heater or without! Good luck & enjoy!!

We ordered takeout through Caviar tonight. We dined there in person before the pandemic and the takeout version did not disappoint. The food traveled well -- we live in Midtown and it arrived thoughtfully and elegantly packaged with bonus biscotti. We had the Cacio E Pepe, Green Salad, Wild Boar Ragu and the Tiramisu. In a year with a lot of takeout orders, this food was among the best. We look forward to doing it again!

Ordered pickup for NYE; placed the order a day in advance and chose 6:30.  After arriving at 6:25 I was told food would be ready in "10 minutes".  AN HOUR later, my food was ready.  Stood outside in the cold waiting, with zero updates from the staff after the first "10 minute" wait time - all while my husband waited with a screaming child in our car.  I get you are trying to recoup as much business as possible in these trying times but, come on - be transparent with your customers (I wasn't the only one waiting forever outside in line for late orders) - food was good but certainly not worth the hassle and blatant disregard for their clients.

Of course the food at our favorite spot is the best but our server Angela is worth a mention. She is always funny, polite and a familiar face we love seeing!  We always look forward to seeing Angela. Superb as always!!

Horrible service. Asked for a reservation for a heated seat, waited an hour for the table. When we arrived we were sat in a non-heated section and a heated seat was available. Asked if we could be moved and was told that seat was already spoken for and that there are no other seats. Spoke to the manager who said they place people on a rolling basis, no designation for heated or not heated, so we should have been able to seat at that open table. He did not offer any fix for this problem even though we told him we have been waiting, only chose here because it was heated. 

Completely rude, horrible service and a huge waste of time and money. Can't believe we get service like this in NYC.

I've always loved Via Carota so this feedback is only based on my last experience which was 1) during Covid period when only outdoor seating is permitted, and 2) during the cold cold January winter month. We were probably given the worst table at the restaurant during our visit which was just at the entrance beside some tree which meant the pavement floor wasn't even and my chair was half on the pavement and half on the planted gravel area. The table was unsheltered from the cold wind and there were no heaters provided. So while I watched other guests seated in the covered veranda area under nice heated radiators enjoying their meals (there was a table available which I thought was for us but the server told us that the table was reserved) we had to rush through ours since we were freezing our butts off and our food was getting cold almost as soon as they arrived. Within 5 mins, our pasta was clumped up which really ruined the experience for a friend whom I brought to this place for the first time. I understand that it is not the restaurant's fault at all and on hindsight, I only blame myself for having accepted that table that was offered to us. But perhaps as a feedback, the restaurant should not offer tables that are unsheltered from any wind and cold that would affect both their overall food quality and diner's experience. I would definitely go back to Via Carota but probably not during the winter time and pandemic when only outdoor seating is available.

Maria took great care of us, made nice recommendations, and just had a really pleasant vibe. Thanks so much for the great service and a nice evening!

I'm also so glad this restaurant has you wear a mask whenever staff is present at the table! I've been other places where they don't care and it's a much less pleasant experience

Outdoor dining was set up fairly nicely and the servers were polite and attentive. Cocktails were nice and strong. We were a party of 2 and they kept serving the dishes one at a time. One of the pasta dishes were served and when the server came by I told her that we would wait for the other dishes to be served to have together. She went on to say that she was going to bring them out after we had finished the pasta. Why on earth would we want to eat one dish at a time. Each plate was also too oily. Not anywhere close to any good Italian I've had in the past. We also had a reservation for 830 and outdoor dining closes at 10 and they didn't seat us until close to 9 on top of this so overall not a great experience.

We came for Saturday brunch! The outdoor seats were fairly spaced apart and they had heaters at the top of the outdoor tent are. I enjoyed their oat milk latte to start. 

While the handmade pasta was good, my favorite dish was the cavoletti- shredded Brussel sprout salad with pecorino, apple and walnut. The grilled mushroom was also really good! I think we agreed the starters were the highlights.

Be aware this restaurant charges 10% COVID recovery fee, not to mention $2 for usually free bread which is hard and cold and only 3 small pieces. Main dishes portion are so small definitely overpriced. And their "famous" $20 salad is just a pile of green leafs. They'll show you the bill on a screen with things you ordered but only total price and then you insert your credit card, a default 20% tip showed up.
Worst of all while all tables are eating and talking, a homeless maskless guy walk table by table asking for money and say rude things if you ignore him. The restaurant staff are all inside no one even bother to come out to stop the guy.
Have been dining out so many restaurants all over Manhattan since December 2020 and this is the only one we said we will never come back. I wish I could give zero star.

God damn that was GOOD!
The butter anchovy crostini ... there are no words ...it's a slice of bread...four anchovies...half a stick of butter...and worth every calorie. 
Also the rabbit...very delicious...and the bread it comes with is a showstopper.
For dessert, you're never too full for an espresso martini...and who needs a dessert when they have this deliciousness?! Not this girl.
Full disclosure: I tried my friend's wild boar ragu tagliatelle and was way underwhelmed. Oh well...nobody is perfect.

Extremely disappointed with my experience at Via Carota this evening. My group and I arrived a little after 6:30 and were accommodated with a smaller table since we did not have a reservation. We waited approximately 15 minutes before our server came over to inform us the menu was to be found online and we had to keep masks on when the servers were around.
