We ordered our drinks and food which all came out in a timely manner. The food was mediocre but the service was terrible. I have worked in the food industry for many years and never experienced anything like it. The waitress never came over after we were brought our food (by another wait staff) and we had to ask for the bill after sitting for 30 min once the meal was done. We eventually had to ask another server for the check plus the bread that was never brought to our table. The disappointing part is we are a crew who does a few rounds of drinks and dessert. When we expressed our displeasure to our waitress she had offered a cold apology and then we watched her walk into the restaurant to yell at what appeared to be the manager. With so many delicious Italian fare places nearby in the west village with bigger portions and better service at the same price point (carbone, bar pitti, don Angie) you're better off taking your business elsewhere. Unfortunately, not worth the hype

Via Carota is just astonishing. Sooooo good and well priced. Everything that I have tried was really great and I would come back to have it again! Not to mention, the service was great and the staff was very helpful. Via Carota is definitely one of my go to's when I come to this area.

Around 3 stars for food it's not bad, but definitely minus 1 star for the awful outdoor setup and price.  If you want to eat here make sure you reserve a table in advance and bring 3-4 people.  Only 1/3rd of the tables have heat lamps and they are all 4-tops.

For how much money this place makes I'm 100% sure they could have done a better job with their outdoor seating.  Otherwise enjoy scarfing your $20-30 a plate food down as fast as possible before it freezes over due to cold weather.

Food is not bad but it's not worth the hype. We had the mushroom appetizer, cacio e pepe, arancini and fried sardine. Everything was well made but portion is small. 

Also we weren't impressed with the outdoor setup. This is definitely one of the pricey restaurants in the neighborhood and they only had very few heat lamps. They definitely could've spent a bit more to make their customers more comfortable while dining in the frigid weather.  Yet we weren't allowed to book in advance with 2 people or sit in those 4 seaters, so it's just sitting on those cold steel chairs while trying to wolf down the food before it gets cold. We probably waited for the seating longer than the time took us to finish the food, just overall wasn't a pleasant dining experience. :(

It's been hard to get a reservation here for the past few months. We finally were able to on a Monday night. This place has been on my list of restaurants to go to for a while now. I had very high expectations, but they just weren't met.

For Covid precautions- staff were wearing double masks, menu was online, and you must wear your mask when speaking to your server/waiter. 

We started off with the pere e gorgonzola bruschetta. This came on a long piece of bread sliced into 4 pieces. I really enjoyed the gorgonzola, walnut and honey combination. However, I couldn't really taste the pear. Maybe the slices of pear should've been thicker to get the actual flavor. It seemed like the pear was just put on for decoration rather than flavor. We also ordered bread and olive oil. The bread was cold and tough to chew. I then got the cacio e pepe for my entree. The bowl seemed small but it definitely filled me up. This dish was very greasy for me, and there were chunks of cheese in the sauce, which didn't have the smooth consistency I'm used to with cacio e pepe. I also ordered the broccoletti, which was broccoli rabe with garlic. You could really taste the fresh garlic in this dish, but wasn't too overpowering. I didn't find anything to be spectacular and memorable with the food here. 

The service was great. They would come by frequently to ask us if we wanted to order anything else and would fill up our water often.

A friend was in town and we were surprisingly able to snag a same day reservation on a weekend (granted it was a 4:15pm reservation). Everything was amazing from the appetizers to the dessert. 

We ordered the burrata & prosciutto, bruschetta with pear and gorgonzola, brussel sprouts for our appetizers. For our entrees we ordered the cacio e pepe, pappardelle boar ragu, and fried rabbit. And for dessert we got the hazelnut semifreddo and tiramisu. 

The pasta was cooked absolutely perfectly (can't go wrong with any of their pastas) and the fried rabbit (which I'm typically not a fan of) was crispy, non gamey, and very delicious. I would 10/10 come back. 

Only caveat is that during Covid they are not seating tables larger than 4 people. 2 of our friends who wanted to join had to either wait for another table or go elsewhere.

Impossible to make a reservation. They say it is a walk-in but the only tables for walk in are the bad ones on the side walk. Resy is supposed to help with a 14-days in advance reservation (really, 14 days? Is this a Michelin restaurant?)...but guess what? Not even that work as I tried to book for May and nothing is available. Very bad customer experience my dear via Carota!

To be clear: this place gets a five star for the food.

Great salads, pasta, and so much more. Eager to come again.

So why the four star rating? Believe it or not - out waiter was great, but the hostess was extremely rude and stand-off-ish. I was actually pretty surprised, as it's usually the other way around, but it almost led us to want to go to another restaurant and not wait for our table.

Nonetheless, glad we ate here. 

I know we all have off days, but seems like the culture of the hostesses at this place and how they treat customers can get a little fixing, here.
The food is good and service as well if you get a seat.  They are horrible with reservations.  Horrible

One of my favorite restaurants. We don't come here enough because there is always a wait, but everything we've ever tried has been exceptional. They have a knack for elevating really simple ingredients/dishes. Veggies and salads are usually an afterthought (for me at least), but here, they're standout. I don't even like rabbit, but trying the fried rabbit here was the first time I did. It's a great place to be adventurous with your ordering.

Ordered from here once during the pandemic, but we don't live close, so it wasn't the same. Can't wait to come back soon and dine in person!

Absolutely stunning food and vibes. Went over the weekend and was surprised that there was no wait. We ordered their cacio e pepe and pappardelle, both were outstanding. I definitely think the cacio e pepe was my favorite. Creamy, perfectly al dente, and the pepper created a distinctive flavor. 

The salad was very refreshing and the ideal dish to balance out the heavy carbs we inhaled afterward. 

Super friendly service, loved the outdoor seating. I am returning to try more dishes very very soon.

The food (and the Negronis) is great, but there's a 70% chance that the hostess/host will give you some attitude for just daring to want to put your name down. Good god. They make it seem like they're doing you a huge favor by telling you how long the wait is, and they would in a really hostile way tell you that you can't get seated at a four person table unless the entire party is here (I get it, but also it was Easter Sunday at 11am and half of your restaurant is empty, and I was the only moron standing around waiting)

I live in the area and come here probably once a month or so, but tbh if I see that it's one of the meaner hostesses I walk away. You can order most of this stuff on Caviar anyway

Some favorite dishes:
- Fried olives & sausage
- Cacio et pepe
- Pork belly
- Steak
My favorite Italian place in NY, it's always a joy to explore this menu! Was there for dinner with a friend and we both loved everything we ate!

Our favorite local spot these days, even for delivery. Most of the dishes are great, but our favorites are the insalate verde and polpette. The drinks are really amazing too - we have been doing the martini italiano on delivery, and it's so well made. We can't wait until we're back to eating in-person at the bar on a nice Friday afternoon!
Totally overpriced ...the food is at best terrible ...the servicethe waiters are mean and arrogantQuite frankly nothing tasted good nothing..,,

This place is pricey, but the Cacio E Pepe was 100% worth it. This was the best pasta that I've had outside of Italy. I've never had a good cacio e Pepe and if you ever want to try a simple yet flavorful dish, I would recommend trying this once in your life. 

Everything about this dish is what I crave. I could eat this everyday and for every meal. It wasn't too heavy on the dairy, yet evenly distributed. The pasta was handmade and perfectly al dente. 
The octopus was crispy on the outside and super soft and chewy. 
The artichokes I could pass on, but it was full of flavor and tartiness. I just wouldn't say there was anything special to it. 

It has a reputation and I'm glad that I experienced what they had to offer first hand.

This is the second time we had take out delivered in a week, so clearly the food is worth repeating.  The first time we ordered the proscuitto and burrata with some bread (which there was an additional fee for) as well as the tiramisu.  Everything was delicious although very pricey.  
Last night, we ordered the fritto misto which was out of this world.  Cooked to perfection, amble serving size, absolutely delicious.  The canellini beans and spinach were delicious and the olive oil it came in was superb, but for $19, it amounted to about half a cup of beans and a few spinach leaves.  I couldn't believe they would serve such a small portion.  Sadly, the broccoli rab was so terrible we threw out the entire thing.  For $19, we got a bland bunch of tough stems that was truly terrible.  This is such a basic dish and so easy to do well...can't understand how this could be served.  On the up side, the tagliatelli was fantastic!  Worth every penny although it was actually ice cold when it arrived.  To finish the meal, we once again ended with the tiramisu which was prepared to perfection and not too sweet.  Unfortunately, we will not be ordering again.  For the price. it's just not worth it.

Arrived at 8 for our reservation and were seated at 8:32. Then there was another 10 minute wait for a waiter, with attitude, to arrive and take a drink order, and another 10 minute wait for him to bring the bottle, which had been sitting on the bar. We didn't see him again, not even to refill wine glasses, which we certainly can and did do, until we ordered dessert and another bottle of wine, seemingly to his chagrin. The food was good. Nothing spectacular given the hype. Other similar restaurants, Rezdora, Lilia etc. have better food, infinitely better service and make for a much better experience.

Meh. Not worth it. Definitely riding their name and local reputation to success more than their quality. Fritto was too salty, the verdure left something to be desired, and the pasta  wasn't especially great. The bussers were really friendly and polite, but the server and hostess  seemed to be going through the motions, not really caring or engaging. Kinda like they knew others would be coming whether we came back or not (and they would not be wrong, there was a line down the street during off hours). Arrogant vibe and WAY overpriced! I just expect more.

This place is a New York favorite and everyone knows it. After covid they opened up a massive outdoor dining area that's especially stunning in the summertime. They are no longer walk in only so you can reserve via Resy, just be sure to plan in advance.

I personally think their funghi is one of the best starters. The creamy texture and the layer of cheese is exquisite. The tagliatelle is of course a staple, but I think pairing it with the pappardelle is the way to go. The tomato based sauce and the wild boar rage are a nice balance to the creamy cheesy sauce with the tagliatelle. We got the steak (which kind of looks like a burger) to end off our meal. It's extremely decadent and just melts in your mouth.

We weren't feeling like drinking so we ordered sparkling lemonades (off menu) on a whim. Such a delicious summer drink, I highly recommend.

Great food esp the pasta but here's the issue. We felt a little like we got hustled.  Owner, please take note that it is not  a good take away as a customer.  
Chilly night and got colder as we sat. Asked waitress to turn on the heater - which are above each table on the street side.  Her response was "oh!  I'm not sure, I will check." She never  came back with an answer so we tracked her down asked again and she said her GM told her they couldn't to get the door to the boiler room to open. We knew it was a blow-off answer but we let it go. I asked the GM myself and she didn't seem to have a problem and offered the heater on or instead, "why don't we turn down the plastic side flap to block the wind". The flap seemed to help a bit without the heater but not enough. We let it all go as we didn't want to make a big deal about it.  Lastly, the bill contained a $35 dollar Covid surcharge.  We paid via a charge card device as the waitress hovered looking down at the device adding pressure for a good tip. The device offered tip suggestions starting at 20%. We typically would have tipped more but felt vary patronized at this point.  There was no way to tip pre covid charge or pretax on that device so they got away with another hustle. I won't be returning.
I enjoy my food at this place I wanted to try it for so long and the service is good real Italian food

Food is fabulous but taking a star off for how snobby the hostess here is. I've been going here on Sunday's for a while and the experience almost becomes unpleasant because of how folks are treated by the hostess. 
But the cacio e Pepe, Ragu pappardelle, arancini and carrots do a solid job of compensating!

Food is spot on when you can get a seat or a delivery. But getting a seat is impossible so don't waste your time. Someone looked at me with a straight face and said three hour wait. Like are you kidding me just say booked for the night and get rid of attitude. You serve pets not fckin dreams. 

And ordering from there is a crapshoot as well. 

Save your money and time and go to Italy and eat all of this everyday at every restaurant for 1/4 of the price.

Yummy fresh preps. A little pricey for the portion size but its totally worth it even for vegetarians. I chose Asparagi verdi and stracci pesto as my entree and main and it was yum enough to polish both the portions!

I don't understand why this restaurant has such a good reputation. To be fair, the food is good, but not that good, especially when considering the price. Our bill was around $72 for 2 small pastas and bread. Honestly, I think Italian restaurants like II Corallo Trattoria, where my partner and I can eat for around $35, tastes almost as good. I think Via Carota is one of those places that you expect to be amazing because other people and media outlets hype it up, but let me tell you, there is no substance backing these claims. I don't get it. 

There were two things that made me particularly annoyed and made me feel like the restaurant was cutting corners. First, what kind of Italian restaurant charges for bread? I don't think I've been to another Italian restaurant in nyc that does that, and I've been to a lot. We decided to get it because we thought it would be special and amazing since they charge for it. It was completely average and underwhelming bread. It's only $2, but seriously, if you're going to charge for bread, make it taste better than restaurants that don't charge you a penny for it. 

Second, in the bathroom, they have aesop soap containers filled with non aesop soap. For anyone who doesn't know, aesop is a very expensive soap brand with nice smelling soaps. I always get excited when I see these in bathrooms because it is satisfying to wash your hands and the smell is incredible. Turns out it was completely generic soap. They filled an Aesop soap container with the most generic and cheap soap you could possibly buy. Where else are they cutting corners? 

There are plenty of amazing italian restaurants in nyc that don't cut corners and where you get better bang for your buck. Out of the 50 or so that I've been to, this one is the worst when taking into account value. Don't recommend.

We ordered 4 different dishes for 3. And we receive 4 small plates (like an appetizer) for a price of $100. Total rip off ! Waiter was not friendly and temperature was very cold (as they opened all doors). Don't go there !!!

A friend and I came here, unabashedly, for a second dinner because we're far too indecisive but holy moly was it delicious. It was early April with only outdoor seating and was absolutely freezing and even THEN it was totally worth it. 

We ordered the cacio e Pepe and fried rabbit. My god. Chefs kiss. The cacio was perfectly creamy and the fried rabbit really came through. It came with a piece of fried bread that and taught me fried bread is something I never realized was missing from my life. The wine was good, the service was attentive, and the food was memorable. I can't wait to come back.

I was finally able to stop in here with some friends on a Saturday night. We weren't able to make a reservation, so we came around 4:30pm to put our names on the waitlist. We were prepared for a long wait, but to our surprise, they said they could seat us outside around 7pm. They will send you a text and you have 15 mins to get to the restaurant to claim your table. 

Once seated, we looked over the menu and got some drinks to start. They have a lot of Italian wines, beers, and cocktails, so something for all palates. As a starter, we ordered the carrots and burrata/prosciutto. I ordered the Boar Ragu for my main. The food was good. The carrots were especially good  and were served with a nice yogurt sauce. My ragu was delicious, but my only knock is that it was an extremely small portion for the price of $27. 

Ambience was nice. We sat street-side, but didn't feel bothered by cars or people passing by. They had socially distanced indoor seating as well. Our server was good too. She came over to check on us and made sure were enjoying everything. 

Overall, I'm glad I was able to stop in. Like I mentioned, my knock is that the food is a bit overpriced for what you get. That being said, I'd still come back as the food was good and the vibe was fun.

I tried Via Carota for the first time a few weeks ago, and overall, I had an enjoyable experience. It was a rainy spring Friday, but the outdoor seating comfortably protected me and my date from the elements. Service was solidly friendly and welcoming throughout the visit, and like many restaurants these days, you can access the menu via a QR code.

I shared the artichokes with anchovies and mint and the fava beans with escarole while choosing the stracci with pesto Genovese as my main dish.  The portions were moderately sized, which helped me avoid feeling stuffed, and the food was flavorful yet perfect for a light late lunch. Dessert was an affogato, and it's hard to go wrong with coffee and ice cream! I would definitely return again given the great first impression this restaurant made.

I want to start saying that the food was amazing! But I don't know if makes up for how bad we where treated by the women host of the restaurant! We made our reservation many days ago and we were looking forward it, as soon as we get in I needed to use the restroom and when I was trying to ask for it the hostess screamed to me and my boyfriend to get outside several times without letting me ask for the restroom or even asking if we had a reservation which she thought we didn't!
Via Carota never disappoints. Everything on the menu is amazing and has remained one of the best spots in New York for years. A must visit for the west village
Acciughe E Burro. Wow. Do yourself a favor and order this along with the Olive All'ascolana.

Absolutely loved this meal. We went in the pouring rain and were worried about our outdoor table, but the set up was perfectly sheltered and even had heaters still working in May. We ordered nduja arancini, carciofi alla griglia, tonnarelli, pappardelle and semifreddo. The pasta was of course amazing but the arancini and artichokes held their own--highly recommend trying one of the many veggie dishes on the menu. The semifreddo was good but had whole hazelnuts throughout, so just something to be aware of for people who don't like whole nuts. Can't wait to come back and try more veggies (and more pasta of course)!
This restaurant is phenomenal. Phenomenal pasta, pretty good wine and wine list, great atmosphere and great service. Worth the wait and the splurge.
Came here while visiting NYC from SF. Loved the appetizer salad and the rainbow carrots. Only reason this place didn't get 5 stars was because the cacio pepe pasta was a little too salty.

Visited for our June date night. No wait for indoor dining - which requires full vaccination. We are, but they don't ask for proof. That was disappointing,  but fingers crossed. (We are not yet dining indoors without full vaccination requirement due to unvaccinated children). 

Anyway, we started with the artichokes, the green salad, and the arancini. All delicious, but the artichokes and salad were the standouts. (Artichokes were life changing, salad was really delicious- surprisingly so.)

Alongside these, we had a whiskey sour and the Italian beer option. (Yum to both!)

For pasta, we did the Cacio e Pepe and the wild boar ragu. Good combo. First was very good-such fresh noodles. Boar was great, too, but I'd try another compliment next time. No dessert-too stuffed!

Service and atmosphere was great. Wonderful experience.

This restaurant gets four stars because of the people that work here. First off, thank you to the person that gave us a reservation because it was our 35th wedding anniversary.  Very kind.  Secondly, thank you to the maitre'd who still seated us even though we were 30 minutes late because of the parade traffic.  Thirdly, thank you to our server...a sweet young lady who got us settled, ordered,  and served in just 45 minutes so we could watch the sunset at Little Island.
Food-wise, we shared a great bottle of champagne with our zucchini fritti and the tagliatelle.  Everything was delicious but the pasta was just a tad overcooked.  
All in all, a very good experience.  We would definitely recommend this restaurant.  (and, next time, we are getting the insalada verde...everyone around us had it and said it was amazing)

Knocked off the star due to the service. 

THE HOST WILL LIE TO YOU ABOUT THE WAIT TIME FOR A TABLE depending on how he judges you.

This is the first time I spoke with the tall slender man. HE TOLD ME THERE WERE 59 PEOPLE ON THE WAITING LIST TO GET A TABLE. Talk about LOL!!! This isn't a club. 

If they tell you it's a long wait ignore them and tell them to add you to the waitlist. I was told a 5 hour wait and I got a table in 9 minutes. 

And even if it was true it's mathematically impossible for him to text all 59 people and give them 10 minutes to respond before I got a table.

Anyways food is good as always. Try the spice carrot appetizer! 

Also- they are charging for bead and olive oil now. They didn't use to do that.

The best meal I had in two weeks in the city. Fresh pasta was the BEST! The Cacio E Pepe was truly next level with such amazing flavors. The salads were also great, especially the little gem. Grilled Octopus was cooked perfectly and not at all chewy. The Fried Rabbit was insane--it blew my mind how good it was. I will be returning as soon as I can.

Fair if you like small trendy portions. As a resident for over 30 years, i have to say despite popular reviews, food is nice. Service, however, a little less to be desired. A host/manager, Andre, has no customer service delicateness that most of us in service are accustomed to.  Aaaaaaaaaand won't go back or patronize sister restaurants like Isodi, Buvette, or Bar Pisellino.
But please experience for yourself. Otherwise I suggest more traditional, IMHO, less monopolized Italian food like Malatesta or Babbo for even more upscale.

Don't understand the excitement about the Cacio e Pepe. It's a mistake. A big buttery mistake that isn't even edible.

Service was very good. Nice wine selection. Other dishes were good, not great. I was expecting a lot better.

Via Carota has always been considered a New York staple that is classic and cool and maybe not so effortless. The food is good and while the menu rarely changes, except for a few specials that are typically delicious, you really cannot order wrong. While some rave about this being the best of the best for NY Italian. The inability to get seated (or having to wait 2+ hours) is slightly deterring.

Where do I begin. The owners of this former gem seem to have lost their values. $25 for overly salty cacio e pepe even with wine. The point is. Even Olive Garden doesn't charge you for bread. While
It may be advertised on the menu, $2 for bread and olive oil. I have never seen a restaurant in NYC or even Oklahoma City charge for bread unless it's a dish itself, even don angie offers you 3 pieces of complimentary garlic bread upon request, but maybe that's why they have a Michelin star. The server was incredibly aggressive In taking our order and we just felt that they wanted "our" table back even though they had multiple openings and we were spending well. We were asked 7 times
If we were done. It was a perfect way to not make us feel valued. The $2 bread seems desperate. Just don't offer it. When you pay with the handheld card reader outdoors the minimum suggested gratuity is 20%. This place is a joke.

I don't understand the hype. First of all the no reservations system is a horrible experience and the restaurant staff is rude and unbothered.

The food is solid but there's no reason for the hype. There's better Italian restaurants with better pasta nearby without rude service and long waits.

Also, if you're sitting outside be prepared for your meal to be interrupted by the many homeless people that live nearby.

Wow - this surprised me. Exceeded my expectations food-wise - friends and I shared cacio pepe, papardelle pasta, grilled artichokes, and insalada verde salad. Each dish was excellent. Drinks were also great - I had the negroni rosa , very refreshing. Dessert was also tasty. The manager, Andre was very accommodating after moving to a separate table later on. I would definitely make a trip from BK again. Thanks guys for a great night.

Totally over rated and over priced. Staff is lovely and the food is good but not worth the hype or the wait or the cost. As a lifetime New Yorker I can promise you this is NOT one of the best restaurants in NY. If you want phenomenal homemade Italian, fresh, real and fairly priced go to Frank on 2nd  Ave & 5th st or Max in Tribeca. Now those are some of the best restaurants in NY. This place is tourist hype.

Wild boar Ragu- excellent
Tagliatelle - the tables favorite 
Stracci Pesto - good but not great
Grilled mushrooms - excellent
Grilled artichoke- very good
Broccoletti - meh

As with most popular West Village restaurants, it is almost impossible to get reservations here. My friend and I decided to take a chance on a Saturday evening, the plan was to put our names on the waitlist and go get a drink elsewhere. The host told us that they were booked for the night, but he offered to take down our name and let us know if any spots opened up. Within 30 minutes of putting down our name we got a text saying they had a table for us, giving all these details just to say that don't drive yourself crazy over reservations. So many people came after us and still got a table on a Saturday night. 

Now for the food we tried the zucchini fries (it was amazingggg!!), burrata (good), cacio Pepe and pesto pasta (good), olive oil cake (passable, go to L'artusi instead). The wine pours were really stingy. The whole experience was 3.5 stars really, but our server was amazing and that's why rounding it to 4. It's worth the hype, but not if you have a 3hr wait. I'd gladly come back!

Much like the sister Bar Pisellino across the street, I think Via Carota is quintessential west village in that it's cute, it's expensive, and it's overblown. Hard to get in, easy to get out. We put our names down for a walk in around 5:30 and we were seated around 8:30. Not terrible. We had a cute little private room secluded in the back. Service was fast and attentive. The Negroni I started the night with was good albeit a little weak. 

We began splitting a salad, the arancini, and the grilled artichoke. Salad was boring, bitter, and unidimensional. Arancini and grilled artichoke were both great.

For mains, we had the Cacio e Pepe, the risotto, and the svizzerina. Cacio e Pepe was good. Risotto was missable and again, too unidimensional. It didn't go far beyond risotto, cream, and lemon. Svizzerina was possibly my favorite dish of the night but at the end of the day it's a glorified burger patty.

Desserts (olive oil cake and tiramisu) were forgettable. Tiramisu was fine, olive oil cake was notably bad. 

There were a couple things they were out of through the night which was disappointing. 

It was a nice dinner and I'm glad I went but can't imagine I would return.

Disappointed. Very very salty. I had the Mixed Fried Seafood and it came with no sauce. In addition, the fried shrimp
was served with the shell on. I have never had shells on fried shrimp. Not a fan. My husband had the peppardelle which was salty but tastier.

Everything about Via Carota was amazing! We dined on the outdoor terrace which was beautiful. There was a chance of rain and though it didn't end up raining, it was nice to see that the outdoor seating was still covered enough that we would have been able to continue sitting outside! To start, we ordered the insalata verde (delicious) and bread with burrata that came with zucchini and eggplant. Everything was so flavorful! For pastas we ordered the pesto and the cacio e pepe. Both were fantastic and the pesto was so fresh. We skipped dessert but I already can't wait to come back here to try it! Definitely worth the reservation I had made weeks in advance!
Theres a reason you'll always spot A-List celebs here. The food is possibly top 3 best italian in the city. If you're a cacio e pepe fan you MUST order it!!!!

I've heard from multiple sources that Via Carota has some of the best Italian in the city. I have to say, I was NOT mad about it. The ambiance felt comfortably upscale. We sat at the bar and asked the very kind, very vibrant bartender which wine he would recommend, under $70 per bottle. I was a little nervous that we would get scoffed at for our budget, but he excitedly recommended a beautiful red wine for us. I really appreciated his attitude and his service. Everything we ordered was per the bartender's recommendation, and those recommendations did not disappoint. We ordered the heirloom tomatoes as an appetizer. It was the kind of dish that makes you close your eyes as you chew, so that you can fully soak in all of the amazing flavors happening in your mouth. It was quite a big portion as well, definitely could be split among 4-5 people. My friend, who is vegetarian, ordered a special for his main dish. It was a dish full of grilled vegetables and it was marvelous, and very filling. There are a ton of great vegetarian options! I ordered the Orata Alla Griglia, a fish dish of grilled sea bream and charred escarole. It was very filling as well, and perfectly seasoned. Yum!! I highly recommend Via Carota.

This was  our best meal in NYC in terms of food quality but also the absolute worst in terms of service.

We had a reservation here tonight and were excited for some good food after a long and tiring day. We started (and stayed) with the Cynar Spritzes: love! We need to make those at home. We got the zucchini fritti, and were expecting fritters, but out came a tower of zucchini shoestring fries. They were delicious and well-executed, but there should have been some kind of dipping sauce to go with them because they got dry and boring quickly. The bread is great, but it's kind of lame that they're charging you $2 for it when everything else is so expensive.

For dinner, we shared the grilled octopus, tagliatelle, and a side of the carrots. The pasta was wonderful: such a creamy and delicious sauce paired perfectly with the prosciutto and peas. It was delicate and decadent at the same time and was our favorite dish of the night. The carrots with the spiced yogurt and pistachios were very good though they seemed(?) overcooked. But we liked them. The octopus was super tender and heavenly with the olive pesto, a combination that we had never tried before and are big fans of now.

Dessert was the semifreddo and tiramisu. The latter was fine--certainly no better or more impressive than you can find at any upscale Italian joint worth its salt. Also cannot believe that they were calling their chocolate mousse a semifreddo! LOLZ. It was BARELY even cold. Such a joke. Very lame.

OK, buckle up for the atrocious service portion of the review. We were dining outside and must have sat down in between shifts because we were basically only helped by the runner with the water before the server appeared 20 minutes later to take the rest of our order and he had such a disgusting attitude that it almost felt like we were being punked. Rude beyond belief for no reason! Uuuuuunnnntil we saw that we magically had a new woman server after a couple dishes came out who never bothered to introduce herself. Ah OK, so the guy was a total jerk because he knew he'd have to transfer the table over, not get any tip, and could thereby be a totally obnoxious wretch of a human being. The woman was fine, but her section was MASSIVE and she could not accommodate each table well enough to do a good job. It's clear that this place lost their A-team during Covid. 

So, service: 1-2 stars. Food 4-5 stars. Bummer that we had to land on three stars for such wonderful food, but so be it. 

Also, we feel like we need to mention that our daughter's lemonade cost $7 here. Oh, NYC, you're not a cheap date.

This review is for service only. Poor; Period. I think restaurants have basically given up even bothering to educate and train staff. They hire any warm body they can find, throw them on the floor and call them staff.  It's so sad, so lazy and so disappointing. No finesse, no hospitality. Runner serves my frito misto.  Spills 2 shrimp on the floor, picks them up and walks away. Doesn't replace them. Doesn't apologize. Nothing! And then when you are signing the check and tipping the waiter is hovering over you, breathing down you neck watching your every move. It's disgraceful. I was thinking, man I'm so overtipping you w/18% I should have my head examined. Again, no thank you. Just snatched the gadget and walks off.
Foods not that good, won't be returning.

Via Carota is one of my favorite go to Italian/pasta spots in Manhattan. Their menu consists of a variety of classic Italian dishes done well, including a large vegetables section. 

Recently, I was able to make a reservation on Resy for three for dinner on a Sunday to take out visiting friends and had another great meal.

We ordered a bottle of wine, the carote, insalata verde, cacio e Pepe tonnarelli, and tagliatelle with peas and prosciutto (on the side to accommodate a friend). 

For a light but still fulfilling dinner, I think what we ordered was perfect for three. The carrots with the spiced yogurt and pistachios make for an interesting combo and the salad was crisp and light. Both tasted great and can't go wrong as starters. For the pastas, the cacio e Pepe and peas and prosciutto tagliatelle are also can't go wrong options I think. Cacio e Pepe had a little al dente bight to it which was nice. Both are great hearty cheesy pasta options and the tagliatelle comes with a nice portion of prosciutto. 

Whenever the next visit is, I'd like to try the coniglio fritto (fried rabbit) or the fritto misto (fried shrimp, calamari, cod). I tried the via carota svizzerina a previous time and it was cool to try and split amongst others, but slightly underwhelming as it is essentially a fancy version of a burger patty.

Stracci with pesto Genovese - large sheets of pasta with homemade pesto and LOTS of pine nuts, which I appreciated (they're expensive haha). I don't usually like pesto but I like pasta sheets (one of my favorite shapes) and this was the dish recommended by the waiter. Although I don't usually enjoy pesto, this pesto was pretty good. I would recommend this dish if you haven't tried it, but I would also like to try something new next time so wouldn't order again. 

Carciofi alla griglia (grilled artichokes) - included grilled artichoke hearts, grilled lemon (always love!) and grilled onion. Didn't eat the aioli bc I'm not usually a fan of aioli. Loved the artichokes and the smoky/lemony flavor. Would order again.

This place is a shadow of what it used to be pre Covid. 

One of the worst service experiences we have had recently. I think we showed up in between shift changes and for half an hour plus they didn't even know who our server was. 

Cacio Pepe, a dish we used to love, was just over salty pasta. 

Bruschetta was hastily put together. 

Carrots looked unappetizing. 

Just not worth the hassle at all. Go elsewhere. BTW we love pasta at Scarpetta.

Totally not worth the hype! As a New Yorker very versed in Italian food this is a not worth the hype place for the amount of money. Save your money and take it elsewhere. The risotto was mediocre and I felt like it look like a diy project. Bro what I was expecting at all.

Great meal for a special occasion or for a business dinner. I've been a few times and found I enjoyed it the most when we can share a bunch of the vegetable plates and pastas. The salad is one of the best I've had and I've tried my best to replicate the dressing several times and can't seem to get it right. However, overall it is pricey if you're going with just 1 or 2 other people and there are other places in the neighborhood worth trying.

Piselli salad is BOMB get it. 
If you can't get a resy and want to skip the wait, come between 3-4:30pm and they basically seat you right away. 

I'd say pass on the arancini but I know they're famous for it so up to you! 

Very cute space, but be ready for small tables which is pretty typical of nyc.

Pretty fantastic!  Everything is fresh and delicious.  Great staff.  Pasta, pesto, insalata... oh my!  We ere looking for brunch on our last day in NYC and were in the the neighborhood were looking for a place with a fresh menu.  This place was "perfect".  The staff was smart, effiecent in a relax dinning way, attentive, and so comely.   The food was generous, tasty to perfection, and met a farm-to-table ideal rarely achieved.  

Go here for a relaxed meal with good service and good drinks to take the time to enjoy youself.  You deserve it.

Rating: 8.5/10 

My cousin recommended this Italian place to me. I didn't know it was well known spot in the city. I should've known after waiting 30 minutes for a table. The restaurant itself is pretty small so I wouldn't come here with a large group or when you're hangry.

 I ordered the cacio peppe while my friend ordered the risotto. I thought the pasta was good, needed more salt and pepper in my opinion. For 25 dollars, I don't think I would come back. I mean look at the portion size (relatively small in my opinion) and a high price for no protein or vegetables either! Not sure why this place is popular on TikTok/Yelp/ etc because I feel there there are better places in the city!

I don't really think this place is worth the hype.

Unbelievable spot. Perfect cynar spritz. My bf and I split the octopus (perfectly cooked, bunless burger (best burger I've had in my life) and heirloom tomato salad (though I think the soled bread was missing). Sat and the bar, fast service and fresh food - will come back.

THIS WAS MY ABSOLUTE FAVE NYC RESTAURANT PRE-COVID  

This is for service only. The food is great but at those prices I want a nice overall experience. Was there tonight to celebrate a birthday.  We had the piselli and artichokes, chicken and Swizzerina. All of it excellent. However the service was atrocious. We did not know who our server was, drinks came late and no-one stopped by to see how we're doing or ask if we wanted more drinks. Finally we flagged someone down to order a second glass of wine. It never came. We finished eating and I flagged down a server to cancel the wine since we were done eating. No reaction. No apology. Nothing. The service has lost its soul. 

I know things are hard after Covid but Rita and Jody should spend time here and see how things have changed for the worse and figure out how to get some experienced servers back. 

Please fix it. I want you to be great again!!

I'd been waiting to check out Via Carota for years. I was really disappointed despite really wanting to love it. A couple of observations.
- we were sat at the bar after waiting two hours, which is fine, but the service we we received was phoned in. It felt like we were an afterthought when in fact it was my fiance's birthday and it was supposed to be a special evening.
- I make the Via Carota insalata verde at home, and frankly I feel like I put more care into the dish than the one we received. I'd read that stacking the greens was a big part of the presentation that it's part of why the dish feels so special. Our greens were just thrown in a bowl and didn't taste salted properly.
- We were encouraged to try the Heirloom Tomatoes and the presentation and taste profile just felt sloppy and not thought through. 
- The pastas were good, but overall unmemorable. I've been to lots of less prestigious restaurants that had better homemade pastas than what we had at Via Carota.

I'm hoping it was an off night, but based on other Yelp reviews, it doesn't seem like it. I believe there was magic at Via Carota once, but it doesn't seem to be there anymore. I hope they refocus their kitchen to put the same amount of care into their food as they used to. I look forward to coming back and trying more food someday, but I'll be avoiding Via Carota until I hear otherwise.

This place was great. Pasta was clearly homemade and tasted amazing. I had the Cacio e pepe and I'm looking forward to going back for that and trying their other pasta dishes. Service was good, quite quick actually. Would give this 5 stars if my appetizer was better. We had the zucchini fritta. It was not good at all. There is a certain type of traditional Italian elegance that this place portrays and I think they really dropped the ball with this specific appetizer. The portion was way too large and besides that, it was just tasteless and odd to eat because there was just so much. It was like something you would order out at a pizzeria.
Nevertheless, I am looking forward to going back because the pasta was so good but in my opinion, it's best to not waste your time with the zucchini fritta

We ended up in New York for our 3 year anniversary and were advised to try and go at about 5 o clock and try to get a seat as reservations are pretty impossible 
We knew this may be the case so we did not mind .They found us a table of 5(the host was so kind) at 7:30 and we had the best time .Our table had liver,piselli salad that we shared and then the tagliatelle ,the pork belly ,the fish ,the rabbit and lots of wine 
The highlight for me was the Piselli salad and even though I enjoyed my pasta I have to say my husband's pork belly was really amazing. We are happy we came here and I will definitely make it there again on our next New York trip :)

It's an Italian places, but the Piselli salad steals the show. It's a green goddess dressing that pairs well with all the flavors and textures. Get it! The boar bolognese has nice tangyness and tonnarelli was a sleeper pasta. Just butter, cheese and pepper but done perfectly.

This remains one of our favorites. Latest visit, we got arancini, panzanella, carrots, broccoli rabe, stracci with pesto, and the chopped steak. The carrots, arancini, and chopped steak are just perfect, and it's hard to come here and not order those. The stracci with pesto was good, but -- as I wrote last time -- a little too basil-heavy for my wife's preferences. The panzanella was great but not a must re-order, given the stiff competition. The broccoli rabe was really excellent (if not the most exciting thing), and definitely a re-order candidate.

One thing I'll say is that I'm more and more convinced that you can't really get the best possible experience here with a party of two -- the portions are big, so if you want to get a bunch of different things, it's better to do so with four.

Cacio pepe lives up to the hype!

A few cocktails, the insalata verde with its bewitching dressing, an over salted fritto misto and 3 pastas.  Cacio Pepe was easily the star, as expected.  An off-menu garlic and olive oil pasta was surprisingly satisfying, even though it was somehow even simpler. The pappardelle was a surprising disappointment, as the ragu was also too salty.  A few strange miscues but a very solid meal overall.
What a delicious lunch spot! The pastas were all amazing and so yummy. Great portions and great service. Can't wait to go back to try more things!!
Just okay, completely overhyped Italian.  Service was extremely slow, which probably explains the consistently long wait times.

Lives aren't worth the amazing food. Yelp actually deleted the below review claiming I was at another location or the experience wasn't first-hand. This is wrong. Yelp is sadly just protecting its ad business that is based on prolonging COVID-19 and killing people. To be clear the food is really great - the seasonal peach dessert was literally the best peach dessert I've ever had.

COVID-19 is now the United States' deadliest pandemic having killed almost SEVEN HUNDRED THOUSAND people and with the extremely contagious delta variant still killing hundreds of people everyday these business owners think it is ok to have people tightly packed inside literally next to each other with NO mask on eating, drinking, talking and spreading COVID-19 everywhere so they can increase their profit - truly terrible. More absurd is for some reason they require people to wear a mask walking from the front door to their indoor seat where they promptly take the mask off - this obviously does nothing to save lives.

Worst experience in our 2 weeks stay in NYC. Arrived at 16:55. The place was busy so we waited patiently for the waiter to come get our order but he didn't come. So after 20min we told him we are waiting. He said he will get our order "soon". We left the place after another 10min.

My first time at Via Carota!

We were lucky enough to snag a reservation at 5:30pm on a Wednesday. The vast majority of people who come here don't have a reservation and just wait, which I would've been fine doing. We sat outside in their major outdoor dining area - it was nice!

We started with the zucchini fritti, grilled artichokes with aioli, and insalata verde. Of course, we had to try the cacio w Pepe and the via carota chopped steak. Everything was delicious, and there's nothing I would've order again! The cacio e Pepe was great, the pasta had a really nice texture, and it was made the traditional and Simple way. The chopped steak was really more like a seared tar tar which was vey delicious. 

Don't visit without ordering the panna cotta!

It's one of those standard Manhattan restaurants where they barely offer  reservations and it's nearly impossible to get a table quickly unless you come during lunch on a weekday. Upon arrival, the staff was cold and standoffish. They seated my friend and I at a table outside where my chair was over a sidewalk grate, and they wouldn't let me change the position of my chair around the table even after I told them I was uncomfortable sitting over the grate. There were other available tables as well and they would not move us. 

The food was just alright. Everything we tried was very overpriced for small portions that were not too flavorful or unique. Nothing we tried was so stellar that it was worth the cost, especially the Svizzerina. The staff told us it was like a steak tartare but it was not. You're paying $29 for a burger patty. 

We tried:
*'Nduja Arancini - rice and spicy pork fritters $15
*Acciughe E Burro - cultured butter and salted anchovies $15
*Tonnarelli - cacio pepe $25
*Via Carota Svizzerina - hand-chopped grassfed steak $29

This place is close to my mani pedi spot in the village. I went here for a quick small bite before my appointment and I had the dish with sausage and beans (pictured) below. I forgot the name but it was perfect - it's on the starters and was quite filling. It was so tasty I was thinking about it the next day. Highly recommend.

I love the ambiance however the food is marginal at best. This restaurant is way over hyped.  The truffle pasta dinner special was over cooked and a very small portion served on a very small plate  for a $40 price tag.  The Brussel sprout salad was drenched in sauce.  Sat at the bar, the bartender was very professional but very unfriendly.

We have wanted to try this place for a while after hearing our friend raving about the wild boar ragu. Finally made the wait (~45 min) on a lightly rainy Monday evening. On weekends, it's almost impossible to get a table without reservations.

We started with Nduja arancini, which had a surprising kick of spice in it. For the Pappardelle with wild boar ragu, the sauce was beautifully rendered and hearty, even though I couldn't taste the difference between pork and the wild boar. Would come back for it. Tagliatelle prosciutto was less than perfect for me, as I'm not a big fan of prosciutto in general. Though to be fair, the sauce itself was so refreshing and I could taste some sweetness that is rare in other restaurants.

This is not just another Italian place, the cooking has heart in it; however, considering the abundant options of Italian foods in NYC, you can find better and cheaper options that doesn't have a long wait.

I've always wanted to come here but it's almost impossible to get a reservation! We arrived around 10:30pm which is the one of the few times I think you can sit right down. I loved the ambiance inside but there's plenty of outdoor seating outside. I am celiac but this Italian restaurant had plenty of gluten free options when it comes to vegetables, fish, and meat (no GF pasta but there is GF risotto). The brussel sprouts with apples and walnuts was a great appetizer. The octopus was cooked perfectly but had a very strong olive taste that wasn't my thing and the pork belly with plum sauce was phenomenal, and quite filling. The Chianti I ordered wasn't my favorite but I got the negroni terra and wow I've been thinking about that drink all day! It had such a nice vanilla taste that I wasn't expecting. Lastly the service was not the best. I don't know how many different waiters came to our table throughout the night but it may have been 4 or 5. Both our table and the two next to us were being sent the wrong items. I understand the staffing issues in these covid times though so can't get too frustrated!

Excellent food! We had the walnuts and pear bruschetta and the fungi with cheese followed by the crispy pork belly with plums and it was all extremely delicious. The desserts -- the olive oil cake and the raspberry turnover -- were less interesting. 

The place is extremely crowded all the time so reservations are probably the way to go. We waited an hour and fifteen minutes to be seated. Also, the black metal chairs on the sidewalk are not comfortable or stable so try to get the wooden chairs. 

On the service front, we felt it was a little inconsistent and we had to wait for long intervals before we could spot our server to come around and help us. 

Overall, amazing!

Ok...so you're probably wondering "why is this place soooo hard to get into?"   Cuz it's a great mix of small size, personal friendly service, and smack-down flavorful food.  I have sat at the bar, inside table and outside.  Matters not...the smells lure you in, and the service and food keep me coming back

Via Carota is a West Village staple. The line is starting to get long again. Around 530 pm, it's 20 deep or so. I went a few times during the pandemic and was lucky enough to not have a wait. The pastas are all very good. Decent portions and very fresh ingredients. I like the tortellini and pappardelle. The salad... it's so simple, but just completely magical. I've tried to recreate the vinaigrette at home, to no avail. Yes, it is $20 for a pile of leaves. Yes, you should order it every single time. The octopus was kind of meh. It was pretty salty and the texture was chewier than I'm used to. I'm not a big dessert person after dinner, but their affogato is perfection. Service is always good. Nothing great, nothing bad to note. The servers kind of stay in the background. They've never been pushy and foster a lazy dinner to be savored. 

All in all, Via Carota is lovely. An absolute killer date spot if you can get a reservation, otherwise you'll be waiting in line for quite some time.
Simply put, some of the best food I have ever had.  I went here with my wife 4 times over the course of a week while we were in town.   Everything was just amazing. Well worth the wait.

While the venue is cute, and the staff nice and friendly, I was very disappointed with the food.
Paying $27 dollars for a plate of pasta that was not fresh is not right. Pieces of pasta were stuck to each other which tipically happens with pre-cooked pasta. 
My husband had the rabbit and while the flavors were right, it was unfortunately very salty.
The arancini saved the meal, perfectly cooked and right texture.
It's just very disappointing to visit from another state with so much excitement and not have the best experience in such a highly rated place.

The line nowadays does get quite long so would recommend going early in the day to get seated and enjoy a leisurely lunch/brunch. Felt that the apps and the cacio e pepe were the highlights, so definitely do not miss the pear bruschetta! As for drinks, they have a pretty extensive wine list and a great list of Negronis to choose from. Also, service was fantastic and even though the line was getting longer when we were getting seated, we did not feel rushed at all!  I'm not sure this warrants a wait longer than 30 minutes, but nevertheless, a great dining experience.

I'm writing this post because everyone is sleeping on the fried rabbit! I know rabbit isn't a favorite protein in the US, but it is fried to absolute perfection, and comes with a giant piece of FRIED BREAD, plus two cloves of roasted garlic to slather on it. It is somehow both one of the most decadent and minimalist things I've ever had. I've been here twice and gotten this both times--I really want to try the Svizzerina, but I can't resist the rabbit and bread.

We've also had the cacio e pepe on a previous visit; it is absolutely delicious. But last night we had the tagliatelle with prosciutto and parmigiano and it was ridiculously good--they add nutmeg to great effect, and I'm glad we ordered it because that's another classic italian combo that you don't see enough here. Sides included leeks (got those the first time and needed to get them again) and the cabbage/farro/parm/speck salad, which was also very tasty and I think one of the heartier veg dishes. As others have said reservations are few and far between; we showed up at 7:30 on a wednesday and weren't seated until almost 9:30 (though they do now text when your table is ready and you have 10 minutes to claim it, so you can easily grab at drink at a nearby bar while you wait).

My ill feeling is it is mostly walk in with very few reservations but it appeared everyone walking in had a reservation. The fried zucchini had very little zucchini. The pastas don't compare to those of sistina, Caravaggio, and other top Italian spots in NYC. The service was mediocre at best. My opinion is if one is going to spend $120 a person, go to sistina or Caravaggio. I won't return here

I highly recommend this restaurant! The food is delicious and the ambiance is lovey. We got the grilled artichokes, burrata, cacio e pepe, tagliatelle, and cannolis. The artichokes were amazing--they were soaked in a buttery sauce. (They came with an aioli but we didn't use anything of it). The burrata was a highlight. It came with garlic greens that were packed with flavor! The two pastas were cooked perfectly and absolutely phenomenal. The pasta is worth the hype. And last but not least--the cannoli dessert came with 4 mini cannolis. Great way to finish off the meal. Only complaint was one cannoli had a piece of pistachio shell that was really hard and unpleasant.

We had a reservation on a Saturday at 6:30 pm. Definitely recommend getting a reservation for a weekend otherwise the wait is insane

We were excited to get a table and be seated right away. We were celebrating 24 years of marriage and this was our night out. Our waiter was the worst. He put in the wrong order for my entree. So I had to send it back because I am GF and couldn't even eat what they brought me. So I watched my husband eat and waited 20 minutes for my meal. The waiter didnt check on us once or even offer to bring me something to nosh on or drink while we waited. I was so upset when my meal came I took it to go. The waiter charged us for the entree and never offered a dessert or coffee. Also, the risotto I ordered came out soupy and gross. Honestly I would have made it better myself My husbands dinner was disappointing as well.. BLAND. UGH. I am still upset by this experience. Our waiter really just didn't care at all.
food was tasty, but it is overpriced , and I also don't recommend sitting outside, service was pretty slow.

Cacio e pepe is a winner!! 

Reservations: Super hard to get; I've been checking Resy for weeks trying to get one to no avail. I was walking past the area Friday night around 7pm and scored a walk-in for two at the bar. We took the last 2 bar seats and felt very lucky. Tip for those not glued to Resy: Come before 7pm and sit at the bar.

Food: Cacio e pepe is a must. Very hyped up and this exceeded my expectations. Came out piping hot and was soo delicious. Close your eyes and slurp the buttery fat carbs without looking at the giant mound of butter/oil at the bottom of the pasta... ignorance is bliss!! Also got the boar pasta. It was just okay. Cacio e pepe is def the winner here.

Vibes: Dark and romantic and old-fashioned decor. Great first few dates spot. Not like this is relevant but I did notice the entire restaurant seemed to be filled with only white people.

I walked in for lunch in the middle of the day which happened to be quite busy. I opted to sit at the bar instead of a table since I was a lone diner. Normally bartenders are chatty and friendly but unfortunately mine could not be bothered with even minimal conversation (isnt that half the fun with sitting at the bar?) Anyway, I was really excited to try the fried rabbit since my grandma makes rabbit and it is one of my favorite dishes. Upon receiving my order, I was super disappointed before even having a bite. I was under the impression that the rabbit would have been pan fried but it was deep fried (looked like fried chicken from KFC). It tasted NOTHING like rabbit (honestly they could be feeding people chicken and first time eaters would not know the difference). Very greasy and just overall disappointing. Topped off my meal with dessert which was good. I feel like I need to give this place another try and have something else on the menu but this just was not it.

I wanted to love it, but it is just not worth the hype. You can find better Italian in the city for a lower price and with a bit less drama over getting a table. 

However, it certainly fits the West Village vibe; very trendy, bustling, hip, etc. if that's what you are looking for, you won't be disappointed.

If you are looking for outstanding Italian food, you won't find it here. The Arancini were good, but the pasta and fish dishes we just serviceable.

We got lucky and found a Sunday lunch reservation for 2 people that opened up the night before. We booked that as fast as we could and showed up promptly (and very hungry) at Via Carota the next day.

Despite having a reservation we still needed to wait in the walk-in for about 15 minutes until we could be seated. But given how busy this restaurant gets it was understandable.

Food, service and ambiance once we sat down were 10/10. We were seated outside in their gorgeous, greenery lined outdoor seating area in the West Village. Our waitress arrived quickly and we ordered the Cacio e Pepe and the Wild Boar Ragu. Needless to say the Cacio e Pepe lived up to the hype, it was the best version of this dish I've ever had outside of Italy. The handmade pasta is cooked perfectly al dente and the sauce is pepper forward (which I love). The Wild Boar Ragu was fantastic as well, the meat was so juicy and flavorful tossed with such a good quality handmade pasta. Definitely coming back here again despite the long wait times. 100% worth all the hype!

The restaurant apparently doesn't have heat as the servers were all wearing thick jackets and hats to combat the cold, and indoor diners had to wear jackets as well. It ended up being colder in the restaurant than outside (it was 45 degrees and windy). The hostess was quite rude and tried to scoot us out of the restaurant for diners that didn't yet arrive to the restaurant. Classic NYC Italian spot that thinks that they're better than their patrons. 

As we were leaving, I noticed that one server had toppled some of the insalata verde (1/3 of the salad) while bringing it over to a table and casually caught the greens with his bare hands and just pushed it onto the plate. I thought that to be pretty gross and unforgivable considering the ongoing pandemic.

Ordered: 
acciughe e burro - delicious and would order again
insalata verde - simple but what every salad should aspire to be
pappardelle (wild boar ragu) - salty, devastatingly small portion size, uninspired, would not recommend
coniglio fritto - under seasoned, unexceptional, would not recommend
tiramisu - worst i've ever had 0/10

TLDR: No heat, not worth the wait. It was fine.

Anytime I meet someone from nyc or who's lived here for awhile, I ask the same question every time - " what restaurant has wowed you?" And boy oh boy did via carota wow me. 

Amazing service, amazing food - I'm still thinking about the artichokes as I write this. The pork belly, the pappardelle, the cacio e pepe, even the dang olive oil that comes with the bread is exquisite. I absolutely cannot wait to come back - this is so worth trekking over for at 4pm to snag a reservation. 

GET the grilled artichokes, get the olive oil cake, and get so many bottles of wine - you will not regret it.

What a charming West Village spot! I've been a long time fan of Buvette and have been meaning to check out Via Carota for the longest. My friend was visiting town and so we decided to come here for an early dinner. Because it was early we were able to get seated quickly without reservations. I ordered the tagliatelle with ragu, a glass of wine, and some arancini to share. Everything was delicious!

I've been truly disappointed by every dinner I've had there so am done believing all the rave reviews. Food was just okay. There is far better to be had in the neighborhood. We tried many things, including desserts and didn't go nuts over anything. The selections could be better also. I preferred I Sodi, their other restaurant. That they don't take reservations also makes this a pain. People are willing to wait several hours for a table. I truly don't get it. My other review (which said the same thing) was removed.

This restaurant will speak for itself. If does not disappoint! It's very hard to get a reservation they mostly do walk ins so we went at 10 am on a Saturday. If you want pasta for breakfast or lunch or dinner this place is fabulous! You cannot go wrong with any of the pasta dishes but there's also so many hidden gems like the carrots or ricotta truffle bruschetta. If you haven't been here it is a must!!
Extensive Negroni list. Wild board ragu is delicious. Lemony creamy risotto. Crunchy brussel sprout salad. The best tiramisu ever.

honestly the food here  is pretty amazing. I'm kind of cranky and I don't like to stand in line but one of my friends decided that she wanted to eat here badly enough that she would do it for us. So she stood in line and we got to sit at the table pretty quickly. Be warned that there definitely is a wait and you definitely have to physically be present with your entire party present in order to be seated.

they have some outdoor seating available which we sat at because of the lack of space. They don't have too much space inside maybe only 6 to 8 tables inside the restaurant, but they have a lot more seating outside. Best to come when the weather is a little bit warmer. 

The wait staff was friendly and approachable and was able to give us good recommendations with our order as well as our preferences. We had a baby with us and they accommodated us really well 

we tried the brussels sprouts, the carrots and the kale salad, the Apple and gruyère toast ( which the baby loved) and we got the pork Ragu, the octopus, and the cacio y pépé. we also tried the roasted pear for dessert. One of my friends had wine which he enjoyed and I got the cocktails which I definitely recommend. The food was completely amazing. All the ingredients were well thought out, very fresh and flavorful, thoughtfully combined and presented. I would probably recommend trying everything on the menu honestly I don't think you could go wrong. Some dishes are simpler with fewer ingredients but everything tastes absolutely delicious with complex flavors no matter what dish it is.

Worth the hype. The star of the show was definitely the cacio e pepe. The pasta was the perfect size and the sauce didn't feel overly heavy despite it being a cheese-based dish. I would also recommend the olive oil cake with a side of the berries and mascarpone for dessert. Honestly, everything was fantastic. I know I will be coming back soon!
Was recommended to come here by a local. Cacio e Pepe is one of the best I've ever made. They hand make all their pasta. Would love to come back

The cacio e Pepe was exactly what I wanted from it. Noodles cooked to the exact texture I like, and the sauce cut through perfectly so that the simplicity of the dish did not feel as if it lacked anything.

The food here is good! I came with friends and there were so many good items that we had.

Insalata verde: Mix of leafy greens and the dressing was pretty good. The only thing is the oil at the bottom of the bowl was super salty. 

Cardi fritti: These are fried cardons which reminded me of artichoke. The cardons were crunchy and slightly lemony. 

Pappardelle: The pasta was almost like lasagna noodles and were a little soft for my liking. The wild boar ragu was pretty good and tomatoy.

Tonnarelli/Cacio pepe: Pretty good and creamy but when it arrives, eat it first before it starts to congeal!

Coniglio fritto/rabbit: The rabbit was kind of like a game-y chicken but was delicious. The order was 3 pieces and came with a side of cheese bread and garlic. Although it was good, the bread was my favorite.

This restaurant has a great heated outdoor seating option, which kept us nice and warm and out of the wind. The bruschetta with anchovies was pretty good, and the burrata was just OK. We ordered three of the pasta dishes, and all were just mediocre, nothing spectacular at all. The service was good. Generally I would not recommend this restaurant, especially given how many good restaurants there are to choose from.

The food here is very good. Highly recommended the Pappardelle, Cacio Pepe, and Acciughe E Burro. Skip the Polipo (octopus) looks amazing but was very mushy. Make sure to make reservation in advance to avoid the long wait (I waited for 3 hours)
The ambiance is awesome and the staff is great but the food was underwhelming. Very ok Italian food that you can find in any average place in NYC. Tough to justify the hype and the price.

Had the pleasure of dining during artichoke season. As a Californian I have a deep love for this awkward and time consuming ingredient. They were cooked then tenderly grilled to perfection served with a delightful aioli and drizzled with olive oil. And to gild the lily I also ordered the omelette with baby artichokes. Sigh!

After perusing many positive recommendations and finally snagging a reservation after 2 months, I came to Via Carota on a Friday night at 5:00pm. This dinner was disappointing due to service, food quality, and ambiance. Our server did not approach our table until 15 minutes after we were seated and we had to flag down wait staff to put in appetizer and entree orders. We ordered ricotta toast, bruschetta, burrata, mushrooms, and 3 different types of pastas. Everything was fine...I can name 10 better places in the area that I would personally prefer. Additionally, during our meal, we had 3 homeless people approach us crying, weeping, and lingering around our table with no intervention from the restaurant. I would try Don Angie, I Sodi, Malatesta, St. Tropez, and others in the area instead.

I checked a week beforehand and no reservations online for Saturday lunch. But when I arrived for a late lunch everyone in line without a reservation got a table. Indoors they decorated the tables with pomegranates which was pretty. I sat at the bar and the floor as covered with  saw dust. 

The Cacio e pepe is served in a soup bowl. I didn't get any bread even though I saw others were. The pasta was made with thick spaghetti noodles in a good sauce that was very rich and peppery. 

Note it's cold inside the restaurant, they don't put the heat on. The bathroom is served regularly and has Aesop soap.

***Delivery order review***

I highly recommend ordering from this place if you're craving a healthy Italian meal. The artichoke and mushroom was cooked to perfection, but more iconic was the branzino. I'm already planning a future order. Delivery came well packaged!

I really do like this place! I just feel like there's limited pasta options but the veggies are phenomenal and the pasta is really delicious too! It's a long wait, but definitely worth it. The cacio e Pepe is delicious.

Was delish, came for my anniversary with my bf, we got a bottle of wine, a truffle bruschetta, burrata, and broccoli rabe to share, we each got the cacio pepe for ours mains, and got tiramisu to share for dessert. Our waiter was very attentive and very nice. If you can get a table, definitely go!

We booked way in advance and I finally know what the hype is all about. Not only was the ambiance great, but the food was also amazing. The portions aren't too big which is perfect for the four of us. We really enjoyed the Insalata Verde because of the light and fresh dressing and the Cacio Pepe. Would definitely be back!

Have heard so much about this place and wanted to give it a try! Super cute spot in the west village for something casual or something a bit nicer as well. 

Reservations are definitely hard to come by - we booked pretty far in advance for lunch. 

We got the truffle bruschetta, insalata verde, cacio Pepe, and tagliatelle. The bruschetta was amazing - lots of truffle, no flavors were too overpowering. Would come back just to eat this again. The salad was surprisingly good as well. It was simple leafy greens with dressing but it paired well together. The pastas were al dente, creamy, and flavorful. Lots of cheese (which I don't eat) but other than that was really good. The prosciutto on the tagliatelle went perfectly with the pasta. 

The waitress looked quite disappointed when we didn't order more. She mentioned that we should probably order 1-2 more dishes given we were 4 people but we decided to play it by ear and found that the dishes we ordered were actually enough.
Via Carota was recommended by so many people. I was beyond disappointed with the food. It was very underwhelming. The couple next to us also got in a fight and really killed our vibe.

4.5stars | This is a pretty trendy restaurant, and a great place to bring a foodie friend visiting from out of town (you'll seem so cool.) Can be hard to get a reservation so plan far in advance. It's popular for a reason - the food is really good. It's apparently quite popular among chefs. I had the octopus and the papardelle and both were very good.

My friends and I had Via Carota on our restaurant bucket list for quite some time thanks to an Instagram account that frequently posts celebrity sightings at this place. Also, the pasta looked really good. I made a reservation for us about two months in advance for an outside table at 9:30 pm (that was the only thing available). On the day of our reservation, I decided to pop by earlier (around 7:30) to see if they had any tables inside at an earlier time, and the super nice host said yes. That was awesome and we felt lucky. 

The service: Amazing. Really attentive and lovely servers, hosts, etc.

The drinks: *Pretty* good, but pricey for what they are. We started with a round of aperol spritzes which tasted decent but were extremely expensive at $17. 

The food: We started with the arancini (4 rice balls), the burrata, and bread & olive oil. Between four people, these three apps felt sufficient. Still, we all agreed that each dish tasted pretty mediocre. For our main dishes, we ordered the Cacio Pepe (seen on many a TikTok), Tagliatelle, Pappardelle, & the Risotto. I LOVED the cacio pepe was but was surprised at the portion size -- it was really like a small bowl. The risotto was good but very lemon-y if you like that. My friend loved her pappardelle and felt the size was perfect and my other friend enjoyed the tagliatelle but felt it was too small. Overall, while the dishes were definitely tasty, we all agreed we'd had better pasta for cheaper prices. 

With the addition of a $67 bottle of Chianti (the cheapest red on their menu), our bill came out to about $100 a person. We were glad we checked Via Carota off our bucket list, but agreed we would not go back probably.

You must, I repeat must, order the insalata verde. Yes, I am talking about a salad, but oh, this isn't just ANY salad. The salad dressing was just right, the combo of bibb lettuce and endive divine. We couldn't finish (in anticipation of many dishes to come) and I gladly took the leftovers home with me.

As for the mains, we sampled the cacio e pepe, the wild boar ragu papardelle and the fried rabbit. Of the three, I would say the cacio e pepe is out of this world amazing, and the fried rabbit was crispy perfection. And how could I forget the dessert? It was a custard on top of fresh raspberries and it's so good, you'll wish it was appropriate to lick a plate when you're dining out of your own home, lol.

All in all, this restaurant is wonderful. Great service, great wine, incredible food and a cozy atmosphere. I can't wait to return again, and perhaps order 2 salads, one to eat there, and a second to take home, lol.

The reception staff were a bit rude when my partner and I came in. However, when we sat down the waiters were fantastic and quick. The food was delicious! We had the risotto, insalata verde and branzino al sale. Will possibly return, hopefully I will have a much nicer welcome.

I have never had such a disappointing dining experience as I have at this establishment. We were sat outside in the freezing cold and the heaters were not working or barely even on. We could see our breath just to give some context. The food was also subpar, within 5 minutes of the food being brought out it was cold. There were so many items that weren't available that we wanted. Myself and party were so cold that we almost got frostbite and hypothermia. Our waitress barely came out to take our order or ask us if we were ok because she was so cold as well. The treatment was honestly inhumane and the fact that this establishment thought it was acceptable to go seat parties outside without proper heating and insulation on one of the coldest days in NYC is honestly unacceptable.

The grilled octopus here is soooo good!! The best in town. Yes I said it, it's the best. Not many restaurants In Nyc can do it so perfectly. Their spicy pork arancini is dangerously addicting. Pasta is something you have to order here but it's their risotto that took me to cloud 9.

Finally figured out how to land a reservation at Via Carota! Although available on resy, I was never able to secure a reservation or make it off of the waitlist, so I walked in and inquired about dinner availability. I was kindly placed on a wait list for a perfect 8pm indoor dinner slot.. walk in seems like the way to do it and it's totally worth the wait! 

Food was delicious! For starters we enjoyed the arancini, bruschetta with butter and sardines (never had anything like it.. amazing!), and the wildly refreshing & massive insalata verde. Would do all those appetizers all over again next time! The verdure section on the menu is by far the largest, so next time I'd explore more options there. For pastas, we loved both the pappardelle in wild boar ragu and the tortelli with smoked ricotta, but the tortelli was the standout for me.. had a unique smokey and oniony flavor that I couldn't get enough of! We also ordered the Sicilian meatballs which were good but not the best.. the raisins made them a bit sweet and not my favorite flavor profile for meatballs. 

All in all, Via Carota exceeded my expectations between the heavenly Italian dinner, excellent service, and cozy ambiance. Excited to be back!

Hands down one of my top 5 favorite restaurants in the city. Amazing food, great ambiance and lovely service. 

We always get some veggie options (which rotate seasonally) along with a few pastas. Also don't forget to try their cocktails!

The manager Sharissa was the rudest person I've ever met. The hospitality was terrible. I had a reservation at 9:30. We were kicked out and hour and a half after because she needed to clean up the restaurant.  We told her we were waiting for our Uber. We were forced to wait outside in the cold. I've never experienced such disrespect and poor hospitality. This restaurant treats their patrons like they are a burden to them. Don't go here unless you want to be kicked out early.

Very popular spot for Italian dining in the West Village. My boyfriend and I came here for dinner on a Friday night and all tables were filled with a long line of standbys - I highly recommend having a reservation. We were seated swiftly by the staff who were very quick and efficient at turning over tables. 

We had the grilled anchovies special and some bread and olive oil to start. The anchovies were fresh and delicious however the bread was a bit stale and the crust was tough. For our mains, we had the wild boar pappardelle and cacio e pepe. Both were delicious but I personally like the flavor of the pappardelle more.
