We finished with the olive oil panna cotta which was my favorite item of the evening. It was simple yet well balanced in sweetness and texture. 

As for drinks, my boyfriend had some red wine recommended by our server and I was surprised to find out that they didn't have any soda or diet beverages. They only had house made orange or ginger soda which I opted for the ginger hoping it would be similar to ginger ale. It was quite spicy and I found it difficult to drink due to it resembling more of a medicine taste. Not the best selection here for non-alcoholic beverages, stick to water.

Food is fabulous and shout out to the sweetest host! I asked to move tables because we were near the restroom and I was hoping to grab a window seat. She totally accommodated once a table opened and I am very appreciative!

Be warned if you're going with kids -- no matter their age. 

We ate at Via Carota with our two boys, aged 15 & 12. They have great manners and are adventurous eaters who were really excited about Via Carota. When our server saw that we were dining as a family, he asked my wife and I what we wanted to drink, and completely ignored our boys. He only returned to our table again an hour later after our entire meal was finished to ask my wife and I if we wanted another drink (we had finished our cocktails 30 minutes before, wanted wine with dinner, but couldn't order any due to the lack of attention). We were the only table with kids in the restaurant, and perhaps that's uncommon, but we did not feel welcome. There were no pleasantries at the end of the meal -- he just gave us a payment terminal with a pre-selected 20% gratuity.  

Now, the food was very good. The tortelli and grilled artichoke were even excellent (we also ordered a white asparagus special, the fava & escarole salad, orecchiette special, and cacio e pepe pasta ... all delicious). Zero issues on this front. 

We're encouraging our kids to be thoughtful eaters. Via Carota did not encourage us to bring them back. After a month of anticipation, this was a disappointment.

Expensive Italian food, high end restaurant and a good location, but not for me. Went here for the second time after being unimpressed the first.

I just don't understand the popularity of this kind of restaurant in NYC, it brings nothing new to the table. I guess maybe designer cocktails to go with their uninspired Italian food.

I'd go to Rubirosa or Parm the next ten times I'd like Italian food before I go back to Via Carota. I know that these places are more red sauce Italian american, but VC isn't really helping me to explore a new region.

Also, still checking vaccines at the door. I'm happy to know that the restaurant is run by epidemiologists who know better than the CDC.

Not going to comment on the food, but the woman seating patrons was condescending. There were 2 separate lines: one for those with reservations (like me) and one for walk-ins. She seated the group of 4 in front of us. She came back out and then started taking names from the walk-in line. Another couple came with reservations and stood behind us. She proceeded to check them in and seat them. When she came out again, I clarified that we were actually waiting for 5 min. In a very rude tone, she asked me how she was supposed to know (it's her job). When I calmly stated that we were standing behind the group of 4 she seated with reservations, she condescending said, "Are you good? Are you calm?" A simple apology would have been nice, but she couldnt admit that she was wrong. It ruined the dinner for me. This was on 4/23/22 around 6 PM.

The wild boar ragu and the cacio e pepe were perfection! This place is totally worth the hype. The atmosphere is cool, but not too cool, like not intimidating. The service is good as well. Will try to order some dessert next time. Keep up the good work!

The food is ridiculously good but the waiter was suuuuuper rude. I think his name was Michael. I am never rude to waiters, I worked as one for a while and I know how hard it is to put a smile on your face constantly but there is an element of making the experience nice for the diners especially as it was a special occasion and this guy made us feel like we were unwelcome/lucky to be there/rushed out. Might have just got unlucky with the waiter tbh

I returned at an atypical dining time, so there was no wait for a table. 

Service as always is top notch. They're friendly and attentive without being intrusive. 

Finally tried the cacio e pepe pasta and my mind is blown. I'll caveat with saying that I'm normally not a fan of Cacio e pepe because it's usually too rich and creamy for my palate, but holy moly. This is divine! It's creamy and rich, but in an incredible way. And I can tell the cheese is great quality. It's so luscious and they added the perfect about of pepper. Sublime. Perfection. Al dente. Happiness in one little bowl. I guess that's my only "criticism"...give me more pasta pleaseeeeee! You can't make pasta that delicious and not expect me to want a whole vat of it. 

I could not recommend this pasta enough. It shall forever be in my daydreams.

Best food of the trip. We did a full meal from desserts, salads, pastas, and drinks. Such authentic Italian with every course. We managed to sneak into the restaurant for a 3pm lunch. Glad we tried despite not getting reservations for normal dining hours. So worth eating at the off hour.

Via Carota was an extraordinary experience! Booked a reservation a few weeks ago (one hot ticket) and had a wonderful time. The host checked us in at the door and walked us to our table. The menus were folded into the chair which I found very nice. Once we sat, we decided to order the 'Nduja Arancini and Burrata as the starters. Both were mouth watering and filled us with anticipation for the main dishes. Once ready, we ordered the Tonnarelli, the Rigatina and a Caves de Donnas to go along the meal. This was easily one of my best meals in NYC. Everything was incredibly delicious and had me wondering about the other dishes I need to try on my next visit (because I am definitely visiting again soon). To top it off, we had the Tiramisu as the closer for the evening. Next time someone asks me for a recommendation on where to go for delicious culinary experience, I will be directing them to Via Carota.

i was really looking forward to going to this popular restaurant in my neighborhood. The food was good, but be sure to ask about price if you order a "special." Our waiter convinced us to get the ribeye special, along with our other choices. The steak was fully one-third to one-half fat. Fully. He didn't offer the price and, our fault, we didn't ask. It was $79, ala carte, plus tax and tip made it $100 for only a few bites. That's outrageous and left us feeling a bit taken advantage of. Again, our fault for not asking, but that price for a small, fatty steak is outside of the norm.

Very limited menu. $28 for three meatballs with nothing - I mean not even 3 oz of pasta with them . The meatballs were good but come on three meatballs and nothing - that is bs.  You want some bread well thats $3 - really.  Keep your freaking bread.  And keep your freaking restaurant for that matter.

Here visiting my kid who lives in the West Village.  Popped in for dinner without a rezi but scored two seats at the bar.  The food was incredible!!!!!!!!
Tons of options for vegetarians like myself.  
Good people watching. 
High energy.
Can be loud but who cares?
YUMMMMM!

It's our favorite Italian place! My 8 year old daughter and I always walk over some days after school when she's in the mood for Italian. We have our staples but we need to venture out of them to taste other things here. They would never have their fresh off-menu specials but things on the menu is always available. I love the fungi (different types of grilled mushrooms over cheese) and insalata Verde (5 types of greens with sherry vinaigrette) and tonarelli . My daughter always get the calamari and tagliatelle. We get different desserts because most of them are all great. I'm very partial to the panna cotta and berries with zabaione. It's a pricey place but it's a great place to treat yourself once in a while.
Absolutely incredible pasta, vibe, and my favorite- the spicy arancini!! Delicious :)
Authentic and yummy! Ordered the sardines and prosciutto as a bar snack and the Manhattan drink. Super cute place

My daughter chose this place after seeing it recommended by David Leibovitz, so we tried it on a Saturday night.  
I'm not sure if it was not as good as hyped, or if we had a bad service experience, or maybe we just didn't have the right expectations, but it was no more thank "meh/Ok".
We came by around 7:30-8 without a reservation, gave our number, and were told it would be about 1-1.5 hrs. Fine, no problem - we walked around, got a drink, had a nice time waiting and soaking up the neighborhood feel. We get the text around 9ish, sit down, and we peruse the menu.  All good.  Waiter shows up with a thick italian accent, runs thru an incomprehensible spiel about the specials, and when I say "we'll probably start with..." he responds with "the kitchen's closing soon, so you better hurry up and order".   This would've been a great heads up, except the place closes at 11, and when we left at a little after 10, people were being seated and ordering food - so clearly, the kitchen was not "closing soon".
It's not a big deal, but it threw us off our rhythm, made us feel rushed, and that was about the extent of our interaction with the waiter - he made no attempt to explain the dishes, the format, nothing - he took our orders and that's it.
As for our dishes, they were a mixed bag - we had the chicken liver bruschetta, which was a lot of liver - so that was good (in the sense that you get what you pay for), but it was kind of dumped on the bread like a can of dog food, so it wasn't the best presentation, and it was pretty much all liver with not a lot else going for it.  I don't know that I can fault that - I mean, it's a liver bruschetta, so... 
but it was so much, that we ended up ordering the plain "bread and olive oil" just to have something to chew on.
Our other "non-main course" was the "carciofi alla romana", which was ok, but there plenty of leaves that were very "toothsome"/inedible, which detracted from the dish - but i'm not sure if we're just not clued in on what restaurant artichokes are supposed to be, or they were prepared poorly.  Regardless, our waiter when clearing both partially eaten bruschetta and partially eaten artichokes, never asked our thoughts on either.  
For the mains, my daughter had the taglietelle and I had the polpette - they were both fine.  The pasta was clearly fresh, and while I didn't particularly care for the peas (I thought they were tough), my daughter liked the dish.  The polpette were good as well, but then again, it's hard to mess up meatballs, and it was *just* meatballs.

Overall, Via Catora was ok - I think a 2 star review is about right - I wanted to like it, but it just wasn't all that great, and I feel like after paying almost $200 (food, plus 2 25cl things of wine, plus a 25% tip (I feel guilty not tipping a bunch nowadays, although that was a reflexive tip and I don't think our waiter deserved it).  I think with a better waiter, and a more relaxed experience, and trying more vegetables, it could be pretty good - but what we had was "meh", and I wouldn't go back - I don't know if it's actually "not good", or maybe we just "don't get it", but either way, I think you can find a better meal somewhere else.
Been here numerous times and it has always been fantastic. Very authentic Italian. Fantastic ambiance, great food (especially the cacio e pepe). Never disappoints!

The restaurant is popular for a reason. Everything is delicious and the service is good. We were surprised by how good the grilled mushrooms were, the svizzerina, and even the ricotta cheesecake. There's lots of outdoor seating as well, so it's a great spot for warm weather. Note that they do accept walk-ins, so my party put our names down and they said it would be about an hour and we went to a nearby bar, but got a text the table was almost ready in just 30min.

Can't recommend this place enough. Took my parents here and we loved everything. The salad was top 5 salads I've ever had and it was so simple and so flavorful and delicious. The apps were all so good. Loved the cacio e pepe. Love the environment. Can't wait to go back!

Cute little Italian place conveniently placed right off of Christopher St. Came here for lunch with a friend and was impressed with their Negroni menu and the appetizing food menu. I ordered the Negroni 1937 and was told it would be bitter. Unfortunately it was relatively sweet. The Negroni Terra made up for this though. I love cynar in my Negronis.. 

I ordered the pork belly which was a generous fatty slab of meat. My friend ordered the wild boar pappardelle. The ragu needed a bit of salt but the pasta itself was good.  Very small for the price, but this is Manhattan. The biggest issue was the food took at least 45 minutes to come out and the drinks were only about 10-15 minutes ahead of that. We weren't in a rush and it was nice day outside, but it was very slow. Overall, a good experience and I would likely return.

While we have had some excellent dinners at Via Carota, their team is highly deficient in their ability/interest to follow up with their patrons. My partner loves it here, so my family decided to send him a gift card last November. It became a months-long process to try to track down the gift card - it never arrived despite Via Carota's claims that they would send another.

A couple of weeks ago, I attempted to make a reservation for a group of friends to dine here to celebrate my partner's birthday. I left two separate voicemails and sent an email each on separate days - I received no response and we went elsewhere.

The food IS good, but is the poor service and follow-through for their guests worth it? Not for me at this point.

Honestly pretty disappointed with my experience here all around.  After all the hype, I was so excited to come with some friends the other night.  It started out with horrible service, our waitress was so unhelpful and just seemed irritated by our entire presence. She hardly checked on us, and the tables next to us that were seated after us were getting their drinks/apps while we just sat there waiting for her to come back to take our order.  The food was okay? No gluten free pasta option which is kinda surprising honestly, and when I asked if they had any, she simply said no and offered no other solutions or options. The portions were decent, and flavors were good but can't say I'm dying to go back. Would recommend some other Italian spots near by before trying to go here again.

Theres nothing I love more than a restaurant that seems so simple but is so much more! This restaurant is awarded by the James beard foundation for both food & love! Before I even read their press site, I can tell you the food here is not only broken down by a science... but it's made with love & with history! Not one dish failed. Every single dish was a wow factor! We also ordered 4 more dishes that aren't pictures including desserts! Wishing a Michelin star for via carota!

W-O-R-T-H I-T ! We've been wanting to go to Via Carota for a long time now. Definitely not the easiest of NYC restaurants to get into, but given time and room...shoot your shot!  We'd highly recommend eating inside as the ambiance is amazing. 

We started with the Insalata Verde which is a staple. Very simple & satisfying. The Arancini parlayed great with the greens. 

For the pasta, the Cacio e Pepe seems to be the go to. We went with the Tagliatelle which was great. Very flavorful and a healthy portion of prosciutto.

Living in NYC, it's not always easy to find a restaurant you know you'll be back at...But this is one!

Bon Appétit

How does anyone not love Via Carota? Impossible prime time dinner reservations and we hadn't had much luck with weekend walk ins but finally on a summer Thursday at 5:30 we Ubered over and were immediately seated to enjoy the really, really great meal we had anticipated. 

The prosciutto burrata was dreamy. Melt in your mouth tender prosciutto and luscious, creamy burrata. Regretted not ordering a second. 

The artichoke was also greatness. All the fibrous parts hacked away to leave flavorful seasoned bites for us to enjoy. 

Strangely the cacio e pepe wasnt our fav, good but completely outshined by the tortelli. Gooey, delicious caramelized onions over ricotta stuffed pasta was exceptional! 

The server explained that everything there is just simple, good food - and he was right, simple, really good ingredients are the magic of this place.

Foods food not Great. U cud get Italian just as good and must as hearty at plenty more places in the city. I came here tonight 7/8/22 wait was 1.5 hours long which is the shortest it's been in my 5x trying to get in here. Host was rude n not accommodating she didn't take my name down , when I told her my number she seemed to brush me off. I came back 1.5 hours later to check in on table n she sed o it's ready. Mind u this lady never texted me as she sed and wud and was probably surprised to c me still waiting. Margarita our server was very helpful n pleasant n if I cud I wud give 5 stars just for her. Good is good but not worth the wait or the rude attitude from host n or
Other staff. The host originally sat us outside along glass n that server seemed to be fed up with me asking if anything else was available. I mean listen I get it place is busy n by the time they sat us I guess the servers were miserable but wen I Sed I wanted to sit I side margarita
Was very hospitable. Foods good but idk if it's worth the trouble but margerita almost saved the night. 2 stars for good food n good service from margerita the rest is for bad service from host n original waitress outside along with the wait.

Food varies in quality. Our shared starter was really good. However, our pastas were no better than your average  Italian restaurant.

Wine list very pricey & not well selected.

Issues - we asked for some grated parm to be sprinkled on our pastas. They did that, but it was poor quality cheese - AND they actually charged extra for it!!!!  Unheard of. You also had to pay extra if you wanted a slice of bread!!

At their  prices , this nickel & diming is absurd. 

No way we will return.
I know this place is good when you eat there but don't do takeout you'll just be disappointed. My prosciutto pasta was soggy.

Delicious food and lovely place! The green salad is perfection. It's enough for 2-3 people. The pasta is amazing. You should definitely go! If you go on a week day for lunch, it's not difficult to get a table.

Via Carota has been on my list for a long time and I was finally able to snag a table for two on a Sunday afternoon. The staff was attentive and helpful from the moment we were seated.

We started with the Arancini, followed by the carrots, cacio e Pepe, the square pasta with pesto special and tiramisu. My favorite dish were the carrots, extremely flavorful and cooked to perfection. Unfortunately, despite the reviews I've read, the pasta was disappointing. It was fresh but lacked flavor. 

The tiramisu was also a winner with the perfect touch of espresso in every bite. I will probably go back at some point to try a different set of pastas.

It started off badly when the person taking names and giving wait times is sarcastic & rude, but we decided to wait it out & walked over to iSoldi to check them out for a future meal! When we returned and were finally seated, the waiter was nice, but didn't want to accommodate a simple request that the ricotta cheesecake be taken out of the refrigerator to get to room temp by the time we finished our meal!  He said it couldn't be done!  REALLY!  When r food arrived 1 in r party got the wrong dish, pasta with pesto instead of the pork belly!  They took it away & the pork belly arrived when the other 3 in the party had finished their meals!  The pork belly was inedible, we sent it back, they obviously took it off the check, but really? These owners lived in Italy?

I don't really understand the hype over this place, it was good but not exceptional. Had the tomatoes with bread and oil to start, then the cacio e pepe and a lobster pasta special for mains. I'd go back but I definitely wouldn't call this one of the best Italian spots in the city
Via Carota is the most beautiful restaurant--- food, service, atmosphere, location is all exquisite. . I never miss it when visiting NYC.

Was recommended because we couldn't get to I Sodi.( rude doorman) on a Sunday afternoon. Ordered caccio e Pepe. Pasta was soggy  and had too much kraft ? Parmesan. It felt like it was a warmed up leftover with some garlic oil. My partner said her pasta tasted like a salty chef boy r dee. Service was slow and the appetizer tasted like a rice ball from a deli. Skipped dessert for obvious reasons.

Via Carota is the best restaurant in the West Village. The Leafy Green Salad and Artichokes w/ Aioli are an absolute must. 

While it may seem extravagant to spend $21 on a salad. Each leaf feels like it was hand picked for your bowl and carries the perfect amount of dressing. NOTE: It can be a bit challenging to eat--the leaves are piled sky high, well-oiled, and plentiful--so if you're with someone with whom you'd like to think you are graceful (dates, employers, etc), I recommend something less challenging like the Cacio E Pepe (also fantastic) 

Ambiance is wonderful--the bar is particularly beautiful and the pew-style chairs with menu cubbies give Italian catholic school. 

The staff is very friendly (even when they tell you the wait is 3+ hours, which can be hard to pull off!). 

Getting seated is objectively impressive and the lack of reservation enhances the experience. After all, patience is a virtue.

I've been here 4 times. Once was ok, all other visits were just bad. The service lacks warmth and hospitality. Its also slow and inattentive.  The food is really sub-par. Occasionally I've had a dish like, for example on my one good visit I really enjoyed the watermelon salad  (Cocomero) and I had a nice grilled Sea Bream. But those are the only two items I recall liking in particular and I wouldn't say either are worth running back for.  And of course its all very expensive! Poor service, food that mostly misses, and expensive - big thumbs down. I think the food is the most important part but if the service and general experiance of eating here was better I'd have given it 3 stars.

We finally freakin made it. After a couple attempts we finally got a table outside around 5pm on a very very hot Tuesday. Service got better as the evening went on since we really liked this one guy who ended up taking the table from another waitress? She seemed very cranky and suggested we ordered things on the menu that were expensive options only, which comes off kinda insincere. 

Ok onto food- we ordered cocktails to start and waiter immediately ordered Zucchini Fritti for us- yum! Great to share with cocktails! We then ordered Burrata (very small sadly) and the Carciofi alla Griglia (grilled artichokes with aioli)- this was delish! They are known for artichoke dishes so I would recommend you try one! Yum. We then shared the Tagliatelle (with prosciutto/peas) - pasta was good! We liked the meal.. not sure it's worth waiting over an hour though? Glad to finally check this off the list!!
Don't get me wrong this place was good. However, I felt like it is overrated for the cost. I got the pasta with prosciutto. It was good, but it was expensive and the portion was small.

Everything was DELICIOUS!! Best pasta we had in NY. Everyone was so nice, they seated us right away, and the atmosphere was great. I would go back here in a heart beat and definitely recommend going to everyone I know!

I LOVE THIS PLACE SO MUCH!!!

Read many 5-star reviews of this restaurant and they did not disappoint.
We visited Via Carota on a weekday for my birthday brunch. We were worried we would not be able to get a table since all reservations were booked so we arrived right when they opened at 11 AM and we were seated immediately.

The food was amazing! We ordered the Tonnarelli, Pappardelle, Tagliatelle, Pesto, and Polpette. The Tonnarelli (cacio pepe) was our favorite but all the dishes were just as delicious.
The service was great too. Everyone was so kind. We even brought our cat in a stroller and they gave us a private room.

The hype is well-deserved and I will 100% return the next time I am in New York. You need to visit this restaurant!!!!!!!

Got an outside table for 5 of us on a hot Saturday afternoon.  The food was delicious, the wait staff was professional and courteous.  Dishes were a bit small. Homemade pasta was delicious. Started with the shrimp and calamari appetizer.  Delicious! Dinner we ordered, seafood salad, parpadelle, lobster spaghetti, tagatelli, just enough for one person. Check this place out delicious and yummy!

I have been wanting to try this place for a while and it didn't disappoint!

We started with the octopus as an appetizer. It was cooked well but I wasn't blown away, and I probably would not order it again. The pastas were the star of the show. Such fresh al dente pasta. The cacio pepe felt decadent but somehow not too heavy with just the right amount of peppery in my opinion. Some of the best cacio pepe I've had. The wild boar ragu was very flavorful and the meat was tender. We got the chocolate mousse dessert which was just okay. 5 star purely for the pastas and I would come back to try some of the other pasta dishes.

Tip- It can be a struggle to get a reservation here, so if you have the flexibility I recommend coming early, putting your name down, and getting pre dinner drinks at any of the many cute bars in the area.

This place is a super tough table to get - and for good reason. 

Walking in, you definitely feel the old-school Italian vibes with the decor and simple cocktails list. 

We ordered Carciofi Alla Griglia (grilled artichokes and aioli) to start. The flavours were great, but there were portions of the artichoke that were super tough and not chewable. The dish might honestly still be worth it if you love artichokes, but just a heads up. 

We also ordered the Tonnarelli (cacio pepe) and Svizzerina (hand-chopped grass fed steak). We thought both these mains were amazing. We're not normally fans of cacio e pepe, but this was the best we'd had so far (and we've tried a lot of the other Italian heavy hitters in Manhattan and beyond). I also really enjoyed the Svizzerina: it had a great texture, and spreading the roasted garlic on top was amazing. 

For dessert, we finished with an olive oil panna cotta. Light and delicious, with some biscotti on the side. 

Overall, I would highly recommend visiting and I totally understand why it has such a good reputation! I'd love to come back and try some of the other appetizers.

First off, staff was so friendly and extremely accommodating helping me store my luggage while I ate.  As for the food: it was great!! The carbonara, Negroni, and shot of espresso were perfect.  This place really made my afternoon something to remember!

I typically post food from off the beaten path type restaurants. People ask me if I ever go to regular restaurants.  

Well last night (right after work) I was at Via Carota NYC. 

The dinner was 

Panzanella (salad)
Fava Escarole (salad)
Coniglio Fritto (Rabbit)
Meyer Lemon Risotto

Place was picked by my daughter (close enough to her office) and so were the dishes we ordered. Needless to say, how can you not love the food at a place that everyone loves.

Overall great experience! The staff were really kind and friendly, and my waiter took the time to share his favorite dishes from the menu! Food was delicious! We had to wait an hour without a reservation on a fairly busy weeknight which I've heard isn't too bad. I'd return again!

This is a tough reservation to get. There is usually a long line of people waiting for a table. We managed to snag a reservation and sat in the outdoor dining shack. Despite it being winter it was comfortable. The pastas are good but I loved the Fried Rabbit

I've been to Via Carota twice and I think it's the best Italian spot in the city that I've been to. Both times I didn't have a reservation but got there early on a week night (5:30-6:00ish) and sat without having to wait. 

Everything we ate was phenomenal but my favorite dish is the Tortelli w/ Ricotta pasta. It has so much flavor and melts in your mouth! I definitely recommend giving Via Carota a try.

Via Carota in the West Village has indisputably the best Cacio e Pepe in the city. Beyond the Cacio e Pepe, the wild boar ragu pappardelle was perfectly tender, and I cannot praise the perfect al dente texture of the fresh pasta. The nduja arancini was perfectly crisp and filled with spicy pork sausage and cheese. We ended the meal with a the silky tiramisu. A special place to go for a date if you can manage to snag a reservation.

This is a great Italian spot in NYC and the west village. The cacio r Pepe is excellent and so is the wild boar ragu pasta. They take a limited amount of resos each day so it's good to put an alert on Resy so you can snatch up the reservation.

The food is def worth the hype. The issue is the wait lol but hey that's nyc. Now to get into it... we came Sunday of Labor Day weekend, stood in line ~20 min to put our name down around 7:30, got our seat around 9, which honestly, for this spot, isn't too bad! In the meantime grabbed some drinks near by.

For food def do the green salad, very fresh! We also got the carrots which were cooked deliciously, came on a spread of Greek yogurt and tons of parsley. I will say these are slightly sweet, different than sides I've gotten at other places, but I def enjoyed! For main got the cacio pepe, def cannot go wrong here. We got tiramisu for desert which was delicious, I wouldn't recommend skipping out on dessert after all the hype lol. 

I def enjoyed this experience, the food was all great, I just don't know if it's worth the long wait. Overall a must experience for New Yorkers to get off the list, but hey  there's a lot of amazing Italian in nyc... Nevertheless these guys know what they're doing!
Outstanding food and service- arrived after theatre so despite other reviews we had no wait. Great waiter who explained the menu and made some great suggestions. Will certainly return.
Cacio y pepe. Mushrooms. Anchovie burrata with thick butter. Very decadent and worth every calorie!

I have not visited the restaurant for sometimes, it used to be the place where I would go when I felt homesick. I was extremely disappointed. I have found Via Carota tired and neglected. I sent back a embarrassing pasta dish that looked  as if it was already been digested only to be told that is the consistency of 'homemade pasta'.
As an Italian I can tell you, it is NOT true.
After a very disappointed lunch I hoped I could regain some confident with a good coffee at Pisellino, (same owner) next door coffe/cocktail place.
First of all Pisellino is just filthy and coffee was so bad I could not drink it.
Overall, very very very disappointed.
Delicious every time, good service, and it's nice to be able to walk in and grab a seat at the bar on the earlier side

Our absolute favorite Italian in the city, so happy they could seat our large party (6) on a Thursday night! People are not exaggerating when they say the cacio pepe is the best. We also had some excellent starters: mushrooms were a highlight! Also the gorgonzola bruschetta was *chef's kiss*

This place is average at best. The amount of peas in our meal from our salad to our pasta was insane--truly incredible. Didn't know we produced that many peas to be honest. The flavor was incredibly bland as well. We ate everything the waiter recommended. This is also a group opinion and not just my own. I think herd mentality is getting everyone here because it's just a hard pass at the price point. So many other fantastic restaurants in the city. Besos, John

10am Sunday morning brunch: The absolute perfect time to come and enjoy a quiet, attentive meal before the place gets LOUD by ~11:30am.

First off, Via Carota isn't a pasta restaurant. Expecting pasta at every Italian restaurant is like expecting sushi at every Japanese restaurant. Don't come here expecting to be wowed by pasta. This isn't what VC specializes in. It's all about the secondi here, so while there are a few pasta options, you really want to save your appetite for the entrees.

We got the Porri alla Cenere to start: charred leeks with sheep's curd. They were tasty but not easy to eat with a butterknife--I really wish we'd been given a sharper knife to cut through the stringy leeks. 

The pasta options were all super basic and uninspired, but we felt the need to try one to assess the quality of the noodles. The Tagiatelle with prosciutto and parmesan was a bit overcooked but obviously homemade. I liked the addition of lemon to make the cream sauce less rich. Still, this was meh, and I wouldn't bother with any of the pastas next time.

The standout of the meal was the Coniglio Fritto, fried rabbit, rosemary and garlic. It's so rare to find rabbit in an Italian restaurant, so when you do find one, please don't shy away from ordering it. In this case, the rabbit was perfectly crisp yet juicy and tender on the inside. The fried rosemary needles were the perfect accompaniment, and the fried bread piece that accompanied the rabbit was just carb icing.

Service was pretty quick and friendly during our first hour, then noticeably less attentive when things picked up. Still, we were able to pay and leave without waiting too long, which is bette r than many other hot spots I've been to.
We were tempted to order the famous cacio e pepe but decided to try something different. The pappardelle and tagliatelle were not bad, the arancini had to be my favorite and the salad was hefty.

Worth the hype. Any dish with prosciutto or artichoke in it, get it. The salad with peas and prosciutto--I don't know how they do it or what the dressing is, but it's one of the best salad dishes I've ever had. All the pastas are delicious, you really can't go wrong.
Every dish impressed! The aesthetic is gorgeous. The service is solid. Can't wait to return!

We came here right when they opened before our two show day to have a leisurely lunch and it was amazing. Every menu item was cooked to perfection and we were able to relax and enjoy our meal. We ordered too much food because it all was so good. We will be back.
Make a reservation! Amazing pasta and wine list! I love this place because not 'heavy' pasta feeling, but light and delicious.

The worser one of its sister restaurant, I Sodi, but I give this place 3.5 starts rounded up to 4. Mostly because of our waiter, who was really moody in general. He also gave us the wrong pasta and tried to persuade us to keep it when we immediately acknowledged we had ordered a different pasta in addition to the pasta we were supposed to receive. The fried rabbit was good (like a tender fried chicken) and the artichokes were alright. The wild boar ragu consisted of good fresh pasta but the meat was a little salty and oversauced. They also really take advantage of the outdoor seating. Wait on a Saturday afternoon was 30-45 mins for an outdoor table for two.

Horrible attitutde from host and manager, seems to be an ongoing problem looking at other reviews.  We walked out after waiting an hour and terrible communciation skills from host/mgr.  Food has been dissapointing as of late but still a loyal customer for almost 10 years, no more...there are better places with nicer staff.

We were on a quick weekend trip to NYC and Via Carota was the main restaurant on my list. We arrived without a reservation just before 8pm on a Friday night and were pretty quickly seated at an "unheated" sidewalk table, but it wasn't too cold (in late October) and I liked being able to see in the restaurant and be part of the city walking by. 

Dinner was efficient and completely delicious, start to finish. I had just heard an interview of the chefs on KCRW's Good Food and they spoke about the vegetables, so that was my main focus, though we were just two people, so we only ordered one: butter beans and spinach which is incredibly simple and oh so good. The other items were the 'njuda arancini, tender meatballs, the daily special pasta with truffles (my god), and zabaglione with fresh berries for dessert. My wine was perfect. 

We were out of there by 9:10pm in time to zip over to the Whitney for the pay-what-you-want Friday night!

I wish I got to try more food but I only got the fried rabbit dish and the cacio e Pepe. I was really torn between the cacio and the tagliatelle, but since they're famous for the cacio, I ultimately went with that. 

The cacio e pepe gives an Al dente bite, is peppery without being too peppery (very important for me), and is very butter forward. The Al dente chew was a touch too much for me and it isn't my favorite cacio e pepe in the city, but it's good. I would not have it again. 

The fried rabbit (coniglio fritto) was super good. The meat was juicy and flavorful BUT the fried bread it came with, spread with garlic confit, was amazing! This dish was memorable. 

Overall I recommend Via Carota but I feel it is overhyped. The line that started to form as I was leaving was really wild, and I've heard people wait 4 hours to get a table.. I'd like to try more of the menu in the future to see if that changes my mind, but for now, this isn't a "wait for 4 hours" restaurant. But it is good!

To be quite honest, the waitress was awful. She was so rude an inattentive and it was my boyfriends birthday so it made it extra unpleasant to deal with someone as deeply negative as her. Will not be returning. I spend plenty of money on food and wine but the condescending and deeply unfriendly tone of the female waiter waiting the outdoor tables tonight... simply unacceptable. I hope she gets a wake up call soon because no high quality service industry professional should treat people that way.

Stopped by here on a whim for an early dinner and drinks before catching a show. The food did not disappoint, I had the wild boar pappardelle and we were promptly seated  at a table for two outdoors, as we had asked. Our server was kind, but a little bit overstretched, so it took him a while to stop by our table between drinks and dinner, and settling up. All in all, a good experience, great people watching, and delicious food.

difficult to make a reservation. Hotel tried phoning but only a voicemail which said they take walking. went as a walk in and got a cold reception from the hostess, not very inviting. got a table 2 hours later and they brought the wrong salad from what we ordered as a starter.
Food was generally good,  it li it's menu, would not go back

I think via Carota is a little over hyped. There are better easier to get into Italian restaurants in nyc. I ordered the salad which was plain and the cacio e Pepe. The cacio e Pepe was cooked perfectly but still a little plain. I don't remember the wine I had but their wine was so good!
The hostess last night, Josie was rude. You can be polite and simply tell people a restaurant is full. No reason for the attitude.
Great food, atmosphere, and customer service. I recommend the cacio pepe and wild boar ragu.

This was hard to get a reservation so I waked in for lunch and got sat immediately at the bar. The place was rusty and cozy, and the service was ok. I got cibreo toscani (chicken liver w bread) for appetizer and the dish was warm and nice, but can be a little bit overwhelming. I also got Tagliatelle which was disappointing and a tad salty. Overall, the place was ok, but I was not impressed with the experience.

It's good..... not wait for hours good though. I know they probably like the long lines infamy but it would be so easy to just say no walk ins and open up actual reservations that people can realistically get (I believe they only have reservations in name only, typically almost all will be gone even weeks ahead and your best bet is to waitlist). 

The cacio e pepe is good of course, I personally love the dish sizes but a lot of people might find the lack of sides and small potions wanting. Aka my guest with me!

Cacio Pepe - stellar as was the risotto! Service excellent on all fronts, got help with the wine pairing, menu suggestions (even though we were there for the cacio de pepe )

I'd go back in a heart beat

We arrived with a party of 6 and were seated in a private dining room. Unbelievable experience with the highest of service! Excellent drinks and food was unbelievable. We f we I'll certainly come back and recommend this place to all of our friends.

Before I talk about the food, I have to give props to Vincenzo our server -- we had a reservation for 8:30 pm on a Wednesday and had to wait nearly 40 min for our table. I think we managed to stay pleasant and polite but were clearly a bit at the end of our rope once we sat down. Vincenzo very quietly had a complimentary appetizer sent to us, as well as refilling my husband's (very good) wine twice without charge. All of which was much appreciated and we thought reflected very well on Via Carota's hospitality. 

That really made our dinner -- so it was truly a bonus that the food was of course very good as well. We had the grilled artichoke, arancini, papardelle w boar ragu, tagliatelle w prosciutto and svizzerina (which was quite accurately described by Vincenzo as "like a seared steak tartare") -- the tagliatelle is definitely on the richer/cheesier than expected side (and wish it had a little more prosciutto to balance out said cheesy pasta). Otherwise, highly recommend all.  And aside from the wait, we found the overall atmosphere warm and friendly.

Food amazing. Salads huge, pastas normal sized. Reasonably priced. Nice feel to inside of the restaurant. Lot of authentic touches. 

Service professional, but brusque (ok, it's been a few years since I've been in NY...) Lots of butter and olive oil, which is part of why it is so good. Bread mediocre... cold (as if out of refrigerator) and on the dry side. 

Oh, lastly, when I asked to see a display copy of their cookbook (which they display for sale all over the restaurant, the server said, "we don't have a desk copy for you to look at," then pretty much left. Too bad, mighta bought a cookbook if I could've looked at it.

Radiaccio grilled salad is delicous. The pasta is also delicious and perfectly al dente.

I ordered Pomodoro (not on the menu) it was ok but lacked a bit of flavor.

Also I asked for a but of parmesan and they charged it like a side which is pretty bizzare to me.

I would come back for sure.

Be prepared to wait or come early and leave your name.

I never wait in line for a restaurant, however a friend suggested this place and we waited about 45 min at 5pm and were seated by 5:45. To start, the service was great and everything we ordered was delicious. I highly recommend sharing plates here, the cacio e Pepe and steak were so damn good, probably the best I ever had. We were so hungry so we had the fritters and bruschetta of the day as appetizers as well. I would Highly recommend this place if you have the patience to wait.

Impeccable service and delicious food. Chicken Liver on toast was great. Their bread with olive oil was good too. The salad was fresh and just perfect. Pasta (pappardelle with wild boar ragu) was cooked to perfection. For dessert we had their chocolate mousse and panna cotta which came with a biscotti on the side. It was packed and we were told the wait time would be approximately 30 mins but they called us within 10-15 mins. Highly recommend this restaurant for great Italian food. The only thing I would avoid would be adding a tiny bit of extra virgin olive oil over the panna cotta it's a little too overpowering.

One of the best Italian meals I have had in the city. There was a long line at 5 pm on a week day so we sat at the bar (it was a shorter wait) and were waited on by a very helpful bar tender. Outstanding food and reasonably priced wine. We'll be back soon.

Apparently, this is the place to be if you want to people watch as my wife said that various local celebrities frequent this place.   Not sure if it was the time we went as it was early for dinner and most people there at around 5pm are just getting drinks or a late lunch.  For us on the other hand, i guess you could say we were having and early bird dinner since we didnt make any reservations and were just walk ins.  Overall the food was decent but to be honest nothing to rave about and the prices were a little steep.  I dont know if its because i was comparing this place to Don Angie but man was i blown away with their dishes last year.

Disappointed. Went after a long day at work and wanted to walk in for a solo meal of wine and pasta. Was seated right away at the bar which was good. Ordered a glass of red wine, sad pour for what you are paying, got the parpadelle ragu, fine but nothing special, tiny portion. Dont need to go, there is plenty better, glad i crossed that off the list, wont be returning. 
Side note, cocktails that i didnt get looked good and guy next to me's cacio e pepe smelled bomb. :)

It helps to have a friend who eats here often and can recommend exactly what to order!  We started with the grilled artichoke and insalat verde, then moved to the broccolini and cacio Pepe, then I had the grilled fish. Paired with a Negroni terra. And finished with a cannoli. Service was excellent!

Fantastic meal! Long wait for a weekday evening (1.5 hr wait at 6pm on a Wednesday), but well worth it. We had the bread and olive oil, the insalata verde, the Fagioli All'Uccelletto (cannelli beans and sausage), the wild boar ragu pappardelle, and grilled pork belly. Everything was beautifully plated, seasoned perfectly, and left an impression. This was the perfect amount of food for two pretty hungry people. Wine list was great as well and service friendly and responsive.

My second favorite Italian restaurant in New York, right after the sister restaurant of I Sodi! Hard to grab a table via resy, but what I definitely recommend is going on a week day and putting your name down with a friend and bar hopping in the area. Feels like the wait isn't too long then. Loved their lemon risotto in particular but I'll be going back again and again as a regular. Go ASAP!

This place is almost impossible to get a reservation, I tried a few times and eventually opted for walk in. We waited for about 20 mins on a Friday afternoon, so it wasn't too bad. When I tried for dinner walk in during summer time, I was told that the restaurant was fully booked for the night TWICE. So, I wouldn't try for peak dinner time walk in. 

We got seated in the party room, it's large enough to fit 12 people and we were seated at one end of the large table while there's another family sitting at the other end of the table. For food, we ordered funghi, cacio e pepe and the boar tagliatelle. The mushroom was lacking a bit of flavor but great when mixed with the tagliatelle pasta sauce. Cacio e pepe was amazing! The pasta tasted really fresh, the texture and flavor were on point, portion size was also  generous. 

Food came out quickly, service was good, I'd love to come back another time!

Via Carota has been on my list for forever, but it's impossible to get reservations. We luckily got off the waitlist on Resy and were able to get a table for 2 at 5:45.

Ambiance is great - a cute, bustling Italian restaurant with both indoor and outdoor seating. 

Food was amazing 10/10. We loved our grilled artichokes and cacio e pepe, but the star of the show were the meatballs with pine nuts and raisins. Pretty pricy for 3 meatballs for $28 (feels more like an appetizer to me), but the sauce was phenomenal.

Service on the other hand was a bit strange and left a lot to be desired. We didn't order drinks and felt judged for not doing so. We were mostly ignored and rushed. We were in and out of there in around an hour. It felt like they didn't think we were going to get much, so didn't treat us like paying customers. V disappointed, otherwise would have given this place 5/5 stars.

4.5 stars! Loved it here!! The ambience was so nice and so fun. I got to catch you a Pepe and we got the fried macaroni and cheese and wine. It was just so delicious. I would highly recommend and come back.

lovely atmosphere, food very good.  unfortunately we had a waiter who rushed through descriptions and was very unhelpful, difficult when it came to the bill   manager had to fix it. would definitely go back for the food, vibe but hope this waiter is working elsewhere

The best and most consistent Italian spot in the city.

The grilled artichokes are a must! My favorite pasta dish is the Tagliatelle.

My first experience at Via Carota felt so special. It was a warm early summer day and a close friend was in town visiting. A group of 6 of us arrived when they first opened and were immediately seated. Everything tasted good! I wasn't the biggest liver fan, but the liver mousse on toast was good to try. To this day, I don't know if it was the friend group or what, but that meal always stuck out to me as one of my favorite meals in NYC.

Fast forward to the post-pandemic world where I've learned forget about trying to score a reservation on Resy. Instead, just get to the restaurant any time between when they open and 30 minutes after they open and you can usually get a seat. 

Via Carota is best with a group of 3+ and 6 is perfect because there's not much space in the restaurant for large groups, but 6 allows you to try a little bit of everything.

The green salad always is a nice opener. Pastas are great and the fried rabbit is not bad. At the same time, all of the food is delicious. 

Would I wait 30 minutes for this place? Nope. 

However, it's a great meal if you're able to score a table right away.

We sat outside but it was heated and warm enough. Didn't need jackets but kept my sweater on. Got a peak of the inside which was cozy and warm feeling and very busy .
Ok so for the food- I felt it was pretty average Italian food. Maybe because it's so hard to get reservation and it's on everyone's list to try, so I had high expectations? I had the tonnarelli and it was just okay. My friend had the tagliatelle pasta and she also felt it was just okay. For starter we had the salad, castelfranco - the hazelnut honey dressing was delicious. Best part was the chocolate mouse dessert, I don't know the name for it as it was a verbal dessert menu.
Service was great! Friendly and fast.

I went to via Carota on a nice warm summer day and sat by the bar with my friends. We were able to be seated immediately. We ordered as an appetizer the baguette, with a dollop of butter and anchovies. We ordered a cheesy pasta and some cocktails. The bartenders were very pleasant, and we even had some side conversations with the other patrons. Although the restaurant was extremely busy, the service remained impeccable.

Been dying to try it for a really long time and it didn't exactly disappoint. We ordered the classics - salad and the cacio pepe- they were both great, the salad is a bit much for two people but very well dressed. Of course it was expensive

Stopped here for bite to eat, was seated immediately and the wait staff was attentive. The food was delious and savory. Definitely recommending it to family and friends. Great place to eat before Eddie Izzard's GREAT EXPECTATIONS premiere!!!!

We were lucky enough to pick up a canceled reservation on Resy and had no choice but to bring our dog, who they accommodated beautifully! The food was unreal, service was solid and people watching was fun! Can't wait to return.

I heard a lot about Via Carota, it is a bit overrated. The food is good but nothing worth going crazy about especially for the price! We had 2 different servers that night, which one of them was extremely rude. It's cute and intimate but a bit loud. 
The mushroom was everyone's favorite dish. I definitely would not get the tiramisu again. It was pretty bad. I dont know that I will be going back.

Great causal neighborhood vibe, good food, really rushed service.  The entrees came on top of the appetizers, and by the time we finished saying the word "tiramisu", it was at our table. Maybe it was a Saturday night thing, but it felt like they wanted to turn our table over the second we sat down. Loved the atmosphere, but can you please just let us have a bit of a breather between courses?

Food- 9 out of 10
Price-7 out of 10
Service- ZERO OUT OF TEN

Of the 8 visits, I had ONE waiter that understood service. The rest are INCREDIBLY RUDE, disconnected and give off the "I'd rather be any place but here" attitude. ESPECIALLY the ones behind the bar

in one word 
"pretentious " I every aspect 

Keep in mind some of the most popular hard to reserve ( intentionally) restaurants are no longer in business.

Never disappointed at Via Carota. The atmosphere gives Tuscan home in the countryside and the food is out of this world. Their menu always amazes me with the perfect blend of both pastas and heavy mains with delicious shareable veggie dishes. 

I bring all of my visitors in the city to Via Carota and they are always in awe.

Need to know: walk in for lunch on a week day or be willing to eat outside under their heaters on a cool night,

Must order: Cacio e Pepe, wild boar ragu, Pere e Gorgonzola bruschetta, a Negroni :)

Best italian food in town.
Absolutely loved it. 
The cacio.peppe was amazing.
Highly recommend.
Worth the wait. Amazing food & drinks and the line moved faster than we were anticipating. Definitely worth a visit!

My friend and I hadn't seen each other for a month and decided to meet here on a freezing evening to catch up over some food and drinks. There were no tables available on Fri eve but we got a place at the bar and we ordered a bottle of wine, appetizers, entree, dessert, plus wine by glass and after 3 hours and after spending over $250 were rudely shoved a check in our face and asked to leave by their assistant general manager - Andrew.

Having lived in NYC for over ten years, I know that there is never ever a time limit to sit at a bar, at a dinner table, yes. Also, if that was a rule, we should have been informed at the door before we sat down. After talking to both the general managers - we were told rudely by Mr. Andrew that he is pals with the management and doesn't care about a customers feedback.

My friend and I left. Never going back there again. Even if the food was great, the staff and their treatment of their customers was off putting. Ruined our night. Went there excited to try a place with great reviews about food, but left with a bitter taste.

Disappointing food. I was SO excited to try the infamous Via Carota- known for their cacio e Pepe and star-studded regulars- as it's been on my list to try in NYC for years. It's also owned by the same chef as I Sodi, its equally as well-known sister restaurant.

We were able to walk-in and get seated with only a 30 min wait for Saturday at lunchtime. Reservations are almost impossible to get, but they're one of the few "top restaurants" that accepts walk-ins.

Overall, the food was fine. Not great, not bad, just fine. I truly don't understand the hype? We started with the Gorgonzola, pear, and walnut bruschetta, and that was honestly the best part of the meal.

Then, my sister and I split the cacio e Pepe and one of their specials of the day, a ricotta tortellini with mushrooms. The special pasta had a lot of flavor, and it got better with every bite, but it wasn't my favorite pasta flavor.

Now, for the ever disappointing cacio e Pepe...when it came out it was very clear that there's almost no cheese on the dish- just some grossly torched mozzarella on the top. The pasta itself was homemade (you can tell), but there was ZERO flavor, so all you could taste were little pepper chunks. It felt like I was eating straight pepper...

The tables are close together, so we ended up talking with the couple next to us, and they agreed everything was simply fine. They also didn't get the hype.

We didn't get the salad, but it seemed like every other table in the restaurant did. When I tell you that it's straight lettuce (not even cut up) with no dressing- what are these people thinking?! It looked like they grabbed a bag of lettuce and put it in a plate and served it for $22.

Overall, would not come back as there are 17937161 better Italian places in the city. Also, this restaurant group is known for their rude service.

Although something neat is that they don't have any sodas because they make their own. My sister got the pomegranate soda, but it tasted like pure juice with no carbonation.

Oh...and the Trader Joe's cacio e Pepe is better than Via Carota's. I said what I said!!!

LOVED their green salad and bruschetta. The mushroom pasta and carrots were both good but not special in my opinion (also the carrots are served cold and not hot which was not what I expected). My friend got their gnocchi with Gorgonzola sauce and said it was one of the best gnocchis she had ever had.

This place has been on my radar for the longest time, and considering it is hard to book, I was ready for the challenge to get a reservation. I managed to finally get one, and my friend and I were excited to go since it seemed so popular. We entered the restaurant and were met by a cozy and cute interior, with white table cloths covering every single table. Except ours. Which was a little strange, but my friend and I are not particularly picky, so we didn't ask to switch tables. We were seated and given some time to look over the menus (which are very cutely situated in the back of your seat), and since we looked at other people's reviews beforehand, we were ready to order right away:

Drinks:
Cynar Spritz and Old Fashioned - the cocktails that I and my friend got, respectively. Both were very solid; I particularly liked mine since I feel it was sweeter than a normal spritz, but if you have ever had an Old Fashioned and like spirit-forward drinks, the Old Fashioned here was very solid.

Food:
'Nduja Arancini - came first with the other appetizer we ordered (which I will talk about next). Very, very solid arancini. The outside was really nice and crispy with a soft and very savory interior (because of the 'nduja) which I liked quite a bit. A very good start to the meal, though I wouldn't say it broke barriers as far as arancini goes.

Carciofi alla griglia (grilled artichokes) - the other appetizer we ordered because it was mentioned time after time after time in other people's reviews, and goodness me, these people were RIGHT. Def some of the best artichokes (if not the best) I've ever had, with a nice citrus and smoky flavor paired with such a smooth, light, but creamy aioli. Absolutely delicious, would definitely get these again if I were to come back!

Funghi (mushrooms) - we actually ordered this at the end since we wanted one more savory dish before dessert, but I'll include it here before the entrees since it gives more appetizer vibes. Pretty solid mushrooms, but it really came together once you took a bite with the scarmoza cheese included at the bottom of the dish. Quite tasty, but I wish they included more cheese since it only came with three pieces for so many mushrooms.

Tonnarelli (cacio e pepe) - one of three entrees we ordered, and one of their most famous dishes according to other restaurant goers. It was definitely a very good cacio e pepe; really nice sauce with that nice peppery flavor, just what I was expecting. However, that's just the problem imo; it was just as I expected. It was for sure yummy, but I really don't think it blew me away like how I expected it to based on the rave reviews. I would def try it though if you go here and if you like cacio e pepe.

Pappardelle (wild boar ragu) - one of the other entrees we ordered and the other pasta of the night, both my friend and I liked this a lot since we both love pappardelle and ragu. Super flavorful with the meaty goodness of a good ragu, and the pasta was cooked perfectly (which I forgot to mention about for the cacio e pepe, since that was perfect too in terms of texture). Probably our personal favorite over the cacio e pepe, but I think we prefer more acidic, meatier sauces anyway.

Via Carota Svizzerina - the last of the three entrees we ordered, and probably one of the most unique dishes we have had at an Italian restaurant. It's funny because we both though it looked like a Salisbury steak, but once we took a bite, we both fell in love. The crust from the searing was absolutely AMAZING, while the interior was nice and smooth, characteristic of high quality meat. Honestly one of our favorite dishes of the night; so unique, and probably something I wouldn't be able to get anywhere else (at least from what I've seen).

Dessert:
Zabaione - one of the desserts we got, and this was super surprising because it was so simple yet SO good. The custard paired so so well with the fresh tartness of the raspberries (which were so good btw). I know it looks and sounds simple, but you won't regret getting it because it was just that good!

Semifredo - the other dessert we got; basically a Ferrero Rocher in dessert form! So chocolately and hazelnutty, and packed with real hazelnuts. Def super yummy, but nothing super groundbreaking.

Overall: I think it was a very solid meal. Didn't dislike anything, service was pretty good, and interior was very cute. However, for the amount of effort I had to put in to get this reservation, I think it falls just short of me wanting to try again in the near future. If someone were to invite me to go though, I would def consider!

We went there on a Wednesday afternoon. They start taking names for walk-ins at 5 pm, which is a plus, and the wait was immediate. The ambiance is comparable to Il Buco, cozy and not packed, unlike Balthazar: decent-looking servers and a comfortable atmosphere. Perfect for singles, couples, or even group dine-in. 

Steven was a charm when he brought up Chef's special menu, which includes the following. I forgot the names, but I only remember how delicious and mouth-watering it was and is worth the price. Okay, less the Negroni Rosa. 

YOU WILL NEVER REGRET DINING IN! I am telling you!

I got violently ill from last nights dinner. The chickpea appetizer and cacio e pepe were the only good things. The tagliatelle was mush and insalata verde was tasteless. Do yourself a favor and go to L'Artusi, significantly better.

It's worth the hype. A Negroni that beats out Dante's finest, every dish and drink we had left us impressed. The Negroni bianco is smooth, goes down so easily. How lucky I was to go in a larger group-- we did family style, which gave us the opportunity to sample en masse. Who knew salad, the insalate verde specifically, could be this decadent? The tagliatelle was fantastic, as was the cacio pepe. Same with the svizzeruina! I wasn't as keen on the pappardelle., though, and felt like you can probably get a better espresso martini elsewhere. Still, Via Carota delivers.

Appetizers were okay - the main star of the night was the cacio e Pepe. However, you can get the same cacio e Pepe at Vic's restaurant where there are better apps and it's less of a hassle to snag a resy.

Not worth the wait or the hype; disappointing; please think twice! 
1.) the service was not good -- long waits for attention or food, as well as 3 different servers asking the same questions repeatedly (it's oddly annoying to tell 2 different people you've ordered drinks.) Plus, the servers won't explain to you that the menu is made to share family-style. This has happened twice now and is truly unprofessional. It's helpful to know something like this in advance. 
2.) The food was cozy, but nothing worth the long wait. This was my second time eating here and it was exactly the same as the first -- bad service and mediocre food.  Go elsewhere if there's a wait! Please!! 
3.) The food preparation was well-intentioned but not quite right. Namely, too much overly rich pasta sauces (think olive garden.. i'm sorry to say)
4.) some recs instead: Lilia or Rucola in Brooklyn. Max in Tribeca.

We come to New York 2 to 3 times a year and on each trip we make a point to dine here.  We ventured out on Super Bowl Sunday knowing the restaurants in New York would be quiet.  Our party of 3 was able to get in without a wait.  Our server was very pleasant however she forgot to tell us the specials and we only realized at the end of our meal when we heard another server explain it to their guests.  Our trips to Via Carota were always for the pastas.  On this visit, we had the Tonnarelli Cacio Pepe and the Pappardelle Wild Boar Ragu.  The Tonnarelli lacked flavor and had no pepper taste, just a plate of cheese pasta.  The Boar Ragu was tough and bland.  We left the ragu on the plate and ate the pasta.  Both pasta portions were smaller than usual. The Panissa - fried chickpea was delicious.  A very pleasant surprise as we had no idea what to expect.  Very disappointing trip after so many wonderful visits.  Sadly this will not be our go to restaurant in New York anymore. A lot of money to spend for below average pastas.
Very cozy yet vibrant vibe. The staff is really nice, helpful, and service is quick and attentive. Highly recommend their salads and vegetable-based dishes. The pasta and risotto were good too.
The most overrated restaurant in NYC. Small portions and not good food. Not worth the wait or reservation.
Food, ambience, and service were perfection. Went on a Monday and waited about an hour and a half at the cute bar across the street. Worth the wait.

This place was very solid all around.  I went with a buddy and grabbed a reservation a month in advance through Resy, and given how notoriously difficult it is to get a reservation, I had high expectations coming in.  The staff was great and prompt, and the ambiance was very nice inside and a little posh which gives it a cool vibe. The food was good - I got a few dishes with some corresponding pictures below:

Arancini: not pictured below, but these were really really good. Light and crispy with chili oil inside gave it a very nice kick to the creaminess of the filling.

Cacio e Pepe: I've seen so many reviews claiming the best in the city, but this was so so and not worth getting again imo. The noodles were very very firm, and there was too much butter. Not for me unfortunately.

Tagliatelle: this was a very unique take on a tagliatelle inspired dish and I honestly was impressed, even tho it was heavy again on the butter.  The dish itself was like a butter cream sauce with prosciutto on top (the prosciutto was definitely imported btw because it basically melted in your mouth), with parmesan sprinkled on top. What made this unique was the use of nutmeg in the sauce which gave it an aromatic bite that reminded me of like a fall dish - very cool, and I would probably get it again.

Pappardelle: another classic, this was the best dish imo. This came with a boar ragu that tasted very similar to an osso buco like dish - with the Parmesan balancing it out the dish was very well rounded and the noodles were great (you can tell they're homemade too based on the texture, delicious!).

All in all, it came out to about $120 after tip with no drinks, so it's right in the price range of the nice Italian restaurants in the city (arguably with a bigger portion size than rezdora for example).  I think this gets in between a 4 and a 5 on yelp only because of the cacio e pepe, which again as usual is overhyped in nyc. Still very solid Italian food and if I could somehow score a res again I would def come back.

I've tried several popular Italian restaurants in the city, and Via Carota was the best recently (my second favorite was Misi in Brooklyn). Via Carota not only makes fantastic pastas, but also it has lots of other choices for balance, like meats and vegetables. My favorite non-pasta dish was the Radicchio Treviso - which is grilled radicchio, with some soft goat cheese on the bottom and pine nuts on the top. It was super delicious!! Many restaurants have great salad, but barely has great cooked veggies.

Speaking of pasta, I ordered gorgonzola gnocchi and my friend ordered mushroom ragu stracci - the latter one was not on the regular menu, it was a special dish. Both of them were super nice!! I was going to order cacio e pepe, but had a craving for gorgonzola so I decided to try how it goes with gnocchi, and it turned out to be a delightful surprise! And mushroom stracci was also nice! The only thing that was not perfect was the stracci pasta sticked together a little bit - it didn't affect the overall experience, but could've been done better.

The fried green olives with pork was also great! Never tried this kind of combination and I liked it!

Last but not least - the dessert! They have too many dessert choices and I wanted to try them all - too bad I only have one stomach lol. Finally we ordered zabaione and coffee affogato. I liked them both! They were not super heavy or sweet, so they were perfectly balanced.

Finally I want to mention the services. Before I came here, I saw some reviews saying they were famous for rude services, but my experience was great. Our waitress and other staff were far away from "rude". They were super nice and considerate. When we ordered, we were too hungry so we ordered much more than we could eat, so in the middle of the meal, we asked our waiter if we could cancel the rest dishes that had not been served yet, and she very kindly did it for us.

Overall all, I loved Via Carota and will definitely come back soon.

My girlfriend and I made our third visit to New York this year (yay Southwest Companion Pass!) and I signed up for the waitlist on Resy a couple days before our arrival. We were fortunate to get a notice for a 2pm outside patio table as we were taking the bus shuttle from LaGuardia. Upon arrival we were further excited to have our outside patio table upgraded to an inside table which made the experience so much better. The service was friendly and efficient and the food (carpaccio, cacio de pepe) was excellent. Sitting two tables away from an actor we both greatly admire made the experience even more wonderful. NY!!!

Very average... left disappointed.

Server was very unfriendly.

No need to revisit this restaurant.

Not worth the hype. Waited 30 minutes for an 8:45PM reservation with no apologies from the rude hostess and when asked about it, she said you came at 8:50PM which is besides the point. 

The grilled artichoke and Cacio e Pepe were decent but the food overall was underwhelming. The portions were small and expensive. Will not be coming back.

We walked in for a weekday lunch and was able to get seated immediately on the "communal table' (a long table that can fit 12 but it didn't feel packed). The restaurant was busy for a weekday! The servers were attentive and checked in with us but not to the point that it was over bearing. As for the food

Salad was delicious and tasted super fresh! I would say it is overpriced for what it is though and I don't need to order it again.

Cacio pepe was the star of our meal! It was al dente and buttery. Perfect in every way and had the right amount of pepper. Even though the dish appeared small it was filling. 

Wild boar ragu pappardelle was a bit on the dry side. Wish it had more sauce.

Affogato was delicious! Expresso was very fresh and the gelato was delicious!

Will definitely be back to try other stuff!

Really enjoyed the outside dining with heating and space. Our server Janice and her support Alejandro were so caring and attentive. They were there at the right moments and so professional yet put you at ease at the same time. 

The food was a star as well with the Cacio Pepe and the grilled sea bream cooked to perfection. I want to take the insalata verde salad dressing home with me. 

Also the Negroni terra was my favorite of the variations on the menu.

Just okay.  Mediocre food.  Tagliatelle pasta should've been more al dente and lacked flavor.  The Brussels sprout salad needed acid. 

On top of it, we had a really condescending and inattentive waiter.

We visited on Saturday for lunch.  Perhaps we got the B team or maybe it was a off day for Via Carota but I won't be back to find out.  There are better, more consistent restaurants in the city.

Pretty disappointing. Took a lot of effort to get a reservation (practiced refreshing Resy right at 10am) and can definitively say it wasn't worth it.

We had mixed reviews on the food. We enjoyed the fried olives and the fried rabbit, but the cacio e pepe was very average, and the carrots were cold and bland, bad enough to be difficult to finish. 

Service was also a bit lacking. They were running about 10-15min late on reservations, and service felt rushed. It was hard to get a hold of the server, and we had items forgotten from our order.

This place usually has a long wait for a table or during dinner always booked with reservations. My friend and k luckily got here at a great time (1:15pm on a Sunday) and were able to get a table right away. 

Service was a bit slow but the team is very nice 

It's a cute spot, of course nyc scaffolding really sucks and takes away from their cute outdoor aesthetic but inside is adorable. 

Food is decent. Not the best Italian, my noodles were a little too soft but flavor was good. Cacio e pepe was cooked perfectly. Artichokes were SO good. 

Pasta run about $25+, and medium sized portions.
Went for brunch on Saturday. All food was spectacular. My only criticism was things felt very rushed and servers added to that f

Food was great - risotto was not too creamy and had a big portion size for the table. Salad was fresh. Cacio e pepe was great!! It was creamy and a surprisingly big portion. Risotto balls had an interesting spiced pork/mixture inside which was great. 

Service was ok! It was super busy so didn't get too much attention from the waiter after our food came
Not impressed. Food not memorable. Service adequate. Will not return. Sad because we were excited about it. There is no reason this is such a tough reservation.

This has been one of my favorite restaurants in the city for years.  Delicious food, and a lively yet cozy atmosphere.  

I was on my way home late on a weeknight and decided to try to make a quick stop for dinner at the bar.  My cacio e pepe was as delicious as ever, and the service very attentive.  

But I was just a bit let down by what felt like a lack of polish/upkeep - maybe needs a little TLC or revamp to keep it fresh.  And some more seasonal menu changes.  That being said, I was surrounded at the bar by regulars, and there is a reason for that - the food is great.

Finally got to mark this one off my list! 

Amongst a party of three, we split the 'Nduja Arancini and got our own cocktails (Spagliato, Gran Spritz, Aperitivo Blanco) and pasta dishes (Tagliatelle, Pappardelle, Tonnarelli). I'd love to go again and try their other dishes to share for the table and order the Tagliatelle.

The interior vibes were intimate but still bustling, and there's two outdoor sections - a few tables that face the street (for a more Parisian effect) and right across are some heated tables.

Via Carota exceeded our expectations! Every dish we got was so delicious. My favorites were the grilled artichokes and the tagliatelle pasta with prosciutto. The service was delightful and the vibes were unbeatable! Not to mention the fantastic cocktails and wine. The negronis are top tier.

Can't recommend Via Carota enough and will 100% be returning!
Highly overrated, somehow I have had much better Italian at many other places around town that don't require you to book out weeks before. Would not recommend.

We tried almost every vegetable on our most recent trip with a big group, and WOW everything was just so perfectly done. The charred leeks in vinaigrette w/ sheeps curd was mind blowing.

I also loved the cacio pepe and the risotto w/ meyer lemon was SO bright and rich and yummy for a few bites. Actually - we just really loved all the pastas too.

We sat outside in their dining shed, and had a lovely experience at Via Carota. We managed to get a last minute reservation, by checking Resy week of, and when we arrived at 6:30 we were seated right away.

The service was excellent, and our server was able to help answer questions around dietary restrictions. They don't have gluten free bread or pasta, but the risotto and most of the vegetable, meat, and fish dishes were able to be made gluten free.

The risotto was delicious and the pasta was a hit, but the surprise favorite of our table was the Piselli salad. Highly recommend trying one or more of the salad/vegetable options.

Is it worth the hype and waiting in line for a chance walk in? Hard to say. It isn't the best Italian that I've had in NYC but it was certainly a fun experience trying it out and people watching!

Haven't eaten yet, because the gatekeeper keeps seating people ahead of us. We put our name in 45 minutes ago and she's told us 5-19-15 minutes for 45 now. Two different tables have been available the entire time. What a troll
This was an amazing experience! The service was excellent and so was the food. Definitely worth the wait, you won't regret it!

I've been trying to come here the past month or so, but I know their price went up after Taylor Swift was here a few weeks back. We got here at 11:45am on a Friday and decided to try our luck. I took the day off don't judge me. 
Still a 45-minute wait. I know this feeling all too well (10 minute version).
We opted to wait and grab a coffee across the street at Bar Pisellino as I think everyone does while waiting for their res. Get their hot chocolate, it's elite. 
After about an hour and 2 americanos to the dome the text came through. Our table was ready. BABY WE DONE IT!
I order an Aperol Spritz before my butt even hits the seat. This may be controversial, but I just much prefer a Spritz in a wine glass. If I wanted this type of glassware I would have ordered a Negroni. My glassware issue aside, the spritz was delicious and refreshing.
For food, we ordered prosciutto (ODE!), Insalata Verde (a must get), Wild Boar Ragu (disappointing), and the Arancini (Good).
To be quite honest, I was underwhelmed by the whole experience. I understand that expectations are the root of all heartache, but all the hype mixed with the wait time built a certain amount of anticipation I couldn't help but feel. Maybe it's a me problem. It's me. Hi...
To be honest, I have absolutely had better Italian food in the city. Also they charge $3 for bread and olive oil which is just annoying. 
The crown is heavy.

Didn't want to leave and - just like in Italy - no one rushed us out. Been dying to go here so walked in at 2 pm on a Tuesday. We had to wait about 1/2 hour. Had the arincini, artichokes, escarole and beans, pappardelle and chicken. Ended with an espresso. Yum is all I can say. Love the more casual, rustic feel. Service was excellent. Can't wait to go back.

Last minute Resy for lunch. Seated promptly outside which we didn't mind on a nice day. Ordered a bottle of Gavi, cacio e pepe, fried rabbit and chopped beef.  All were excellent and served promptly.
