Portions were a bit on the smaller side but quality was excellent. We definitely enjoyed Al fresco lunch and I could have easily ordered more especially salads that screamed fresh and alive.

Dropped into NY recently to catch sole shows and I had a list of restaurants to try, Via Carota being at the top of the list.

I got out of my Broadway show a little after 9:30 and took the train down to the  Christopher St station. I have to stay I was quite surprised they sat me but there were plenty of seats available. What happened to the city that never sleeps? This places closed at 11pm! People in NY used to go to dinner at 9:30 and 10pm.

The bar was full so they gave me a seat at a communal table which I thought was a great idea. I liked that as an option and more restaurants in LA should that. I think  République does this.

I ordered a lot. A cocktail, the bread, the cacio e pepe, the skate and the cannolis for dessert. The pasta is one thing everyone raves about and while it was good, I still thought it was on par with a lot of other restaurants with the same dish. The cannolis were pretty bland and the bread was good. The skate was the real star. Wish I hadn't filled up on pasta. That fish drenched in butter and lemon literally melted in your mouth. Amazing! So I amazing dish out of 3.

All in all, this does seem like a place you just go to be seen. I mean Dakota Johnson was sitting at the table next to me. It's just a tiny bit overhyped. Still good! The service was impeccable and they sat me immediately with no reservation. So thumbs up on all that! For the food, just don't expected too much and enjoy yourself. I'll be back.

Stopped to see if a friend and I could walk in and were lucky enough to get a table around lunch time. We sat out on the patio and ordered Arnold palmers which were refreshing for a warm may afternoon. I ordered the prosciutto pasta without peas and my friend ordered the prosciutto salad vegan style. The service was quick and the food was delicious. They were very accommodating to dietary restrictions. Would totally recommend this little spot.

Ate here for lunch today at the bar.  Michael was my server.  He noticed I was sweating and filled my water glass like 5 times.  Great service.  

Had the famous salad.  Best salad i can remember ever having.  Only greens and light dressing.  Flavors of the bitter greens, sundive and butter lettuce are just amazing.  I'm not even a salad person.   I ordered a Manhattan which did not go well with the salad at all.  It didn't matter, the salad brought my palate back every time.  I know this sounds pretentious as fuck but I don't care.  

Salad is huge and I couldn't finish it.  Brought the leftovers to my mom, she agreed one of the best salads she ever had.

I got my mom the pasta with prosciutto.  She said it's much better than Olive Garden.  She usually likes Olive Garden.  We will be back this weekend.

this was worth the hype! your best bet for avoiding the long wait is to go around 3pm on monday-wednesday; I was able to walk right in and got a nice table on the patio! the cacio e pepe and insalata verde are a a 10/10, I did not know pasta could taste like this !

The food and cocktails were excellent. The service was awkward. We were seated a couple of minutes late, even though we arrived right on time for our reservation -- nbd. But despite ordering quickly and generally working through things at a reasonable pace, it felt like we were being rushed out the door as soon we were served dessert. 

This feeling of being rushed put kind of a damper on the meal.

I also suspect that they're watering down their 20-year Pappy. My pour was noticeably less viscous and lighter in color and flavor than pours I've had elsewhere. Maybe they just got a bad bottle?

Apps were great & the cacio e pepe was the highlight! Wouldn't order the tagliatelle again but prosciutto was a nice touch. Sitting outside on a nice day is the best especially for people watching! Service was great & very helpful with what to order.

Excellent food and not the usual Italian and yet it is Italian!  I love the anchovy with butter in Bread.  You have to order it because it's just that surprisingly good!  The sardines is freshly grilled served with good amount of vegetables.  Also delicious!  The desserts are a must.  We had 3 kinds from their panacotta,  Chocolate semifredo,  to the berries with zabaglioni sauce - they were all equally great!  The meat balls were also very good and the seafood with beans.

Enjoyed my Aperol spritz but was not served in the usual large wine glass. I didn't like it in a short glass. 

We were 3 guests. We ordered appetizers and mains.  

The sardines, bread with butter and and spicy meatballs were delish. The cuttle fish was not very flavorful. We were thinking the pork belly would have a crispy top but it was not served that way. The marinade was good though. All three desserts were not overly sweet and tasted fresh and creamy. 

The staff at the start didn't look very peppy or happy. They were coming from a 3 day holiday. As the 2nd hour approached they became more attentive and friendlier. First impressions.  

Would recommend it since it's also located a stones throw away from the number 1 subway train.

Overall loved my lunch experience here! The key is to show up early if you don't have a reservation. We got the famous salad, 2 orders of tagliatelle, and the lemon risotto and shared it all. The double tagliatelle order was a recommendation from my friend who had been before and I'm glad she suggested it. Pastas we're delicious! The salad was also very good, but I want to give a disclaimer to readers that it's truly just greens piled high with a light vinaigrette dressing. It's VERY light and greens forward, so if you are someone who likes a dressed salad this may not be for you. That being said, my favorite part of the salad was the bottom that had extra dressing as a result of gravity (lol). They had one non alcoholic (non soda) beverage which was a house made ginger-ale that was good but VERY gingery. Cute interior, with a nice outdoor seating as well, service was quick, although at times it did feel as though they were trying rush us a bit. Again, if you can get a reservation great, but if not just go for lunch and show up at 10:45!
Came here from out of town with a local friend who's a regular. Imaginative menu. They have a cookbook also.

I've been wanting to try Via Carota ever since Taylor Swift dined here back in April!

My friend and I walked-in around 6:00 pm on a Thursday evening and were seated right away. Between the two of us, we shared nduja arancini, funghi and the famous tonnarelli. The portion size of each dish was great, we even had some leftovers. Out of the 3, my favorite was the arancini, which had a spicy and flavorful filling. I liked the savory cheese in the funghi entree but overall found the dish to be too bitter. The cacio e pepe was a bit of a letdown compared to all the hype surrounding it. I thought it was pretty bland and similar to all the other cacio e pepe dishes I've had.

Overall, the food at Via Carota is decent. I wouldn't recommend going out of your way to secure a reservation here or wait in a long line but if you happen to be in the area, it might be worth a try!
Very refined Italian dishes but portion sizes were quite small and prices were at a premium. Service was excellent and very attentive. Overall experience was ok, may have to give it a try again.

We loved Via Carota. Such a fun atmosphere and experience. We are on their patio and had a nice time. We order the Carciofi Alla Griglia as an appetizer. It was amazing. The artichokes had great flavor. For our main courses we had Pappardelle and the Tagliatelle. The food was great and we enjoyed the bread service as well. 
The only down side would be the service was very slow. 

We joined the walk up list around 6 pm and sat right away! The wait line looks more intimidating than it actually was. Great spot!

I was so excited we actually got seating even though it was outside with homeless people walking by every few minutes. I guess that's the service we were gonna get for just walking in and getting lucky enough to eat at the place New Yorks elite and celebs like Taylor swift and Dakota Johnson frequent.

I was so disappointed in the food. What I thought was supposed to be the city's number one trending Italian restaurant, the best thing they served us was the olive oil that came with the bread.

The Cacio Pepe was disgusting and tasted like barf food. Like when you taste the back of your throat when throwing up, I was like wow this is so bad. Yet this was the number one trending thing at this place.

The broccoli rabe was extremely bitter like they couldn't figure out how to cook it right.

The special of the day was some raw ish vegetarian pasta which green shmutz that might as well have been rabbit food. 

I think Pizza Hut makes better Italian food than here. 

I would never return and I'm shocked how positive the ratings are, makes me think they might be sponsoring them. 

Also a homeless person walking by dipped his finger in our water and the staff did nothing to stop it or change the water after. I was like ok we're done here and then left

Unfortunately had a very unpleasant experience at via carota. Not only was the service extremely underwhelming (our waiter never came back to check how our meal was) but the food was glorified butter noodles and extremely dry bread. They didn't have either very common wines we requested or any sodas for our non alcoholic drinkers. Cannot understand the hype or why there is a line out the door. Must be tourists.

Wanted to love this place so much!  Service was terrible and the server was so rude!  We were sat relatively quickly for not having a reservation and looking forward to a cocktail before our meal. Tables to the left and right of us were sat after us and received their cocktails before we even were asked for our order. Then we ordered our food and asked the waitperson to bring our drinks and bruschetta before our other food (as we were still ordering, we asked this question!), but we were told they had already submitted our vegetables, so they would come first, then our bruschetta and then our mains.  Asked for a glass of wine with the mains, and waiter said they would bring over the bottle to taste first, but then proceeded to clear tables and other things before even bringing a taste of wine (which was their offer, not my request), so mains arrived with no wine. At the end of the meal, I asked for an ice cube to refresh my half finished spritz.  Never came.  Asked ten minutes later, and after a while they came back to discuss the dessert menu, still without the ice cube, and were told that it would be ten more minutes for the ice!  Just rude, condescending attitude throughout the meal.  Never an "I'm sorry" or a "Let me check on that for you" or any kind words- just annoyance that we actually asked for anything!  Let me also mention - we were not in a hurry what so ever- it was just inordinately poor service, while the tables next to us were moving through their meals and receiving their requests in a timely manner, so it was very apparent that we were being intentionally treated poorly. The food was good to very good, but don't think we will be back.
The ambiance is great! The staff is good. The food is FABULOUS!! I would recommend trying this spot.
Food was good but service was terrible. Waiter took our order but never came back, which was very dissapoint if
Great pasta spot in NYC (even without celeb sightings). Get there at 5 to avoid a massive line. Solid portions for a place of this quality. Nice ambience and outdoor seating too. Fast service

My partner and I wanted to have an impromptu date night, and we were fortunate enough to get two seats at the bar at Via Carota (was around 8:30pm on a Sunday, place was packed). This Italian restaurant has been on our radar for quite some time and we were excited to be able to finally try it. 

We ordered a couple drinks to start (the house Italian martini and a glass of rose); I would probably do one of their nigronis next time instead. The rose was delicious though!

The service was friendly -ish, attentive, and spaced out dishes at a very appropriate manner, which we greatly appreciated!

Now on to the food... We ordered a total of four dishes between the two of us (and yes it was a lot of food). But I do recommend 3-4 dishes if sharing with another (5 would've been perfect for 3 people). We started with the bruschetta with cultured butter and anchovies (little pricy, but one of my favs for the night), then got a generous portion of Frito misto (which tasted fresh and was delicious), then we got the famed tagliatelle pasta with prosciutto and peas (I recommend either this one OR the cacio y pepe - as quite similar in sauce), and last we ended with the char pork and onion dish (forget official name, but this was a surprise sleeper too!)

Overall, happy we were able to finally try Via Corota and happy with the dishes we ordered!

I am not a huge sit-down for Italian meal type guy. Usually it's heavy food, and I cancel my plans after I am full of tomato sauce and cheese. But Via Carota is somewhere I would return to over and over. Girfriend and I got fresh pasta dishes and dessert. The ragu was great - but rich. The taglietelle prosciutto was FIRE. Suble flavors but rich sauce. Amazing.

The hostess/host team is consistently the most disagreeable group of individuals you could EVER encounter. Add rude add indifferent layer in nasty & you got it. Food is delicious. Service staff is wonderful. The host team is nasty nasty nasty. Hospitality is not a brand code at VC. 
P.S. the verde salad is delicious btw!

So glad I finally got to try this place! We came on a Tuesday around 5pm and had to wait 45min for a table inside..  which wasn't so bad. It was pretty busy already. We could've gotten seated outside right away, but our party wasn't complete, so we decided to get on the waitlist for indoors. 
The menu is pretty big, good for sharing. We started with the beets, fennel salad, and fried calamari & shrimp. It was all delicious and refreshing. The fried seafood was perfectly done. Then, we had the cacio pepe, tagliatelle, and fried rabbit. The pasta dishes were well-executed, they didn't feel too heavy. The fried rabbit was a highlight, flavorful and crispy. For dessert, we had tiramisu and panna cotta. This was the right amount of food for our group of 3. 

Service was friendly and attentive at all times. I'd definitely recommend coming here for classic Italian fare in a lively atmosphere.

Stopped by around 4:15p on a Saturday and was able to be seated for two at the bar, serving full menu! The food and cocktails were amazing and the service at the bar was quick. The Meyer lemon risotto was perfection as was the grilled octopus, which was perfectly tender. I highly recommend both and will come back next time I'm in town. Also learned there is a cookbook published from the restaurant so will be creating the dishes at home too.

In my Top 3 restaurants of all-time. When people ask for NYC eat recommendations, I point them to Via Carota. This quaint little restaurant transports you to Italy, with decor that reminds me of travels through Europe. The food is always a hit. Not only are the dishes tasty, but the drinks are also delicious as well. The Bicicletta is a great take on an aperol spritz. Although the dishes are smaller in size and pretty pricey, it is a nice place to splurge once in a while, I definitely think it's worth it to try at least once. Will be back many many times!!

The best pasta I tried while in NY. We stopped by and were told they had no open reservations but could wait. We waited and 3 minutes later had a nice table outside!

I got the side of mushroom and cacio e pepe. It was simple but perfect.

Awful. Now I remember why I haven't been back in 2 years. Condescending staff, fake Italian food and cockroaches in the bathroom. Further they never promote minorities. You only get promoted if you are white. Fact. Do not believe the hype. They treat patrons like garbage and get away with it. No more. Go to Il Buco instead if you want the real deal.

The artichokes were AMAZING - lemony, tangy, fresh. We opted for the mushroom special and it was really wonderful, not too heavy like all the other pasta options. The aperol spritz was SO tasty. 

The only downside was the service, the server was somewhat curt and to add to that she put in the incorrect order so it took a bit longer for our food to come out. 

Otherwise a lovely food experience.

I read about this place on Pete Well's top 100 list. Number 4. It did not disappoint. There were so many things we wanted to try, that we'll have to go back. I took Pete's recommendation and ordered the fried olives stuffed with sausage and followed Char's recommendation of the razza as my main. She kept the whole experience chill as she managed the chaos behind the bar. My wife had the Caio Pepe and the artichokes. We finished it off with the best cannoli I've ever tasted.

The food at Via has always been top rate. Even the seemingly simplest things are exquisite, and I also appreciate an extensive Negroni menu.

However, I've noticed with the increasing popularity a tendency to rush diners through a meal. Especially weekend lunch. Like, trying to clear plates while we're still eating. I was really shocked. It's so not done at this level of restaurant. 

So....diners beware. Or try to go for dinner versus lunch on a weekend.
Our food was incredibly salty. I couldn't believe we were at the famous Via Carota. The chef should taste the food before he sends it out.

I walked in for Saturday lunch and we got a seat at the bar. Our server was very nice and had to recite the specials. We had the Cynar Spritz, burrata with zucchini and eggplant, wild boar Ragu, chicken, and affogato. The burrata was tasty and balanced with the side veggies. I wasn't a big fan of flavor of the Ragu. The affogato was the best part. That espresso was amazing.

I'd give Via Carota a strong 3.5 stars. Fortunately, I was able to walk in and get a table for one while it was incredibly busy. My waiter was kind, patient and was eager to share the specials of the day. My appetizer -- the insalata verde was delicious. It was fresh, light and a large portion. For my entree, I got the risotto special, which was fine. However, my dessert was the best part. Berries and mascarpone! For all the hype this restaurant receives, I did expect more. I would definitely return but only for dessert and or salad.

We stopped in last night and took our chances on finding a walk-in table. We were hoping that the gloomy weather would discourage a long line of people, but it didn't! If we weren't so lucky enough to get a table for 2 right away, the wait would have been minimum of an hour. 

We were seated outside at a small table. We started with the Cynar and Gran Spritz, which if you haven't already had one before, is an acquired taste. We got the fried rabbit as an appetizer to share. It was so juicy and delicious, and came with some fried bread. 

For mains, we shared a cacio e pepe and a wild boar ragu. Both were so fresh and flavorful! I think my friend liked the cacio e pepe better, but I was a huge fan of the wild boar ragu. 

For dessert, we shared an affogato and semifreddo. The affogato is usually hard to mess up, and was delicious as always. The semifreddo was SO tasty! I think it's a hazelnut mousse, and it's absolute perfection! 

The service was pretty good. Our waiter was attentive without being overbearing, and friendly.

I definitely see the hype about this place. It seems like as the night goes on, the line gets shorter, so maybe try your luck later in the evening for a better chance to score a table.

I'll definitely return to Via Carota!

One of the most amazing meals ever ! Good thing we went with people who had previously bee there to guide us thru amazing menu choices & try new things. Food and service is impeccable. Beautiful ambiance , a bit noisy. They have outdoor street seating. You have to stand in line @ 5 to be eligible for a reserved table that night. No advance reservations. Walk ins for lunch are probably best chance of getting in , no waiting in line for mid day table

The restaurant has a nice ambiance. However, the service was a bit slow. 

Skip the bread and olive oil.

Wild Boar ragu was tasty but not game changing.

Tldr: the long wait was definitely worth it!!

We've been wanting to go to Via Carota for a while now, and decided to stop in on a random Thursday. We were a group of three and got there at 5:30, but the earliest they could seat us was 9:30pm.... needless to say, we went home, took a nap, and came back for our time slot

We sat in the little side room past the indoor dining area with the bar. The door to outside was open so it was nice being a little more secluded but with a breeze. The little room had a large communal table, and lots of cute old Italian general goods store decor. 

We ordered the arancini and a daily special bruschetta to start, pea pesto pasta with ricotta, boar ragu, and cacio pepe for pasta, and the zabaione for dessert. 

It was such a delightful meal, I would definitely come back! The arancini were surprisingly huge and the bruschetta was really well balanced in terms of flavors and textures. The only thing that was good but not great was the pea pesto dish, as the sauce was really chunky (odd texture) and tasted quite mild. Everything else was perfectly cooked with lovely classic Italian flavors. The pasta was also really filling and the three of us could barely finish them. Most places' desserts fall flat but the zabaione here was so creamy and delicious I'd come back just for that. Overall, I'd rate this a 4.5/5. Via Carota is a good value for money, and I can't wait to come back!

Excellent excellent, amazing Italian food. I have never been to Italy, so I'm not an expert, but the dishes that we ordered were delicious.
Tiramisu was not too sweet.
Wine was delicious as well.  We didn't order a bottle, instead we opted for glasses of different wines and each one did not disappoint.
Service was very nice and attentive.

Only thing is that this place is sooo popular that the wait time is crazy.

I stopped by Via Carota a few weeks ago looking for ONE bar seat and was told the wait would be an hour. I left and decided to take my chances another day. That day was today - a rainy, muggy, nasty July day; I got a bar seat in 5 minutes!! The service was incredibly friendly and helpful, from the hostess to the servers and bartenders. I got what I think may be the best aperol sprtiz I have ever had, the arancini (which was insanely creamy and flavorful), the charred artichokes (I'm not normally a veggie fan but they looked good in photos and the lemon sauce was INSANE), and the tonnarelli cacio e pepe. This dish was UNREAL! The pasta came out nice and hot, and it was perfectly chewy, cheesy, and peppery. My only regret is that I did not have room for dessert. I will 100% be back here and plan on bringing family and friends!!

Got here for a quick lunch, surprised I didn't have to wait for long. I arrived when the restaurant just opened on a weekday (11am) and got seated within minutes at the bar table.

I ordered their Piselli salad

The salad was perfect. It was refreshing, creamy and flavourful. The greens were fresh, the prosciutto was high quality, perfect with green peas and robiola cheese and oregano. The favlour combination was so well thought out with their ingredients selection. Definitely one of my go to spots if the wait isn't long.

Food was great , Green Salad  , Cacio E Pepe , and special Risotto amazing . Our server however a little snotty.  Sort of ruined our lunch . I understand everyone has a bad day every once in a while but you shouldn't let the customers see this and definitely not take it out on them

A lovely meal from start to finish, in a beautiful, homey setting in the heart of the West Village. (Heads up that the salads are huge, so order accordingly.) The pasta dish pictured below was amazing -- the pasta alone would have been enough, it had so much flavor and was silky smooth. The extensive cocktail menu is great, including inventive aperol options. And the tiramisu was perfect (and generous). Enjoy!

We had heard great things from friends, but the service, and food was just okay. We were seated inside at the end of a long table, shared with a larger group. It appeared to be a retail area within the restaurant. It felt like we were tucked away and at times forgotten about. 

Overall the pasta was just okay, nothing extraordinary...have had better. The bread was dry. Heirloom salad was okay, but again, nothing spectacular. Maybe our expectations were too high.

Am i the only one who did not like this place? I've been to lots of Italian restaurants in nyc and been to all the 'hard to get into' Italian restaurants and this falls at the bottom of the list. We got the arancini,  insalanta verde, cacio e pepe, and tagliatelle and I don't think we liked any dish. The arancini was whatever. The salad only had light dressing on the top few pieces so the rest just tasted like straight up grass. And for $21?! I could've bought a whole box of spring mix at costco for $5. What a scam. The cacio e pepe started off okay but as we got down to the bottom half, the rest of the pasta was just sitting in a pool of oil. The tagliatelle was one of the blandest pastas we've ever had. The prosciutto gave it a little saltiness but overall, the pasta itself was tasteless. We didn't finish either pasta. Only giving two stars bc the service was friendly, ambiance was nice, and portions were huge

I think this 4 is based more so on it not living up to hype than a fully objective view. On a Thursday it had a 4 hour wait (5:30 entered; seated at 9:30), which if you live closeby, is stomachable. Just put your name down!

The environment is cute, especially to be seated in a small back room with a longer table; feels like I'm in a wine cellar in Bologna, ya know?

The starter was what stood out to me; a whipped ricotta toast with sundried tomatoes?? So beautiful to look at, and even more tasty. Don't miss out on it, as those tomatoes were just perfection. My entree fell a bit flat (one of the daily specials: a pea pesto pasta with ricotta (the green one). The sauce was pretty chunky (nuts from the pesto), making for a strange texture; flavorwise, it was a bit lacking, dominated by oil + butter rather than spice. However, my favorite at the table was the Cacio e Pepe, if you're looking for a suggestion

Got a Zabaione for dessert which was good (especially the sweetened strawberries), but a bit more cream than I could muster to eat. Overall, I appreciated the service in the end, but I don't know if this meal is worthy of the #4 NYT restaurant in NYC. Would still say people should go and see if the hype is real!

This restaurant is worth the hype. Walked by on a Monday around noon, and got lucky with an open table for a party of 4. The bread and olive oil were amazing, and the cacio e pepe, pappardelle with wild boar ragu, and piselli salad were my absolute favorite. Love the classic Italian decor inside too. Excellent service. Will definitely come back!

I feel Via Carota may be resting on its laurels at this point -  the risotto is quite delicious, but it is never updated to reflect the seasons. Shortly in the heat of summer, the risotto could incorporate seasonal flavors.  Keep the classic, of course, but please update to reflect seasonal changes in ingredient availability, as they always do in my beloved Italy.

The best Italian restaurant in Manhattan, without a doubt. I've eaten here an uncountable amount of times and it is always mind blowing. They also do amazing Negronis. The interior has such a lovely NYC, fall-like vibe. Eat here!

The food here is SO good. The Caccio Pepe was truly some of the best I've ever had. The Calamari & Meatballs were also delicious. The service was a bit weird and confusing but the amazing made up for it.

Solid Italian dining in the west village without being stuffy or pretentious. The service was on point and the space felt authentic. We got the pesto stracci and the daily pasta special which was a tortellini with caramelized onions. The artichoke bruschetta was so unique and flavorful - highly recommend! The svizzerina which was basically a beef patty/steak tartare was okay. The mushroom (funghi) with scamorza (baked cheese) was memorable though and unlike anything I've had. For dessert, we had the olive oil panna cotta and hazelnut chocolate semifreddo.

Okay Via Carota really is that girl. Taylor Swift loves it for a reason. The Pappardelle was very tasty, the tiramisu tried and true, and the Tagliatelle w prosciutto & peas was WHERE IT WAS AT! Great balance of richness with the sweet peas and nutmeg for balance and sharpness. That said my absolute favorite bite was the Zabaglione with berries, especially delicious during the hot summer with ripe summer berries. I could eat that ALL day long, and even made a version of it at home. Via Carota really is a little crown jewel, with reasonable portion sizes for the price and deliciousness I have to say I will certainly be back.

We sat at 4pm on a Friday and we were glad we came early because the line was really long when we were done at 5pm. We enjoyed the lemon skate fish, Cacio e Pepe, and boar ragu tagliatelle. My favorite was the Cacio e Pepe since it was creamy and had the right amount of pepper. We finished with tiramisu for dessert! The service was good and the place is a cute restaurant. Remember to go early to skip the line!

Wandered in for lunch on a Friday. Only learned after I dined here that it's one of the most hyped restaurants in the neighborhood. As an expensive whimsical lunch, a nice surprise. As a dinner planned two months in advance, a bit iterative.

It was tasty, not life changingly so, but good nonetheless. Everything was made w a high level of precision. The octopus and heirloom tomatoes were great, cacio e pepe definitely the star. Tiramisus pretty yum and not too sweet (!!!), heavy on the cream filling. 
I think there are probably a lot of nice italian restaurants around the city u could get the same quality of meal without the difficulty of getting a spot, and for me it was just missing that special flair to draw me back for another visit. But it was a good meal fs

I absolutely love this restaurant. I think I've been there 10 times in the last 3 months and I don't even live in NYC. I can't eat gluten but there's still a ton for me to eat. It's very vegetable forward and they do change the menu to reflect the best of the season. I've had the prosciutto over melon, the insalata e accchiuge ( a must if you love anchovies), the piselli salad, the lemon risotto, the charred leeks, the grilled artichokes. The other day I had the vitello tunatto as an appetizer and that was a standout. Get it if it's on special. I only ever sit at the bar and the service is very attentive. 

My only criticism is the uncomfortable bar stools. All bar stools should have backs on them. If they changed that out this place would be an 11/10.
Amazing meal. Perfectly portioned pasta, amazing appetizers.... Superb salads and sides.... It's really quite exquisite.

I was so excited that I was able to get a reservation. My reservation was at 10:30 pm on a Friday. My friend and I were wandering around West Village and decided to see if we could be seated earlier than 10:30 pm. We were able to be seated at 10 pm. 

The restaurant has a very cozy and homey vibe. There is seating outside too. We were seated inside. Paper menus are on the back of the chairs. 

There are 3 single stall bathrooms in the back. 

We weren't that hungry so we split:
- Grilled artichokes - Super yummy 

- Pappardelle - Beef was tender and melted in your mouth  

The food came out fast and was delicious! I prefer Via Carota to L'Artusi for the food and the vibes.

For how much hype this place gets, it was just ok. There is definitely better italian places in the city. We came here for an early dinner on a Friday. We got there around 5:15pm and were seated immediately outside which we were super excited about! Shortly after we saw a line start forming so definitely get there earlier! Here's what we got: 

Cacio e Pepe - this is usually my favorite thing to get at any italian place. I heard a lot of great things about this dish here so I was really excited! Unfortunately, it didn't hit the mark for me. There was not enough sauce and there was just no creaminess that you expect with a cacio e pepe. It also didn't have enough pepper. Overall, this was not it in my opinion. 

Lemon Risotto - this was also ok, really lemony so if that's not your vibe steer clear but it was like very runny. Usually risotto has a bit of a bite to it but this was very soupy in my opinion

Papardelle Ragu - my friend got this and he thought it was good but again nothing super out of this world

Overall, this place is very expensive and overly hyped in my opinion. I've heard their apps are pretty good so maybe I'll give those a try next time but I don't think I'd come back for a full meal.
Close your eyes and get transported to Italy! fun decor, cool vibes, knowledgeable servers and staff. olives w sausage different and yummy. had seafood platter fried zucchini etc

Insanely good. We've eaten out all over NY for 10 days and Via Carota was stand out excellent. Italian made the way it should be. Perfectly cooked dishes the traditional way. Hands down the best  meal we've had in NY. The Cacio e Pepe was as good as any we've had in the best eateries in Italy. The service and setting were as good as the good - attentive, knowledgable and friendly in a traditional setting both inside and outside. Simply glorious all round.

Great place, service and food!
If you write down your name you'd probably get a table in 30-40 mins, and it's worth it!

Great friendly and kind service. The food was great! We got artichoke, zucchini, salad and leeks. Artichoke was beyond and second best east the leeks!

We've tried 3 pasta; cacio Pepe, Ragu tagliatelle and peas and prosciutto tagliatelle. I love love love yhe ragu, and if you like a lighter taste the peas was a great touch on tagliatelle!

Not a fan of tiramisu and the green salad but otherwise everything was beautifully made and tasted delicious!
Good portion sizes on the food but I was slightly underwhelmed by the flavor. Servers were great and attentive. We went right at opening without a reservation and were sat right away.

it was the first time I had been to via carota and I was impressed! make sure you get a reservation or prepare to wait  since it's so popular!piselli [$23]: this salad  was life changing and I still think about it to this day. it's so meticulously made; the prosciutto  spaced evenly between layers of lettuce  along with the peas  & perfect hint of dressing made it a stand out. the proportion and freshness of the ingredients was unmatchedzucchini fritti [$23]: this appetizer was a satisfyingly crunchy and salty snack. it's lightly  fried but comes in a huge mound so I highly recommend sharing. pollo alla griglia [$29]: the chicken  was amazing as well. it's flavored perfectly and came out at a great temperature  as well! the chicken  was succulent and juicy as well!

I think 95% of restaurants in NYC have overpriced and overrated food, BUT Via Carota is NOT one. This is the kind of restaurant you write home about. The Acciughe E Burro (cultured butter and salted anchovies bruschetta) was one of the top dishes of my life. 

Thank you Via Carota for making me believe in good great food again.

My only recommendation is the Martini needs a bit more of a bite-- too watered down/lite.

I went back to Via carota on my trip to New york, it's one of the places that I keep going back on every trip. But this time around I was very disappointed, definitely looks like the chef may have changed, as the food wasn't up to the mark. The servers were less helpful than before as well.

Ordered all their classics, standouts, and the food is authentic and delicious, but don't come here unless the ambiance further justifies the price. 

There's better Italian food in the city for even cheaper if taste is your only criteria. But for example, Via Carota is noticeably better than Carbone. I'm not the first to propose it, but claim the crown Via Carota. 

Standout Italian food and very cute. So an unparalleled date spot if pasta and Resy are a few of your favorite things. But worth all the hype?

4.9 or just about as close to a perfect meal one could have.
On my bucket list for a while, and on a whim, I made a Resy reservation about a month in advance.
What I noticed is that the time slots for dinner  were either very early or very late. I snagged a 4:45/5 PM slot and we were sat outside. A line started to form around that time with most people being accommodated, including indoors! Go figure.

Browsing the September/current menu, we ordered the Gran Spritz cocktail  which was a refreshing twist comparable to the Aperol only a different liquor and color (yellow). It was very delicious and kind of strong.

Our server was helpful and offered feedback on ordering since portions were  on the generous side.
The selected appetizers were Fritto Misto (calamari and shrimp) and Tonno with beans.
They both arrived to the table around the same time. 
The Fried Calamari were piled high and included  just 2 jumbo shrimp and the tentacles (of the squid). It was served on its own without side Marinara sauce but oh so delicious. Cooked just right. The seafood was tender while the batter was crispy. Not oily or overly seasoned, this pick was a winner.

When we got to the Tonno with Beans, it was unlike anything I ever tried. Pieces of cubed raw tuna mixed with cannellini beans tossed with grape tomatoes and parsley in a delicious dressing.. A must order selection.

For main, we shared 2--- the Skate and Risotto (with Meyer Lemon). Risotto came out first---creamy and lemony. Excellent choice.
The Skate, which was perfect for sharing, was pan fried and sprinkled with capers. Another delicious selection.

Our meal ended with the Italian Zabaione  served with berries. If you aren't familiar, this is a must try. In a nutshell, it's an Italian custard and very good. 

A few things to note:
Both the Skate and Risotto were a little too salty for my liking.  I wish they weren't as over seasoned . I wouldn't say it was a negative to the experience but some people such as myself aren't a fan of dishes being prepared with too much salt.
Another observation--the Skate was pan fried (although it could almost pass as deep fried) and had I known, I would have selected another main.
Having ordered the Fried Calamari, it lent to too much fried like selections. I wish it was described as such on the menu.
When our original server ended his shift, service went downhill at times.
Glasses and plates remained on the table just a little too long. I get it. Via Carota is a happening restaurant and rightfully so but there were a few lulls when it came to service.

The overall experience was phenomenal and we agreed that dinner at Via Carota was one of the best meals we've had.
Highly recommend and would absolutely return again (if I can get past  the headache of the reservation process).

Service was awful from the start. With a 9:30 reservation the hostess told us to wait in the corner while she sat 3 parties of the same size ahead of us and sat us in a noisy street corner outside. The waiter was rude and it seemed like the restaurant was very understaffed. The cacio e Pepe was under-flavored and the broccoli was completely inedible. When we sent it back, very politely, the waiter was very sassy and then sent some other employee to bring the check and still included the dish on the bill. We asked to remove it and it took 20 minutes for them to return the bill. Overall not a great experience.

This and I Sodi are probably my favorite restaurants in the West Village and definitely among top 10 in New York City. The food is absolutely phenomenal. Their insalata verde is much talked about and with good reason - never would I have thought that a simple green salad of lettuce, watercress and endives would have such complexity of flavor. It is truly the holy grail of green salads. The pastas here are also must orders. The cacio e pepe has got to be one of the best in the city. I've also had the rigatoni with bolognese (a special the last time I was here) which was equally delicious. Both pastas are cooked to a perfect al dente and enjoy a just right ratio of sauce to noodle. This is truly one of those places where it's hard to find anything wrong with the food or the dining experience. A well-deserved 5 stars.

after wanting to try this place for years, decided to walk in w my friend @ 11am on a sun... restaurant was empty, breezed right in!

didn't order much but both the prosciutto salad and cacio e pepe were truly to die for... did not disappoint and was def still riding off the high of getting seated right away

had heard reviews of the cacio being salty or slimy but did not experience that at all !! paralleled the ones I have had in italy with such good black pepp flavor

On line experience with Resy is super annoying. No phone number to call the restaurant. Tried for lunch and dinner to no success. Called at exactly 9:00 AM one month in advance for 3 days. Not going to "walk-in" and take a chance when there are a lot of other good Italian restaurants. We only have 3 days/nights in NYC. Disappointing!

So good I seriously considered coming right back the next day. The atmosphere and service was that sweet spot of sophistication without stuffiness. Started with a fabulous negroni, the brussels, and carpaccio (a special). Both apps were so elegant and full of flavor. Next we got the clams and a pesto pasta dish (also a special) - both so good, with perfect portions that gave us enough room to have dessert and coffee. 

Also, there was a big line, but as clueless out of towners we just walked up to a server and were seated right away. Not sure what was going on with the line!

Via Carota definitely lives up to the hype. The butterhead lettuce is absolutely delightful, and the pastas melt in your mouth. It may be difficult to get a reservation, but the wait time is manageable if you walk in!

The grilled artichokes were lovely and the lemon risotto was perfection. However....

The skate was overcooked and quite dry. Worse yet, it tasted very strongly of ammonia at the very first bite and never relented...it was impossible to finish it. I really wanted to send it back but to be honest, I felt intimidated by the restaurant's reputation to do that. 

The fried rabbit was overcooked and void of any charcater. While the breading was not greasy which is appreciated, the protein was akin to dry bland chicken, lacking the gamey notes one expects from Rabbit.

I've been wanting get into this reataurant for ages and was so excited to score a table on a lovely sunday afternoon. Despite the wonderful artichokes and lemon risotto as well as a negroni my partner loved, I couldn't have been more disappointed. Definitely not worth the $264 we spent.

We will come back, but for cocktails, vegetables and pasta/risotto ONLY...we'll be avoiding the pesce/carne like the plague.

Forty five minutes to get two bowls of pasta is a bit much, but even setting that aside both dishes were way, way too salty to even eat. Pasta and sauce quality was good, but more saltier than a bag of chips.
We arrived at 11am on a Monday so no reservation needed and sat outside. Service is great and the food is phenomenal. Every bite is delicious!

Would've been a "great" meal if it weren't for the last dish that we ended up getting because none of the $30 dishes were filling enough: the bruschetta with the chicken liver (see photo). It has WAYYYYY TOO MUCH CHICKEN LIVER which was "chopped" into such erratic pieces that it only ended up looking like a pile of POOP  (see picture). The chicken liver was also too salty and just extremely heavy. No idea who thought it was a good idea to have this dish on the menu. Like, there's literally nothing aesthetic or enjoyable about this dish. Salty mushy poo liver for $18? Nah. Showed the picture to our friends afterwords and they literally gagged and then burst out laughing hahah. Sorry to be savage but there are no excuses for that dish at an establishment such as this one. 

The highlight of the meal was the bruschetta special, with gorgonzola pear and walnuts. Nothing bad to say about that it was delicious.

Still, I think this restaurant is severely overpriced for the quality, and saltiness. Considering how many people complain about the saltiness I'm surprised that it tastes like nothing has been done to address it. Also the green salad for $21? That was a very simple vinaigrette with a bunch of uncut fresh leaves. Yummy, refreshing, but I don't go out to eat things I can make at home. Not sure what was so special about that.

Dined here twice now and sorry I simply cannot get the hype. I love love love their sister I Sodi but I simply cannot fall in love with Via Carota. None of the dishes I had convinced me, I even forgot their names (the pasta with peas and prociutto, the cacio pepe). I am the greatest pasta lover but yeah those are not for me. And the salad with prosciutto, way to much dressing. 

But other people love it so give it a try if you make it in and make up your own mind. You'll find me at I Sodi (if I make it in there ;))

Came for a late lunch/early dinner on a Sunday. We sat outside under the heaters which are toasty enough. The menu is simple and has the cocktail/wine list on the back. Cocktails are not described and basic: martini with grappa instead of vermouth, manhattan, old fashioned. I asked for a cosmopolitan.. I know. How Y2K.. server said "we don't make them"... I asked what was similar. He referenced the above martini. I said OK how about a Diet Coke.. they don't serve those either. I get it- you want a vibe. But also- hospitality, no? Assuming these two requests come often enough.. wouldn't you have alternative recommendations at the ready? Instead they'd rather forgo an additional $50-80 in bar tab? Odd. Finally asked the waiter to speak with the bartender to see what they would recommend.  Their answer? Grapefruit juice & vodka. The grapefruit juice was fresh pressed..but that's the best cocktail you can make? Yikes.  Still. Our table had 5... so... a plus to them otherwise they would have missed out on the $. 
Onto the food: had the chicken liver bruschetta. Taste good- but literally just chopped chicken liver. No fruit. No jam. No arugula.. nothing more. Grilled artichokes were sublime. Great charred flavor & excellent texture. The cacio e Pepe.. eh.. could have had more Pepe.. and the portions are teeny. The tagliatelle with prosciutto was better and seemed like a larger portion. Server never came to see if we wanted pepper or cheese. Weird. 
Dessert was the tiramisu- best I ever had and I typically hate it. The panacotta had a weird bitter citrus jam on top that tasted as if it was made of rind and pith. No thanks. All in all. I have eaten better Italian at my local pizza place.

Awesome spot! Every single dish was amazing. We didn't necessarily order everything I wanted, since the girl I was with eats much healthier than I do, but we got the Brussels sprouts, artichoke, pappardelle, and branzino. Everything was great. There are lot of great Italian restaurants in the city but this spot stands out as 1) girls really want to come here because Taylor Swift once ate here and 2) the ambiance, really cool setting
Very very bad service and rude manager. Once I want to tell manager my complaints. He responded as he didn't care. Would never recommend this place. Manager name is Timothy if I got it correct.

Definitely overhyped and overpriced, but pretty solid cooking. The best dish was definitely the seasonal truffle pasta, followed by the zabaione. Wasn't super impressed by the cocktails. Service was friendly and it was pretty lively even on a weeknight.

This place has gone downhill, and I'm assuming it's from the massive extension to exterior dining in the wake of Covid, and beyond.  Perhaps quality control is not what it used to be.  Stopped by after a screening to have a late dinner (9P) and drink with a friend.  We were seated in the dining room and looked forward to a delicious meal.  We ordered our tiny $19 glasses of wine and waited with anticipation.   The Tagliatelle with Boar Ragu arrived and the meat was tough, dry and tasteless, altho the 4 strips of pasta were fresh and delicious.  We inquired and the waitress sent it back to the kitchen and asked if we preferred anything else.  We ordered the truffle special pasta - which was delicious-  but a scant 3 strips of pasta, cream sauce with a nice helping of shaved truffle.   When we asked for bread, we got 4 pieces of stale tough, ends and decided we didn't want to order more for fear of the same.   What happened, Jody - this place used to have spectacular food, service and I don't recall these minuscule portions?  Very unsatisfying to be starving after spending over a hundred dollars.   Back to Morandi for decent sized portions and excellent service!

This was the dining experience I've been craving from NYC for a long time. Located in Greenwich in a super cute neighborhood where the street side seating offers the best people watching.  The food was to die for.  The highlight for me was the tagliatelle with prosciutto and the bold wine list filled with Italian specialties.  The service was outstanding and we will definitely be back next visit!
The pork belly was amazing. The service was excellent. Plates are small so you will want to order more than 1.

I'm going straight to the reservation portion. It's hard and the key is to just walk in right when they open. Was there Sunday, sat at the bar because the place was already packed at 11am! Bartender said Sundays are their slowest day. Lol. I can only imagine this spot on a weekend night. Thank Taylor for the free advertisement! Had the CAVOLETTI SALAD (shaved Brussels sprout salad) & the cacio, guys you can't go wrong with their cacio very simple dish but absolutely delicious! Will definitely come back and hopefully for dinner next time.

I have wanted to try this place and it lived up to the hype! My favorite part of this place is the walk-in availability. The hardest part of NYC is getting reservations at certain restaurants and the restaurants not accepting a lot of walk-ins. Via Carota changes that. I recommend going around 5pm and you can put your name down for a certain time and they will text you on when to come back! My sister requested 6:30pm so we could have a little Happy Hour before dinner.

My sister and I loved our dinner here. You must order the frito misto, it was not heavy and the perfect appetizer. I am a sucker for calamari and fried shrimp so this dish was just perfect. We are about balance so we ordered a salad and a restaurant salad, they are so good. Now on to the pasta, we were so happy with our Tagilatell order. The taste and the texture, all of it was so good! Of course we had to order a bottle of wine to go with this meal and they have affordable bottles between $50-$60. 

We will definitely return because not only is the food is good, but the experience of being able to put your name down for a certain time and grab a nearby HH before, perfection.

Overall pretty good, would come back to try more dishes!

It's a little tricky to get a reservation, so what my friend and I did was go around 5:30pm, stand in the line to get onto the waitlist (~30m), wait on the waitlist for about an hour while window shopping in the neighborhood, and come back at 7pm for a perfectly reasonable dinner time. We got seated outside, which was pretty fun as we got to people watch during our meal and try to spot famous people walking by us.

Service was quick and ambiance was fine. Now for the food - 
- Burrata e Verdure: 7.5/10. My friend LOVED it, i thought it was pretty good. Everything tasted fresh and very well flavored.
- Pappardelle and Tonnarelli: 8/10. Solid bowls of pasta. Nothing terribly incredible, but definitely expertly cooked pasta with well-seasoned sauces and good consistency.
- Dessert (panna cotta and crostata): 9/10. This was the highlight of the meal for me. I had the panna cotta and thought it was the perfect balance of sweet and sour with the marmalade on top. This was a must-have.
Our aggressive hostess, Josie, made the experience less than amazing. Overall, the food was above average, but probably won't come back, because of how we were treated.

Food was great, but the service leaves a lot to be desired. Our hostess Josie was rude and did not make us feel welcome. We had to wait for 45 minutes post our reservation time, and she was annoyed and irritated by us asking when we will get seated.

NYC has many Italian pasta spots... The reason you come to Via Carota for its Cacio e Pepe and this review is for that pasta dish only. I've had their pappardelle and it's forgettable. The pepe is where it's AT. The hand made noodles are cooked to utter perfection, perfectly al dente and have a satisfying chewiness mouth feel to them. I've heard some batches of pasta don't have enough pepper in it, but fortunately every time I've gotten cacio e pepe, the black pepper is the hero. A delicious saltiness comes through from the cheese which just brings the whole pasta dish together. 

We get our food as take out every time because the line is just too long, and the pasta is still so delicious even after it sits in a takeout container for a while. Only downside is there will be a small pool of butter if your takeout gets cold. But honestly don't care because it's so worth it. 

For those who aren't impressed by Via Carotas cacio e pepe, please DM me your recs for better spots. Until then Via reigns supreme.

There was this server who looked like a tik toker so I kept staring at him and I know he could tell I was staring at him because when he would approach our table he would look down at me in like a dominatrix kind of way (maybe he should do that on the side?) but anyways he was very accommodating for our time restraint and made sure to ask when we were trying to leave by -- to catch our flight -- and made sure to have all the food out in time so that was nice. 

Food was good, someone else paid tho so can't rate the price to quality ratio

The line at Buvette was very long so we decided to try Via Carota for lunch and man were we thrilled. Felt like we were at a decades old neighborhood favorite in Florence. Ate at the bar and had the most sublime torn pasta sheets, a cloud like salad of tender leaves showered in a veil of cheese and delicious Italian wine, service was impeccable and the atmosphere? Perfectly curated antiques with modern touches. Loved the stemmed glasses so much, ordered a couple cases for our thanksgiving dinner. Ciao Via Carota, we will be back often!

Stopped by for lunch on a weekend - we had a res (that I made ages ago) and were able to be seated immediately. I do think that they must keep a lot of their tables available for walk-ins, because even though reservations are not the easiest to come by, there were always a few empty tables while we were eating. Also, turnover seemed to be pretty quick, so I don't think there was much of queue at all.

We started with the 'nduja arancini. I loved the risotto; risotto dishes are a dime a dozen at Italian restaurants, but good risotto - not too heavy, not overcooked - can be hard to come by. The pork was a bit lacking though; we didn't really think it had any of the usual smoky/fiery flavours of 'nduja (it even felt closer to buffalo chicken wing sauce,,,). Each piece wasn't too heavily breaded or fried, though, so it was a very nice, lighter choice to start with.

For pastas we got the tonnarelli (cacio pepe) and the pappardelle (boar ragu).

The cacio e pepe is their speciality, I'm told, so of course we had to try it - and honestly I was really quite pleasantly surprised. I often find there to be too much *cacio* in cacio e pepe - I even had to do a cheese pull of sorts at a different restaurant once - and thankfully that wasn't the case here. Each bite was really well-balanced between the oil and cheese and the perfectly-cooked pasta - chewy but not too much.

Well, until the second half of the dish. By the time we got to the bottom, the pasta was sitting in a really-too-thick puddle of oil, which made eating the remainder a bit unenjoyable. Obviously every bite felt really heavy, and the pasta was getting soggier by the minute. (idk were we just eating too slowly? i feel like that can't be the case)

The pappardelle was nice, but really nothing special. The ground pork was really delicious - rich, savoury, flavourful - but the pasta was meh. It tasted a bit overcooked / soft (not at all al dente), and it didn't seem to have much flavour at all. It kind of felt like the pasta and the sauce were separate dishes thrown together at the end.

Overall, a decent meal, but not amazing. (if you could just order the top half of a bowl of pasta it would be much better lol)

I think for this type of higher-end restaurant, the price point was pretty reasonable. I'm not sure if I'd order the same things if I were to come back, but the menu is decently large, and I think some of the meat entrees did look promising. (Not to mention some of their rotating specials that sounded yummy too...)

Such a hyped up spot in the West Village and so had to try. We walked in at around 2pm on a Weds and there was still a 15min wait for indoor tables so we decided to sit outdoors. Service was extremely slow and we waited at least 10-15min before someone took our order. Service in general was quite subpar (1 out of 5 stars).

I tried the cacio e pepe which everyone seems to rave about and their insalata verde. Tldr; is that the food is decent but really not worth the price. The pasta tasted fresh and pretty bouncy but the sauce was so plain. Maybe that's what I should have expected but for it's price tag, I expected something more. It came in a plain plate and no fancy decorations or cheese or anything to jazz up the boring dish. The insalata verde was a few fresh veggies with a very basic dressing. I almost felt like I was eating the mixed greens assortment from the Union Square market with some olive oil. For $21, I expected more.. I'd probably give the food a 3-4 out of 5. Perhaps their other pasta dishes are more worth it.

For the given price, I feel like there are much better spots you can go to for an exciting meal.

The hype is real. Came here at 4:50pm and waited in  line outside in the dark and cold to be let in at 5pm- so worth it. The appetizers were very average, but the wine, pastas and dessert were so good that it deserves a 5 star rating. 

We started with Cardi fritti (tastes like fried zucchini and very average), olive all'ascolana (fried olives with pork sausage- decent appetizer and would get again) and the grilled artichokes, which were good not great. 

Pastas were incredible- tagliatelle with prosciutto might be my new favorite pasta.  Wild boar pappardelle was incredible and meaty. The dessert- BEST tiramisu I've ever had EVER.  Will be back ASAP!

DROOOOOOOL. 

CACIO PEPE. best dish hands down. Most amazing dish. Craving it. Craving it now while I'm writing this. 

Not sure how to encapsulate my sentiment about the food here so I will have to stick to describing this all in one word : phenomenal. 

Get here when the place opens and get on the list. I like the bar area best. If you order the Cacio Pepe to share, be prepared to order another one. Ya. It's that good y'all. 

Service was fast and friendly. Negroni is a must. Classic Negroni. Good price point for the quality and quantity of foods you get. 

Top it off with the affogato. You HAVE to. The tiramisu was really good but pales in comparison tot he affogato. 

Do yourselves a favor and make the time and effort to visit this place. See for yourself. You will not be disappointed.

So many people love this place. Meh. The fried zucchini looks so impressive but is SOOO greasy, with oil pooling on the one sheet of paper that comes under the mound. The rest of the food we ordered was good - meatballs (not a fan of the raisins, tho), clams (yum!) and stracci with pesto. We sat at a table outside next to some very loud conversation so that made the experience not so great. We probably would've enjoyed sitting inside better. Service was slow and not the friendliest.

*THIS* is amazing authentic Italian food. 
Pricey yes, worth is absolutely.
Cacio pepe is definitely a must. The arancini was a bit rich for me but everyone enjoyed. We got a bunch of the specials, which were just incredible, best rib eye ever. The waiter was so helpful with recommendations, he was exactly right. We ate outside which was really fun, but a bit cold even with the heaters. The bread and oil is essential, very inexpensive and delicious oil. I think my favorite was the grilled artichoke, I'll be dreaming of that for weeks to come.

Delicious food, good service and cool ambience. A great first visit and although we arrived without a reservation( highly recommend booking in advance), the hostess was able to accommodate our 2-person party.

I have nothing but laudatory praise for Via Carota's cacio e pepe. It firmly places itself in the top three pastas I've had in the city.

More than 90% of the time, I'm been disappointed by cacio e pepe...often times, it's too salty or there's too much pepper or the cheese is overpowering. I walked into Via Carota with high hopes and it delivered. The tagliatelle with boar ragu was great as well -- very generous on the boar, which made for a thicker sauce. Portion sizes for pastas are perfect; anything more and I can see how the flavors would become repetitive and too heavy.

Probably one of the best Italian places in NYC and the best Italian food I have had outside of Italy.  While it can be a long wait sometimes, it really is worth it.  All the appetizers were good - especially the leeks.  We got a spread of pastas - all of which were amazing.  The meatballs and ragu were the highlights. We also got the fried rabbit - which was quite good and definitely a must try if you haven't had rabbit before! The wine selection is PHENOMENAL and wine fans should def check it out.  Desserts and coffee were also super tasty.  Overall, cant go wrong with anything on the menu and definitely a must try for italian food and wine fans!

We went here for lunch on a Monday. We had reservations but they do take walk ins. By 12 pm, bar seating was full and there was a wait. We had a really great experience. Servers were attentive and dishes were coursed out appropriately. Great atmosphere as well. 

Insalata verde: a hefty serving of greens dressed perfectly in a sherry vinaigrette. This was very light and fresh. 

'Nduja arancini: perfectly crisp on the outside and pillowy soft on the inside. Great flavor from the 'nduja and the cheese sprinkled on top.

Cacio Pepe: fresh pasta with just the right amount of cheesiness and pepperiness. I would've preferred the noodles to be a little more al dente but regardless, this was the standout dish for me. 

Meyer lemon risotto: very rich and creamy risotto; not too lemony; a little olive oil drizzled on top and couple basil leaves as well to garnish. 

Semifreddo: perfect dessert - the chocolate and hazelnut mousse provided just the right amount of sweetness and the chocolate dipped gooseberries balanced out the sweetness from the mousse. The whipped cream also cuts into the sweetness a little bit and adds to the creaminess. Comes with 2 biscotti as well.
Cozy Italian restaurant with rustic charm, great service and absolutely delicious. Can't wait to go back.

Sadly, the experience was very mediocre.  Gruff and indifferent service.  Pastas that were overcooked, and slathered with cream, with no finesse.  Very average desserts.  Some very good dishes - salads, pork loin - but overall a shockingly pedestrian experience for a restaurant with this reputation.  Hope it was just an off night...

After waiting an hour to get our table we were greeted with a friendly staff. The service was above and beyond consistently filling my water which I appreciated. We ordered the Carote which was delicious with the yogurt sauce. 
Pappardelle Al Cinghiale was excellent with great flavors. Lastly, we had the Pork Belly with a reduction sauce. The pro belly could have been charred longer and the reduction sauce was overly sweet which made it unappetizing. I was disappointed with the dish but still ate it without dipping!

Overall, I would recommend this restaurant. I have this review 3 stars because of the reduction sauce.

Taylor Swift came here after ending her six-year relationship with Joe Alwyn. I can see why. Via Carota is a comforting yet sophisticated restaurant in the lively West Village. I had dinner here with friends before a comedy show one night. The Coniglio Fritto was my favorite dish that I tried-- the rabbit was perfectly fried. The Tonnarelli and Pappardelle were also tasty and cooked perfectly. The tiramisu was a delicious ending to the meal, as to be expected. However, I was disappointed with the Broccoletti-- it was overcooked, and I wasn't a fan of the plating. I'm interested in going back to try the other verdure options.

This is an overpriced and overhyped restaurant. My friends and I came here because we were curious (and excited) to find out why so many celebrities frequented it -- I was not left with an answer. From the start, the hostess who took our name down on the waitlist was extremely rude and overall condescending. Not a good look. After we were seated, our waiter was also snobby and not personable at all. He went through the specials quickly in a disinterested manner. I asked him to explain what was on the dessert menu, and he just listed the items. Like how am I supposed to know what is contained in each dish??

Onto the food--I ordered the tagliatelle with prosciutto and the semifreddo for dessert, which is a hazelnut chocolate mousse. My friends both ordered the cacio e pepe. My tagliatelle was pretty bland, and no seasoning was offered. The only flavor came from the butter and oil, and the salt from the prosciutto. My friends agreed that it was good, but that messing up a butter and cheese pasta was basically impossible. 

The plates are small, though it's still a decent amount of pasta for a five foot girl. If you're larger than that, you'll probably need two dishes.

The star of the meal was definitely my semifreddo--it tasted like a Ferrero Rocher in mousse form. It was rich while being light, and beautifully presented. The vanilla ice cream tasted very fresh, and my friends enjoyed the cannolis.

The interior was nice and dimly lit, so perhaps good for a first date or something. But pasta was mediocre, and I expected more.

personally, I think it's very mediocre. We started with Arancini which was very good, but not amazing. I could probably re-create it very similar. and then I had a bruschetta which was just OK. pasta had good flavor but nothing crazy. i was expecting a lot more as well as drinks were good I think that drinks were the best thing out of everything. Personally, I don't think I ever come back. I think it's a little overhyped and overrated.

food was so mid. not a single dish was good. even the tiramisu was a miss. definitely did not live up to its hype:/ the tagliatelle was alright but it honestly just tasted like a fancier version of fettuccine alfredo

Food was delicious. I had the wild boar and we all shared the Brussels sprouts. Both were very good. Service was great. Only downside was sitting outside but since we didn't have a reservation expect to be outside.

I wanted to eat there for years- for the same reason as everyone: the salad. Was it Nirvana? No. It's a really good salad. And there's a great Negroni menu. 
We didn't have reservations. We were told there was no room, so we wandered around the village. But we took a chance on the way back and squeezed into a tiny table in the back. Cold, cramped. Still happy to be there. Our server was fine.  But please tell the Aryan kid running the door to just crack a smile- be gracious. 
Would I go back? Yes. More strategically next time.

We recently had the privilege of eating at Via Carota in Grove Street in NYC's West Village - we hosted a celebratory firm dinner for 8 in the beautifully appointed side room. 

The food and service were phenomenal! Cocktails are deliciously prepared and beautifully presented - Rita and Jody have mastered the Negroni with multiple variations (and you can even ordered bottled versions for when you entertain!)

Best menu items include:
Cacio e Pepe
Lemon Risotto
Sicilian Meatballs
Grilled Artichokes
Carrots
Branzino

And then the desserts! Cannolis, Tiramisu, Olive Oil Cake - elegant and delectable!

If you are up for an after dinner drink, enjoy an Espresso Martini or an Aperol Spritz (yes,even after dinner!)
 
Molte grazie! Non vedo l'ora di tornare!
Amazing!!! I have been waiting to visit for a long time but always worried about the wait... There is always a wait but it's definitely worth it. TRUST me...

Gotta know what to order here. Dishes were either very lackluster or blow your socks off! I might regret sharing this but the octopus was the best in the city that I've tried thus far. And I always judge a place by its octopus. The mushroom dish is what I'd want Every mushroom dish to be, a bit rich and supremely flavorful with different textures and notes. The egg with artichoke special was on point, the chef really has his French omelette skills down. The cappuccino was amazing- flavorful, mild in acidity and perfect foam. I had 2 :D. The sardines were just pretty good, maybe some flaked sea salt might improve it and a lemon wedge. Things to skip: raspberry pie was a disappointment as it was a tough crust with jam, tiramisu was lacking in coffee and liquor, the fennel salad did not stand out, the roasted carrots with yogurt were cold (would have been better warm to contrast the chilled yogurt). I would like to go back and try the rest of their dishes, as a few left me quite impressed and I have to wonder what else does this unassuming place have in store.

Not my first time but definitely one of my favorite restaurants to return to in NYC. The food never disappoints! For starters, they make one of the best espresso martinis. Started with the insalata verde, cavoletti, and arancini ...delicious! Every time I come here I get the cacio Pepe but the Tagliatelle was even better! I remove the prosciutto because I'm pescatarian but I'm sure it tastes even better the original way. The staff is always super friendly and attentive. We had to sit outside because it was the best option and they offered us blankets to keep warm. Overall, it's worth the wait (no reservations) and you won't be disappointed. Make sure you go early and put your name down because people do fight about skipping lines! Don't forget the tiramisu!
The Cacio e pepe is worth they hype. It is definitely one of my favorites in the city. The sauce was just thick enough

Went in with high expectations, seeing as every time I pass this place there's a line around the block. I figured there must be a reason why people are willing to degrade themselves by waiting an hour in line to eat dinner at 4:45 PM. 

Can confidently say that this was the most disappointing meal I've had in NYC. The cacio e pepe was bland, heavy, and tasted like a butter/cream/cheese soup. The wild boar ragu was meh. Bread costs $3? Lame. 

Service was bad. I think we had about 5 different servers throughout the hour that we were there. Did not enjoy the wall of windows looking out onto that god awful outdoor seating area. All around it was a miss! 

Will wrap things up by saying the tiramisu was great, I at least have to give them that.

My coworker texted me that this restaurant is Taylor Swift's go-to in NYC... so of course we booked the first reservation we could find! We had gotten an 11:30am lunch reservation, but the timing worked out for the better. The restaurant is a bit smaller than I expected. There are a lot of small tables and communal tables where everyone can sit. My friend and I got a pretty small table and it was a little hard to fit everything we got on there, and we only got 2 entrees, an appetizer, and 2 drinks. I was looking at the menu and saw two vegetarian entree options - the cacio e pepe and the meyer lemon risotto. We ordered drinks and went with their appetizer special of the day, the pear and gorgonzola toast.  I went with the meyer lemon risotto as I've never had risotto before, and my friend got the potato tortellini with bolognese sauce. We waited a really long time for our drinks to come out, and I felt like the service was a bit slow considering the restaurant was pretty empty when we went. Once we got the appetizer, we dug into it because it looked so good. Personally, I think the gorgonzola pear toast was the star of the show. I loved how the sweetness of the pear balanced out the salty, earthy flavor of the cheese. The roasted walnuts also helped with the texture and taste. It was a solid 8/10 for me. Next was the entree - the risotto. I thought it was good, very lemony which is right up my alley. I felt like the taste got a bit bland though once I kept taking bites of it. I think I started to lose the taste, not sure why that happened. Considering that it is a little pricey to eat here, I was disappointed with the lack of vegetarian options. I hope they expand their menu so vegetarian or vegan folks don't have to settle for a salad. I think Via Carota is a great restaurant for a one time experience, and maybe I'd come back if their menu changes!

Had a great time here! The food was absolutely delicious, and I had high hopes because of all the hype. The Cacio e Pepe was one of the best I've had in Manhattan, and the broccoli rabe was delicious. The prosciutto pasta could have definitely been more flavorful, but was creamy and yummy. 

The service was good - nothing notable in the positive or negative. The place itself had cute old school Italian vibes. Luckily we were seated at a standalone table, but there was a large section of couple's tables that were extremely close and I was glad we weren't seated there. Overall: Yum!!

No reservations, no problem because we will definitely wait for the amazing food here. Our wait was about 40mins on a Saturday bite which wasn't too bad. We were seated outside in the heated outdoor seating and they even provided blankets which was perfect. This definitely made it a cozy vibe for our girls dinner. 

Our waiter was excellent, very informative about the menu and asked us about our likes and dislikes. We started off with drinks of course , I had the espresso martini which was so good ! 

Next we started with a few appetizers, the Carciofi Alla Griglia- Grilled artichokes & aioli , 'Nduja Arancini -
Rice & spicy pork fritters & the Insalata Verde -
Leafy greens in sherry vinaigrette. Let me just say all of this is a must , so full of flavor and the quality of the food was just incredible and prepared perfectly. 

For dinner we opted for the Tonnarelli pasta , which was very light and the pasta was cooked perfectly. The simplicity of this dish left you satisfied with every bite. 

To end our dinner we had the tiramisu which was the perfect ending to all the delicious food we had. This place is truly lovely and if I could give it 10 stars I would, it's a place everyone should experience.

Came here for lunch, nice casual environment. Overall staff was great and service was attentive.

We started the meal with the brussells salad and arancini. Brussels salad was amazing and would have again, arancini was cooked nicely but the nduja was only ok. Pretty disappointing that the bread and oil was an additional charge and not just given to us, but $3 from every table adds to the profit!

Pastas we did the tagliatelle and pappardelle. First dish was pretty delicious, but the 2nd was disappointing in terms of portion and it seemed old, almost like its been sitting out a while. Taste was still good though! Doesnt warrant losing a star.

Tiramisu at the end was very very good, perfectly paired with a latte!

Will come back :)
Average food and average service. It's not worth the hype. I think it's fantasized by Hollywood

Sadly this place has gone downhill massively. The green salad and wild boar pappardelle were good tonight, but the truffle pasta, wine, and service were pretty awful. The pasta was so overcooked it was mushy and lacked any flavor - it was like cafeteria butter noodles with truffles on it. Really substandard compared to several years ago.

Well, everything was so lovely that I forgot to take pictures of anything. Great service, amazing food I would definitely suggest the Castel Franco. A magical salad to say the least. Also had a special of the day of sardines and they were done so beautifully and perfect. Can't wait to go back another time when I can actually be in the restaurant because I was out on the deck, and it was a little breezy for me even with the heaters.
Great food and service.  Probably one of the best restaurants in the west village.   Il soti, buvette by the same duo are just as good and nearby.

What a bummer!  I stopped in around 12:30 this afternoon and asked if by chance they had a single.  They did! - at the bar.  I thought I was the luckiest guy on earth.

To start, I had the ribollita.  It was certainly a gusty stew of pulse and greens but completely lacking in taste.  Yummy ain't the word for it.  (The well-meaning but limited bus boy voluntarily packed up the unfinished bowl for me in a cardboard container that ruined my carry-all.)

Next came the papardelle in ragù.  The pasta was legendarily thin and tender and the ragù was meaty, but the ragù had very little liquid and was inadequate to sauce the pasta.  It was tiresome to eat and I brought half of it home, to which I will add some much needed sauce.

If only I had gone to Cowgirl Hall of Fame (as I originally intended) and had their wonderful chili!

Does Taylor Swift have good taste in food? The answer is a resounding yes. Every aspect of the experience was amazing. 

The restaurant staff was so kind in making sure I would have a table that fit my accessibility needs. Nicole went out of her way to be helpful and everyone else I encountered went above and beyond in making it an exceptional experience. 

The food is totally worth the hype, especially the tonnarelli pasta (cacio e pepe)! We also got the Brussels sprouts salad on recommendation of our waiter and absolutely loved it, as well as the roasted carrots. We got the mushrooms to go with our pasta and they were good but my least favorite veg. The tiramisu is also a must! 

Wheelchair access: no steps to get inside, there is a great wheelchair accessible bathroom at the end of the bathroom hall. The outdoor patio is flat with the street and has heaters. The are street tables too.
