They charge $3 for extra Parmesan. I honestly can't imagine anything tackier than that. Charging THREE DOLLARS for a sprinkle Parmesan on a $25 plate of pasta. This place used to be a wonderful. The salads used to be amazing, the veggies were excellent. Now, everything seems to have faded. The service is lackluster, the server seem mildly annoyed that you're there and the food is just mediocre. But the $3 surcharge for a spoonful of Parmesan just sent me over the edge.
This place most times has amazing dishes. It's one of our favorite restaurants. We have been multiple times and almost never disappointed. Ambiance and service are great too.

Stopped in here and grabbed two seats at the bar with no problem.  As usual the food and wine were outstanding.  We enjoyed the huge salad which is so perfectly dressed and vibrantly green.  The chicken livers, cacio pepe and the pasta special were A+.  There are so many great sounding menu items that we will continue to come back and work our way through the menu.  We really enjoyed our Sunday afternoon here.

polipo
grilled octopus & green olive pesto with a glass of white wine 
And 
rigatina
charred pork belly & cippolini agrodolce with a glass of red.
Everything was delicious 

I sat at the bar and the service was 1st class, attention to detail, professional & charming. 
The ambiance was simple, & elegant.

The servers were very polite, so no qualms. The food was somewhat of a miss. The cultured butter and anchovies were my favorite. The bread was fluffy and fresh, butter was delectable and I love salty anchovies. If I had a complaint, it was that the butter on each slice was huge and made me too full for other things, but is that really a complaint? Unfortunately, the arancini filled with spicy pork, although cooked very well and crisp on the outside, had an off smell and flavor. The brussel sprout salad was quite large and fresh. It did not have much flavor other than being fresh. The pastas were extremely salty. Albeit the pasta itself was well-made and soft. The cacio e pepe was so salty I could barely eat it. The pappardelle had good flavor, but the wild boar pieces were dried out. It was also very salty.

Probably will not return.

Popped in for lunch on a trip to NYC. Vibes were so nice. Service was a bit mixed, with some staff being more pleasant than others. Had high expectations of Via Carota because of all the online hype. While it's a beautiful restaurant, the food fell short. It was a bit bland, portions were smaller than average, and just didn't quite align with the pricing. I was with three other people, we all had different dishes and shared the same sentiment.

No reservations!! So we got there at 4:08pm and I was the 7th pair/group to wait in line the line got crazy at around 430 by 5 there was more than 50 pairs (Saturday)
Cute space nice/simple decoration 
Our waiter was friendly 
The arancini were big and delicious they have some spicy pork inside yum! 
The salad was simple but really good. big perfect for sharing 
We ordered the ragú and pappardelle the pasta was really good a bit on the salty side but yummy 
We ordered a beer and the pomegranate soda very refreshing 
I think is fairly priced for the neighborhood and the hype 
The only thing I don't like it's the no reservations/waiting in line 
So if you want to try it go during the week

Via Carota offers simple yet great Italian cuisine. My favorite dish on the menu is their Cacio e Pepe, which I highly recommend pairing with a side of broccoli rabe. Everything on their menu is delightful.

I recommend going for lunch especially on the weekends to avoid waiting for a table.  If you need to wait, also check out a nice bar two doors nest to it called Grove Street Social.

This is a pretentious dining spot with average food and very inconsistent service.  Plus they were advised it was a birthday in the Resy reservation and this was no acknowledged.
  This was a complete waste of money and time.

One of the best Italian spots in the city! Outstanding food, great service, the vibe is old and cozy. Their Cacio e Pepe is the best I've ever had, the homemade noodles take it over the top and the sauce was perfect. My dad got the special which was a pesto papardelle and it was outstanding. We also got the zucchini frites as an appetizer and they were so delicious (and a huge portion). This place is frequented by celebrities and it's clear why.

The food is good but service not so much. The server claimed that tiramisu is plated at the moment and cocoa on top is sprinkled fresh but when I asked if I could have one with no cocoa on top (a very basic request) he said they can't make such modifications. Same for cannoli: he said they are filled with ricotta at the moment of order and then dipped in chocolate drops and I said "can I have mine not dipped in chocolate" and again no modifications. Oddly annoying.

I don't usually leave reviews, but have to call out the terrible service. The waitress was disinterested, inattentive, and would not make eye contact with us when giving the specials. It felt like we were a burden being there. Did not check in on us during our dining and we had to flag another waiter down for another round of drinks. The food was fine, but nothing I would come back for given the vibe.

I don't get it. For all the fuss, they give you the longest wait times and the servers/waitstaff seem to get a pleasure out of being rude to you. The food isn't extraordinary. They make a good Negroni. I've been a long time patron of Rita's establishments but this makes no sense. Service is everything. Food is so important. But one without the other is no for me.

Stopped by Via Carota after a long stroll this afternoon and left very satisfied. At first I thought there'd be a wait time since this restaurant is so popular, but I was immediately seated at the bar -- the best thing about solo dining. The bartenders were nice and displayed the perfect balance of being friendly while minding their business. The service was efficient but not once did I feel rushed. The amount of food you're receiving is rich, abundant, and protein packed -- VC isn't skimping out on the good stuff  Additionally, everything on the menu is unique and this restaurant is the kind where you can try a new dish each time you stop by. Definitely coming back to do that! Restrooms are clean but there's usually a line. Management is very professional when handling mishaps -- diners next to me received a poorly cooked pork chop and they received a new one plus the fee for this dish was taken off their tab! Price per person averages $40-60.
Mediocre. Over cooked fresh pasta. Rude irreverent service. Not rushing back. Don't bother. Don't believe the hype.

I've been wanting to come here for awhile (after finding out it is one of Taylor Swift's favorite restaurants). They promised my friend and I an hour wait, but it was more like an hour and a half. What was annoying was they seated a party of 2 before us even though they arrived after us and put their names down after us. They said we could sit at the bar or sit at the table they prepared for us after they cleaned it, and we chose the table, but there must have been some miscommunication because we waited longer and then they STILL sat us at the bar. Whatever, it's fine, we were hungry. 
I ordered the papardelle and it was sooo delicious. Worth the price. However, the portion size of the pasta was a bit smaller than other places I've been to in NYC. I savored every bite, but I wish we had ordered apps to go with our mains since the portion sizes were small. 
Also, since we were at the bar, the bartender was making drinks right in front of us, and a few times splashed me, which wasn't a pleasant experience...
We ordered dessert, I got a frozen chocolate mousse thing (the menu is in Italian) and I was unpleasantly surprised to find that it had a bunch of nuts in it. My friend got the tiramisu and really enjoyed it. 
They have matchbooks if you want to collect them.
Overall, it was a delicious meal, the ambience is good, but the wait was annoying and the bar seating is less than ideal.

Even after all of the horrible food reviews I have seen about this restaurant I still decided to give it a chance. The food was less than impressive and couldn't have been more average. At the end of dinner after paying the check we decided to stay and chat for a while. We then got accused of not paying our $600 bill, which we did indeed pay. The woman who handled this situation couldn't have been less graceful or kind. She was extremely rude. I highly reccomend avoiding this restaurant. Not worth it.

Officially made it to Via Carota and I feel as if I have finally lived. An A++ meal. 

My partner and I didn't have a resy but got in line outside around 5:15pm on a Sunday. There were probably already 15 people ahead of us but within 30 minutes or so we made it to the front to put our name down and had an estimated wait of 45 min. Worth noting that the people ahead of us actually got a spot at the bar. 

Once seated we ordered drinks but had to have our full order (apps, mains, etc) ready before we could order. We ended up going all out because why not, and we got the arancini, acciughe e burro (butter and anchovies bruschetta), the insalata verde, carciofi alla griglia (grilled artichokes), pappardelle, and the Via Carota Svizzerina. The absolute most incredible thing of all was the Svizzerina -- a hand chopped grass fed steak. This was reminiscent of the most perfectly cooked burger you could ever dream of -- crispy outside and PERFECTLY seasoned, with a beautiful cook on the inside. The pappardelle was good but I'd try something else pasta-wise next time. The insalata verde was top notch as well. Perfectly dressed and super fresh and crisp. The acciughe e burro was a top dish for me, sooo delicious and mouthwatering. My only note is there is a TON of butter on these guys, so I scraped a bit off knowing what else was coming after. 

All of that said, every single dish was delicious. We were blown away the entire meal... which was a really nice surprise. Sometimes with popular spots like these you worry they may not live up to the hype, but Via Carota does.

Last important mentions of the night were the Negroni Bianco (SO GOOD) and the Zabaione. The best dessert I've had in a while. A must.

Via Carota is a place no contrarian wants to love. But the 'nduja arancini, insalata verde, and cavoletti are each in my top 10 NYC dishes, and that was just our first course. While our pastas were a bit salty, the always-excellent negronis (same as at Bar Pisellano and I Sodi), an indulgent affogato and tiramisu (albeit a bit too much cream), and possibly the best spot for people-watching in the city left my contrarian streak shattered on Grove Street.

Unfortunately this place has dropped off majorly. The host staff has always been snooty and standoffish here, but they've gotten much worse since Taylor swift has turned this into a tourist spot. We cane at 5 pm and they tried to sit us at the very small end of a longer group table without saying a word to us that this was an option. We asked to change it and got a dirty look until they did and put us at another table with just a bench and no back. No one came over to our table for 20 minutes. We had to ask and then it was another 10 minutes until someone actually came and there was no apology or mention of it. Just asked what they could get for us. When we ordered drinks, mine had a bug in the bottom of it. I told them and the brought it back out and never apologized at all or mentioned it nor did they offer to comp it or take it off the bill. After all of this I ordered a decaffeinated cappuccino and it absolutely had caffeine in it and kept me up until 4 am. And then they had the nerve to kick us out of our seats after not coming over to wait us on for 30 minutes without any mention of a spot at the bar. This place has completely lost itself if it ever had one. The food is good but it's not worth this. Save yourself a disappointing experience.

Walked in on a weekday just after noon and were seated outside. We shared the insalate verde and the tagliatelle with parmigiano and prosciutto. Nice selection of wines by the glass in the $16 to $20 range. We skipped on drinks, so the two items came out to about $60 with tax and tip. Service was attentive and the food was ready fairly quickly.

What a fantastic dinner for my 50th birthday!! Thank you, Via Carota! 

This neighborhood spot lived up to the hype, and I am still beaming with joy from our amazing dining experience at Via Carota.

While this is mainly a walk-in only restaurant, our party of 5 had reservations (they have limited reservations that open up 30 days in advance, at 10am daily). But the people before us took a while to leave, so we waited a bit by the bar before being seated. We were seated in the back room at a long table, which was more intimate and quieter than the main dining room. I was very grateful for that. 

The service was impeccable. Our servers were all so friendly, helpful, and knowledgeable when it came to the wine list. They have a fantastic wine list, with some Italian wines that I don't see very often on restaurant menus. We ordered two bottles - a Nebbiolo and a Schioppettino -  that were both fabulous. 

Our meal was lovely. Rustic Italian comfort food with simple ingredients that were allowed to shine in each dish. The pastas were classic pasta dishes that were well executed. We had the tagliatelle, cacio pepe, and papardelle. Delicious. The carrots are phenomenal! Charred just enough to bring out those natural sugars, with thoughtful herbs and seasonings. Definitely order the carrots!

And of course, order the Insalata Verde. Their signature salad is a beautiful pile of layered greens and a light dressing that should be bottled (it might already be?). Two people can easily split one order.

The desserts are delicious as well. We had the cannoli and olive oil cake, which were delightful, fitting desserts to round out the meal. 

I also found the prices to be super reasonable considering the quality of food and wine, and how popular the restaurant is. 

Is it worth the wait? I think so. I've heard that lunch is a good time to go, to avoid long wait times. We all really enjoyed the whole dining experience here -- the entire staff is amazing! -- and I will absolutely be back on future trips to NYC!

Worth the wait. They don't take reservations, so scoring a table isn't for the faint. I got lucky with a great bar seat at lunch time. Food was amazing as promised. Cacio Pepe was REALLY good. Great staff. Pretty interior. I'd say it's a great date spot.

Reservations are not accepted. In other words, Via Carota essentially gives a big GFY to people with meal timing  issues (Type 1 diabetic here)  or those with mobility disabilities who need to know when they can expect to be seated.  Restaurants with that attitude should get over themselves.  My experience rating is not based on the food but on the overall customer experience, which has been extremely disappointing because of the uncaring nature of Via Carota for customers with special needs.
This place is a gem. Fantastic food and ambience. Great service. Always a must when in New York.

Happily influenced by Taylor Swift because it led us to this gem! There was no wait for a walk-in lunch on a weekday. We opted for their cute patio seating to finally enjoy spring in NY!

The tonnarelli (cacio e peppe) was the best I've had, but the vegetables are the stars of the show. We love a seasonal menu! If you're lucky enough to dine during ramp season, this is a unique dish and a must order. The salad is refreshing and crisp - I'm inspired to shave boiled eggs now too. They're very generous with their broccoletti servings as well. 

The hype is real. I can't wait to dine here again and share even more dishes with friends!
Love this place for lunch. Sit outside and get an aperol spritz and one of their tasty salads. I sat outside and enjoyed people watching and the sun. Perfect afternoon. Trust

Lovely Sunday lunch at Via Carota...One hour wait at 1pm. Sunday is the best day to go as Traffic and parking are simple.
Service is outstanding.
Seating is tight but not uncomfortable.
The arancini are absolutely outstanding as is the Grilled artichoke with a lemon aioli. 
The cacio e Pepe might be the best I have had while the Parmigiano and prosciutto is slightly less successful. The homemade pasta is wonderful and cooked perfectly. The tiramisu was disappointing as I felt there was too much mascarpone which doesn't have a lot of flavor on its own so in turn the dessert was flat. I have to agree with most diners as charging $3 for bread at their price points is a bit ridiculous. 
Overall a wonderful experience and I would return for the Arancini and Cacio alone.

This place continues to be a 10/10. The food is always consistently good and you know what you're getting. Everyone is always freaking out about the wait but in my opinion I've never had longer than an hour. Come here on a week day at 6ish and you'll get a table in 20/30 minutes. Come here for a weekend brunch and you'll probably have to wait 45 but it goes fast and they text you. That being said If you want to go for a weekend dinner you will have to put your name down at 5.

I can back to Via Carota recently and was so disappointed. I expected better when they have been ranked so highly in so many lists for where to eat.

First, it took us 30 minutes to get seated. Next, I shared my allergen then was served bread with my allergen.

It took over an hour for our pasta to come out.

Raw artichokes: 8/10

Pretty good dish but nothing crazy. Took 40 minutes to come out and there's no cooking required.

Pappardelle: 8/10

Pasta was fine. I wanted it to taste more fresh. I didn't like the wild boar in it either. It was dry.
Been wanting to try this place for a while to see the hype. I do think its a bit overrated. The pasta was pretty good but it wasnt a super memorable dish for me.

It wasn't bad but wasn't worth the hefty wait times some people were quoted. We honestly wanted an app and some outdoor drinks while in the neighborhood. Service was the most off putting- the waitress generally seemed confused and offended we didn't want to order mains. At the end of the meal she kind of lightened up but it was weird to question how much food we did or didn't want to have.

Espresso martini was good, aperol spritz was tiny and OK. Grilled artichokes great but for the price, you barely got anything. Bread was fantastic and so were the arancini.

Trendy looking spot, I'm sure the pasta was decent but seemed too uppity with snooty service to match.

Absolutely one of the best Italian places I've dined at in NY (and Chicago). The staff was overall friendly. Our first server had a ton of attitude, but his shift ended during our dining experience and the server that replaced him was great. The food is wonderful. It's worth the wait.

Ate here 3 times over the years. For all the hype, all times were just ok. To be clear, not bad but not great.

1 time ordered a chicken. And it was literally just that: a chicken leg. Nothing else. No condiments, garnish, sides, or salad. Nada. Just a piece of meat on a plate. Was quite off-putting.

I wonder how much following it would have if not for their location.

I really don't understand all the hype on Via Carota. Is it good? Yes. Is it worth waiting two hours in line for? Probably not. 

I came in for lunch on a Friday and it was totally packed by 11:45am. Thankfully I snagged a bar seat. I ordered the "iconic" cacio e Pepe - I thought it was good, but not the best I've ever had. If you can easily get a table here, then definitely go, but with so many amazing Italian restaurants in NYC, a long wait just isn't worth it.

I came for lunch on a Friday at open and there was no wait. And honestly, I wouldn't say Via Carota is a place that's worth waiting in line. It's solid but I prefer Don Angie which is nearby(ish). The famed cacio e pepe was quite salty and my friend and I basically had to coerce each other to finish it so that we didn't waste it. The pappardelle was much better but not so good that it's worth waiting in line for.

Incredible food and warm inviting ambience with neighborhood charm.  Seasoned, courteous service.  This is a special and memorable place which is hard to top!  The only complaint would certainly be that it's very challenging just to get in or obtain a reservation.

You already know about this place. 

The appetizers and the smaller bites are better than the mains. In fact, the pasta was terrible and overcooked. Just get the chicken liver and a few smaller salads and dishes and a bottle of wine and chill for a bit. Portions of the appetizers and are legitimately big so you won't miss the mains.

Came here with a 8pm res on a Tuesday and was really packed! 
Brocollini - was over salted and not very good :( 
Cacio e Pepe - really nice bouncy pasta and tasty, but nothing spectacular 
Meatballs - very solid, but nothing spectacular 

Overall was a bit disappointed given how hyped the restaurant was

Nothing like the reputation it gets. No,  there's nothing to complain about, but I wouldn't go out of my way for this particular restaurant. In other words,  if you're in the neighborhood give it a try.

Expected a lot more from this place based on what I'd read. The peas and fava beans were excellent. The pork belly was an embarrassment and the Baccala was just bland. Service was ok, but our waiter never came to check on us, while positioned  for many minutes next to the bus station across the sidewalk. Location is beautiful but the ownership obviously isn't paying attention. Sad.

One of the worst Italian meals I have ever had. Order the bruschetta if you want to eat puke on toast. Pappardelle has no flavour at all. I don't know who ever claimed this was a good restaurant because it's not. Only redeeming feature is service is really nice and the ambiance inside/outside is charming.

We absolutely loved our dinner at Via Carota. To us, it lived up to the hype without ever seeming like it was trying to live up to the hype. That made for a perfect evening.
We started with the fava bean, pecorino, escarole and mint salad. Fantastic, and I think a great example of what makes this place so good. It was a pretty simple thing, but that vinaigrette was just perfect.  Perfectly thick, perfectly salty, perfectly acidic. And the mint. And the favas. And the pecorino. Probably the best salad I've ever eaten.
Then we had the cacio e pepe and the svizzerina. Also simple, but also both just excellent. 
Service was friendly, casual, even funny, but also very knowledgeable. We really appreciated the advice they gave on the menu.
Is it worth standing in line for two hours? We didn't have to, but probably would have. And it's not like you have to literally stand in line. They take your cell phone number, you go have a cocktail somewhere else, and they text you when your table is ready. 
Thanks to everyone at Via Carota for making this meal so enjoyable.

Service was great and the ambiance was nice.  The food was not as good as it was 6 months ago in December.  The meatballs were very dry and not seasoned on the inside.  Not good.  Pine nuts inside of them tasted old?  Should have returned it but I felt bad... Boar Parpadelle was "okay" but not as delicious or moist as it had been in December.  Something is amiss!

So good reviewing it a second time. Seriously, such incredible pasta, appetizers and desert. Lovely outdoor seating. Nice selection of wine including some really outstanding desert wines. Great people. Can't think of a better spot for a birthday dinner
Excellent.  This is such a great restaurant. Service is great, atmosphere is filled with high energy and everything we ordered was delicious. I need to come to NY more often just to have food here.

Utterly unpretentious and prompt service, surprised we got a table within 15 minutes on a May Thursday night. Super kind server, gave us great suggestions and did not steer us wrong. That toast with butter and anchovies? We should've ordered extra bread for the butter mounds, addictive and simple. Great cacio e Pepe, tasted like Mac and cheese which I suppose is how it should taste. Sexy and smoky Italian ambiance.

It's really too bad I have to say this given all the hype and how much I was looking forward to this but... Via Carota is most definitely OVERRATED. 

Let's start from the beginning...

Because of the popularity and everything I have heard about Via Carota, I have been wanting to try it out for years, but was never able to get a reservation. And so, one day, I decided to just line up with the others outside the restaurant and try to get in via walk-in / waitlist. They start adding people to the waitlist at 5pm, but even before then, a lengthy line had already formed (which I joined). I waited in line for about 45 minutes to get my name on the waitlist. It was a little over 2 hours later that I got a text that my table was ready and I finally entered the restaurant. But at this point, I had expected this given the popularity, so all was still okay.

The first strange thing I noticed was that our waiter never mentioned the daily specials to us, although he did for the tables next to us... so we just ordered from the normal options.

Naturally, I had to order one of their classic pastas, so I got the Tagliatelle ($27). Surely, a nice Italian restaurant like this couldn't mess up their basic pasta, right? Wrong. The tagliatelle was EXTREMELY mediocre. The pasta was kind of mushy and far from the al dente preparation I hoped for. The sauce didn't really add anything to the dish either. Aside from the pasta itself, they just had a clump of parmesan on top with a handful of mediocre peas and a few bits of prosciutto. I am neither Italian nor a particularly great chef, but I am fairly certain I could have made this dish just as well... and probably for 1/5th of the price. 

In addition to the pasta, I also ordered the Orata Alla Griglia ($28), which is grilled sea bream (a fleshy white fish) with charred escarole (a green veggie). The fish was really very ordinary - no special flavor or anything... just tasted like normal white fish. Same for the veggies - they weren't even really seasoned and seemed to have just been thrown onto the pan and then onto the plate.

Throughout our meal, our waiter never checked in on us once. We had to flag him down to ask for the dessert menu, after which he put one single menu on our table for the two of us.

We ended up getting the Tiramisu ($15) for dessert. This was actually the best thing we ordered, as the tiramisu cream was a particularly good creamy consistency and was tasty. The softer ladyfinger parts of the dessert seemed to have been soaked in rum or something in addition to coffee as there was a slight hint of alcohol that actually paired well with the coffee flavor. $15 is a bit steep for this though.

The restaurant's interior has a pretty nice vibe with white tablecloths and wooden chairs to give the vibe of a nice Italian restaurant without being too formal. The space is not that big, but they have also spaced out the tables enough that it feels very comfortable and not crowded at all (perhaps this is why it is so hard to get one of the limited tables).

Overall, I have to say that Via Carota is certainly not worth the effort of trying to get a reservation or waiting for hours to get a table. The food is honestly very mediocre and overpriced. If I was served this at a normal casual restaurant with lower prices, I would probably be fine, but that was not the case here. I think Via Carota might just be one of those places that's popular simply because it's popular and not because it actually deserves it.

Last night we had the pleasure of eating at Via for the first time and boy did it exceed all of our expectations......when we arrived (as expected) it was quite hectic people acting entitled and impatient.....it was clear to us that Evelyn (the GM I believe) handled the whole situation with grace and dignity and patience.......wow, she is super at her job, truly.....and then we had the pleasure of being helped by both Kendall and Jonathan.......she is just fantastic at her job......kind, and helpful and the absolute best recommendations........we LOVED everything she suggested......and she was helped by Jonathan and he too was amazing........they all deserve special recognition and Via Carota is fortunate to have all three on their side....they represent the Via Carota brand well.....thank them for us, it was a really fun evening......

Tried to make a reservation here but it was impossible. Walked over and put my name on the list. the hostess was not the most pleasant person but given the crowds at this place I guess she has it rough. I was told I would have a 30 minute wait. I was seated after about 45 minutes. 

The waiter was excellent and the little table outside was perfect on a beautiful day.

Ordered for arancini, the green salad and the pasta with peas. The food was absolutely delicious!! My friend and i shared all three dishes and there was plenty of food.

If they accommodated reservations and the hostess were a bit nicer it would rate a 5 for sure.

Overall: Incredible. I had been wanting to go here for a very long time and finally made it. Absolutely worth all of the hype it gets. The pasta is so fresh and the service was great. 

Reservation: Hard to get a reservation. Put our name down around 7pm and got seated around 9pm. We anticipated a long wait so we didn't go there already hungry and just bounced around the area getting drinks. 

Service: Good service but nothing of note. 

Ambiance: We sat outside and I didn't feel that sitting outside hindered the experience in any way. 

Food: Outstanding. Pasta was so fresh. We got the Tagliatelle ($27), Caccio e Pepe (our favorite $27), octopus ($28), and a Brussel sprout salad that was a special. The salad should absolutely be brought onto the main menu it was a highlight of the meal. Overall the cacio e Pepe was better than the tagliatelle but wroth trying both. The octopus also was a stand out dish, I'd definitely order it again. They brought me cannolis for my birthday that were delicious!

Please remind me that when a restaurant is called " trendy" not to go there. Trendy is code for overpriced inferior product you're supposed to believe is good. We went there after the final performance of Enemy of the State ( which was great!) because my daughter is a huge Michael Imperioli fan and he favors this restaurant. Anyway, we waited two hours for a table ( because it's trendy) and ordered a salad and Burrata. Michael says the salad it amazing. I say it's assorted greens with an unremarkable dressing. Burrata is Burrata. They didn't invent it, so I'm not giving them credit for putting it on a plate. My wild boar ragu was an extremely small portion. I know what you're thinking... well in italy.... I've been to italy. They serve nice portions of in house , made from scratch items. No restaurant starves you in italy.  My son got the risotto, which looked like a bad version of grits. He said he liked it. I tasted it. He was being kind. Tasted sour to me. My daughter got the clams. Clams in a bowl that they call an entree. Whatever. If there's a saving grace it's the excellent service. The staff was quick and knowledgeable. They kept the water glasses full as we ate outside on a blistering hot day. Sadly, I would never return. Please don't be duped by trendy.
friendly staff - good cocktails which is why I gave 2 instead of one star - the food was awful. No flavor, the famous salad is just arugula in oil....I question the folks leaving great reviews

Great location in the West Village of New York City. The restaurant has great indoor and outdoor seating. You must make reservations as this is a popular location in the West Village. The food is very unique and special and my compliments to the chef for all the spectacular dishes that they serve. I highly recommend if you're in the New York area to make a reservation ahead of time and having a great experience with great food and service.

We waited 1 and half hour for our reservation. I ordered martini italiano , I took a small sip and didn't like it. Server Miles S. , I got his attention and I said I really don't like this Martini so I ordered another martini which wasn't any better and didn't it at all. For the food , We ordered prosciutto Menlo which was good , insalata verde which was great. 
We also ordered Pappardelle which was too salty,tonnarelli too salty and risottos which was good. 
The bill comes, they didn't take the Martini Italiano off the bill. I asked Miles why didn't they take the martini off the bill , " he said since I told you what  it is in that martini and talked to my manager Evelyn you will be charged no matter what". I told him that is all I need to know. 
Poor guests service and poor management. Never again when you have so many other options.

The food was disgusting, no flavour at all. I thought it was a Greek restaurant instead of an Italian one. All they seasoned the food with was olive oil and salt. The service was terrible, the server only came to take our orders in the beginning and never returned, possibly because the restaurant only caters to the whites. If you're coloured, I do not recommend this restaurant for you. Spent $180 on food I could have cooked better.

This restaurant is absolute robbery. This is definitively the worst Italian restaurant I've ever eaten at. The food was nasty, came in small portions, and every single item on the menu costs around 30 dollars or more. The food tastes like it's barely seasoned. The only dish that wasn't was the fish, and the fish was overly salty. I couldn't even eat the fish how disgusting it tasted. The meatballs tasted like frozen ones you could buy from a grocery store. And the meatballs just came with 3 sad looking meatballs with no pasta at all. The chicken tasted like it was boiled and just quickly seared to give it color. The service was atrocious. The waiter just took orders in the beginning and then left and never returned. She only treated the white customers well and treated everyone else like trash. She absolutely did not deserve a tip and over was a horrible waitress. Honestly people like that should look to get a job outside of the food service industry, if you can't treat customers well you shouldn't have a job. This place clearly didn't train their servers properly either. The ambiance was nice but it doesn't make up for the disgusting food and the nasty attitude from the server.

This was a quaint and quintessential west village restaurant. I've heard so much about it and really wanted to give it five stars, but there were some misses. The Fritto Misto was delicious but was very surprised to see that the shrimp were unpeeled. Entrees were delicious (prosciutto pasta and clams), but on the salty side. The tiramisu was excellent. The service was decent but should have been more on point at such an exclusive restaurant. - 4 stars
Delicious meal but not necessary the best ever as it's been hyped up to be. Service and atmosphere are great

A lot of New York restaurants use Resy for their reservations.  For this NY trip, many of the eateries I tried to book went immediately to "Notify" on Resy the instant the designated time to book came up.  Via Carota was one of these places.  Granted, they only release a limited number of reservations for non-VIP's and operate primarily as a walk-in place (or so they say).

 So that is what I did.  I arrived about 15 minutes before their 11 am opening time and was the first in line.  Others gathered quickly in a haphazard way until a repeat diner informed us where the line usually forms, and everyone then queued properly.  The restaurant has indoor and outdoor seating; inside there is table and bar seating.  Needless to say, the place filled up pretty quickly.  Service was pretty attentive at first but became more sparse the busier it got.

Via Carota is one of five West Village restaurants run by Rita  Sodi and Jody Williams.  Three of them, Bar Pisellino, I Sodi and Buvette, can be seen from Via Carota.  Via Carota and I Sodi are the most difficult to get into.  

Here's what I ordered:  
1)  Grilled artichokes with aioli. 
2) the daily special pasta--Stracci pesto genovese
3) fried rabbit
4) raspberry crostata

Everything was tasty, but my faves were the artichokes and pasta.  A lot of surrounding tables ordered the bruschetta with butter and anchovies, the huge insalata verde salad as well as the even larger daily special of grilled vegetables.  

There are many other dishes I would like to try in the future.  I don't know if I could stand an hours-long wait, however.  I would guess early lunch or "linner" (4 pm-ish) would be the least crowded times.
Very good place to eat. Service is good. A small restaurant usually with a 15-20 minute wait but you can walk across the street and have a drink at the bar Pisolino.

The food was out of this world. Prepare yourself to magnificence!!!
We had Pappardelle with wild boar ragu, roasted chicken that would melt in your mouth, Tagliatelle: parmigiano &prosciutto. Cacio pepe, which is homemade pasta that was excellent!!! Plus insulata that was very refreshing. We had the most amazing combination of burratta cheese over grilled spinach that was perfected w/ rich flavor and the garlic flavor was just perfect and not overpowering. We also had grilled mushrooms and another dish of grilled artichoke w/ delicious aioli sauce that were surprisingly very good. 
We had cannolis that melt in your mouth, not hard at all. We had grilled peaches with crema that was just heavenly. We also had almond cake that was also very, very good.
We had to wait for a while to get seated AND they do not sit you down unless your whole party is there present. 
We sat outside and the atmosphere was amazing, great weather and loved people watching.

you've probably heard enough people hype this place up but trust me when i say this is the best italian food i've had in my life AND I'VE BEEN TO ITALY. 12/10 literally broke my scale. the texture of the pasta was incredible and the flavor was honestly chefs kiss. my favorite pasta was the pappardelle and the 'nduja arancini was a MUST GET. if you can somehow get reservations here, DO IT.
Of the 5 dishes we ordered, the only standout was the charred leeks. While we loved those, the rest of the dishes we didn't enjoy.

Service was okay, we were seated outside in about 10 minutes without a reservation-- Friday afternoon around 3:15.  Waitress never inquired how are food was, if we needed anything.  Restaurant was very busy.
Inside was quite noisy, outside was fine.  Many guests had dogs.
Food -- large green salad was good, much too large for just 2 people.  The main course-- cod with chickpeas and olives was dry and tasteless, no sauce, I only ate several bites of it.   Waitress didn't inquire why.  Boar ragu was good (not great), heavy.
Zabaglione with fresh blueberries and strawberries 
was a large serving for more than 2.  It was good but   didn't taste like zabaglione, no Marsala wine taste.
No bread offered.
Total with tip was a little over $100.
I doubt we'll bother eating here in the future as getting a table usually is a hassle, not worth the effort.

Absolutely outstanding food and vibes! The servers were also really friendly which made the experience really nice. 
For apps we got the Zucchini Fritti which was a huge portion, very tasty and just something to munch on for the table. This one can be skipped though. 
We also got the Funghi/ grill mushrooms which were super tasty. 
For mains I got the cacio e Pepe and it was really good! Would recommend this dish for sure.

Ventured into the city for early dinner today and we came across Via Carota. We were looking for something with a more casual vibe and this place had that so we decided to give it a try. It was cute, food was decent, service was good. The pasta itself was great but the flavors were underwhelming. We enjoyed the arancini as they had good flavor and a nice crispy outside.
Food was so delicious, the service was immaculate and the restaurant was small but very nice and cute.
We went for a late lunch and were able to walk right in. Everything was delicious - great food and drinks. We'll be back.
Good cacio e Pepe. The sauce was more on the buttery side than most cacio e Pepe dishes, but the texture of the pasta was great. Awesome vibe

Is it worth it? No. Save your time and spend your money elsewhere. The West Village, SoHo,  and even Little Italy have comparable pasta places. Everything we tried was ok to good but definitely not remarkable in any way. It left a lot to be desired. Maybe that's the misfortune of being so highly regarded but good pasta is good pasta at the end of the day, and when so many other restaurants seem to get it right. I will say the salad was simple but delicious.
Absolutely delicious food! I'm still drooling over these photos. Difficult to get a reservation but highly recommend to continuously check resy because it is worth it!
Food was fab, ambiance was lovely, and the service was great. LOVED their salads-- they have so many options, you can't go wrong with any of the (I think 18) salads they offer on their menu.

I've lived in city for years and needed to see what the hype was.  The food is mediocre at best. Not sure what I'm missing and certainly not worth the two hour wait that's for sure. Was it good?  It was just okay! The service....get them in and get them out!

Came back for fish. 

Nicole was super kind in the front. Not too difficult to walk in on a weekend for lunch as it's bustling during dinner, but loved the outdoor seating in the summer.

Tried the Baccalaureate e Ceci this time for the salt cod, chickpeas, olives, and lemon. 

Extremely delicious! The clams are also spot on - highly recommended.

Unable to get a reservation, we waited in line. Line moves pretty slow to put your names down which is annoying but understandable given how popular it is. We missed a table for 2 by just one person and were told to come back in about an hour. We sat in the park for a bit before returning.

We ended up being seated at the bar which was really fun. Major takeaways: the pastas are excellent, the other dishes are not. We ordered the mushroom dish which was extremely acidic/vinegary and the meatballs which had raisins and left us thoroughly confused and unwilling to finish. The pastas, however, are excellent and despite only trying two of them, are enough to get us to come back.

Service was great and food came out in good time, would suggest that they improve the recommendations for guests or ask what we like because we did not enjoy what was recommended.

This place is so popular that it's hard to get seated. I had the fried rabbit which was okay. Tasted like chicken. Pretty tender, came with fried garlic. The cacio e pepe was also just okay. Maybe it's not the dish for me but it wasn't flavorful at all. I could barely taste any cheese!

We stopped by for some coffee snd dessert and loved it! The outdoor seating is very charming and tranquil amongst the NY hustle. Ordered affogatos and tiramisu which came with elegant flare. The affogatos are black spotted vanilla ice cream wells that the server then pours expresso at service. Outstanding! Best affogatos ever and i will be returning to sample more of the menu. Highly recommend!

Regrettably, we had a very disappointing experience at the Via Carota in New York on Monday night, 9/2.  I'm sure the food is delicious, but sadly we never got to taste it.  This experience started 2 1/2 months earlier, when in mid-June I emailed the restaurant to request a reservation while  we were in New York for our long-awaited vacation from Seattle.  The restaurant emailed me back and said they were not able to accommodate my request but limited reservations could be made 30 days in advance via RESY.  Otherwise, most all their business was "walk-in."  OK, I understood the rules, so I set my calendar for 30 days ahead of our arrival.  

When the appointed "make a reservation day" arrived, I went through the RESY system to make my reservation in the early morning exactly 30 days in advance.  To my shock there were no reservations available.  It didn't seem possible, but oh well.  We understood that without that precious reservation, we would have to show up as "walk-ins" and likely wait for a table.

That brings us to last night.  We took a 30 minute cab ride to Via Carota and got in the back of a line of about 10 people, all telling us that was the line for check in.  While waiting, we observed multiple couples arriving and being escorted to their seats.  Our line DID NOT move and NO ONE came to get our name on a list or inform us of a wait time.  My wife walked up to the entry to she if she could get on the list.  She was told she had to get back in line to get on the list.  OK, well she also noted there were several empty seats at the bar and she said we would be happy to be seated there if possible.  She was told those were first come, first serve, which made perfect sense, but we still had to wait in the line.  

So, we waited 30 minutes in line until we finally got to the front.  Voila! the bar seats were still open! We told the hostess, or whoever it was managing the line, that we would love to take those two empty bar seats.  Now, after waiting 30 minutes to get to the front of the line, the rules changed.   We were now told they were holding those bar seats for a couple that was late arriving for a reservation.  That was a bit hard to swallow.  So we said ok, life she is not going to allow us to sit at the open bar seats, let's get on the list for first available table   The answer was it was going to be at least 2 hours!  

So, the way this restaurant operates is that some few preferred people magically get reservations while others cannot no matter how hard they try and how early they make the request.  Then this restaurant makes you wait 30 minutes in line just to be told it will be a 2-hour wait.  And although bar seats are supposed to be "first come-first served" they will arbitrarily deny you access after you wait so they can hold them for people who are late showing up for their reservations.  

I don't care how good the food is.  I can only be disrespected so much.  My advice?  Go to a place that treats you like you matter.  The Lure Fish Bar a few blocks away was wonderful!

We waited about 30 minutes for an outdoor seat for 2 people. The service was really good and attentive even as we sat outside for dinner on a hot summer night. 

The food here was left a lot to be desired. All of the dishes are meant to share and we had about 4 dishes for 2 people. It was pricey for the type of dish and  amount. We really liked the fried rabbit. The coating was crunchy and the meat was tender on the inside. The cacio pepe and little gem salad was very standard. We did not even realize there was egg in the salad until we reviewed the menu. The chopped chicken liver flavor was good, but was served in a way that was the most unappetizing. The server noted it is more of an Italian pate that was less smooth and sweet than a french pate, but this did not prepare us for what we received. And the bread was not warmed nor toasted. The drinks were good and I enjoy they had their own variations of Negronis.

The vibe in this restaurant is very busy and bustling. The vibe is young and touristy. In addition, this restaurant is in the heart of the west village and was a great restaurant to people watch. We saw a celebrity, run club, etc. I would probably come back here for a drink and people watch only.

Everyone I know loves and recommended this restaurant. Maybe my expectations were too high but I was underwhelmed.

The Insalata verde is amazing! Plus, the bread is delicious and they have a lovely selection of wine.

I went for a late lunch and sat outside, which was lovely as it was great people watching. As mentioned, I loved the Insalata verde. I also had a pasta with pesto and it was not good. In fact, I did not finish it. 

Given my mother was sick and unable to join me, I returned the following day determined to have a better meal and experience. It was busy so we sat inside, which was fine. The bread and olive oil were great. My mother had the Risotto with Meyer lemon and despite how it looked, it tasted good/lemony and the risotto was cooked perfectly.

I ordered the Carciofi Crudi. I've had a lot of raw artichoke salads, but this one was odd. The artichokes weren't shaved and they were served with a lot of avocado that looked like mush on the plate and had little to no flavor. Another bad dish.

Maybe I ordered the wrong things and should not have listened to the waitress who recommended the pasta with the pesto, but I was disappointed by both meals which was surprising given how beloved the restaurant is.
Insalata Verde was light and delicious. Tonarelli Cacio e Pepe was pretty good but nothing too special. Great service.

Excellent in every way.  Service , food is amazing.  

The no resy thing is annoying but it is what it used to be.

We went Sept 21st 2024 at 5:30 - the lady who refilled the water for the patio was ON POINT. I've never been so hydrated. Our waiter was amazing. Service fantastic. Top 3 best meal of my life. The artichokes! The risotto! The cacio e pepe! The ribeye! Undeniable, unbelievable, unbeatable. Everything was jaw dropping.

Info for those trying to go but can't make a resy (we couldn't). Show up around 4 - we jumped in a line that was short at th!t time and around 5 they started to add people to the wait list.  We ended up eating at like 5:30 but it was a guarantee. We probably could have let people in front of us to try and target a little bit of a later time.

The only negative....we were approached by lots of kids and adults selling candy....literally at our table. It was uncomfortable

Always a great experience at via carota - the hardest part is getting a reservation there but an early walk in would do the trick! 

The sleeper hits are definitely the pesto pasta, the fried rabbit and the grilled peaches for dessert!

While exploring NYC, we asked our bartender for dinner recommendations in the area. He did not hesitate to recommend Via Carota. We are so glad we asked! We were able to be seated quickly (party of 3), but I would suggest reservations. It was a very popular spot. We chose to dine inside but the patio looked very inviting & popular. Our server brought bread, olives, discussed the menu & wine options & let us take it all in. The food was amazing! Fresh pasta, not drowned in sauce. The perfect wine, some bread...I could picture Italy.

Amazing food and pasta, we ordered a few things and everything was delicious. Service can be a bit more gentle as the plates slightly slams on the table whenever it is put down. Out of all the dishes what stood out the most was the verde salad and the arincini. Probably one of the best salad I have had it is incredibly fresh and dressing was so well balanced. The arancini was so cheesy and had a bit of a kick in the middle.

the service is so rude, inattentive, smug and insincere.   for a restaurant so popular, it seems they took kindness and appreciation for granted and are above the rules of basic exchange of services.    yes charming and classic but the hostess couldnt be less interested, the servers dont communicate and even in a shift change they act like they are doing us a favor for dining there.   dissappointing on many levels.  spend your money elsewhere where it is valued.
First off the ambiance here is so amazing and the staff is so friendly and inviting! The food is at a whole level of perfection!

Been here a couple times, and the pasta is always spectacular! The wait time has become pretty egregious recently, but I love coming here for a weekday lunch with a friend- you can almost always be seated. 

As a pasta lover, my favorites are the Tonarelli cacio e pepe and Tagliatelle w/ prosciutto. The pasta has such a nice bite- and the sauces are classics done well. I also like their fish- so tender and flavorful. The drinks are also good- I love their cynar spritz. Service is great, and the vibes both inside and outside are nice. 

Overall this is a great Italian place, but I personally wouldn't wait hours for a table. If the wait is short or you have a reservation it's great, but otherwise you can find equally delicious pasta.

I've been to via carota twice now, and both times I wasn't impressed. I think it's average Italian food.  I can eat similar tasting pasta at many other establishments.  This doesn't stand out.  The apps were average too.  Nothing that sets it apart from other Italian restaurants.  People go for the hype and it's game but it doesn't live up to it.  Maybe other people just don't know go Italian food.  I'll give the restaurants props on the aesthetics
Everything was perfect! Gabrielle is the best server and always treats us great. Food was top notch and the vibes were off the charts. Will never stop going back!

Did a walk in one Saturday afternoon and it was excellent. Lived up to the hype in many ways! The basil pesto pasta was incredible. The cacio e Pepe was solid but didn't bring the fan fare it was noted for. The grilled leeks on the other hand, wow! Those will knock your expectations off! Leeks on another level. And hot damn, the mascarpone and grilled peaches were sensational and the perfect ending to our meal. One of my fav desserts in a long time! Wow! Loved this place!

Overall we enjoyed our lunch here. We came during the week around 3 pm so we waited a few minutes for a table of 3. Very quaint restaurant with patio seating. It was a really nice and warm day so the patio was pretty busy. They give you a small dish of olives which were quite good. We ordered the grilled artichokes which were very good and had a great flavour. We also ordered the grilled octopus which was excellent as it had great flavours and perfectly cooked. We had the signature tonnarelli (cacio peper) which was cooked perfectly al dente and the creamy cheese and pepper sauce was amazing. It was definitely my favourite dish. The ragu pappardelle was good but wasn't anything special when you compare to the tonnarelli. The grass fed beef was ok. It was grilled on the outside and less cooked on the inside but it was too salty on the outside and lacked flavour on the inside  I would not order that again.

After hearing all the hype about this place, I was very excited to try it myself! We walked in on a weekday for lunch and got seated immediately with no wait. I thought the pastas were solid, but nothing to write home about. 

I especially liked the lemon risotto -- I thought it was very special and captured the essence of Italy. I definitely want to come back next time and try out some other pastas and some of their greens, which I think they're known for! 

The restaurant itself is quite charming, and the area is super cute to walk around in.

Overall, it was a solid meal, but I'm not sure I would go through the effort of waiting or scrambling to book a reservation!

5 emphatic stars for one of the finest Italian dinners I've ever had, in a really cool atmosphere, with staff that went above and beyond.

I was recently in NY and have had Via Carota on my list for a long time. Unfortunately, your girl did not make a reservation in advance (*SHAME*). We arrived and though at first it seemed the wait would be long, we got super lucky and got seated in a private room. If I were planning to have kids, I'd give my first-born to the hostess who made our night!!

Once seated, (again- in a private room!!) we were greeted by our server who was super attentive the whole dinner. He, along with the other staff members who dropped off food along the way, were absolute pleasures!

The Food:
- Fried zucchini: This appetizer was a true mountain of delicately fried strings of zucchini. It was as impressive in flavor as it was in size. Though this could've felt heavy and greasy it was surprisingly light!
- Insalata verde: A gorgeous, bright salad with buttery greens, topped with sherry vinaigrette and welcomed by all at the table!
- Tagliatelle: This pasta dish featured prosciutto and a creamy sauce and topped with parmigiano. The little sweet peas throughout this dish were a nice surprise!
- Meyer lemon risotto: WOW. A risotto can be heavy, this is a given. But pairing it with a creamy meyer lemon sauce added just the right sweet acidity to counter the heavy cream. This is a winner.
- Cacio pepe tonnarelli: Your girl loves a cacio pepe and this may be my favorite version of a cacio pepe of all time. the tonnarelli pasta was perfect for this peppery, creamy sauce. It was really exceptional.


Desserts:
- Tiramisu: Duh. This was fabulous.
- Grilled peach dessert with homemade ice cream: The server told us this was in season and highly recommended it and he was not wrong. The grilled peaches SANG!

Overall a perfect dinner with exceptional food, cocktails, and service. I'll definitely be back! (with a reservation...)

It was good but not as amazing as influencers make you believe. The tagliatelle was way too soft, kind of a one note cheese flavor, and the insalata verde was nice but nothing i can't make at home if i used garlic oil and salt. Overall nice atmosphere, nice waiters, not worth the $60 i paid though.

We managed to get a prime time reservation here for my wife's birthday, although depending on party size and willingness to eat outside, the walk in wait was less than you might expect given the celebrity hype. Probably the best dish we shared was the roast carrots in yogurt which was delicious. The cacio e pepe and grilled octopus were both more good than great. The portions might not look huge at first but it was enough for us to share and feel satisfied. We liked our drinks which had a good smell and sweet taste without being overly sugary. Service was good and helpful, although they didn't acknowledge my wife's birthday even though I noted it in the reservation. I don't think I've ever seen that before so that was disappointing.

Would recommend if you can get a reservation or there's very little wait. Don't wait two hours though because it's not THAT great.

I had such high expectations given how popular this place was. My husband managed to get reservations at a prime weekend dinner time for my birthday. We were taken right away, I heard other people waiting for 2 hours. Service was great, our waiter was friendly and helpful. Our glasses were constantly filled with water. Food came out quickly given how crowded it was. It was a comfortable ambiance - modern rustic with an Italian flare, nice intimate lighting but not too dark. We started with complementary olives. We ordered the carrots, octopus and Cacio e Pepe and shared everything. We also ordered spritzes which were so delicious. The stand out dish was the carrots- cooked and seasoned to perfection on top of creamy tart yogurt. I am still thinking about it! Next came the Octopus and pasta which were standard dishes, not very memorable or extraordinary. I would have liked the Octopus to be over something other than olives, felt a little redundant with the complementary ones. Felt a little overpriced for what it was. I am also a little disappointed, would have been nice to be wished a happy birthday by the staff, especially since my husband added it to the reservations.

Given the hype around this restaurant, I was so excited to try it! Unfortunately, it's average at best. The service was friendly and the ambiance is cozy, but the food isn't great. We got a few of the dishes they're known for: the cacio e pepe was okay, the butternut squash tortellini was delicious, and the appetizers were good, but not great. My zero proof Negroni and the pannacotta were amazing though! We had a 6pm reservation on a Wednesday and overheard the wait for a table for 2 to be over an hour and half. Overall, a decent meal, but in my opinion not worth all of the drama of getting a reservation or waiting for a table.

We were able to walk in a little after they opened on a weekday and got seated immediately. This place is obviously very hyped up, so I moderated my expectations. 

We ordered the arancini, cacio e pepe, and the tagliatelle. Arancini was fine - I liked that they had bits of spicy pork in it since the flavor of creamy rice gets monotonous but it still needed something sharp to give it a kick flavor-wise. Cacio e pepe was a let down; I didn't think the noodles were particularly al dente and it was way too salty. I much prefer the cacio e pepe at L'Artusi. The flavors in the tagliatelle were more interesting but it was also way too salty, especially if the bite had prosciutto in it. The proscuitto was also clumped together at the top which made it difficult to eat. 

Servers were very attentive with refilling our water, but I felt like we got forgotten towards the end of the meal and we had to flag someone down for the check. Overall this meal was a sodium bomb - glad I tried this place out but will not be coming back personally.

My friend brought me to Via Carota for some drinks after our dinner on a Saturday night. We could not get a resy for that particular night, but my friend who has been here before, raves about this place so much! Dining area was packed and in full service.

Thankfully we were seated right away to have drinks at the bar-we were seated on the right side, away from the actual bar which was nice as it gave us some privacy and space.

We ordered an espresso martini and the signature martini (yes, we are tini girlies!). The drinks were strong, and made well!

I would love to come back to try their dinner menu next time!
Sat at the bar late at night, food was pretty decent. The paparadelli had a pretty good texture and the arincini were nicely fried.

Great apps and pasta! Got in line at 4:15pm on a Saturday and waited until 5pm to put our names down for a group of 6 people. We got seated at 6pm! It was a great meal and great ambiance. Worth the wait.

Everything you want it to be. I got lucky and only waited 20-30 minutes for a table on the weekend. The service is great. The vibes are immaculate. The pasta is so delicious and fresh. Also, legit the best fried calamari I've ever had in my life.

Arrogance defined. 
This used to be an absolute favorite restaurant and so it was a must in visiting New York to come back to. We dealt with their completely completely bizarre and ridiculously arrogant reservation system by showing up at around 4:30 to be first in line and then get an early seating. Is the ambience pretty? Sure is the food still good, not as good as it used to be but OK. The homemade pasta is still pretty good. Served a little lukewarm. I was really looking for somebody to absolutely do any kind of care. . Every single person we interacted with including two different servers and the host could not have cared less. They were rude, dismissive, didn't explain anything on the menu. When asked any sort of question or asked for advice on some wine, they acted like we could have just asked them to recite the periodic table---Exasperated and bored all the way around. Only showed some sense of false courtesy with a fake smile and patronizing comments  with no desire to really make someone feel welcome.. No care or enthusiasm for a beloved city restaurant. Sort of just acted like we should be so lucky to be in their presence. They could take a lesson from Danny Myers, and what it means to serve with care for an establishment that is supposed to be in the hearts of many. Would never recommend anyone going there again. Too many amazing eateries in the city with people who genuinely want to see you enjoy your experience. Absolutely jumped the shark.

Walked in for lunch by myself and got seated right away at the bar. I ordered the cacio e pepe and the portion size is average. Some places get this simple dish wrong, Via Carota's cacio e pepe was great. The employees were friendly and offered very quick service. Inside was cozy, quite busy, with many people eating outside despite it being chilly. I got the tiramisu for dessert - the coffee taste coming through sharply, overall enjoyed my meal here.

This place is.... surprise! Overhyped! Relieved my wait was so short since I'm not sure it would have been worth much longer.

Sunday afternoon - put my name down for indoor dining at 4:26, got texted at 4:38 and sped back to the restaurant. My friend and I sat at the communal table, but thankfully the seats immediately next to us were blocked out.

The restaurant is quite cozy, exposed brick, homey kind of vibe. Most tables appeared to be outfitted for groups of 4+ and were placed a bit close to each other - typical space deficit in West Village. The bar seating looked pretty inviting.

Food was good not great. Cacio e pepe was supposed to blow me away but it was just... fine. Not offensive with the cheese or the pepper, but just quite mild and forgettable. The butternut squash tortelli was doused in a buttery sauce, and it tasted good but felt quite simple. My favorite dish was the tiramisu, which was light and not too sweet (for a tiramisu). There's an extensive negroni menu here and I heard good things about it; the negroni rosa I sipped on was enjoyable but not a standout, and I could go without it next time. The vegetable dishes may be worthwhile here so I would try those; they just seemed quite pricey so we glossed over them.

Service was ok. On occasion we couldn't figure out where our server went. Additionally, there was some mini workstation immediately behind me where small plates temporarily sat, so waiters continuously bumped against the back of my chair while moving through that area.

Total after tax/tip was around $65 for one drink, one pasta, and half a dessert, per person. If I went in not knowing about the hype surrounding this place, I would have concluded that this is yet another Italian restaurant not much better than others in the city. A major part of the experience here is the excitement of just being able to get in. I would consider going back if lines ease up (which they probably won't) but if you haven't been here yet, don't despair - you're not missing out.

Everything about my experience at Via Carota was exceptional--the food, the ambience, the service. My companion and I ordered a slew of vegetable dishes, all of which were outstandingly fresh and delicious; the grilled artichokes were a standout, as were the charred leeks. The meyer lemon risotto was fantastically rich and flavorful. My only regret is that I didn't have room for dessert! Our server was attentive and helpful and the wait to be seated was minimal. Highly recommend.

Based on my experience and that of several friends-this is a hyped up
Place.the pastas are good but not the best in the city!
Not better than any fine Italian such as Marea, Babbo,or misi in Brooklyn.
Here's my Take: They hired a great PR agent who heavily promotes it to Actors and Influencers: Note Gigi Hadid just went there with Bradley cooper on a date!
Do I care that she went ? NO-Do you care that she went? I hope not! Is she paying your bill or mine? Heck no !
Perfect food and service in a gorgeous setting. If only every restaurant were this good

We came here as a group of 5 on a Thursday night. Despite my best efforts, I was not able to get us a reservation, but after putting our names on the list we were able to be seated around 7:30. Our table was in a lovely private dining space in the back which made it easy for our group to visit but it lacked the spirit of being in the main dining room. Cocktails and wine arrived promptly and service was attentive throughout the evening. 

For dinner we ordered the insalta verde, carote, faioli all' uccelletto, tonnarelli, pappardelle, truffle pasta special and pork chop special. I had been looking forward to trying Via Carota for a long time and I was honestly underwhelmed. The pasta was good, but not great and the pork chop was so rich that I couldn't take more than a couple of bites. The carrots, in my opinion, were on the overcooked side and lacked pizzaz. Favorite dishes were the cannellini beans with sausage, the green salad and the tiramisu for dessert. Good Italian restaurant but not worth the hassle of trying to get a table.

This place was awesome!!! The food was amazing!!! Service was terrific. Was lucky enough to sit outside. Ambiance was like a curbside French theme. I want to go back to NYC just for this place. You should order the endives salad and the tagliatelle and I am in love.

My friend and I were super excited to have snagged a reservation here for a graduation dinner celebration! We arrived 5 minutes prior to our reservation time, but had to wait another 15 minutes for our table to be ready and there was no proper place for us to stand that wasn't in the way of everyone passing by. It's a small restaurant, so it's not fully their fault, was just annoying. We were seated at a two top directly behind the bar, though there were several other tables available since it was a pretty late reservation, I wish I asked for one of those. We ordered several different dishes to try as much as we could, so some extra table space would've been helpful haha. We ordered the insalata verde, bread, cacio e Pepe (of course), butternut squash ravioli, and a special pasta they had that night with a butter based sauce and truffle. The pasta special and cacio e Pepe stood out the most to me. Overall, the food was tasty, but unfortunately a bit overrated. There are numerous Italian restaurants with good pasta and in my opinion a better ambiance that are easier to get into. I'd give it a total of 3.5 stars. 

Tip: if you're waiting for a table, bar pisellino across the street is amazing and walk in only!

I hope I don't get canceled for this but... Via Carota was genuinely one of the most overhyped and underwhelming restaurants I've ever been to in NYC. It's quite rare that a restaurant disappoints me as much as this one did.

We walked on a Monday at 5 pm and waited around 5 minutes before being seated. 

To start, the complimentary bread that was served was cold, and hard. The crust was so tough that I could barely even bite a piece off. Rough start to the meal...
For our appetizers, we got the Cacioffi alla Griglia (grilled artichokes and aioli) and the Broccoletti (broccoli rabe). The grilled artichokes were not bad-- tasted like standard, good artichokes. But the broccoli rabe was so bitter. I don't understand why it tasted like that. There was very little to enjoy about this dish. I absolutely do not recommend.

For our mains, we got the Polpette (Sicilian meatballs with pine nuts and raisins) and the Pappardelle with wild boar ragu. Once again, both these dishes were extremely average and underwhelming. The red sauce with the meatballs tasted like you could've gotten it from a Ragu can. The meat was also not very moist. 

The pappardelle was very standard, strands of pasta were occasionally stuck together. By no means was this dish bad but it was not worth $30.

Overall, I do not recommend Via Carota. I can't even begin to fathom why this place has so much hype and has people waiting an hour in line to eat here. My advice-- save your money or go elsewhere, there are many other delicious Italian offerings in West Village.

In honesty, my first visit to Via Carota was very underwhelming, but I think we just ordered the wrong things. Have come back several times after and it's one of my favorite Italian spots, living up to the hype.

The space is very charming. It's cozy and feels very West Village.

Loved:
- Tonnarelli cacio e pepe
- Tagliatelle parmigiano & prosciutto
- Pesto Pasta (was a special)
- Carciofi Alla Griglia grilled artichokes
- Arancini

Good/Okay:
- Pappardelle wild boar ragu
- Salad with prosciutto and peas
- Charred Leaks
- Tortelli

Dishes I'd skip:
- Fagioli All' Uccelletto
- Fried Candoon

Looking for a table? Walk in around lunchtime on a weekday for no wait, come on the earlier end for dinnertime, or get lucky on Resy.

I've waited so long to try this restaurant and I was shockingly underwhelmed by the food. Incredibly hard to get a table, seating is way too close together, food was mediocre. However, there was great service.

Good Italian spot. Very hard to get a reservation but on a good day, pretty easy to walk in to get a bar spot with minimal wait.

The Cacio e Pepe is really good. I am not a fan of the noodle choice, but the rich cheesy flavor is there with a nice prominent kick from the black pepper.

They had an amazing special of Iberico pork ribs / chop on our visit. The pork was extraordinarily tender and flavourful (Iberico is the wagyu of pork). The sauce was subtly sweet and rich from the pork fat and prosciutto. A special pork dish indeed!

The burrata was standard, more savory than the other burrata I've had. The bruschetta special was just ok too. The tiramisu was also kind of disappointing. The cream tasted like just cream, it lacked the subtle sweetness and tang that I was expecting with mascarpone.

This restaurant should be shut down. First off we walked in at 7 and the lady said that they would text us when our table is ready max an hour. we did not get a text. we waited at the restaurant next door for an hour and a half and we walked in to ask how much longer it would be or if our table is ready. the "host" was surprisingly rude. told me it would be another 40 minutes. we heard good things about this place .sucks. i hope this lady get fired. she pushed my mom out and we were honestly very confused. told us to not come back. DO NOT RECOMMEND AT ALL.keep in mind people came out from the restaurant and were talking to us about how the food was really bad.
Food, service, vibes. The whole deal! I loved it so much (although we had to wait for a table for overs an hour) that we came back the text day. Food is 10/10 and so is the service!

The food is very average and bland. Real New Yorkers and people who have traveled know that this is fake Italian. I used to go frequently until I realized they serve farmed fish. The staff are all miserable from the owners to the waiters. The nice ones never seem to fit in and always leave. It must be a requirement to be miserable and "tough" to work there. It would be much better to smile for once. They never promote any minorities either.

We were excited to try this place but found it overrated. Definitely not worth waiting in line for. We ordered the arancini, anchovy bruschetta, and artichokes for appetizers and they were all very oily and greasy. There was an insane amount of butter on the toasts. The pastas were good but you can get equally good pasta, or better, for a better price. Service was great though.

We love always love coming to Via Carota-it is always a treat. We Always have great service, wonderful food, drinks, and desserts. We had bread and oil, appetizers, salads, wine, rice balls, meatballs, a few pastas, steak, many desserts etc. We Always love coming by when we have a chance and enjoy this wonderful restaurant.
Enjoy!

Ate dinner here early. Arrived at 5pm without reservations and got right in. It filled up quickly after that.
Was great food and a fun vibe 
I got the special rib eye steak and Gregg ordered the pork chop also a special 
We had the beets as an appetizer and a bottle of red wine 
Everything was delicious and waiter was great

Very nice, rustic decor makes the experience cozy. Had the chicken livers and arancini to start. Both excellent. Truffle noodles and Branzino baked in salt were outstanding. Great Italian wine selection. Excellent server. The only drawback was the hostess kept call us 'guys' like we're on a loading dock. "Wait over here guys." "I'm gonna get you a table guys."
This place specializes in negori drinks and it did not disappoint. The beet salad on crème fraîche with julienne strips of endive is simply divine!

Excellent! I will go again!
Friday night 5pm- 30-40 min wait for a bar seat. No worries it's Friday night . Host was polite and very welcoming. Got a bar seat- bartender very polite- made an excellent whiskey sour. 
I ordered the arancini- yummy!
The Brussels sprouts shaved salad- excellent- I ate every bite, but in hindsight wished I would've saved room for the pasta. Since it was my first time here, I felt obligated to get the caico e pepe which did not disappoint!!!! 
All of it was excellent. I was too full to try dessert but I'll definitely go again. The parpadelle ragu looked amazing, as did some of the other vegetable dishes.

Forget the overprice tag.  Money isn't the issue even though I'm bringing it up.  There was no taste to the truffle pasta!!  It was just oily.  The salad was, meh.  You are paying for the scene....unless I ordered the wrong things?

Walked in on a Wednesday during lunch and was immediately seated to my surprise. Friends and I placed an order for a couple of their pastas and their infamous leafy salad. 

Highlights definitely include the salad, the Cacio Pepe is in fact that good and it's a must order, and I was also pleasantly impressed by the arancini which were fantastic. 

If I ever get a chance to come here again I'll definitely be indulging in their Cacio Pepe. Taylor swift was really onto something with this one!

rose: i actually rlly enjoyed the lemon risotto which they made vegan for us

thorn: why did everyone recommend that salad and so we got it and it was a bowl of lettuce and nothing else??? straight up bad. overpriced af too. also 3 diff tables got sat next to us and refused to sit bc we were in the back room so we basically had a private room. is that a rose? maybe but im putting it in thorn. oh also stared at a dead pig head on the wall the whole meal.

bud: you will not see me back at this restaurant.

Solid Italian spot with good food, good service, and cozy vibes.

Stopped by on a cold Saturday at around 5:30 pm to put our names down on the waitlist. It's always a crapshoot on what time you'll get-- I think generally you'll be seated pretty shortly if you arrive around 4 pm, but who wants to eat then? Probably waiting until 4:45 - 5 pm would be what gets you the prime dinner time.

There was a line to put names down which was a little annoying since it was cold. Once we did, we were quoted a seating at the bar around 9 pm.

There's lots of other bars you can kill time at in the area, but my friend and I opted to head to her apartment to wait it out. Got the text that our table was ready around 8:10 pm and arrived back at the restaurant at 8:25 pm. The table wasn't actually ready, but after waiting another 10 minutes we were seated at the bar.

For food we ordered:
- Cacio e Pepe: This was so good! The pasta was the perfect texture and the creaminess+pepper really hit. I would order this pasta again
- Ragu Pappardelle: A solid pasta, great to get a different sauce. Personally I'm not the biggest pappardelle fan so I'd probably skip it again but as the only red sauce on the menu is a very solid and delicious option.
- Castelfranco: So good! Huge salad, a little bit bitter, and a whole lot of complexity. The salads are not to be slept on.
- Polpette: Solid, giant meatballs but honestly nothing that blew my mind. It's well executed and we wanted a carne, but honestly next time I'll probably just order another salad.
