It was the perfect amount to share in my opinion and we left very full! We also each got a cocktail that was pretty solid (a select spritz for me, a negroni for my friend). I'd definitely come back if a friend wanted to check this place out.
Service ambience and food is great. I love it. Only problem is the wait list. No reservations.

Had dinner for Valentines. Much of the night's splendid experience I will attribute to my date but the food did not disappoint.
Ambiance is superb, a sprinkle of industrial, a splash of rustic, so homey you can smell grandma cooking in the kitchen.
Staff are accomodating. The walk-in experience heightens one's yearning to dine here.

We had the leeks, tagliatelle, pappardelle, and rabbit, entire meal was eaten without hesitation, complaints, or a break. We didn't order much because we find ourselves having bigger eyes a lot of times, the nymber of dishes were perfect to satiate 2 adults with a combined weight of 350.

Couldn't ask for a better Valentine's day dinner experience. Get in line early, before 5pm to grab a dining time that suits your preference.

Happy eatings!
Cacio eh? Pepe. One of them was missing. Not sure which but the spirit of the place was replaced with a goop TikTok add. Get us out of here please

Ok this place is TOTALLY worth the hype. Lovely restaurant-- very bright ambiance-- with friendly service. I walked in around noon on a weekday and was able to snag a seat in the bar.

- Arancini: 100/10 (yummmm! Love how there's a spicy kick to it-- really cuts through the grease.)
- Cacio e peppe: 100/10 (I'm usually not a Cacio e peppe fan but ofc I had to get it here because there's so much hype around that dish. This is literally the BEST Cacio e peppe I've ever had!! Soo creamy and flavorful and the pepper gives a nice kick to the dish.)

I'll definitely be back to try out their salads and other pasta/risotto dishes next time!

I met a friend at this West Village osteria for lunch. Chris is a foodie, like me. Truth be told, he edited cookbooks for Rizzoli. I knew right away that I liked the place - lovely, airy and very Florentine! We were lucky to get a table without reservations! The food and service was amazing! So delicious! We started with a salad with anchovies and shared the mushrooms and smoked cheese and had the rigatoni with beef. Yummy! He had Nebbiolo and I had a Gran Classico  spritz. We had espresso after so we can continue to work in the afternoon!

My favorite Italian restaurant in NYC. Via Carota is the West Village osteria of celebrated chefs Rita Sodi and Jody Williams, serving food inspired by old world Italian culinary traditions. They won a James Beard Award in 2019, but have become even more popular (and a celebrity hotspot) in recent years.

If you are not a celebrity, a reservation is nearly impossible to obtain. Your best bet is to queue up at 4pm, to be added to a wait list. On a Wednesday, I was quoted a 3 hour wait for a party of 3. So, I posted up across the street at their bar, Pisellino, and sipped excellent Negronis until my table was ready. 

I dined here with a vegetarian and a vegan, and was pleasantly surprised at how accommodating they were. Via Carota does vegetables very well. We loved the juicy grilled Funghi with smoked Scamorza, decadent Lemon Risotto, rich Tonnarelli Cacio e Pepe, and perfectly cooked Broccoli Rabe. The tiramisu was good, but the wine poached pear dessert was unforgettable.

Perhaps my favorite part of the meal was our Amari tasting at the end, with dessert. Our server made excellent recommendations, and had a great sense of humor. 

We were seated at what was (by far) the worst table in the restaurant, in a dark corner under the coat racks. We watched the grown man seated next to us throw an actual tantrum about the table lol. I can see how that could ruin a romantic date night, but for my friends and I, it was nothing short of perfect. I can't wait to come back.

Regardless of how much hype or exclusivity a restaurant might have, I always try to come with an open mind. Unfortunately I was a bit let down by this place, specifically by the food (and more specifically, by the pasta). With that said, the service was great and there were some delicious dishes I tried. I just think there are sooooo many amazing Italian restaurants in the city that I've had better food at. 

Experience / Ambiance: was able to snag an early dinner weekend reservation. There was a line of ~25 people waiting to put their names down when I got there at 4:30pm and the line just kept getting longer and longer. Based on my food experience, it is not worth waiting in line for. Ambiance is casual, feels intimate and very neighborhoodly. Restaurant isn't big, but larger than I thought. There was a party of 9, so could potentially be good for a large group. 

Food: sadly the pasta dishes were subpar. Noodles were VERY under seasoned. I had to ask for salt & a side of parmesan cheese. I ordered:

-Insalata Verde: to be honest, I'm not sure why this is so famous... it wasn't bad by any means, just very standard. Good to share, simple, fresh, and mild flavored. 

-Polipo (octopus): great to share. Really enjoyed this. Octopus was thick, but perfectly cooked. Very strong olive flavor (which I enjoyed), but if you're not a huge olive fan don't order. 

-Tonnarelli: I was very disappointed by this. But if you go you have to order because it's one of their most well known dishes. Good peppery flavor, but no salt.

-Tagliatelle: similar to the tonnarelli - needed A LOT of salt. 

-Via Carota Svizzerina: highly recommend! Best thing I tried. Thought it was steak - it is not lol. Basically a burger (sans bun) that is charred on both sides. Comes with roasted garlic. It was perfectly seasoned and a big surprise!

-Tiramisu: good size to share!

Tonight, I went to "Via Carota" located on 51 Grove Street in New York City, which is a
charming Italian trattoria that captures the essence of rustic Italian dining. The ambiance is warm and inviting with a cozy interior that reflects a blend of both elegance
and casual comfort. The menu features a variety of traditional Italian dishes, showcasing fresh, high-quality ingredients. Standout items often include their pasta, which is handmade daily,and the seasonal vegetable dishes that highlight local produce. The flavors are authentic and well-balanced, making each dish a delightful experience. The wine list offers a carefully curated selection of Italian wines, enhancing the meal perfectly. The staff is knowledgeable and attentive, providing excellent service that
complements the dining experience without being intrusive.While the restaurant can get busy, especially during peak hours, the vibrant atmosphere adds to the overall experience. Reservations are recommended to secure a spot. Also, Tuesdays are a great day to get a reservation.I had Pollo Alla Griglia grilled free-range chicken in salmoriglio. Out of this world.Risotto Meyer Lemon & parmigiano risotto. Fresh spinach ravioli with homemade pesto. Washed it all down with a
coffee.Overall, "Via Carota" is a fantastic choice for anyone looking to indulge in delicious Italian cuisine in a beautiful setting, making it a must-visit for locals and tourists alike. #onlyinnyc #viacarota #italianfood

It befuddles me that this place remains hard to get in to, as there are so many better Italian restaurants in the city. Our Pappardelle was mushy, the mushroom dish with cheese was greasy and the two ingredients did nothing to complement each other, and the chopped steak was boring and all around not worth eating.  The one saving grace was the Cacio Pepe. They also do one of the best Negronis around.

Food: 4.4/5
Service: 4.5/5
Ambiance: 4.4/5
Value: 3.5/5

I had a pleasant lunch on Monday at about 1pm. I was a solo walk in diner and sat at the bar. There were a few spots there. I was impressed with their selection of different amaro liqueurs. I read that you can use amaro in a negroni instead of Campari or vermouth. The Paper Plane cocktail calls for Amaro Nonino Quintessentia, which they had, so I ordered one ($20). It was refreshing and delicious, though small. I finished it in a few sips.

For food I ate the tonnarelli pasta in cacio e pepe form ($27), along with the wild boar ragu pappardelle ($28). Both were delicious, but the portions were small for the price. The pasta is springy and firm. It's very hot. You need to wait a bit before you eat it. 

Sitting at the bar i didn't have a specific server, just whoever happened to be in my area at the time. All of them were prompt and polite. I like the material that the bar is made of. The bar stool is a bit higher than I'd like, and has no back, but is well made and sturdy. The plates are from Hutschenreuther and are nice.

I'm not sure what the hype is about after many tries we got a walk-in reservation to sit at the bar given it's so hard to find anything on resy. The food is OK but not mind blowing, ambience is OK but not mind blowing, Driks are OK but not mind blowing. I'm not sure why getting a reservation at this place is so so hard. I am most likely not returning here, for my Italian cravings I prefer rezdora.
One of the best restaurants in the entire city by far. We always try to go at an off hour to skip the line. But the food and drinks hit perfectly every single time we go.

I don't usually leave reviews. But I recently had what was probably my 6th or 7th meal at Via Carota. I had not been back since before the pandemic. It had been my favorite restaurant before that, not for the innovation of any individual dish, but for the perfection of a certain way of dining. A way that I have always associated with my travels to Italy: healthy delicious food based on excellent ingredients and lots of seasonal vegetables. All served up with great informality but perfect expertise and a sense of graciousness. It was a dear old friends 57th birthday. We needed to meet in the village. Let's try to get in. Is it still as good as I recalled? The latest Yelp reviews seemed maybe mixed... We arrived at 5:50, it was packed on a Wednesday afternoon (a very good sign the magic is still being made). A warm welcome from the host, a perfect white Negroni quickly in hand, we were then seated. Charred leeks stuffed w goat cheese and roasted funghi on a thin slab of smoked scamorza to commence, we split a lemon risotto (my date is gluten intolerant), and followed with chunks of sweet bacalao with garbanzos and I think some cherry tomato and black olives. All washed down with a Ligurian white wine. The meal was unrushed, expertly served, and delicious. Via Carota is very much alive and doing as well as ever.
